title: Cramer, Rocket Lab President Discuss Future of Commercial Space Industry at UND Summit
text:
***Click here for photos.***

GRAND FORKS, N.D. – Leaders from America’s space discovery ecosystem joined astronauts, Space Development Agency (SDA) officials, and interested students at the University of North Dakota’s (UND) Space Operations Summit. U.S. Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND) welcomed Rocket Lab USA President Brad Clevenger to the symposium. They discussed how today’s rapidly evolving private space industry is merging with the existing policy and government framework created during the space race more than 50 years ago.

Cramer invited Clevenger to discuss his experience in the commercial space sector, advancements in satellite technology, and share his thoughts on the expanding role of private industry in both space exploration and national security. He covered what this means for policymakers, business owners, and the industry’s future workforce.

“Space touches every aspect of our lives, from GPS to banking to improving our quality of life,” said Cramer. “It’s become a warfighting domain for us, one we must defend. Our ecosystem enables us to protect the space domain. We’ve got a great talent pool in the region, but we also have President Andy Armacost, who is nimble, and Robert Kraus, Dean of the School of Aerospace Sciences, who understands the vision. They work with our government partners and private companies to improve our capabilities quickly to meet the changing needs in space.”

The discussion comes as Rocket Lab announced plans to acquire Iridium Communications, a leading global provider of satellite communications and positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) services. The proposed acquisition underscores the growing importance of commercial satellite capabilities and the expanding role of private companies in the global space industry.

Iridium has an established presence in North Dakota, employing dozens of highly skilled workers at Grand Forks Air Force Base, home to SDA’s Operations Center North and its Technology Acceleration Center. These facilities support operations for SDA’s low-Earth-orbit missions.

Clevenger leads Rocket Lab’s Space Systems segment, overseeing its satellite and satellite component businesses. Before joining Rocket Lab, he held executive leadership positions at SolAero Technologies and EMCORE Corporation. Over his two decades in the industry, he has contributed to more than 250 satellite missions and the deployment of more than 1,100 satellites. Under his leadership, the business grew into a global leader in satellite solar power technology.

title: UND, Vorbeck Sign Memorandum of Understanding to Work Closely on National Security and Space Research
text:
***Click herefor media resources.***

GRAND FORKS, N.D. – North Dakota’s growing role in space research and defense technology took another step forward today, when U.S. Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND) joined leaders from the University of North Dakota (UND) and Vorbeck to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) formalizing a framework to accelerate advanced defense technologies while broadening educational opportunities for students and growing the high-tech workforce.

Cramer brought together leaders from Vorbeck, a U.S. manufacturer serving the defense, aerospace, and first responder industries, and UND as part of his efforts to connect promising private sector businesses with the intellectual and educational capital in Grand Forks. Vorbeck opened its new Grand Forks manufacturing facility in May, creating hands-on learning opportunities for UND students while adding to the region’s growing economy. The company also provides internship and employment opportunities and sponsors UND’s Advanced Rocketry Club, giving students a chance to design, build, and test rockets.

The new agreement builds on this momentum, connecting UND’s research capabilities and student talent with Vorbeck’s work developing advanced materials and technologies for critical industries. Cramer spoke about the speed and synergy that come with the relationship.

“I’ve always felt like when you have friends who don't know each other, you should do as much as you can to help them get to know each other,” said Cramer. “And in this position, I was able to make that happen. We're living in a moment when we don't even know what solutions are necessary—but when a solution comes forward, you have to go fast because a week later, there will be something else that needs solving. And we're in a very fast-moving technological moment, where we have problem solving happening before the next problem arises. The synergy which comes along with this allows us to see around the corner, or see the next problem before it's a problem, and start solving for it. And so that's a little bit of my dream, you guys, for this relationship we’re creating today.”

“Having strong partnerships with industry supports the development of new technologies,” said Scott Snyder, UND’s vice president for Research and Economic Development. “Vorbeck’s expertise and manufacturing capabilities complement the research happening across UND. Through this agreement, we can move promising technologies from discovery to deployment.”

"This partnership is about more than advancing technology,” said Tyler Sletten, Site Leader for Vorbeck's North Dakota operations. “It’s about recognizing what we have here in North Dakota: extraordinary talent, a spirit of innovation, and the determination to do things that matter. Together, UND and Vorbeck have an opportunity to strengthen our national defense and show that the future of American innovation isn't just happening somewhere else. It's happening right here in North Dakota."

Twenty years after its founding in Maryland in 2006, Vorbeck chose to relocate to Grand Forks last year, taking advantage of the region’s growing defense industry and its strengths in aerospace, autonomous systems, unmanned aircraft, cybersecurity, and space research.

This combination is putting Grand Forks on the map as a place for defense contractors and technology companies looking to grow, innovate, and build partnerships. With access to university research, a skilled workforce, proximity to Grand Forks Air Force Base and strong collaboration among industry, government and academia, the region offers a compelling environment for companies working on the next generation of national security capabilities.

One of Vorbeck’s latest creations is its patented graphene-based firefighting foam, now being manufactured at its Grand Forks facility. The technology is designed to outperform traditional firefighting agents without using the chemicals in PFAS which are associated with environmental and health concerns. It’s a product with potential benefits for firefighters and first responders.

For UND, the agreement creates more opportunities to connect students and research with industry. For Vorbeck, it strengthens its North Dakota footprint. And for Grand Forks, it’s another example of how the region is building a defense and technology ecosystem capable of attracting new companies, talent, and investment.

title: Duckworth: “Americans Sent a Clear Message: They Are Sick of Donald Trump’s BS”
text:
[CHICAGO, IL] – Speaking just hours after Democrats reclaimed the Senate and House majorities in Congress, U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) emphasized the need for Democrats to seize this moment—and this momentum—to take real action to help deliver relief for the many Americans who've been left behind by the Trump Administration. Joining Governor JB Pritzker and Senator-elect Juliana Stratton (D-IL), Duckworth laid out several of her top priorities for the next Congress, including cancelling Trump's cuts to Medicaid, restoring ACA tax credits, passing legislation that drive down everyday costs for middle-class families and ending Trump's illegal war of choice with Iran. Photos from today’s press conference can be found on the Senator’s website and the full video recording can be found on the Senator’s YouTube page.

Key Quotes:

“Last night, Americans sent a clear message: They are sick of Donald Trump’s bullshit. They are tired of him promising one thing in the morning then going back on his word by the afternoon. They’re done with him putting his self-interest over our national interest. So we’re here today to let those folks know that we hear them. That we’re with them. That we’re just as pissed off as they are... [So] we’re going to use every seat we gained to fight back against Trump and fight for what American families really need.”

“The reality is, from utility bills to grocery bills, health care to child care, far too many Americans feel like they’re one bad day, one doctor’s appointment, one stop at the gas pump away from disaster. Far too many fifth-generation farmers have told me that they can’t sleep at night, because they don’t know if they can hold on long enough to hand the farm to a sixth generation. Meanwhile, Trump has quite literally said that he doesn’t 'give a damn' about inflation so long as he makes a fortune... Well, I give a damn. We give a damn.”

“Americans don’t just want a repair job. They need—they deserve—a top-to-bottom renovation... And when I become Senior Senator in January, with Juliana by my side in DC and JB as our partner here in Illinois, we will fight like hell for that more perfect Union we know we can be.”

Full remarks as delivered are below:

Hello everyone!

Thank you, Governor Pritzker, for hosting us.

I’m so grateful to be here with you all today—and to be able to say and say: Hello, Senator-Elect Stratton!!

Listen: Last night, Americans sent a clear message:

They are sick of Donald Trump’s bullshit.

They are tired of him promising one thing in the morning then going back on his word by the afternoon.

They’re done with him putting his self-interest over our national interest.

So we’re here today to let those folks know that we hear them.

That we’re with them.

That we’re just as pissed off as they are.

And that… with Juliana joining our ranks in DC… we’re going to use every seat we gained to fight back against Trump and fight for what American families really need.

The reality is, from utility bills to grocery bills, health care to child care, far too many Americans feel like they’re one bad day… one doctor’s appointment… one stop at the gas pump away from disaster.

Far too many fifth-generation farmers have told me that they can’t sleep at night, because they don’t know if they can hold on long enough to hand the farm to a sixth generation.

Meanwhile, Trump has quite literally said that he doesn’t “give a damn” about inflation so long as he makes a fortune. And every day, his actions show that he means it.

Well, I give a damn. We give a damn.

That’s why you better believe that in this next Congress, we’re going to fight to hold Donald Trump accountable and deliver real results for families.

It’s gonna be our priority to restore the ACA tax credits and cancel Trump’s cuts to Medicaid…

Cuts that are set to kick millions off their health care plans and put hundreds of hospitals at risk of closure, just so Trump could hand Elon Musk and other Big Tech billionaires massive tax breaks.

We’re gonna work to pass bills that drive down everyday costs for middle-class families… bills that look out for the people we’ve been sent to Washington to serve.

Because I’ve been that little girl whose parents didn’t know how they were going to afford enough bread to make sandwiches for the week.

So I refuse to let any American still facing those struggles feel like they’re falling through the cracks.

And we’re gonna keep using every lever we have to force Donald Trump to end his illegal war with Iran.

A war no one wanted… that has killed at least 23 of our servicemembers… crashed our economy… and put our country in more, not less, danger.

Because unlike that five-time draft-dodging coward, we would NEVER use our troops as political pawns.

And we refuse to let one man’s personal insecurities trump our national security.

Let me just close with this: These priorities only scratch the surface of the mountain of things that need to get done in the next two years.

Because Americans don’t just want a repair job. They need… they deserve… a top-to-bottom renovation. They deserve us not to just fight back against this Administration but to fight FOR policies that will better their everyday lives… things like universal child care, affordable housing and every hopeful parent’s right to access IVF.

And when I become Senior Senator in January… with Juliana by my side in DC and JB as our partner here in Illinois… we will fight like hell for that more perfect Union we know we can be.

Thank you. And with that let me hand it over to the next Senator from Illinois, my friend Juliana.

title: KRQE: New Mexico Sen. Martin Heinrich reacts to Democrats taking back control of Congress
text:
It was a clear message to Republicans and Democrats Tuesday, as results in New Mexico and beyond showed a decisive shift in control, from red to blue across the House of Representatives and Senate.

“Early on, it was evident that this was going to be a very unique election,” said Senator Martin Heinrich, (D) New Mexico.

“It was pretty exciting. You don’t see elections like this very often,” said Sen. Heinrich.

Now in his third term, Sen. Heinrich noted the change in places like Texas and Kansas, states that haven’t seen Democratic leadership in decades.

“I think that ties directly back to just how economically frustrated people are with the pace of inflation, cost of their health care. And so the people sent a very strong message, and I hope we all listen to it,” said Sen. Heinrich.

Heinrich, who is now set to be the chairman of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, said he sees the change giving his party an opportunity to bring down prices. “One of those things, for example, is under current law, a lot of these data centers are able to push the cost of their grid upgrades onto consumers and small businesses. We should prohibit that. We should make it illegal. They should pay their own freight,” said Sen. Heinrich.

But those ideas, Sen. Heinrich acknowledged, will face a president from a different party. “We’re in the majority in the House and Senate, but it takes 60 votes in the Senate, so it’s still going to be important to work in a bipartisan manner. And the, you know, the occupant of the white house is not different today than yesterday.”

“It’s still going to be two years where there are real differences between the direction that the administration wants to take the country and what the public is clamoring for, and that’s going to be hard to manage,” said Sen. Heinrich.

Sen. Heinrich said that another opportunity he sees under Democratic Senate control is the potential of increasing protections to public lands like Chaco Canyon and the Pecos River headwaters.

title: Reuters: Democrat permitting bill authors 'not going to wait' for new US Congress
text:
The Democratic architects of proposed bipartisan energy permitting legislation said on Wednesday they would not delay the bill in hopes of securing a better deal next year when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress.

The measure, known as the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, would overhaul federal permitting processes for energy and infrastructure projects and is expected to be a major focus of Congress now that the midterm elections are over. The bill is the culmination of a years-long effort to pass legislation aimed at speeding construction of transmission lines, mines and both renewable and fossil fuel energy projects.

"This is the closest we have come to actually finding something that can get signed into law, and I'm not going to wait," Senator Martin Heinrich of New Mexico said in a statement to Reuters.

In a separate statement, Senator Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island said: "A good permitting bill comes together over years of complex negotiations... It's a bird in the hand. We'd be fools not to take it."

title: Heinrich, Luján, and Vasquez Welcome Over $16.7 Million to Establish Carlsbad State Veterans Cemetery
text:
CARLSBAD, N.M. — U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), a member of the U.S. Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Military Construction, Veterans Affairs and Related Agencies, U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), and U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (D-N.M.) welcomed $16,711,624 from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to establish the Carlsbad State Veterans Cemetery, which will serve more than 5,000 veterans and eligible family members in the Carlsbad region of New Mexico.

The grant will fund construction at the cemetery, including entry monument and gates, administration building, maintenance building, committal service shelter, flag assembly area, 300 double-depth pre-placed crypts, 250 columbarium niches, 500 in-ground cremation gravesites, and a memorial wall. The VA will also reimburse the cost of fabrication and delivery of pre-placed crypts up to the amount of $625,670.

“New Mexico veterans have sacrificed so much in service to our country, and we owe them and their families a lasting a debt of gratitude,” said Heinrich. “I’m proud to welcome $16.7 million to establish the Carlsbad State Veterans Cemetery, ensuring veterans in southeastern New Mexico have a final resting place where their service and sacrifice can be honored.”

“New Mexico’s veterans have served our country with dignity and honor, and we have a responsibility to ensure they receive the recognition and respect they deserve,” said Luján. “This $16.7 million federal investment will help ensure veterans in southeastern New Mexico have a final resting place close to home. I’m honored to welcome this investment and will continue working to ensure New Mexico’s veterans and their families receive the benefits and support they have earned.”

“We owe veterans the honor and dignity of being laid to rest in a place that recognizes their sacrifice for our country,” said Vasquez. “A new State Veterans Cemetery in Carlsbad will mean a lot to families in southeast New Mexico, who will finally have a place to bury their loved ones with honor and distinction much closer to home.”

title: Hickenlooper & Hurd Lead Colorado Congressional Delegation in Support of Major Presidential Disaster Request for Southwestern Colorado Flooding
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper and Representative Jeff Hurd led the Colorado Congressional Delegation, including Senator Michael Bennet and U.S. Representatives Diana DeGette, Joe Neguse, Jason Crow, Lauren Boebert, Brittany Pettersen, Jeff Crank, and Gabe Evans, in a letter to President Trump expressing strong support for Governor Jared Polis’ request for an expedited Presidential Major Disaster Declaration following devastating and historic flooding and debris flows in Southwestern Colorado and the San Luis Valley.

“We strongly support Governor Jared Polis’ request on October 31, 2026, for an expedited Presidential Major Disaster Declaration for Southwestern Colorado and the San Luis Valley in response to the recent extensive and devastating flooding throughout the region,” wrote the lawmakers. “While this request pertains to the initial flooding on October 22-25, we are writing in the midst of a second catastrophic flooding event across the same region, which adds urgency to this request. These impacts are compounded by the damaging flooding in October 2025, which have seriously strained available resources for recovery for previously affected communities.”

The Governor’s request seeks Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Public Assistance and Hazard Mitigation Grant Program funding for Archuleta and Rio Grande Counties, where state and federal officials have already validated nearly $27 million in eligible damages. The flooding also impacted Alamosa, Conejos, Dolores, Hinsdale, La Plata, Mineral, Montezuma, Ouray, San Juan, and San Miguel Counties, where damage assessments continue and additional requests for federal assistance are expected.

In late October and early November, severe storms brought devastating flooding and debris flows to Southwestern Colorado, damaging roads, bridges, utilities, homes, and businesses, and cutting off access to entire communities. Preliminary assessments for Archuleta and Rio Grande Counties have identified approximately $10.6 million in damage to local roads, bridges, and culverts; $2.44 million in damage to public utilities; and $8.59 million in damage to parks and recreation facilities. These figures do not include additional damage assessments underway or separate federal highway repair costs.

“Without additional support, residents could face unsafe homes and drinking water, long delays in rebuilding critical roads and bridges, and the loss of local businesses,” wrote the lawmakers. “Successful recovery is essential to restoring these communities’ economies, which depend on agriculture, tourism, outdoor recreation, and hunting and fishing.”

The full text of the letter is available here and below.

Dear Mr. President:

We strongly support Governor Jared Polis’ request on October 31, 2026, for an expedited Presidential Major Disaster Declaration for Southwestern Colorado and the San Luis Valley in response to the recent extensive and devastating flooding throughout the region. While this request pertains to the initial flooding on October 22-25, we are writing in the midst of a second catastrophic flooding event across the same region, which adds urgency to this request. These impacts are compounded by the damaging flooding in October 2025, which have seriously strained available resources for recovery for previously affected communities.

Beginning October 22, 2026, torrential rain fell on the San Juan Mountains and San Luis Valley, already saturated by weeks of rainfall. During this initial flooding event, the San Juan River in Pagosa Springs crested at its second-highest level since 1911, and the Rio Grande reached approximately 11,000 cubic feet per second, surpassing its 1949 record. Although assessments are ongoing, totals showed the initial flooding damaged approximately 700 homes across Archuleta and Rio Grande Counties, completely destroying 16 homes and 6 commercial buildings. The flooding caused extensive damage to multiple roads and bridges, overwhelmed wastewater systems, and contaminated private wells. The Colorado National Guard airlifted stranded residents to safety, and we are grateful that no fatalities have been reported.

As outlined in the Governor’s expedited request, the affected counties and Tribe have suffered damages severe enough to qualify for the Public Assistance (PA) Program. The Joint Preliminary Damage Assessment validated$26,989,000 in PA-eligible damages. As assessments continue, additional losses are likely to be identified with additional assistance requested. Granting the Governor’s initial request for Archuleta and Rio Grande Counties will expedite urgent repairs for public infrastructure damages.

The State of Colorado is also requesting the activation of the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program for these counties in order to implement better infrastructure solutions to protect against future monsoon seasons and flood events. As these local communities have historically been proudly self-reliant, they are eager to rebuild more resiliently.

Successful recovery is essential to restoring these communities’ economies, which depend on agriculture, tourism, outdoor recreation, and hunting and fishing. In already isolated rural areas, road closures are cutting residents off from their homes, schools, work, and essential services. We appreciate the Federal Highway Administration moving quickly to approve $6.5 million in quick release funds to help with immediate repairs on US Highway 160, US 550, and Colorado Highway 151, all which provide critical routes into the communities most impacted by this disaster. Without additional support, residents could face unsafe homes and drinking water, long delays in rebuilding critical roads and bridges, and the loss of local businesses.

We thank you in advance for your expedited review and approval of the Governor’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration.

Sincerely,

###

title: Klobuchar, Smith, Finstad Urge Trump Administration to Approve Minnesota’s Request for Disaster Declaration
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Tina Smith (D-MN) and Representative Brad Finstad (R-MN) urged the Trump Administration to approve Minnesota’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration to help communities in southeastern Minnesota that are working to recover from severe weather and flooding this past September. If this disaster declaration is approved, the federal government will be able to provide disaster assistance for various recovery efforts.

“We write to you in strong support of the state of Minnesota’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance under the Stafford Act to assist our constituents recovering from severe storms and flooding. These natural disasters have caused significant damage, and we ask that you quickly grant approval for federal disaster assistance,” said the lawmakers.

The lawmakers continued, “Time and time again, Minnesotans have stepped up to support their neighbors after natural disasters. When flood waters rise and homes are damaged, volunteers and neighbors are quick to fill sandbags, clean up debris, and lend a hand to those in need. Impacted communities will repair the damage and rebuild following these disasters, but rapid federal assistance will speed up this recovery effort.”

Full text of the letter is available HERE and below:

Dear Mr. President:

We write to you in strong support of the state of Minnesota’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance under the Stafford Act to assist our constituents recovering from severe storms and flooding. These natural disasters have caused significant damage, and we ask that you quickly grant approval for federal disaster assistance.

In September 2026, south and southeastern Minnesota experienced severe weather events that caused flooding in the region. A line of thunderstorms formed late September 18 and repeatedly passed over the same communities into early September 19. Approximately 700 square miles across this region received six inches or more of precipitation within 24 hours, according to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources. In the City of New Richland alone, more than three-quarters of homes are damaged and residents of a skilled nursing facility were evacuated and unable to return to the facility. Many homes across the impacted area suffered flooded basements and damaged furnaces and boilers which will need repair or replacement ahead of the Minnesota winter. This storm event has been assessed as at least as destructive as the July 2026 mega-rain that many of these communities experienced and were recovering from just months prior.

Joint federal and state emergency management teams have conducted preliminary damage assessments and have determined that the losses meet the threshold for federal assistance under the Stafford Act through a Major Disaster Declaration. Governor Walz has submitted an official request for disaster assistance for the period of September 18 to September 20, 2026. The request, dated November 2, 2026, covers Fillmore, Houston, Steele, and Waseca Counties.

Time and time again, Minnesotans have stepped up to support their neighbors after natural disasters. When flood waters rise and homes are damaged, volunteers and neighbors are quick to fill sandbags, clean up debris, and lend a hand to those in need. Impacted communities will repair the damage and rebuild following these disasters, but rapid federal assistance will speed up this recovery effort.

We strongly support Minnesota’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance, including for the Individuals and Households program and Disaster Unemployment Assistance, as well as Hazard Mitigation assistance to invest in disaster resiliency efforts. We ask that you grant its approval without delay.

title: NEWS: Padilla, Schiff Announce More Than $116 Million to Improve Railroad Crossing Safety Across California
text:
CALIFORNIA — Today, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff (both D-Calif.) announced that six California projects will receive more than $116 million in federal funding through President Biden’s Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), which Padilla and Schiff voted to pass. The funding, awarded through the Federal Railroad Administration’s Railroad Crossing Elimination (RCE) Program, will improve railroad crossing safety, reduce traffic delays, and strengthen rail infrastructure in Burlingame, Sunnyvale, Richmond, Riverside, San Diego, and Suisun City.

“These federal investments will help make California’s railroad crossings safer, reduce traffic delays, and strengthen the transportation infrastructure our communities depend on,” said Senator Padilla. “From eliminating hazardous crossings to planning future safety upgrades, these projects will improve mobility for Californians and support a stronger regional economy thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. I’ll keep fighting to ensure our communities get these critical investments and the resources they need to grow and thrive.”

“I am proud to help deliver federal funding for critical safety and modernization upgrades for railroad crossings throughout California—made possible by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. All Californians deserve to live in communities with robust transportation infrastructure that helps reduce congestion. These federal investments will help ensure the safety of our pedestrians and drivers,” said Senator Schiff.

The six California projects selected for funding will advance grade separation projects, feasibility studies, and planning efforts to improve safety and mobility for motorists, pedestrians, cyclists, and rail passengers.

Burlingame Broadway Grade Separation Project — $90.42 million: The Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board will eliminate an at-grade crossing by constructing an elevated rail structure and lowering the roadway, improving safety and reducing traffic delays.

Mary Avenue Grade Separation Project, Sunnyvale — $15.50 million: The City of Sunnyvale will advance final design work for a future grade separation along the Caltrain corridor.

Cutting/Carlson At-Grade Crossing Elimination Study, Richmond — $3.36 million: The City of Richmond will plan for a future grade separation at the Cutting Boulevard crossing along the Union Pacific Railroad corridor.

Spruce Street Crossing Closure and Grade Separation Project, Riverside — $2.80 million: The City of Riverside will advance planning and project development for a future grade separation along the BNSF corridor.

San Diego Regionwide At-Grade Crossing Elimination Study — $2.73 million: The San Diego Association of Governments (SANDAG) will plan for safety improvements, separations, or elimination of 39 grade crossings across the regional rail network.

Sunset Avenue Grade Separation Feasibility Study, Suisun City — $2.01 million: The City of Suisun City will evaluate alternatives to separate vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian traffic from the Union Pacific Railroad corridor.

Senator Padilla has been a strong advocate for investing in California’s transportation infrastructure and delivering federal resources to communities across the state. The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, also known as the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, provided advance appropriations for the Railroad Crossing Elimination Program, which funds highway-rail and pathway-rail grade crossing improvements to enhance safety and mobility for people and goods.

title: Padilla Statement on 2026 Midterm Elections
text:
SACRAMENTO, CA — Today, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Rules Committee with oversight over federal elections, released the following statement regarding the 2026 midterm election results:

“Last night, tens of millions of Americans across our nation made their voices heard and their message was unmistakable: It’s time to bring down costs and put working families first. It’s time to end Trump’s chaos, corruption, and cruelty. And it’s time to hold those who exploit their positions of power for private profit accountable.

“Now is the time to focus on both affordability and accountability. When Democrats take charge in January, that is exactly what we intend to deliver.

“We will fight to reverse Trump’s devastating cuts to healthcare and ensure that the ultra-wealthy and the biggest corporations pay their fair share.

“We will investigate the brazen corruption we’ve seen coming out of the White House and finally pass legislation to reform our elections and strengthen voting rights.

“We will do everything in our power to end the unlawful war in Iran, bring down gas and diesel prices, and reverse Trump’s reckless tariffs that are making life unaffordable for the American people.

“And we will work to end ICE and DHS’s terror in our communities, advance solutions to modernize our immigration system, and provide a pathway to citizenship for immigrants who have lived in the United States for years, worked, paid taxes and strengthened our communities. I’ve already introduced legislation to do just that, and I look forward to working with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to get it done.

“After the American people spoke so clearly and so resolutely, even President Trump has acknowledged that the election result was undeniable. But we cannot be complacent — election misinformation and voter disenfranchisement are still real threats. Every eligible vote must, and will, be counted including in states like California, Alaska and Mississippi where the counts are ongoing. That is normal — not every election is called on election night, and that’s nothing new.

“What is new is Trump’s DOJ has tried and failed to purge eligible voters from state voter rolls, and it has not given up on seeking to block the counting of ballots in California and Washington. DOJ’s baseless legal challenge continues in Alaska. So we will remain vigilant.

“Yesterday, the American people showed up and demanded a better future. Now it’s Congress’ job to build it.

“Let’s get to work.”

If this disaster declaration is approved, the federal government will be able to provide disaster assistance for various recovery efforts.

“We write to you in strong support of the state of Minnesota’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance under the Stafford Act to assist our constituents recovering from severe storms and flooding. These natural disasters have caused significant damage, and we ask that you quickly grant approval for federal disaster assistance,” said the lawmakers.

The lawmakers continued, “Time and time again, Minnesotans have stepped up to support their neighbors after natural disasters. When flood waters rise and homes are damaged, volunteers and neighbors are quick to fill sandbags, clean up debris, and lend a hand to those in need. Impacted communities will repair the damage and rebuild following these disasters, but rapid federal assistance will speed up this recovery effort.”

Full text of the letter is available HERE and below:

Dear Mr. President:

We write to you in strong support of the state of Minnesota’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance under the Stafford Act to assist our constituents recovering from severe storms and flooding. These natural disasters have caused significant damage, and we ask that you quickly grant approval for federal disaster assistance.

In September 2026, south and southeastern Minnesota experienced severe weather events that caused flooding in the region. A line of thunderstorms formed late September 18 and repeatedly passed over the same communities into early September 19. Approximately 700 square miles across this region received six inches or more of precipitation within 24 hours, according to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources. In the City of New Richland alone, more than three-quarters of homes are damaged and residents of a skilled nursing facility were evacuated and unable to return to the facility. Many homes across the impacted area suffered flooded basements and damaged furnaces and boilers which will need repair or replacement ahead of the Minnesota winter. This storm event has been assessed as at least as destructive as the July 2026 mega-rain that many of these communities experienced and were recovering from just months prior.

Joint federal and state emergency management teams have conducted preliminary damage assessments and have determined that the losses meet the threshold for federal assistance under the Stafford Act through a Major Disaster Declaration. Governor Walz has submitted an official request for disaster assistance for the period of September 18 to September 20, 2026. The request, dated November 2, 2026, covers Fillmore, Houston, Steele, and Waseca Counties.

Time and time again, Minnesotans have stepped up to support their neighbors after natural disasters. When flood waters rise and homes are damaged, volunteers and neighbors are quick to fill sandbags, clean up debris, and lend a hand to those in need. Impacted communities will repair the damage and rebuild following these disasters, but rapid federal assistance will speed up this recovery effort.

We strongly support Minnesota’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance, including for the Individuals and Households program and Disaster Unemployment Assistance, as well as Hazard Mitigation assistance to invest in disaster resiliency efforts. We ask that you grant its approval without delay.

###

title: Welch Statement on Senate and House Democrats’ Victories in the Midterms
text:

“Our victory is a clear repudiation of Donald Trump’s reckless agenda and his failure to deliver for the American people. The president has forced us into an illegal war in the Middle East, raised costs and taxes by igniting a trade war with our allies, and threatened our democratic institutions. Communities are less safe, hardworking families are struggling to make ends meet, and Americans’ faith in our democratic institutions has eroded. Yesterday, voters said ‘Enough!’

We must be laser-focused on lowering costs for folks in red and blue states alike; we must fight like hell to restore their access to health care and nutrition; and we must invest in rural communities, which have been left behind and hollowed out. title: Congressman Allen Announces 2027 Spring Internship Program
text:
Today, Congressman Rick W. Allen (GA-12) announced his office is seeking applicants for the 2027 Spring Internship Program, to be offered in his Washington, D.C. office.

title: Beyer Testifies Against Trump’s Proposed Vanity Arch, Urges National Capital Planning Commission to Reject Proposal
text:
Congressman Don Beyer (D-VA), who represents a Northern Virginia district in the U.S. House that includes Arlington National Cemetery and Ronald Reagan National Airport (DCA), testified before the National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) today, urging the Commission to reject the Trump Administration’s proposed 250-foot arch on Columbia Island.

The 12-member Commission, which oversees federal construction and planning projects in the National Capital Region and is now led by Trump allies, is expected to vote on the proposed arch later this evening.

During his testimony, Beyer said:

“While the President has called for the project to be “converted” to a base for drones and snipers, that appears nowhere in this Commission’s consideration of the project. Apparently, placing a large weapons cache within feet of tourists, pedestrians, cyclists, Metro riders, and drivers commuting to work is not worth serious concern by a Commission tasked with region-wide planning.

“I can only conclude that by rubber-stamping the Arch without considering that position, this Commission is either calling the President a liar, or knowingly moving forward with an incomplete and potentially-fraudulent application.”

Beyer’s full written testimony is available here, and video of his remarks is available here.

Beyer’s remarks follow below:

“I am proud to represent Virginia’s Eighth Congressional District, home to Arlington National Cemetery and adjacent to the proposed location of this project on Columbia Island.

“In my time in Congress, I have never seen a project with such profound, widespread opposition from the very people who it will affect most.

“I therefore testify today as both the family member of parents, grandparents, and a sister buried at Arlington National Cemetery, and as another voice joining the many residents of Northern Virginia who have spoken out against this project.

“I have seen and heard their concerns, and I expect you to give them the same respect and consideration.

“To echo their sentiments, the proposed “Triumphal Arch” is a disgrace and an unnecessary danger to the area, for no other reason than to build a monument to the President’s ego.

“The evidence before you is overwhelming.

“Despite the Administration rushing this process through every step of the process, the National Park Service still found that it will harm dozens of nearby historic sites.

“That includes creating a permanent blight in the solemn viewshed of Arlington National Cemetery, turning our government’s back on the servicemembers buried there and their families.

“And erecting a 250-foot structure on a small island in the Potomac will not only affect irreplaceable historic sites.

“It will snarl traffic for years, impact the nearby airport, and present even more serious threats to public safety that this Commission has refused to acknowledge and grapple with.

“While the President has called for the project to be “converted” to a base for drones and snipers, that appears nowhere in this Commission’s consideration of the project.

“Apparently, placing a large weapons cache within feet of tourists, pedestrians, cyclists, Metro riders, and drivers commuting to work is not worth serious concern by a Commission tasked with region-wide planning.

“I can only conclude that by rubber-stamping the Arch without considering that position, this Commission is either calling the President a liar or knowingly moving forward with an incomplete and potentially-fraudulent application.

“That is only one of the many times the American people have been lied to at every step of this project.

“They have heard lies that this project was approved by Congress more than 100 years ago. It was not.

“Moving forward without Congressional authorization is a violation of Congress’s Constitutional authority, and that authorization has not been granted.

“The American people have also heard lies that the process would be transparent. It has not been.

“In September, I drove down to Columbia Island myself to find workers operating heavy equipment.

“They refused to answer whether that machinery was part of preparation for the Arch, despite a court-ordered requirement that notice be given ahead of any work.

“It’s time for the lies to stop, and for this sham process to end.

“I urge you to take your responsibilities seriously, and to resist political pressure to rubber-stamp this unjustified, harmful, and disgraceful project.”

Rep. Don Beyer is leading congressional efforts to block construction of Trump’s arch. His Northern Virginia district includes the Arlington National Cemetery, where his parents, grandparents, and sister are buried. He is the author of the Arlington National Cemetery Viewshed Protection Act, which would explicitly prohibit construction of the arch. He previously raised concerns about the projects impacts on traffic in the region, which the Trump Administration has yet to address. The arch has been a consistent source of anger and concern to Beyer’s constituents, who like much of the country, vociferously oppose the project.

title: Buchanan Honors Hometown Golf Champion Nelly Korda
text:
Celebrates the Accomplishments of Bradenton Native, Olympic Gold Medalist, 19-Time LPGA Tour Winner and U.S. Open Women’s Titlist Professional Women’s Golfer

WASHINGTON — Congressman Vern Buchanan joined the City of Bradenton for Nelly Korda Day, celebrating hometown native and professional golfer Nelly Korda. He presented her with a Congressional Record tribute honoring her achievements and an American flag flown over the U.S. Capitol in her honor.

“Nelly is not only the best women’s golfer in the world but also a shining example of everything that makes our community great,” said Buchanan. “My granddaughter is a golfer and Nelly is a true inspiration to her. She, like many others across southwest Florida, watch how Nelly competes, how she handles both victory and disappointment and how she carries herself on and off the course. It means so much for young athletes to see someone from their own backyard rise to the very top of the game. Nelly has brought tremendous pride to Bradenton and our nation, and I was honored to recognize her.”

Korda is an Olympic gold medalist and 19-time LPGA Tour winner. Her four major championships include the Chevron Championship and her first U.S. Women’s Open title this year. She won the first tournament of 2026 and returned to the top of the world rankings as the number one player in women’s golf. In September she represented the United States at the Solheim Cup in the Netherlands, where she and her teammate became the first pair ever to win five matches in a row together. Her 2024 season was one of the most impressive the sport has ever seen. She won seven tournaments that year, including a dramatic victory in front of a hometown crowd at the Bradenton Country Club. She was also named LPGA Tour Player of the Year.

Beyond the trophies, Korda has become a role model for young athletes across Manatee County. Young girls throughout the community now pick up a golf club believing they can become champions too, because someone from their own hometown has shown them the way.

You can read the Congressional Record HERE or below.

Mr. BUCHANAN. — Mr. Speaker, I rise today to honor Nelly Korda of Bradenton, Florida, one of the greatest golfers in the world, whose achievements have filled our hometown with pride.

Nelly was born in Bradenton on July 28, 1998, into a family that loves sports. Her father, Petr, was a champion tennis player who won the Australian Open, and her mother, Regina, played tennis at the Olympic Games. Her older sister, Jessica, is also a winner on the LPGA Tour, and her younger brother, Sebastian, is a professional tennis player. The Kordas could have lived anywhere in the world, but they chose Bradenton as their home, and our community has cheered for Nelly every step of the way.

Nelly turned professional in 2016 as a teenager and quickly showed the world what Bradenton already knew. In 2021, she won her first major championship and, that same summer, stood atop the podium at the Olympic Games in Tokyo with a gold medal for the United States. In 2024, she put together one of the most impressive seasons the sport has ever seen, winning seven tournaments and being named the LPGA Tour’s Player of the Year.

Her bond with Bradenton was on full display in January 2024, when a professional tournament came to Bradenton Country Club, just down the road from the hospital where she was born. Friends, family, and neighbors lined the course to cheer her on. Late on the final day, it looked as though the title might slip away, but Nelly fought back with two brilliant shots on the closing holes and went on to win in a dramatic finish. Afterward, she thanked the hometown crowd for staying positive and carrying her to victory. For one unforgettable week, the golf world turned its attention to our city, and Bradenton’s own daughter delivered.

Like every great athlete, Nelly has faced setbacks. In 2025, she went the entire season without a win. Rather than be discouraged, she went back to work, and in 2026 she came back stronger than ever. She won the very first tournament of the year and finished first or second in each of her first six events, something only one other woman in history had ever done. She went on to win the Chevron Championship and the U.S. Women’s Open, two of the most important events in women’s golf, and returned to her place as the number one player in the world. In September, she once again wore the colors of the United States at the Solheim Cup in the Netherlands, where she and her teammate made history as the first pair ever to win five matches in a row together.

Yet Nelly’s greatest gift to Bradenton may be the example she sets. Across Manatee County, young girls now pick up a golf club believing they, too, can become champions, because someone from their own hometown has shown them the way. Parents point to her as a model of hard work and perseverance, and whenever Nelly’s name appears in headlines around the world, the name of Bradenton travels right alongside it.

This tribute is personal for me as well. My own granddaughter is a golfer, and a very good one. Like so many young players in our community, she considers Nelly a true inspiration. She watches how Nelly competes, how she handles both victory and disappointment, and how she carries herself on and off the course. I have seen firsthand how much it means to a young athlete to watch someone from her own backyard rise to the very top of the game.

Through it all, Nelly has remained humble and gracious. She is quick to credit her family, her team, and the people who have supported her since she was a little girl. She represents the very best of our community: talent matched with determination, success matched with kindness, and a deep love for the place she calls home.

Mr. Speaker, on behalf of the people of Florida’s 16th Congressional District, I ask my colleagues to join me in congratulating Nelly Korda on her extraordinary achievements, in thanking her for the honor she has brought to the City of Bradenton and to our nation, and in wishing her many more years of success.

###

title: Budzinski Leads Bipartisan Postal Caucus in Pressing USPS for Answers on $19.5 Billion Borrowing Request
text:
SPRINGFIELD, IL – This week, Congresswoman Nikki Budzinski (IL-13) led 13 members of the Congressional Postal Service Caucus in sending a bipartisan letter to Postmaster General David Steiner seeking clear answers on how the U.S. Postal Service would use a requested $19.5 billion increase in its statutory borrowing authority. In the letter, the lawmakers ask the Postmaster General whether the increase in borrowing authority would be used to improve on-time delivery for the communities they represent, or to implement more of the network changes that have slowed mail service since 2023.

Earlier this year, the Postmaster General told the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee that increased borrowing authority is the “most immediate solution” to the Postal Service’s financial crisis. The Caucus says it is ready to work with USPS on common-sense solutions, but that Congress needs a full accounting before raising the borrowing limit from $15 billion to $34.5 billion.

The members wrote, “We have all seen service decline in our districts as a result of the network changes stemming from the Mail Processing Facility Review (MPFR) and Regional Transportation Optimization (RTO) and have concerns that granting a significant increase in the Postal Service’s borrowing limit would go towards continued investment in network changes that are not working for our constituents.”

They continued, “For those reasons, we are asking that the Postal Service provide both Member- and staff-level briefings during the November House of Representatives session period to discuss the Postal Service’s financial plans if Congress were to increase the Postal Service’s borrowing limit.”

title: Reps. Chu, Moore Reintroduce EITC Age Parity Act to Expand Tax Credit to Younger and Older Workers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Reps. Judy Chu (CA-28) and Gwen Moore (WI-04) reintroduced the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) Age Parity Act, which would eliminate age restrictions that currently prevent millions of young and older workers without children from claiming the EITC.

The EITC is one of our nation’s most effective anti-poverty tools. In 2024, it lifted 4.4 million people above the poverty line, including over two million children, and reduced the severity of poverty for more than 16 million Americans. But the credit excludes a crucial segment of the workforce. Unless you have a qualifying child, the EITC is only available to those between ages 25 and 64, leaving millions of younger and older works ineligible solely because of their age. The EITC Age Parity Act would solve this issue by eliminating the EITC’s upper age limit and expanding eligibility to workers as young as 18.

“The EITC is one of the most impactful and transformative anti-poverty tools we have at our disposal. Unfortunately, arbitrary age limits exclude millions of hardworking Americans who could benefit from it greatly,” said Rep. Chu. “Right now, a 23-year-old stocking shelves and a 66-year-old still working to make ends meet, neither with children at home, are shut out of the EITC for no reason other than their age. I’m proud to reintroduce the EITC Age Parity Act with Rep. Moore to lift more families out of poverty and put more money back in the pockets of millions of workers.”

“At a time when American families and workers are struggling with higher costs for just about everything, our tax laws should not be taxing workers into poverty. That is why I have long championed updates to the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC), one of our nation’s largest anti-poverty tools. While the American Rescue Plan Act made important changes to the EITC, including allowing younger and older adults without children to benefit from this refundable credit, those temporary changes expired, depriving some of our most vulnerable workers of critical assistance. The EITC Age Parity Act would permanently allow younger and older workers to benefit from the EITC, a crucial first step in ensuring that our tax code can better serve all our workers,” said Rep. Moore.

“We applaud the leadership of Rep. Chu and Rep. Moore on behalf of the EITC Age Parity Act to permanently eliminate age restrictions that prevent young and older workers from claiming the EITC,” said Amy Everitt, President of Golden State Opportunity. “This invaluable tax credit boosts workforce participation and sparks local economic growth. Yet, we need to make sure our policies better serve the workers who have been left behind by our best policies. With the cost of living rising, every worker needs every dollar they have already earned.”

The bill is cosponsored by Reps. Gwen Moore (WI-04), Dwight Evans (PA-03), Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-At Large), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), and Valerie Foushee (NC-04).

The bill is endorsed by Golden State Opportunity (GSO).

title: Lone Star in the Capital: Doggett, Daughters of the Republic of Texas Unveil Base of Republic of Texas Legation Memorial
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Lloyd Doggett (D-TX), Assistant Secretary of the Interior for Fish and Wildlife and Parks Kevin Lilly, a fellow Texan, and the Elisabet Ney Chapter of the Daughters of the Republic of Texas unveiled the Lone Star base of the Republic of Texas Legation Memorial at 630 Indiana Avenue NW, adjacent to its intersection with Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington, D.C. The memorial was approved by Congress in legislation authored by Doggett, the Republic of Texas Legation Memorial Act. It memorializes the Texans who worked for almost a decade to negotiate the admission of Texas into the United States as the 28th state.

Congressman Lloyd Doggett (fourth from right) with Assistant Secretary of the Interior Kevin Lilly, Priscilla Roberts, Kitty Hoeck, Grace Boatright, members of the Elisabet Ney Chapter of the Daughters of the Republic of Texas and National Park Service staff at the ceremony marking the start of construction of the Republic of Texas Legation Memorial on Indiana Avenue NW, November 5, 2026.

The Lone Star base, a five-pointed star of white Mount Airy granite, sits in an existing granite planter on the 600 block of Indiana Avenue NW, steps from the U.S. Navy Memorial. Today’s unveiling marks the start of construction of the memorial. The site sits among five of the eight places where, according to research by the Daughters of the Republic of Texas, the Legation’s diplomats lived and worked out of boarding houses and hotels, including the site of today’s Navy Memorial, where Texas Minister Memucan Hunt resided in 1837 and 1838.

“As a native Texan with more pride in our State after the recent election than ever before, I am pleased that this new monument recognizes an important part of our Texas heritage," said Congressman Doggett. “For almost a decade, eight different Texans conducted negotiations for the admission of Texas into the United States as the 28th state. This will likely become another point of interest especially for Texas visitors to our capital.”

“When tourists come to our Nation’s capital, they are likely unaware of an important piece of Texas lore that hides in plain sight: the lost landmarks of the Republic of Texas Legation in Washington,” he continued. “Its diplomats were sent on the very long and difficult journey from Texas to Washington, and Americans traveling in Europe can find plaques in both London and Paris that commemorate the Texas Legation. Washington had not followed suit. Most appropriately, this work has been spearheaded by the Daughters of the Republic of Texas, our State’s oldest patriotic women’s organization, and Kitty Hoeck has led the way, proving that one person can make a difference with their tenacity and determination.”

“The history of the Texas Legation did not end with the annexation of Texas in 1845. Today, it lives on through the strength of the multicultural and multilingual communities that make our Lone Star State so dynamic,” shared the Congressman. “With this memorial, all those who visit our Nation’s Capital will have the opportunity to learn about this turning point in our Nation’s history and reflect on the sacrifices made by the brave diplomats who made it possible. Because Texas history is America’s history.”

About the memorial

Modest in scale, the memorial will rise from the Lone Star base unveiled today: a five-sided plinth of white granite topped by the Daughters of the Republic of Texas medallion and engraved with the story of the Texas Legation, a map of the Republic of Texas and the names of the eight diplomats the Republic sent to Washington. Plantings native to Texas and the Mid-Atlantic will surround a single sweetbay magnolia, representing the Lone Star State. The site is federal land under the National Park Service.

Background

From 1836 to 1845, the Republic of Texas kept a diplomatic legation in Washington, working first for U.S. recognition and then for annexation; Texas became the 28th state on December 29, 1845. Doggett introduced the Republic of Texas Legation Memorial Act (H.R. 3349) in June 2019. It passed the House and Senate with bipartisan support and was signed into law on December 22, 2020. The Daughters then won final approval of the site and design from the U.S. Commission of Fine Arts and the National Capital Planning Commission in 2025 and raised the full cost privately; the law bars federal funds to build the memorial.

###

title: Rep. Foster Unveils Discussion Draft of Legislation to Modernize Financial Regulatory Reporting and Strengthen Oversight of the Financial System
text:
Financial services driven by artificial intelligence and round-the-clock payments systems may contribute to and rapidly spread financial stress. As the financial system accelerates, real-time information and automated tools can help institutions and regulators respond faster, improve access to liquidity, and better prepare for orderly bank resolutions. Meanwhile, advances in AI are creating new cybersecurity threats. Through enhanced collective maintenance and security built in from the start, open-source software can provide stronger protection against cyber threats. Model open-source software also has the potential to lower development and reporting costs for community banks and credit unions and expand their access to advanced risk-management capabilities.

The Real-Time Regulatory Study Act directs the Federal Reserve Board, in coordination with other financial regulators, to develop, test, and publicly release open-source demonstration software to evaluate how technology can streamline regulatory obligations, reduce compliance costs, and provide regulators with real-time information on the condition of financial institutions nationwide. The Federal Reserve would seek technical contributions from financial institutions, technology providers, open-source organizations, and researchers.
