title: Bennet Announces Support for Colorado Bid to Host the U.S. Space Academy
text:
State initiative has support from bipartisan Colorado federal delegation, higher education, and aerospace business leaders

Denver— Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, a member of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, announced his support for Colorado’s bid to host the proposed United States Space Academy, led by NASA. Governor Jared Polis recently announced an advisory committee to support the state’s effort. This committee will bring together leaders committed to showcasing Colorado’s strengths as the home for the next generation of American space leaders.

“Colorado’s world-class aerospace industry, top tier universities, and critical space installations make our state uniquely qualified to host the new Space Academy,” said Bennet. “As China and Russia race to eclipse our leadership in space, training the next generation of space professionals is of the utmost importance. There is no better place to do so than in Colorado.”

“Colorado is the best place for the next generation of astronauts, scientists, engineers, and space entrepreneurs. Bringing the U.S. Space Academy here would open new doors for students and strengthen the workforce powering America’s future in space. I’m grateful to the advisory committee members and leaders for coming together to help ensure Colorado submits the most stellar proposal possible,” said Polis.

“Coloradans across our state share a passion for space. It’s woven into our identity. Colorado is already home to an unrivaled space ecosystem, including world-class universities and cutting edge research laboratories, leading aerospace companies, critical military installations and units, and a workforce that has helped power America’s space missions for decades. I’m proud to chair this advisory committee and show why Colorado is the best place for the U.S. Space Academy,” said Lt. Governor Primavera.

“If the administration is determined to build a U.S. Space Academy, there is no question it should be based in Colorado. Other states would be starting from scratch. We’re not,” said Senator John Hickenlooper. “We’re home to leading universities, the nation’s largest space economy per capita, and more Space Force Deltas than any other state. When it comes to training tomorrow’s space leaders, Colorado has already shown there’s nowhere better.”

“Colorado is already a hub for aerospace innovation, space weather forecasting, and scientific research, with people across our state making groundbreaking advancements that will shape the next frontier of this industry. Our world-class universities and research institutions, along with the students and researchers who power them, make Colorado well-equipped to welcome the United States Space Academy. I’m confident we’re up to the task and look forward to working with state and local leaders to make the case for bringing the Academy to Colorado,” said Representative Joe Neguse.

“Colorado has the talent, institutions, and innovative spirit to lead the next generation of American space exploration. From our world-class aerospace industry and military installations to our universities, community colleges, and skilled workforce, we have the foundation to make the United States Space Academy a success. Bringing the Academy to Colorado would strengthen our national security, create new opportunities for students and workers across our state, and help ensure America remains the global leader in space. This is an opportunity for Colorado to come together, across party lines and across regions, to advance a mission that benefits our entire country. I strongly support Colorado’s bid and look forward to working with state, local, and federal partners to bring the Academy here,” said Representative Jeff Hurd.

“I’m proud to support Colorado’s bid for the United States Space Academy. It would create high-quality jobs, strengthen our Space Force pipeline, and build on the Air Force Academy and existing space military installations already here. This is a smart step for Colorado’s economy and America’s national security, and I’ll keep working with colleagues on both sides of the aisle and the Trump Administration to advance it,” said Representative Lauren Boebert.

“Colorado Springs has been the cornerstone of America’s national security space mission for decades,” said Representative Jeff Crank. “With the combination of our space assets, academic institutions and skilled workforce, the U.S. Space Academy is a natural fit for our community.”

“Colorado has a strong space tradition rooted in our workforce, universities, and installations like Buckley Space Force Base. Establishing the Space Force Academy in Colorado would offer future cadets unparalleled access to our state’s leading aerospace ecosystem, providing world-class training opportunities. Our state is the perfect place for future Guardians, leaders in the aerospace industry, and NASA employees as they help make sure America remains a leader in space,” said Representative Jason Crow.

“Colorado has always stood at the forefront of space innovation, which is why there is no better place to house NASA’s new Space Academy. Our state is home to leading aerospace innovators and cutting-edge research institutions like the Colorado School of Mines, CU Boulder, and UCCS. Coloradans have been at the heart of NASA’s work, including the most recent Artemis mission to the Moon,” said Representative Brittany Pettersen. “Colorado has already laid the groundwork to support the next generation of astronauts, engineers, and scientists. With Colorado’s aerospace industry growing by 88% in the past two decades, our state is perfectly positioned to be home to NASA’s Space Academy.”

“Colorado has long been the heart and soul of America’s leadership in space. Our state is blessed with innovative companies and a talented workforce ready to continue building our future beyond low earth orbit. Colorado would be a natural fit for the United States Space Academy, and I look forward to supporting the state’s efforts to make that case to the Trump administration,” said Representative Gabe Evans.

Bennet continues to fight to ensure Colorado’s leadership across the aerospace ecosystem. As part of the Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act, he helped secure nearly $300 million in authorizations for Colorado’s military installations and over $600 million in authorizations for Colorado defense and aerospace industry investments. Earlier this year, Bennet fought for and ultimately celebrated the reassignment of 393 Air National Guard (ANG) members with the 233rd Space Group stationed at Greeley’s ANG Station. Bennet also supported Arapahoe Community College’s Colorado Space Institute successful bid to become a NASA State Hub and congratulated their selection in August 2026.

title: Cortez Masto Joins Bipartisan Demand for Census Bureau to Rescind Proposed Rule That Violates Constitution
text:
Las Vegas, Nev. – U.S. Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) joined Senators Gary Peters (D-Mich.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), and a bipartisan group of 23 Senators in urging the U.S. Census Bureau to rescind a proposed rule that would exclude certain non-citizens from census counts and eliminate questions on race and ethnicity. In their letter, the Senators warn that the exclusion of non-citizens violates the Constitution, which expressly says that the census must count the “whole number of persons in each state.”

The Senators note that both proposed methods to exclude non-citizens would cause undercounts and errors in the census counts: “We write to urge that you rescind your proposed rule that would exclude certain non-citizens from decennial census counts and omit questions about race and ethnicity from the decennial census. The proposed rule violates the clear meaning of the Constitution, which requires that the Census Bureau count the ‘whole number of persons in each state.’ The proposed rule would also cause communities across the country to be counted inaccurately, jeopardizing their fair representation in Congress and access to billions of federal dollars for education, health care, and public safety services.”

The letter also describes how the Bureau’s proposal to eliminate race and ethnicity questions would undermine the enforcement of civil and voting rights laws and would degrade the quality of all census data. The compliance of civil and voting rights laws rely on demographic data, and only the decennial census provides accurate and precise data. Additionally, eliminating the collection of race and ethnicity data from the decennial census undermines other federal survey data. Businesses and local governments that depend on this data have said that they would be harmed by this proposed rule.

“In its attempt to undermine the data used for the enforcement of civil and voting rights laws, the Bureau will degrade the accuracy of all other federal survey data, particularly for small and rural geographic areas. The Bureau writes in its own regulatory filing that the proposed rule ‘deteriorates the accuracy’ of ‘fertility/mortality rates, cancer rates, poverty rates, unemployment rates, [and] labor force participation’ because the Bureau relies on accurate decennial census information to adjust and design other survey estimates,” the Senators continued. “The Bureau also admits in its filing that the proposal would hamper the usability of data for state and local governments who rely on precise and accurate population estimates for small geographic areas. Businesses and local governments that depend on reliable and complete federal data have warned that the Census Bureau’s proposal would increase costs as data is degraded.”

Read the full letter here. title: Cramer Hosts HHS Secretary Kennedy in Bismarck for Regenerative Agriculture, Tribal Health Discussions
text:
***Clickherefor media resources.***

BISMARCK, N.D. – U.S. Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND) hosted U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., in the Bismarck area for a series of discussions on regenerative agriculture and healthcare access in tribal communities. U.S. Secretary of the Interior (DOI) Doug Burgum joined both the agricultural and tribal meetings, bringing two Cabinet officials to North Dakota.

Cramer and Kennedy kicked off the visit with a roundtable at Black Leg Ranch in McKenzie, centered on regenerative agriculture. This holistic, principles-based approach to farming and land management uses alternative methods of restoring soil health, increasing biodiversity, and improving the water cycle.

Black Leg Ranch is a leader in regenerative agriculture, managing its grasslands through planned rotational grazing that incorporates high animal impact over short periods, followed by extended recovery periods. The ranch also uses cover crops to enhance soil biology and support its no-till farming practices. It has been using regenerative agriculture practices even before the term became widely known, making it an ideal setting for the conversation.

“We had a wonderful morning out at Black Leg Ranch and had a great discussion on regenerative agriculture,” said Cramer. “North Dakota farmers have been doing regenerative agriculture since before it had a name—which is why they are inspiring others to follow in their footsteps. But the really important thing today is less about us and more about the people that are participating in these events. It was also a good opportunity for North Dakota producers to demonstrate what they do best as the most responsible stewards of the land, highlighting the latest soil and human health research being conducted in our state. These conversations showcased North Dakota’s excellence and offered direct access to leaders in the administration.”

The visit also included a roundtable on healthcare in North Dakota’s tribal communities. Cramer, Kennedy, Burgum, Indian Health Service (IHS) Director Mark Cruz, DOI Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs Billy Kirkland, and tribal representatives participated in the discussion at United Tribes Technical College.

Kennedy shared his lifelong commitment to improving healthcare services in tribal communities, describing how his passion was shaped by traveling with his father. He highlighted several of the agency’s accomplishments, including pledging $1 billion toward addressing the IHS facilities backlog. The investment is aimed at modernizing aging and deteriorating healthcare infrastructure across tribal communities. He also announced the expansion of the Make Hospital Food Healthier Pledge to IHS facilities, an effort to increase access to healthier ingredients and whole foods that support patient recovery and overall health.

The conversation provided tribal leaders with an opportunity to raise their priorities and discuss solutions with federal officials. Topics included the need for enhanced behavioral health services, economic growth, the construction and modernization of IHS healthcare facilities, and opportunities to partner with tribes on chronic disease prevention and other healthcare issues, including diabetes and substance abuse.

title: Durbin Releases GAO Report Raising Alarms Over Changes In Inspections In ICE Immigration Detention Facilities
text:
Due to the failed inspections, ICE facilities have provided inadequate medical care, unsafe food, and failures in suicide prevention

SPRINGFIELD – Today, U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, led the release of the Government Accountability Office’s (GAO) newly-completed report examining the Trump Administration’s decision to cut U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) inspection requirements of immigration detention facilities. These cuts stand in stark contrast to a massive surge in immigration detention. From April 2025 to April 2026, the average daily detained population jumped by more than 50 percent as active facilities expanded from 128 to 172. This growth was fueled by an explosion in funding, with ICE receiving over $45 billion for immigration detention in those two years alone.

With fewer inspections, there is even less accountability for ICE and its contractors, including widely documented failures to provide adequate medical care and safe and edible food and to prevent suicides. The GAO report is released after Durbin called for the GAO to expand its pending investigation of mental health care to include medical care and mismanagement of federal contracts in ICE detention facilities.

In the report, GAO outlines how detention oversight has been gutted during the second Trump Administration. The GAO examined four Department of Homeland Security (DHS) offices charged with inspecting detention facilities. The DHS Office of the Immigration Detention Ombudsman (OIDO), an independent office with statutory authority to conduct surprise inspections, has been shut down entirely. ICE’s Office of Detention Oversight (ODO) office has decreased its inspections following policy changes under this Administration—it went from inspecting larger facilities twice a year to once a year or less. Its total inspections dropped from 194 to 102 in one year. DHS now allows many smaller facilities to inspect themselves and usually tells facilities in advance when inspectors are coming. ICE justified these changes by stating few inspections would ease the obligations on facilities and would make it easier to contract with local and state partners to detain individuals. ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), which inspects medical care in detention, has kept its process the same. The DHS Office of Inspector General (OIG) received $20 million for extra inspections.

Consistent with this Administration’s irresponsible and cruel approach to immigration policy, the GAO found ICE’s changes to detention inspections were not backed by data. ICE failed to analyze evidence, such as past inspection deficiencies or contract compliance, to assess how ICE can adequately conduct oversight over its rapidly growing detention facilities and ensure facilities comply with detention standards.

“On Tuesday, the American people overwhelmingly rejected the Trump Administration’s cruel immigration tactics—including inhumane ICE detention facilities, where people lack adequate access to food, water, and medical care,” said Durbin. “Now that the power has shifted in Congress, the Trump Administration should take immediate steps to respond to this new alarming GAO report, which found ICE has reduced inspections without assessing the impact on detained individuals.”

In the report, GAO also noted that another accountability measure recently lapsed. Since Fiscal Year 2019, appropriations language barred funding a contract with a facility after two consecutive less-than-adequate ODO ratings. That provision was left out of the FY26 DHS Appropriations Act. ICE told GAO that failing ratings now will no longer block continued funding, allowing private prison contractors like GEO and CoreCivic to fail inspections by ODO with no consequences.

In the report, GAO urges ICE to use real data to determine whether the reduced inspections are enough to keep facilities safe and compliant, and adjust its inspections based on what it finds.

A copy of the final report can be found here.

title: Gillibrand Underscores Democrats’ Commitment To Lower Costs, End Iran War, Hold Trump Accountable On NPR’s Morning Edition
text:
Gillibrand: “Our Goal Is To Meet The Needs Of The American People. We Are Going To Focus Laser-Like On Getting Their Costs Down.”

***Hear Senator Gillibrand’s Full Interview Here***

Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand appeared on NPR’s Morning Edition to discuss Democrats’ historic sweep of the midterm elections and their plan to deliver for the American people with their newfound majorities.

She highlighted Democrats’ focus on lowering costs for American families, including by ending the Iran war, undoing President Trump’s tariffs, and restoring access to healthcare, as well as holding the president accountable for his corruption and his prioritization of vanity projects over the wellbeing of American families.

Senator Gillibrand also addressed the president’s threats to veto commonsense legislation head on:

“[President Trump]’s got his little veto cap. But as you’ve seen, he’s much more focused on the Reflecting Pool and his ballroom than anything else right now. So I don’t know what to expect out of this president. But if we have a bill that is bipartisan to restore healthcare for the people who lost their Medicaid or improve access to affordable medicines and other things, like, I dare him to veto that.”

Listen to Senator Gillibrand’s interview with NPR here. Full transcript of Senator Gillibrand’s interview below:

A MARTÍNEZ: For more about what’s next for Democrats in Congress, New York Senator Kirsten Gillibrand joins us now. She chairs the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. Senator, on its website, the DSCC says its purpose is electing a Democratic Senate through organizing, fundraising, and candidate recruitment. It sounds like you went three for three there. What did you see after the 2024 elections that set you up for the results you got in 2026?

SENATOR GILLIBRAND: Well, I knew that the climate that President Trump was going to create would be toxic. And he just continued to double down on things the American people didn’t want. He promised no forever wars, but he got us headlong into Iran. He promised he’d get costs down for groceries and housing and energy costs, and they continue to rise because of his war in Iran and his chaotic tariffs. And his disregard for the American people just kept growing. And so with talented candidates running all across the country, they were able to have a conversation with the American people about what they want. They want groceries to be affordable. They want to be able to afford to live where they want to live. They want to be able to get healthcare for their children and families. And when President Trump goes around canceling Medicaid for families and getting rid of food stamps for families who are struggling just to feed their children, that’s the kind of actions by the president and this administration that made the climate so favorable for these inspiring candidates that then just went to the voters and talked about their vision for America and what they want to get done for the American people.

MARTÍNEZ: So it sounds like, Senator, maybe you weren’t so surprised over the margin of victory.

GILLIBRAND: Well, I was hoping we’d win four. I really didn’t imagine we’d be winning eight or nine seats. We are now up to win nine Senate seats. All of our expansion states and all of the opportunities in these red and purple states came to fruition because these candidates were so transformational. A lot of them are the next generation, a lot of them are very authentic to their states. You look at Mary Peltola who ran on fish, family, and freedom. You look at somebody like Scott Colom, who’s a local DA in red, red Mississippi, really taking it to his community about his vision for his community and what he wants to do to bring down costs and provide opportunity for those families. Those candidacies resonated, and that is why we are seeing unbelievable returns in states that Democrats haven’t had for decades.

MARTÍNEZ: So with control in the House and the Senate, will Democrats try to impeach President Trump again?

GILLIBRAND: Well, our goal is to meet the needs of the American people. We are going to focus laser-like on getting their costs down. We have to end this war in Iran, which is driving up fuel and diesel, and every supply chain problem that’s driving up costs for everything. We have to deal with these chaotic tariffs and get them down because they’re driving up food costs and housing costs and everyday goods costs. And we have to restore access to healthcare. People literally lost – millions of Americans lost their healthcare. So we need to make sure Medicare and Medicaid are strengthened. We need to improve people’s healthcare. Our healthcare system in America isn’t that great. And so we need to make sure people can get hearing and dental and be able to actually get the medicines that their doctors prescribe without breaking the bank. And so good healthcare, cheaper healthcare, better healthcare are all priorities.

MARTÍNEZ: We hear candidates, though, talk about holding the Trump administration accountable. So what if that’s what the people want, too? They want you to kind of, walk and chew gum at the same time.

GILLIBRAND: We do want to hold the administration accountable. Yeah, no, we can do both. And one thing we could do is ban stock trading. We could say members of Congress, the administration, senior cabinet officials cannot be buying and selling stocks or cryptocurrency or anything else based on inside information and lining their own pockets. The amount of corruption in Washington, particularly around this president, is the highest I’ve ever seen. It is so incredible how much pay to play, how much fraud and corruption is within this White House. And so people don’t understand how the president has this unlimited money for his ballrooms and unlimited money for his billionaire buddies, but they don’t have enough money to pay for healthcare or to get costs for groceries down. And so they want this focus that they have to make America better for them, and don’t allow this administration continually put their own preferences and their own wealth in front of the American people. That’s the part of corruption that is infuriating voters, because they’re watching this president, like, focus on his ballroom and his triumphal arch and his airplane and not focus on their lives and allowing their children to get the healthcare they need to survive and thrive. And so it’s a choice that’s being made. And that’s what they’re so angry about. So you have to do accountability of the administration, but deliver for the American people at the same time.

MARTÍNEZ: The reason I asked that is because I was wondering what Democratic priorities would be. So let’s hear from Texas Senator-elect James Talarico on CNN.

TALARICO: I think our top priority has to be delivering for the people of Texas, for the people of this country. They didn’t send us to Washington for political retribution. They sent us to Washington to lower costs, to root out corruption, to get this economy back on track. And that needs to be our focus.

MARTÍNEZ: So Senator, it sounds like you agree with him, at least a little bit on this.

GILLIBRAND: Oh, I do.

MARTÍNEZ: But how do you square that sentiment with maybe a part of the party that might say, ‘Hey, lawyer up,’ like California Congressman Robert Garcia, that’s his two-word statement. He’s gonna be House Oversight and Government Reform Committee chair.

GILLIBRAND: Well, that’s one of his jobs. He’s the head of that committee. And so people want to see that the rules of the road are real. This president has broken the Constitution, the norms, every type of law you can imagine. And people feel deeply uncomfortable that you’ve broken the country in a way that isn’t fixable. So part of our job is to begin to restore order and restore all the things that President Trump has undermined. Like, he’s cut access to healthcare, to Medicaid. He has cut access to food stamps. He’s cut NIH funding. Like, things that go into the community to help the people survive, to give them the healthcare they need, to make sure there’s resources for food and housing. So they want things fixed, and they want things that have harmed them to be reversed. And so we need to double down on providing for the American people. Just as James Talarico has said, they’re expecting that we get their costs down. They’re expecting that we make sure people have healthcare. So those are must-dos. Part of how you deliver that is holding them accountable.

MARTÍNEZ: How do you do that if President Trump becomes Mr. Veto, as he has previewed?

GILLIBRAND: Yeah, so he’s threatened to be Mr. Veto. He’s got his little veto cap. But as you’ve seen, he’s much more focused on the Reflecting Pool and his ballroom than anything else right now. So I don’t know what to expect out of this president. But if we have a bill that is bipartisan to restore healthcare for the people who lost their Medicaid or improve access to affordable medicines and other things, like, I dare him to veto that. I dare him to stand in front of the American people and say, ‘You don’t deserve access to healthcare.’ So, if he decides to veto the commonsense things that get groceries down or housing prices down, then ‘28’s gonna be very favorable for Democrats.

title: Source New Mexico: New analyses contend New Mexico US Sen. Heinrich’s permitting bill would cut emissions, costs
text:
New analyses of a permitting reform bill U.S. Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) has championed say that its provisions would reduce emissions and costs to ratepayers, as well as recover billions of dollars from data center developers.

The analyses, released separately in recent days by four independent nonprofit and industry groups, including the Center for Climate and Energy Solutions, modeled what would happen to energy transmission and green energy production with and without Heinrich’s Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act in effect through 2040.

They found that the bill would lower household electricity bills by $50 to $78 annually by 2040. Moreover, it would reduce power sector emissions by about 20%, which would subsequently help prevent approximately 6,700 deaths and save $54 billion in cumulative public health costs.

Heinrich, the ranking member of the U.S. Senate’s Energy and Natural Resources Committee, announced the proposal along with Chair U.S. Sen. Mike Lee (R-Utah) and other bipartisan senators in recent weeks. He has touted the bill as a way to reform the federal permit review process to reduce delays and give renewable energy developers more certainty and quicker reviews, as well as a way to ensure data center developers don’t pass energy costs onto nearby households.

The bill has received backlash from tribal and environmentalist groups concerned it will fast-track fossil fuel production and reduce tribal input on sensitive developments. Last week, protesters from the YUCCA Alliance railed against the bill outside Heinrich’s downtown Albuquerque office.

But Heinrich has maintained the bill will prevent vital carbon-free energy and transmission projects from facing years of regulatory delays. His office has pointed to the analyses as proof the bill is necessary to achieve climate goals.

“Americans are tired of paying more in utility bills while projects that could lower costs sit stuck in the planning phase for years,” Heinrich said in a statement touting the outside reviews. “These independent analyses show exactly what we stand to gain by fixing our broken permitting system: lower electricity bills, cleaner air, healthier communities, and more reliable energy infrastructure.”

One of those reviews, released Thursday by the nonpartisan Center for Climate and Energy Solutions thinktank, found that passing the bill would reduce annual electricity bills by $2.5 billion by 2035, partially by reducing the queue that power plants, energy storage facilities and energy storage projects idle in before getting approval to connect to the grid.

“It takes years for projects to connect to the grid and be able to deliver that energy,” the center’s president, Nat Keohane, said during a virtual news conference. “When demand is growing and supply can’t keep up, costs go up.”

A separate analysis from Grid Strategies, a power sector consulting firm, evaluated provisions in the 417-page bill related to data centers. The bill would require electrical utilities to impose additional costs on data centers, funding that utilities would then use to reduce transmission costs to ratepayers.

In total, Grid Strategies estimates that data centers would pay $55 billion to utilities over the next decade if the bill goes into effect, a figure that represents an additional $35 billion more than they would pay under existing policy.

Heinrich and his cosponsors have announced they intend to try to shepherd the bill through both chambers of Congress before the next session begins next year. U.S. Rep. Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.) announced last week that she does not support the bill as written.

The bill sponsors’ push to pass the bill in 2026 has drawn additional criticism from the bill’s skeptics, who argue Democrats’ new majorities in the U.S. Senate and U.S. House in Tuesday’s election means a better bill can be achieved.

Moreover, in January, Heinrich may take over as chair of the U.S. Senate’s Energy and Natural Resources Committee, giving him even more power over the bill’s provisions.

However, in an emailed statement Thursday provided to Source NM, Heinrich said he still thinks the climate and country can’t wait any longer to pass the permitting reform bill. He said if he becomes committee chair that his priorities will be reducing energy costs for New Mexicans and protecting public lands, including in Chaco Canyon and the Pecos River.

“But our priority right now is passing the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, which would make it illegal for data centers to shift the costs of their grid upgrades and infrastructure onto consumers,” he said. “We’ve been working toward permitting reform for the better part of a decade, and this is the closest we’ve come to getting something signed into law. I’m not going to wait, and I’ll negotiate in good faith, whether I’m the Chair or the Ranking Member.”

title: FACT SHEET: Heinrich Details How Bipartisan American Affordability & Jobs Act Holds Data Centers Accountable, Lowers Utility Bills for American Families
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, released a fact sheet detailing how his Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will hold data centers accountable, forcing them to pay for grid upgrades instead of passing costs onto electricity customers, helping to lower utility bills for working families.

Heinrich’s fact sheet can be found here and below.

Bipartisan American Affordability & Jobs Act

Making sure data centers pay for their grid costs, lowering utility bills for families

Large data centers can require as much electricity as a small city. When a data center connects to the grid, the utility may need to add or upgrade transmission infrastructure to serve that new demand. If those costs are not assigned to the data center, they can ultimately be reflected in electricity rates paid by other customers. A Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas working paper estimates that data center demand has already pushed up wholesale electricity prices 6.9% nationally, a number that it projects could increase to 12.3% by 2028.

What The Bill Does:

Requires data centers to pay the costs they create. The bill directs the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to require utilities to establish rates that force large data centers to pay for both the cost of serving them and the grid upgrades needed to handle them. This means the cost of accommodating a new data center does not fall on other electricity customers.

Ends a current barrier to charging data centers for grid upgrades. Current FERC policy generally prevents utilities from charging customers for both their share of existing grid costs and the additional grid upgrades needed to serve that customer. The bill directs FERC to change that policy to ensure that large data centers pay for both. If a data center needs the grid to be expanded or upgraded to power its operations, utilities must charge customers serving that data center for those costs on top of the regular cost of electricity. The bill makes these charges mandatory—not voluntary—ultimately driving down costs for consumers.

Gives states a way to reduce costs for families and businesses. States can use the revenue collected from data centers to reduce electricity rates for homes, small businesses, and other existing electricity customers.

Requires the reporting of information on data center energy usage. Requires the Energy Information Administration to update its annual survey to require utilities to report electricity sales to data centers—which utilities currently report for residential, commercial, and industrial sectors, but not for data centers.

title: Hickenlooper, Bennet, Hurd Tour Flooding in San Luis Valley
text:
GUADALUPE – Today, U.S. Senators John Hickenlooper and Michael Bennet and Representative Jeff Hurd toured flood-damaged areas of the San Luis Valley. The lawmakers made stops in Guadalupe and South Fork to survey extensive damage to homes, businesses, and infrastructure and hear directly from local leaders about ongoing recovery needs.

The visit follows a letter sent Wednesday by the lawmakers and the entire Colorado congressional delegation urging President Trump to swiftly approve Governor Jared Polis’ request for an expedited Major Disaster Declaration following historic flooding and debris flows across Southwestern Colorado and the San Luis Valley.

Watch Hickenlooper’s Video From South Fork, CO

“The damage we saw today is almost hard to fathom. Many of these same communities are still reeling from last fall’s floods, and now they’ve been hit again,” said Hickenlooper. “We’re grateful to the emergency management teams and first responders who are keeping people safe. We’ve also been checking in with leaders across the Southwest region to understand their recovery needs. We’ll do everything we can to coordinate with the State and our federal partners to ensure these communities get the resources they deserve as quickly as possible.”

The Governor’s request seeks Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Public Assistance and Hazard Mitigation Grant Program funding for Archuleta and Rio Grande Counties, where state and federal officials have already validated nearly $27 million in eligible damages. The flooding also impacted Alamosa, Conejos, Dolores, Hinsdale, La Plata, Mineral, Montezuma, Ouray, San Juan, and San Miguel Counties, where damage assessments continue and additional requests for federal assistance are expected.

In late October and early November, severe storms brought devastating flooding and debris flows to Southwestern Colorado, damaging roads, bridges, utilities, homes, and businesses, and cutting off access to entire communities. Preliminary assessments for Archuleta and Rio Grande Counties have identified approximately $10.6 million in damage to local roads, bridges, and culverts; $2.44 million in damage to public utilities; and $8.59 million in damage to parks and recreation facilities. These figures do not include additional damage assessments underway or separate federal highway repair costs.

title: Hoeven Discusses Efforts to Advance Regenerative Agriculture with HHS & Interior Secretaries
text:
MCKENZIE, N.D. – Senator John Hoeven today joined a meeting hosted by Senator Kevin Cramer with U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. and U.S. Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum at Black Leg Ranch. Hoeven discussed efforts to support regenerative agriculture practices to improve soil and water quality, stressing the importance of voluntary, farmer-friendly conservation programs. To this end, Hoeven outlined the following priorities he is working to advance through his roles as chairman of the Senate Agriculture Appropriations Committee and a senior member of the Senate Agriculture Committee:

Hoeven-authored provisions he has included in the Senate Farm Bill 2.0:

The SCALE Act – Provides matching grants to support state-led soil health and wildlife habitat programs, like Governor Armstrong’s Legacy Soil Health and Habitat Program.

Joint Chiefs Program – Reauthorizes the program, which has provided more than $3.2 million for partnerships with private landowners to help improve and restore grasslands in North Dakota.

Programs like the Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP), Conservation Stewardship Program (CSP), Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) and Regional Conservation Partnership Program (RCPP).

Agriculture research, including projects focused on improving soil health and grazing and rangeland management that are being undertaken by the Agricultural Research Service’s (ARS) Northern Great Plains Research Laboratory in Mandan.

“Our farmers and ranchers know the importance of maintaining the quality of their soil and water, and we’re working to empower them to do just that. Importantly, these efforts need to be voluntary and farmer-friendly, rather than one-size-fits-all mandates. I appreciate Secretary Kennedy for his willingness to hear from our producers firsthand about the practices that work best for them. This is about supporting the long-term profitability of our producers and ensuring Americans continue to have access to the highest-quality, lowest-cost food supply in the world,” said Senator Hoeven.

Hoeven also discussed efforts important to livestock producers to better help them manage their risk, strengthen domestic U.S. beef production and support grazing access on federal lands. These include:

Strengthening the farm safety net for cattle producers by providing additional livestock insurance options that operate similar to the crop insurance program available to farmers.

Preventing prairie dog colonies from expanding beyond reasonable levels.

Hoeven’s provision in the Farm Bill amends prairie dog management plans for the Dakota Prairie Grasslands to limit prairie dog habitat to no more than 1.5 percent of any single grazing allotment and establish a 1-mile buffer along adjacent state and private lands.

Enhance the risk management tools and disaster assistance available to ranchers, such as the Livestock Indemnity Program (LIP) and the Emergency Assistance for Livestock, Honeybees and Farm Raised Fish Program (ELAP).

These provisions build on measures Hoeven worked to pass as part of the Working Families Tax Cut Act to expand LIP payment coverage and improve assistance through the Livestock Forage Program (LFP) for ranchers impacted by drought.

Improving access to the national grasslands for grazers, including by supporting efforts to revise the Travel Management Plan (TMP) for the Little Missouri Grasslands to make section line rights-of-way available.

title: Kelly, Gallego Announce $9.6 Million to Improve Railroad Crossing Safety Across Arizona
text:
Federal funding will support railroad crossing safety projects in Marana, Yuma County, and Phoenix

Today, Arizona Senators Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego announced $9.6 million in federal funding for three projects to improve railroad crossing safety in Marana, Yuma County, and Phoenix. The funding will support planning and design work to address dangerous railroad crossings, reduce traffic delays, and improve the movement of people and goods across Arizona.

The funding was awarded through the Railroad Crossing Elimination (RCE) Grant Program, established by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which Kelly helped negotiate and pass.

“Arizonans shouldn’t have to worry about dangerous railroad crossings when they’re driving to work or taking their kids to school,” said Kelly. “This funding to improve our transportation infrastructure will keep families safe.”

“Arizona’s railroads are critical links that keep our state’s economy flowing. This federal funding in railroad crossing safety will further ensure people get where they need to go safely and goods move more efficiently,” said Gallego. “Investing in our infrastructure means creating good-paying jobs, improving safety, and making sure communities across Arizona have access to the public infrastructure they deserve.”

“This $6.4 million federal investment is a major step forward for the Tangerine Road Interchange project and the future of Marana and our region. Once completed, the project will eliminate a major railroad crossing, improve safety and connectivity, and help meet the needs of our growing community. We are grateful to Senator Kelly, Senator Gallego, and Congressman Ciscomani for their support in advancing this project and their continued commitment to our community,” said Jon Post, Mayor of the City of Marana.

“For too long, residents of the Fortuna Foothills have experienced recurring and prolonged closures at the Fortuna Road railroad crossing, disrupting daily travel and raising serious public safety concerns. This $2 million federal investment represents a significant step toward a permanent solution by advancing the project through final design and bringing us closer to construction. We appreciate Senators Kelly and Gallego’s support and the Federal Railroad Administration’s investment in this critical infrastructure project. Yuma County looks forward to continuing our work with our federal and state partners to improve transportation safety, reliability, and emergency access for our residents,” said Martin Porchas, Chairman, Yuma County Board of Supervisors.

title: SENATOR MCCORMICK ANNOUNCES HIS 2026 U.S. SERVICE ACADEMY NOMINATIONSADVISORY BOARD
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Dave McCormick (R-PA) recently announced a distinguished group of veterans, public servants, and community leaders from across the Commonwealth to serve on his Eastern and Western Region Advisory Boards that will help select nominations for U.S. Service Academy appointments.

“I’m deeply grateful to this talented group of veterans and leaders who have volunteered their time for such a vital mission,” said Senator McCormick. “Their service on these advisory boards will help us select the finest young Pennsylvanians to attend our United States Service Academies and lead the next generation of America’s military.”

The prestigious advisory boards, one representing eastern Pennsylvania and the other representing western Pennsylvania, have been established to evaluate applications, conduct interviews, and recommend the best and brightest candidates for appointment to our nation’s U.S. Service Academies: the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, the U.S. Naval Academy, the U.S. Air Force Academy, and the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy. Interviews of candidates kicked off this past weekend and continue through the middle of November.

Candidates applying to the U.S. Coast Guard Academy do not need a Congressional nomination for appointment.

In addition to applying directly and meeting the admission requirements of their service academy of choice, interested applicants must also secure a nomination from a member of Congress to be eligible for appointment to a U.S. Service Academy.

title: NEWS: Sens. Schiff, Padilla Announce More Than $116 Million to Improve Railroad Crossing Safety Across California
text:
Washington, D.C. — Earlier this week, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.) announced that six California projects will receive more than $116 million in federal funding through President Biden’s Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), which Padilla and Schiff voted to pass. The funding, awarded through the Federal Railroad Administration’s Railroad Crossing Elimination (RCE) Program, will improve railroad crossing safety, reduce traffic delays, and strengthen rail infrastructure in Burlingame, Sunnyvale, Richmond, Riverside, San Diego, and Suisun City.

“I am proud to help deliver federal funding for critical safety and modernization upgrades for railroad crossings throughout California—made possible by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. All Californians deserve to live in communities with robust transportation infrastructure that helps reduce congestion. These federal investments will help ensure the safety of our pedestrians and drivers,” said Senator Schiff.

“These federal investments will help make California’s railroad crossings safer, reduce traffic delays, and strengthen the transportation infrastructure our communities depend on,” said Senator Padilla. “From eliminating hazardous crossings to planning future safety upgrades, these projects will improve mobility for Californians and support a stronger regional economy thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. I’ll keep fighting to ensure our communities get these critical investments and the resources they need to grow and thrive.”

The six California projects selected for funding will advance grade separation projects, feasibility studies, and planning efforts to improve safety and mobility for motorists, pedestrians, cyclists, and rail passengers.

Burlingame Broadway Grade Separation Project — $90.42 million: The Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board will eliminate an at-grade crossing by constructing an elevated rail structure and lowering the roadway, improving safety and reducing traffic delays.

Mary Avenue Grade Separation Project, Sunnyvale — $15.50 million: The City of Sunnyvale will advance final design work for a future grade separation along the Caltrain corridor.

Cutting/Carlson At-Grade Crossing Elimination Study, Richmond — $3.36 million: The City of Richmond will plan for a future grade separation at the Cutting Boulevard crossing along the Union Pacific Railroad corridor.

Spruce Street Crossing Closure and Grade Separation Project, Riverside — $2.80 million: The City of Riverside will advance planning and project development for a future grade separation along the BNSF corridor.

San Diego Regionwide At-Grade Crossing Elimination Study — $2.73 million: The San Diego Association of Governments (SANDAG) will plan for safety improvements, separations, or elimination of 39 grade crossings across the regional rail network.

Sunset Avenue Grade Separation Feasibility Study, Suisun City — $2.01 million: The City of Suisun City will evaluate alternatives to separate vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian traffic from the Union Pacific Railroad corridor.

title: Van Hollen Pushes Trump Administration for Answers Following Death of Marylander in ICE Custody
text:
U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) is pressing the Trump Administration for accountability following the death of Maryland resident Julian Curo-Churata in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody and subsequent apparent retaliation against Mr. Curo-Churata’s wife. In the letter, Senator Van Hollen seeks answers to specific questions around his death from Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin, ICE Acting Director David Venturella, and DHS Inspector General Joseph Cuffari, as well as the release and preservation of all records related to the death of Mr. Curo-Churata and an independent investigation into his death. The Senator also questions the recent launch of deportation proceedings against Mr. Curo-Churata’s wife, in what appears to be a retaliation for her decision to speak out on her husband’s death.

Senator Van Hollen begins, “On September 29, 2026, Maryland resident Julian Curo-Churata died in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody. His death is unacceptable and both his family and the American people deserve answers as to how this could occur on your watch – including a full, independent investigation. To make matters worse, there is now an apparent attempt to retaliate against Mr. Curo-Churata’s wife, Veronica Ramirez, who received a Notice to Appear dated three days after speaking out in the Washington Post about her husband’s death as she sought justice and accountability.”

“Julian Curo-Churata lived with Ms. Ramirez and their two children in Laurel, Maryland. On June 27, less than a week after he had attended a court hearing on his pending immigration case, he was arrested by ICE as he stopped at Home Depot on his way to work. Mr. Curo-Churata was detained at Richwood Correctional Center, an ICE detention facility in Louisiana operated by a private company, until September 28, when he was taken to the hospital after he was found to be in medical distress. The next morning, Mr. Curo-Churata died in the hospital due to cardiac arrest linked to septic shock. He was the 37th person to die in ICE custody in the past year. Johns Hopkins Medicine describes sepsis as a ‘life-threatening emergency that needs to be treated right away’ by medical personnel in a hospital,” he continues.

Senator Van Hollen challenges ICE’s claim that Mr. Curo-Churata received appropriate medical attention while in ICE custody, writing, “In Mr. Curo-Churata’s case, ICE claims that ‘while in custody, Curo received proper medical care.’ However, the facility’s correctional officers reportedly attested that he had been ‘lethargic and unresponsive throughout the day’ on September 28, but he was not transported to the hospital until late that evening. While ICE claimed he was transported to the hospital at 8:14 p.m., hospital records reportedly show he did not arrive until 10:26 p.m., even though the hospital was just a 7-minute drive from the facility. Mr. Curo-Churata passed away at 4:01 a.m. on September 29 from cardiac arrest due to septic shock.”

“Just over a month later, after speaking publicly about the death of her husband, Mr. Curo-Churata’s wife, Veronica Ramirez, received a Notice to Appear from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), indicating the Department’s intent to remove her from the United States. The timing of this notice is highly suspicious, seeming to come in retaliation for her decision to speak out. It was issued just three days after Ms. Ramirez was quoted extensively in the Washington Post about her husband’s death. DHS has already taken one parent away from their children permanently, and now, in their time of grief, threatens to deport the other,” Senator Van Hollen notes.

Among other questions, Senator Van Hollen asks the following:

Please identify every camera that recorded Mr. Curo-Churata between September 27 and September 29, 2026. That includes but is not limited to housing-unit, medical-unit, hallway, sally-port and parking-area surveillance cameras; body-worn cameras worn by escort and transport officers; and any camera inside the transport vehicle. For each, state the normal retention period and whether the footage has been kept. If any footage has been deleted or overwritten, explain when, why, and on whose authority.

When and how did any Richwood staff first receive information that Mr. Curo-Churata was ill or in medical distress on September 28? Please identify every staff member involved and give exact times.

What was the basis for ICE’s statement to the press that facility staff transported Mr. Curo-Churata to Ochsner LSU Health Monroe Medical Center at 8:14 p.m. CDT? Please identify any documents indicating that a transfer to the hospital was ordered, requested, or occurred at or around 8:14 p.m. CDT.

What internal reviews, mortality reviews, or after-action reports has LaSalle Management Company and/or Richwood started or completed regarding Mr. Curo-Churata’s death? Has the facility given records to the DHS Office of Inspector General, the ICE Health Service Corps, or any medical examiner or coroner? Please provide any findings.

When, if ever, has Ms. Veronica Ramirez been issued a Notice to Appear before the one she recently received?

What was the reason that she received the Notice to Appear at this time?

Who made the decision to issue her a Notice to Appear?

“Given these concerns, I’m seeking the release and preservation of all records related to the death of Mr. Curo-Churata, as well as a full, independent investigation into his death,” he concludes.

The full text of the letter is available here and below.

Dear Secretary Mullin and Acting Director Venturella and Inspector General Cuffari,

On September 29, 2026, Maryland resident Julian Curo-Churata died in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody. His death is unacceptable and both his family and the American people deserve answers as to how this could occur on your watch – including a full, independent investigation. To make matters worse, there is now an apparent attempt to retaliate against Mr. Curo-Churata’s wife, Veronica Ramirez, who received a Notice to Appear dated three days after speaking out in the Washington Post about her husband’s death as she sought justice and accountability.

Julian Curo-Churata lived with Ms. Ramirez and their two children in Laurel, Maryland. On June 27, less than a week after he had attended a court hearing on his pending immigration case, he was arrested by ICE as he stopped at Home Depot on his way to work. Mr. Curo-Churata was detained at Richwood Correctional Center, an ICE detention facility in Louisiana operated by a private company, until September 28, when he was taken to the hospital after he was found to be in medical distress. The next morning, Mr. Curo-Churata died in the hospital due to cardiac arrest linked to septic shock. He was the 37th person to die in ICE custody in the past year. Johns Hopkins Medicine describes sepsis as a “life-threatening emergency that needs to be treated right away” by medical personnel in a hospital.

In accordance with national detention standards, ICE is required to provide a safe and humane detention environment for its detainees. However, since the beginning of the second Trump Administration, at least 57 people have died in ICE custody. According to a Human Rights Watch report, the mortality rate of deaths in ICE custody is at its highest level in over a decade, including during the COVID-19 pandemic. Public reporting on ICE facilities has consistently revealed inhumane detention conditions and evidence of inadequate and delayed care. It is clear that ICE is not upholding its duty. ICE maintains that it is “committed to ensuring that all those in custody reside in safe, secure and humane environments,” that “comprehensive medical care is provided from the moment individuals arrive and throughout their stay,” and that “at no time during detention is a [detainee] denied emergency care.” The death of Mr. Curo-Churata, as well as the public record on detention conditions during the second Trump Administration, contradict those claims.

In Mr. Curo-Churata’s case, ICE claims that “while in custody, Curo received proper medical care.” However, the facility’s correctional officers reportedly attested that he had been “lethargic and unresponsive throughout the day” on September 28, but he was not transported to the hospital until late that evening. While ICE claimed he was transported to the hospital at 8:14 p.m., hospital records reportedly show he did not arrive until 10:26 p.m., even though the hospital was just a 7-minute drive from the facility. Mr. Curo-Churata passed away at 4:01 a.m. on September 29 from cardiac arrest due to septic shock.

Just over a month later, after speaking publicly about the death of her husband, Mr. Curo-Churata’s wife, Veronica Ramirez, received a Notice to Appear from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), indicating the Department’s intent to remove her from the United States. The timing of this notice is highly suspicious, seeming to come in retaliation for her decision to speak out. It was issued just three days after Ms. Ramirez was quoted extensively in the Washington Post about her husband’s death. DHS has already taken one parent away from their children permanently, and now, in their time of grief, threatens to deport the other.

Given these concerns, I’m seeking the release and preservation of all records related to the death of Mr. Curo-Churata, as well as a full, independent investigation into his death. Additionally, please respond to the following questions no later than November 16, 2026.

title: Whitehouse Announces $430,000 in Federal Funding to Expand Mental Health Services at Children’s Friend
text:
Providence, RI – U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse today joined staff and board members of Children’s Friend in Providence to tour its therapeutic classrooms and announce $430,000 in federal funding for the non-profit.

“Children’s Friend does heroic work to support some of Rhode Island’s most vulnerable children and families,” said Whitehouse. “It is wonderful to see this funding at work ensuring that kids facing mental health challenges can get individualized care that meets their needs.”

Whitehouse secured the earmark in the 2026 minibus, allowing Children’s Friend to expand mental health assessments, clinical capacity, therapeutic classroom visits, and staff training. The funding will allow Children’s Friend to improve individualized mental health and disabilities services for over 800 children enrolled in its early childhood centers and to almost double the organization’s behavioral health staffing.

“The mental health needs of young children are growing and are often overlooked. Yet we know that early intervention can make a profound difference in a child’s life. Thanks to Senator Whitehouse’s leadership and commitment to Rhode Island’s children and families, this $430,000 investment will allow Children’s Friend to expand critical mental health services to our young children. This funding will improve services and support for over 800 children in our early childhood centers. This funding is about giving children the clinical support they need at the earliest possible age, equipping educators with the tools to respond to their needs, and helping families build a stronger foundation for the future,” said David Caprio, President and CEO of Children’s Friend.

Founded in 1834, Children’s Friend is one of the nation’s oldest child-serving organizations and a leading provider of early childhood education and family support services in Rhode Island. Through early childhood education and care sites in Providence, Pawtucket, and Central Falls, Children’s Friend provides comprehensive educational, developmental, and mental health services to young children and families, helping build a strong foundation for lifelong learning and well-being.

title: Rep. Aguilar Announces $5.4 Million to Strengthen Inland Empire Water and Storm Infrastructure
text:
The San Bernardino Valley Water Conservation District will receive $5.4 million in funding from the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation to capture more water and store it underground for future use

SAN BERNARDINO, CA – Today, Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33) announced a $5,403,000 million grant for the San Bernardino Valley Water Conservation District’s (SBVWCD) Oak Creek Basins Project. This grant funding will expand SBVWCD’s ability to capture stormwater and store it underground, helping service homes, businesses and farms long after storms have passed.

Captured water will replenish the aquifers our region depends on, so our communities have a reliable water supply even through droughts and dry seasons. The grant award for the Oak Creek Basins Project is the largest award for the Program for Expansion of Recharge Capacity (PERC) to date.

“Access to clean, reliable water is essential for every family and business in the Inland Empire,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar. “I’m proud to announce this funding for the Oak Creek Basins Project, which will help capture stormwater here in the San Bernardino Valley and store it for future use. Investments like this help secure our region’s water supply and ensure that families here can use it for generations to come.”

“Some of the most important investments we make today are the ones our communities will benefit from decades down the road,” said Melody McDonald, Board President, San Bernardino Valley Water Conservation District. “The Program for Expansion of Recharge Capacity (PERC) reflects years of thoughtful planning, strong partnerships, and a shared belief in the future of the San Bernardino Valley. We’re grateful to Congressman Aguilar for recognizing the importance of investing in our local water supplies, and especially proud of the people whose dedication has brought us to this exciting milestone. Their work will make a lasting difference for generations to come.”

“California cannot control when the next storm arrives, but we can be ready to capture the water it brings,” Betsy Miller Vixie, General Manager, San Bernardino Valley Water Conservation District. “The Oak Creek Basins project, part of our broader Program for Expansion of Recharge Capacity (PERC) will expand our ability to put that water underground, where it can support our communities long after the storm has passed. With this federal investment, we are building on more than a century of groundwater recharge experience to make better use of one of our region’s most valuable natural resources.”

This $5.4 million grant award comes from the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation’s Small Storage Program.

title: Bacon, NE Delegation Urge Disaster Declaration for Nebraska Storms
text:
Washington, D.C. – Rep. Don Bacon (NE-02) joined Sens. Deb Fischer (R-NE) and Pete Ricketts (R-NE), and Reps. Mike Flood (NE-01) and Adrian Smith (NE-03) in sending a letter to President Donald Trump supporting Gov. Jim Pillen’s request for a major disaster declaration following severe storms and flooding in Nebraska from Sept. 30 through Oct. 6, 2026.

The requested declaration would apply to Douglas, Fillmore, Lancaster, Saline, Sarpy, Saunders, Seward, and Thayer counties.

Copy of transmitted letter here and text below:

Dear Mr. President:

We write in support of Nebraska Gov. Jim Pillen’s requests for a major disaster declaration and hazard mitigation. These requests follow heavy rain and severe flooding in Douglas, Fillmore, Lancaster, Saline, Sarpy, Saunders, Seward, and Thayer counties, during the period of Sept. 30, 2026, through Oct. 6, 2026.

We stand ready and willing to assist in any way possible to ensure prompt evaluation of this request. Please do not hesitate to contact our offices with any questions.

title: Legendary Vietnam Gun Truck to Ride in DC Veterans Parade
text:
A replica of the Vietnam-era gun truck “Brutus” will travel down Constitution Avenue on November 8, 2026, as part of the National Veterans Parade, honoring the soldiers who defended American supply convoys during the Vietnam War.

WHAT: “Brutus” replica participating in the National Veterans Parade

WHEN: Sunday, November 8, 2026; parade begins at noon ET

WHERE: Constitution Ave., Washington, D.C., from the National Archives to the White House

MEDIA OPPORTUNITIES: Photography/videography, Veterans Day-related coverage. Interested media should contact Noah Slayter to coordinate coverage opportunities.

The tribute has personal significance for U.S. Congressman Jim Baird (IN-04). The Congressman served as a convoy commander for the 523rd Transportation Company. The company is known for multiple renowned gun trucks including Ace of Spades, Proud American, King Kong, and Satan’s Lil Angel. As a first lieutenant, Jim Baird led convoys of up to 200 vehicles and often rode aboard the gun trucks that protected them.

“One of the greatest privileges of my time in Congress has been creating opportunities to honor Vietnam veterans,” said Congressman Baird. “Those I served alongside and all who sacrificed for the cause of freedom in that war deserve the recognition too many were denied when they returned home. As we celebrate America’s 250th anniversary, seeing Brutus travel through our nation’s capital will honor their courage and remind Americans of the immense service and sacrifice of Vietnam veterans.”

The original Brutus served with the 359th Transportation Company, defending supply convoys against enemy ambushes. To protect trucks carrying supplies from coastal ports to inland bases, soldiers transformed ordinary Army cargo trucks into “gun trucks,” first adding sandbags, then reinforcing the vehicles with steel armor and mounted machine guns. These improvised defenders helped protect fellow soldiers and keep vital supplies moving.

The National Veterans Parade is a nonpartisan celebration of every veteran, regardless of branch, generation, background, political affiliation, or religious belief.

The 2026 National Veterans Parade is expected to feature more than 150 participating units, including numerous marching bands, active-duty military ceremonial and performing units, historic military vehicles, floats, pageant titleholders, and special tributes to veterans of the past.

title: Castor, Bilirakis, Soto Introduce Bipartisan Locality Pay Adjustment Act to Establish Pay Localities for the Orlando and Tampa Metropolitan Areas
text:
HILLSBOROUGH COUNTY, Fla.—Reps. Kathy Castor (FL-14), Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) and Darren Soto (D-FL-09) introduced H.R.10898, the Locality Pay Adjustment Act—bipartisan legislation to direct the President’s Pay Agent to establish pay localities for the Orlando and Tampa metropolitan areas.

“The cost of living in the Tampa Bay area has escalated rapidly and is pricing out the civilian federal workforce. From our air traffic controllers and TSA agents at Tampa International Airport to our Social Security Administration employees and the more than 8,000 civilians working in critical missions at MacDill Air Force Base, these individuals make an incredible commitment to service every day,” said Rep. Castor. “Tampa’s current lack of a unique locality pay designation—which determines compensation—fails to acknowledge the high cost of living and is harming the ability to hire and retain talent in the public and private sectors. Congress can help fix this, so I am introducing bipartisan legislation with Reps. Soto and Bilirakis to stand up for our hardworking neighbors and proper compensation.”

“Our civilian federal employees serve our Veterans, support our military, and help protect our nation. Yet an outdated pay designation hurts recruitment and retention at MacDill—including SOCOM and CENTCOM—with real consequences for national security. This legislation will ensure relevant factors, including cost of living, traffic, and commute times, are updated to reflect the true cost of living in our region. We must give our federal agencies the tools to attract and retain the skilled workforce our country depends on,” said Rep. Bilirakis.

“In Florida’s Ninth Congressional District, so many of our constituents form part of the civilian federal workforce—whether it be by working at the Space Coast, Orlando International Airport, the Lake Nona and Kissimmee VAs, and so many other critical places that help keep Central Florida moving forward,” said Rep. Soto. “I am proud to introduce this bipartisan bill with Reps. Bilirakis and Castor to support our federal employees as the cost of living continues to increase in the region.”

“The Tampa Bay Chamber strongly supports legislation to establish federal locality pay for the Tampa metropolitan area, ensuring compensation better reflects our region’s competitive labor market. From MacDill Air Force Base to our veterans’ healthcare facilities and other federal agencies, these employees play a vital role in our economy, national security, and quality of life,” said Bob Rohrlack, President & CEO of the Tampa Bay Chamber. "Establishing locality pay is an important step toward strengthening workforce competitiveness, attracting and retaining skilled talent, and supporting the long-term success of our region’s federal institutions.”

“AFGE appreciates the bipartisan bill from Representatives Soto, Castor, and Bilirakis to improve pay for federal employees in Orlando and Tampa. Federal employees all across the country are substantially underpaid relative to their counterparts in the private sector and state and local government,” said Tatishka Thomas, National Vice President of AFGE District 5.

Currently, federal employees in the Tampa Bay and Orlando areas receive “Rest of U.S.” pay, while federal employees in South Florida and the Melbourne/Space Coast areas receive supplemental locality pay, meant to align public sector pay with private sector pay in their respective regions. In the Tampa Bay and Orlando areas, people serving in federal government positions across the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, U.S. Social Security Administration offices, airports, and at MacDill Air Force Base and other military installations do not receive locality pay, even as both the cost of living and private sector pay continue to increase.

title: García, Jackson, Casar Lead Colleagues in Letter to Secretary Rubio Urging Suspension of Military Assistance to Ecuador as President Noboa Escalates Repression
text:
CHICAGO — Representatives Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), and Greg Casar (TX-35), joined by 10 colleagues, sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressing profound concerns regarding surging authoritarianism in Ecuador, a country with which the Trump Administration has deepened military ties despite the rapid erosion of democracy and human rights there. The recent arrest of former presidential candidate Luisa González and crackdown on other opposition officials and parties marks the latest alarming phase in Ecuador’s descent into de facto one-party rule by President Daniel Noboa and his allies.

The letter outlines how under President Daniel Noboa, “Ecuador has seen the repression of opposition actors across the political spectrum, attacks on judicial independence, and restrictions on the freedom of the press.” The members urge Secretary Rubio to “immediately suspend all U.S. security assistance and military cooperation with the Noboa administration until democracy and the rule of law are fully restored, and the persecution of González and other opposition figures and parties cease.”

Other concerns expressed by the Members about the Noboa government include its undermining of the judiciary, a prolonged “state of emergency” under which Noboa has claimed extraordinary powers, restricted civil liberties and abused human rights, and committed other abuses including torture, extrajudicial killings, forced disappearances, arbitrary arrests, and sexual abuse in women’s prisons.

The Members warn Rubio that if the Trump Administration fails to take action to deter the Noboa government’s authoritarian actions, Congress will use the tools at its disposal to compel a change of policy in the United States. The Members conclude, “The United States cannot credibly claim to support democracy and the fight against drug-trafficking and organized crime while at the same time expanding its security relationship with a government that is rapidly tightening its authoritarian grip on power.”

In addition to Representatives García, Jackson, and Casar, the letter was signed by: Representatives Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Summer Lee (PA-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-00), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), and Nydia Velázquez (NY-07).

title: Resources and Updates for Arizonans Impacted by Severe Flooding
text:
Last weekend, historic rainfall caused severe flooding across Arizona. Lives were lost, homes and infrastructure were damaged, and many Arizonans were forced to evacuate. Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ) is in frequent contact with federal, state, Tribal, and local officials regarding ongoing recovery efforts and assistance.

Constituents impacted by this disaster are encouraged to visit the Arizona Emergency Information Network’s November 2026 Storms page for official updates and safety guidance. Please see below for county-specific resources:

Apache: Apache County Emergency Management

Coconino: Coconino County Flood Recovery

Gila: Gila County Community Resource Center

Navajo: Northeastern Arizona Public Information System

Yavapai: Yavapai County November Flooding

Since the storms, Rep. Crane and his staff have been on the ground to survey damage and receive the latest information. From Prescott to Kayenta, his team has met with law enforcement, first responders, and community leaders. Rep. Crane is also communicating with Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Administrator Cameron Hamilton, Tribal leadership, and the office of Governor Katie Hobbs.

Federal engagement has already begun with FEMA, the Federal Highway Administration, and land management agencies such as the U.S. Forest Service. Much of FEMA’s disaster assistance requires a major disaster declaration under the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act. Only a Governor or a Tribal Chief Executive can request this declaration, and the President decides whether to grant it. Members of Congress cannot initiate this process. At this stage, damage assessments remain underway, and no request has been submitted. Rep. Crane is coordinating with partners and will use the tools at his disposal to advocate for future requests.

In the meantime, constituents are welcome to reach out to Rep. Crane’s team with questions about the process, where to find current assistance, or anything else related to the flooding. The Prescott District Office can be reached at (928) 286-5338 and the D.C. Office at (202) 225-3361. While staff cannot override an agency’s decision or guarantee a specific outcome, they are available to point residents in the right direction and provide timely updates.

title: Van Hollen, Elfreth Lead Colleagues in Fight to Expand Veterans’ Care at Walter Reed
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) and Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (D-MD-03), a member of the House Armed Services Committee, led their colleagues in urging the Department of Defense and Department of Veterans Affairs to select Walter Reed National Military Medical Center in Bethesda, Maryland, to expand access to care for veterans as part of the implementation of Elfreth’s “Improvement of Availability of Care for Veterans from Facilities and Providers of the Department of Defense” provision of last year’s National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). The Senator and Congresswoman were joined by Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD) and John Fetterman (D-PA) and Representatives Steny Hoyer (D-MD-05), Andy Harris (R-MD-01), Jamie Raskin (D-MD-08), Kweisi Mfume (D-MD-07), Glenn Ivey (D-MD-04), Johnny Olszewski (D-MD-02), and April McClain Delaney (D-MD-06) in their advocacy for Walter Reed.

Elfreth worked with Congressman Derek Schmidt (R-KS-02) on this provision to expand access to care for veterans nationwide and is now urging the selection of Walter Reed as a demonstration location to serve veterans in the National Capital Region and Pennsylvania area. The law specifically allows military and VA medical facilities to strengthen resource sharing, increase the utilization of military medical facilities with available capacity, and increase the volume of complex cases available for professional medical education.

“Walter Reed is well positioned to advance these objectives. As the Nation’s flagship joint military medical center, it brings together highly specialized clinical services, medical education, research, rehabilitation, and operational medicine. Its location in the National Capital Region will allow the hospital to serve a large population center of veterans across Maryland, Virginia, West Virginia, Pennsylvania, and the District of Columbia, providing the best site to launch this program and study its success. Walter Reed maintains strong partnerships with leading health and research institutions, including Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, University of Maryland Medical Center, the National Institutes of Health, the VA Maryland Health Care System, the Washington, D.C. VA Medical Center, and the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences,” wrote the Maryland delegation members. “Together, its clinical capabilities, regional reach, and institutional partnerships make Walter Reed a strong location to demonstrate how closer coordination between the Departments can improve veterans’ access to care while strengthening military medical readiness, clinical expertise, and professional education.”

“We therefore respectfully request that the Health Executive Committee: Provide the criteria being used to identify participating facilities and the anticipated implementation timeline; Conduct a joint assessment of Walter Reed’s available capacity, clinical capabilities, and suitability for inclusion in an action plan under the FY2026 NDAA provision; Engage Walter Reed leadership and the directors of relevant VA medical centers in developing a facility-level implementation plan; Select Walter Reed as a demonstration location whose practices and lessons could inform future health care sharing agreements nationwide,” the members continued.

Elfreth learned about the ability to expand veterans' access to care on her visit to Walter Reed, which was one stop on her statewide defense tour during her first year on the Armed Services Committee.

The Department of Defense and the Department of Veterans Affairs’ Health Executive Committee are anticipated to make a final decision in the following months and provide a report to Congress a month later on their selection and implementation plan.
