title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON MS NOW: “IT WAS AN INCREDIBLE VICTORY FOR THE AMERICAN PEOPLE AND A DECISIVE DEFEAT FOR MAGA EXTREMISM”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on MS NOW’s PoliticsNation, where he emphasized that after a historic midterm election victory, House Democrats remain committed to fighting for an affordable America and holding the crooks who are ripping off the American people accountable.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Joining me now to talk about it all is a man at the center of it all: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries. Thanks for joining me tonight on PoliticsNation. I will say, Majority Leader—Minority Leader Jeffries, soon to be something else we’ll talk about. But first of all, I want to congratulate you on the Democrats’ strong performance. MS NOW estimates your party will hold 256 House seats, giving you a clear majority. What are your thoughts on how we arrived at this moment?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, good evening, Rev. Great to be with you. It was an incredible victory for the American people and a decisive defeat for MAGA extremism. Clearly, the American people are fed up. The cost of living is way too high. There are far too many people in this country—they’re working hard, they’re playing by the rules, but they can’t thrive and can barely survive. Democrats promise to fight for an affordable America. We promise to fight to lower the high cost of groceries and gas and housing and to fight to make healthcare affordable for every single American and, at the same time, in the face of all of the rampant, unprecedented corruption that has been unleashed on the American people, to hold the crooks accountable.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, any hope that these midterm results would prompt President Trump to change course and seek compromise seems to have already been dashed. His first major move after the midterms this week has been to elevate longtime aide Stephen Miller to White House Chief of Staff, replacing Susie Wiles. As you well know, Miller has been the architect of some of Trump’s most controversial policies, like mass deportations. And just earlier today, we learned that President Trump announced he has offered former UFC President Dana White the job of White House Press Secretary. It’s unclear if this is an official offer. What do these decisions tell you about where we are headed in the next two years?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Donald Trump and MAGA extremist Republicans are clearly tripling down on the chaos, the corruption and the cruelty. It’s a failed strategy, and the Republican Party, if they pursue this, will continue to crash and burn as we saw on Tuesday. Democrats are going to continue to focus on the issues that matter to the voters all across the country. We’re going to fight hard for people in urban America, in rural America, in small-town America, in the heartland of America and in Black and Brown communities all across America who want dramatic change in this country, and we’re going to work hard to deliver it.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, you announced in a letter to your colleagues on Wednesday that you intend to run for Speaker of the House in the new session. You have enjoyed unanimous support as Leader of the party during these past two terms in the minority. And so far, no one else has come forward to challenge you. However, Axios is reporting that more than a dozen lawmakers say Democratic House Members and Members-elect are being inundated with calls, and I put that in parenthesis, urging them to not vote for you. MS NOW has not matched this reporting. But what do you make of that? And what do you say to a voter who’s cast their ballot for Democrats seeking change, who might also be feeling some hesitance about having the remaining House leadership, even though even progressives voted for you to be the Minority Leader? Is this just noise? What do you think of this?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’re going to continue to work hard to make our case to every single current member of the House Democratic Caucus, as well as incoming member of the House Democratic Caucus. In the new Congress, we need to focus on affordability, accountability and bringing back to life American values like liberty and justice for all, equal protection under the law, access, in an unfettered way, to the right to vote and a return to our nation’s great heritage as a nation of immigrants. These are the things that I believe House Democrats have forcefully advocated for in the current Congress, against all odds, repeatedly pushed back against Donald Trump and MAGA extremists, battled them on every issue, battled them on the economy, battled them on tariffs, battled them on the reckless war of choice in Iran, battled them on ICE funding, battled them on the Epstein files and battled them on their corrupt and incompetent Cabinet officials and other members of the Trump Cartel, a few of whom we successfully ran out of town, like Kristi Noem and Pam Bondi. And so this was a historic victory for the American people, historic victory for House Democrats. We’re going to have an incredibly broad Caucus of great patriotic members. It’s been my honor to lead House Democrats over these tumultuous years. And hopefully I’ll have the opportunity to continue to work hard on behalf of the American people moving forward. We put it in the hands of the House Democratic Caucus members.

REV. AL SHARPTON: And you and I have talked a lot during the years, and I’ve told you the story. I was there in South Africa when ANC won the election in ’94, and Mandela said, ‘Now we have to govern.’ Now, everybody’s going to be looking for you and the Caucus to govern. What are we going to do? I’m certainly going to be pressing the John Lewis voting bill to come back and George Floyd bill. But I want to talk to you about Black representation. We mentioned at the top of the historic gains in terms of Black senators and Black governors. The situation in the House is more complicated. The Supreme Court decision in Louisiana and the gerrymandering wave that followed directly impacted House districts. So even in a blue wave, the number of Black representatives have gone down slightly from 61 Black Members to 58, not including non-voting delegates. That’s not as bad as it could have been or they intended it to be. But what can Democrats in Congress do to make sure it is not eroded any further?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we certainly are going to fight hard to make sure that we aggressively advance the John Robert Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act so we can end the era of voter suppression in the United States of America once and for all. We worked hard to make sure that we held some of the seats that were most aggressively challenged by Republicans in terms of unleashing this unprecedented gerrymandering scheme. We defeated the Republican scheme in Missouri that was trying to rip away a congressional district from Reverend Emanuel Cleaver. He’s coming back to the United States Congress. Don Davis successfully defeated a Republican gerrymander in North Carolina. He’s coming back. Shomari Figures also ran a great race. I campaigned with him on the final weekend in Alabama. They tried to gerrymander his seat out of existence and rip it away from African American voters in the heart of the belt that brought us the civil rights movement, and Shomari Figures is coming back. And we’ll build upon this progress to ensure that we have a Congress that continues to reflect the American people in every possible way.

REV. AL SHARPTON: And Shomari Figures will be on the show with me tomorrow. But we’ve talked a lot down through the years. You’re a member of National Action Network, so I know you always talk big picture. So let me finish by looking at the big picture for Democrats post-midterm. Since Tuesday, there’s been a lot of discussion about what the priorities should be. Should Democrats be prioritizing investigations of White House officials? Will impeachment be on the table or should the primary focus be on delivering in terms of affordability or all of the above? What is the focus—if you were to become Speaker—that you would be pushing for?

LEADER JEFFRIES: It definitively is going to have to be an all-of-the-above approach, but we have to relentlessly commit ourselves to making life more affordable for the American people in an environment where the cost of living is way too high. And no matter what part of America you live in right now, people are drowning in this failed Trump-Republican economy. And so, we’re going to work hard to move bills very early on to end this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed gas prices on the American people. We’re going to work hard to reverse the Medicaid cuts, reverse the SNAP cuts. We’re going to work hard to end the Trump Tariffs, which have increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year. We also need to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits so we can provide economic relief to tens of millions of Americans who’ve seen their health insurance premiums skyrocket, in some cases, by over $1,000 per year. We’re going to work hard on affordability. We’re going to work hard on accountability, as we’ve indicated, because there’s a cost to corruption when you have folks who’ve been in office focused more on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends and their donors, as opposed to making life more affordable for the American people. And we’re going to work hard to bring about a restoration and return of American values.

REV. AL SHARPTON: So, you say all of the above. And I’ll have to leave it there. Thank you very much for joining us tonight, Congressman Hakeem Jeffries.

Full interview can be watched here.

title: SCHNEIDER CONDEMNS TARGETED CAMPAIGN OF ANTISEMITISM IN PHILADELPHIA
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – In response to the planned boycott targeting Jewish-owned businesses in Philadelphia on the eve of the 88th anniversary of Kristallnacht, Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10), a Co-Chair of the Congressional Jewish Caucus, issued a forceful condemnation of this targeted campaign of antisemitism.

“Eighty-eight years ago, on November 9, 1938, Nazi leaders launched a series of riots in Jewish communities throughout Germany. In what come to be known as Kristallnacht (Night of Broken Glass), Jewish-owned businesses were targeted and destroyed, while more than 1,400 synagogues were burned. It was a dark inflection point in the lead up to the Holocaust.

“Tomorrow’s Philly Bike On Your Left ‘boycott ride’ targeting Jewish-owned businesses is contemptible on any day, but especially on the eve of the anniversary of Kristallnacht. Targeting businesses simply because they are owned by Jews and singling out Jewish Americans to make them feel unwelcome and unsafe is neither reasonable nor justifiable protest. It is rank antisemitism, plain and simple.

“Our Constitution enshrines the right to free speech, including vile, hateful speech. It also protects to right to freely practice one’s religion without fear of discrimination or intimidation. We can vigorously defend both while at the same time resolutely standing against hate.

title: Capito, Lee, Whitehouse, and Heinrich Release Substitute Amendment to Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026
Heinrich, Whitehouse, Capito, Lee Release Substitute Amendment to Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources (ENR) Committee; Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee; Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairwoman of the EPW Committee; Mike Lee (R-Utah), Chairman of the ENR Committee; released a Substitute Amendment to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA). The Substitute Amendment includes clarifying, conforming, and technical edits to reflect feedback received since BAAJA’s introduction in September.

“I’ve worked hard to incorporate the feedback we’ve heard from Tribes and New Mexicans into this Substitute Amendment, and I’m proud to join my colleagues in releasing it today. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will help lower energy costs, strengthen Tribal consultation, and create more good-paying jobs. It also makes sure data centers pay for the energy they use and the grid upgrades they cause, instead of passing those costs on to New Mexico families. Americans can’t afford to wait for lower electricity prices. We need to pass this bill now,” said Heinrich.

“I’m grateful for the input throughout this process from Senate and House colleagues, environmental and labor organizations, and Tribal leaders. Our manager’s amendment improves BAAJA and addresses the thoughtful feedback we have received. Now’s it’s time to pass this bill so we can lower costs, juice the clean energy economy, build big things again in America, reduce pollution, and create tons of new well-paying union jobs,” said Whitehouse.

“This substitute amendment preserves the foundation of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, while making targeted changes based on feedback from our members and stakeholders to further build support. I’m thankful for my colleagues’ efforts to strengthen this legislation, the contributions from members of the House, and the support of countless organizations from across the country. I urge the swift passage of BAAJA to make life more affordable for American families,” said Capito.

“We have spent months working across party lines on both sides of Capitol Hill and with President Trump to deliver permitting reform that makes it easier to build in America. This substitute amendment reflects that work and brings us closer to getting the job done. Our permitting system takes too long, costs too much, and leaves too much uncertainty for the people trying to build what our country needs. We have an opportunity to lower costs for American families, and get America building again. It’s time to finish what we started,” said Lee.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON ABC: “WE ARE GOING TO VISIT ACCOUNTABILITY ON THE WRONGDOERS”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on ABC’s This Week, where he emphasized that with strong majorities in the House and the Senate, Democrats are committed to making life more affordable for the American people and holding the corrupt crooks accountable.

JONATHAN KARL: We begin with the man expected to become Speaker of the House in January, Hakeem Jeffries. Leader Jeffries, thank you for joining us.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Good morning. Great to be with you.

JONATHAN KARL: Obviously, a huge election for you. Have you spoken to President Trump yet?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I have not spoken to President Trump. It was a big night for the American people, a tremendous repudiation of MAGA extremism and a cry out for dramatic change in terms of the direction that we need to take to make life more affordable for the American people, to restore American values and, of course, to hold those who have visited unprecedented corruption on the American people accountable.

JONATHAN KARL: I mean, usually, at this point, I would have expected that the President would have reached out to the Democratic leaders. He hasn’t called you? Have you tried to call him, or will you try to call? I mean, you’re going to have to deal with him.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’ll see what happens in terms of moving forward. But I have spoken to three former presidents, and I’m thankful for those conversations—of course, President Obama, President Biden and President Clinton, and many other leaders across the nation. And, most importantly, I’ve had the chance to speak to everyday Americans who were the ones that powered this election and want us to actually deliver a Congress that no longer functions like a reckless rubber stamp for Donald Trump’s extreme agenda, but functions like a separate and coequal branch of government designed to make life better for the American people.

JONATHAN KARL: It was interesting to see the President’s response to all of this. He didn’t cry fraud. He didn’t challenge the results, contest the results, not immediately anyway. And when I spoke to him shortly after Tuesday, he said to me, ‘I think we can get along. It’s good for the country if we do. The country has had enough.’ Obviously, he’s sent some different signals since then. But what’s your sense? Are you going to be able to work with him?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, the country clearly has had enough. And we’ve got to fight for an affordable America. The cost of living is way too high. There are far too many people in this country who are working hard, they’re playing by the rules, they can’t thrive and they can barely survive. People are drowning in this failed Republican economy. And enough is enough in that regard. That’s why we’re going to fight to lower the high cost of living on all the things. And we have to. We’ve got to fight to lower groceries and gas and housing, and certainly we’ve got to fight to make healthcare affordable for every single American. Now we’ll see whether our colleagues on the other side of the aisle actually are willing to listen to the American people so we can work to get things done. The good news is, Jonathan, that we’ve got a robust majority in a Democratic House and a robust majority in a Democratic Senate to be able to get to work.

JONATHAN KARL: So what is the goal? There’s kind of, there are two approaches you can take, oversimplifying a bit here. But you can pass legislation that you think the President might sign, or you can pass a whole series of bills that you know he’s going to veto. What’s the approach?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, the American people clearly want change that’s bold, change that’s transformational and change that is dramatic. They also want results because relief needs to come to the fact that so many people are struggling throughout this nation. And that’s everywhere. That’s in urban America, in rural America, in small-town America, in the heartland of America and in Black and Brown communities all throughout America. So from our standpoint, we want to do things like end this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has made life way too expensive. We need to stop the Trump Tariffs. We need to reverse the Medicaid cuts that put the health insurance of millions of Americans at risk and threatens to close hospitals all over the place. We certainly need to reverse the SNAP cuts. And we need to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits. And hopefully, we’ll see some courage by a few of our colleagues on the other side of the aisle to work on these issues to get things done.

JONATHAN KARL: And the only way, ultimately, you get things done is if either he signs them or you get a lot of colleagues on the other side of the aisle to overturn his vetoes. There are a couple of things that I see where you could potentially get him to sign. I mean, President Trump asked Congress back in January to cap credit card interest rates at 10%. He also pushed for most-favored-nation status pricing on prescription drugs. And Republicans, Republicans never acted on either one of those. So will you—are those two areas where you could see passing bills in those two areas and saying, go ahead, Mr. President, sign it?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we certainly need to provide credit card relief to the American people and we need to lower the high cost of healthcare across the board, and we look forward to working on those issues. There have been a lot of Democratic bills that have been put into the public domain, a lot of Democratic ideas to try to drive down health insurance costs and the cost of being able to just live and live an affordable life, a comfortable life and a good life. So we’ll see what the opportunities are. But we’re committed to moving aggressively during the first 100 days of the new Congress and beyond to keep our word, to fight for an affordable America, to bring about accountability because we’ve seen unprecedented corruption that has been visited upon the American people. And we are committed to holding the crooks accountable and making sure that Congress functions like a separate and coequal branch of government and a check and balance on an out-of-control executive branch. And we also have to restore American values like liberty and justice for all, equal protection under the law, our commitment to the unfettered right to vote and to lift up our glorious history as a nation of immigrants.

JONATHAN KARL: You had some choice words for Stephen Miller’s elevation to Chief of Staff. You called him a ‘dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist,’ said he ‘had blood—American blood on his hands.’ How does that—what does that mean for your ability to work with that White House, with that Chief of Staff, this President?

LEADER JEFFRIES: It’s an awful choice. Stephen Miller is the architect of Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine and has unleashed billions of taxpayer dollars to brutalize and kill American citizens like Alex Pretti and Renee Nicole Good, and, at the same period of time, to violently target law-abiding immigrant families and communities all across the country. So you know, it was an irresponsible decision, in my view. There’s not going to be any opportunity, certainly, to work with Stephen Miller and what he represents. And we’re committed to forcefully pushing back against the extremism that they may try to continue to unleash on the American people. And we’ve got a firewall in the House and a firewall in the Senate, thanks to the American people.

JONATHAN KARL: Because, as I understand it, you talked on occasion or had some communication with Susie Wiles in your role as Democratic Leader, her role as Chief of Staff, which is natural in any White House, any Congress, but you’re saying that can’t happen with this new Chief of Staff?

LEADER JEFFRIES: It’s not going to happen with this new Chief of Staff to the extent that he lasts because he clearly represents, along with Pete Hegseth and a few others, a really toxic brand of political engagement, of politics and of governance. And the American people just voted for that kind of MAGA extremism to be eradicated, which is why they’ve been defeated up and down the ballot all across the country in the House, in the Senate, in governors’ races, in other statewide races and, certainly, in state legislative bodies.

JONATHAN KARL: Well, let me ask you about Pete Hegseth because Thomas Massie, of course a Republican, tells me that he intends to introduce a resolution of impeachment of Hegseth as Defense Secretary as soon as tomorrow. Are you going to support that? Will Democrats vote in favor of that impeachment resolution?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I’m a hard Yes on the Hegseth resolution. The so-called Secretary of Defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe. Pete Hegseth has got to go.

JONATHAN KARL: And you’re confident all other Democrats are going to join you on that?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We’ll certainly have that conversation on Tuesday morning when we reconvene for the first time in Washington, D.C., but I believe there will be incredibly strong support for that resolution.

JONATHAN KARL: What about the rest of the accountability agenda? Your incoming House Oversight Committee Chairman, Robert Garcia, put it simply as to his agenda. He said, ‘Lawyer up.’ That’s the message to staffers in the White House, administration officials. Is that what it’s going to look like?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, there’s a cost to corruption. And throughout this campaign, we promised that we would focus, certainly, on affordability and driving down the high cost of living and on accountability in the face of the unprecedented corruption that we’ve seen unleashed on the American people by the Trump Cartel. As a matter of fact, our view has been, if you’ve got folks out there who’ve been shortchanging the American people, screwing over the American people or stealing from the American people, then they need to be held accountable in a manner consistent with Congress’s role constitutionally as a separate and coequal branch of government and a check and balance on an out-of-control executive branch. And my view is that we’ve got to follow the facts, apply the law, be guided by the Constitution at all times and then let the chips fall where they may on behalf of the American people and highlight the fact that there certainly is a cost to corruption when you have people in high office who are solely focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends and their donors, then they’re not focused on making life better for the American people. We’re committed to cleaning up the mess wherever it’s found. That’s in the Congress, in the Supreme Court and with respect to this administration. That’s why I strongly support banning Members of Congress from being able to trade stock as one of the things that we’ll need to do as soon as we’re back in control.

JONATHAN KARL: Do you expect Stephen Miller will be called to testify in some of these Oversight investigations—hearings?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I’m going to defer to Jamie Raskin and the Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee, as well as Robert Garcia and Democrats on the Oversight Committee in terms of how they’re going to proceed. We’ll have a conversation about that over the next few weeks and I don’t want to get out ahead of any investigation other than making clear that we are going to visit accountability on the wrongdoers.

JONATHAN KARL: And we’re just about out of time, but I’ve got to ask you, what does it mean to you to be on the verge of being the first Black Speaker of the House in American history?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, listen, this is representative democracy, and it’s been an honor and a privilege to be able to serve the people of Brooklyn, as well as to work on behalf of the people of this great country. It was definitely meaningful as I closed this campaign with Shomari Figures in Montgomery, Alabama, the birthplace of the Civil Rights Movement, thinking about all of the struggles of those great heroes like Dr. King, Rosa Parks and so many other foot soldiers who helped to get us to this point. Listen, we have to continue to push back against the national nightmare that has been visited upon the American people. But I’m confident, standing on the shoulders of so many great heroes, that we are going to be able to continue this country’s long, necessary and majestic march toward a more perfect union.

JONATHAN KARL: Alright, Leader Hakeem Jeffries, thank you for joining us.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Thank you.

Full interview can be watched here.

title: Congressman Al Green Condemns Reported Crackdown on Independent Journalism in Egypt, Calls for Release of Detained Journalists
text:
(Washington, D.C.) — On Monday, November 9, 2026, Congressman Al Green expressed grave concern over reports from Amnesty International and other international human rights organizations regarding the detention of six Egyptian journalists associated with the independent investigative journalism platform Matsadaash, as well as recent legal actions against the independent Egyptian news outlet Mada Masr and its editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah.

According to information provided by Amnesty International and other human rights organizations, Egyptian security forces arrested six journalists associated with Matsadaash on September 28 and 29, 2026: Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emeira, Abdallah Qadry, Islam Barakat, Omar Helal, Mohamed Mahmoud and Mohamed Adel. Reports indicated that security officers confiscated electronic devices and that the journalists were subsequently held in undisclosed locations without access to their families or legal counsel for five to six days.

Amnesty International and the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR) further reported allegations that the six journalists were subjected to torture and other forms of mistreatment, including efforts to coerce fabricated statements. According to EIPR, the journalists faced charges related to terrorism and the dissemination of false information, despite prosecutors reportedly failing to present evidence substantiating these allegations. All six journalists denied the charges against them.

Additionally, Amnesty International raised concerns regarding recent legal proceedings against Mada Masr, an independent Egyptian news organization, and its editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah. According to the information provided by their organization, on October 27, 2026, an Egyptian court ordered the closure of Mada Masr’s website and imposed a fine of three million Egyptian pounds. The ruling is subject to appeal. Amnesty International further reported that Attalah faces a separate criminal trial scheduled for November 11, 2026, on charges related to allegedly spreading false information and operating a website without a license, with the possibility of imprisonment.

Congressman Al Green stated, “Based on the information provided to me, I join Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, the Committee to Protect Journalists, Reporters Without Borders, and other international human rights organizations in condemning these reported actions against independent journalists in Egypt. I call for the release of the six detained Matsadaash journalists and for the protection of the fundamental rights of Lina Attalah and all journalists seeking to report freely and independently.”

“A free and independent press is fundamental to any society that claims to uphold democracy, justice, and the rule of law. Freedom of expression is not a privilege to be granted or withdrawn at the discretion of those in power. It is a fundamental human right that must be protected.”

“I call upon the Egyptian authorities to address these serious allegations, ensure that the fundamental rights of these journalists are protected, and permit independent journalism to operate without fear of persecution. The allegations of torture and mistreatment must be independently investigated and those responsible must be held accountable.”

“Let us be clear: No government should silence journalists merely for reporting information that those in power may find objectionable. Justice demands that freedom of expression, due process, and human dignity be respected and protected for all.”

title: Congressman Allen, Colleagues Lead Bipartisan Letter Requesting EFRP Funding for Foresters and Landowners
text:
On Friday, Congressman Rick W. Allen (GA-12) joined a bipartisan group of Members in sending a letter to House Appropriations Committee Chairman Tom Cole and Ranking Member Rosa DeLauro requesting additional funding for the Emergency Forest Restoration Program (EFRP).

Demand for disaster programs, including EFRP, have increased substantially in recent years due to large disaster events, particularly in Georgia. Congressman Allen has consistently heard from growers in the 12th District about the importance of EFRP funding, which currently has less than $1 million available for allocation to states and counties. The current backlog of requests exceeds $255 million.

In the letter, Congressman Allen and his colleagues write: "Hurricane Helene struck the eastern United States on September 26, 2024, causing severe damage across multiple states. While the impacts in the Southeast were especially visible, forestland owners across the country have since faced mounting recovery needs from hurricanes, wildfires, floods, tornadoes, and other qualifying disaster events. EFRP is the only federal program designed to help private forest owners clear debris, prepare sites, and replant after disasters of this scale."

The Members continue: "In several states, only a small share of obligated funding has been disbursed, and others have received no outlays at all, despite documented damage and approved agreements. These figures underscore the widespread demand for forest restoration support following recent disasters, far beyond any one state or storm... With EFRP serving as the primary federal mechanism for forest debris removal and reforestation, the exhaustion of funding places forest owners nationwide at risk."

The Members conclude: "We respectfully ask the Committee to examine options to ensure additional funding for landowners relying on EFRP to complete disaster recovery efforts, both for Hurricane Helene and for other federally recognized natural disasters."

To read the full letter to Chairman Cole and Ranking Member DeLauro, CLICK HERE

title: Schrier, Bonamici Introduce Bill to Protect Lunch and Recess Time for Kids
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.– Today, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08), introduced her Healthy Meal Time Act to ensure schools schedule enough time for children to eat a balanced, nutritious meal each day. Congresswoman Schrier is joined in introducing this legislation by Congresswoman Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01).

“Kids need to have enough time to eat and play at school," said Congresswoman Schrier, M.D. "As a pediatrician and a mom, I know that students will often skip lunch and rush to recess without eating enough. I am proud to introduce this bill to make sure our kids have the time they need to eat a nutritious meal at school. Creating schedules that ensure kids have enough time to eat and exercise will help them focus in school and stay healthy.”

The Healthy Meal Time Act would direct the U.S. Department of Agriculture, with input from the U.S. Department of Education, to create a study to share successful efforts and current best practices with schools surrounding meal and recess timing. Currently, no federal guidelines surrounding adequate school lunch times exist.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends that students have a minimum of 20 minutes of seated eating time at lunch. This legislation would require best practices to take into account this CDC recommendation, the time it takes for non-eating activities, and the time it takes to eat minimally processed and unprocessed foods.

“School meal times let students refuel and refresh their growing brains, and learning is limited when kids don't have enough food or time to eat. The Healthy Meal Time Act would establish best practices for lunch timing and length, giving schools key guidance and resources to make the best decisions for their students,” said Congresswoman Bonamici.

“Providing nutritious school meals is essential, but children also need adequate time to eat and benefit from them,” said Tamara Randall, MS, RDN, LD, CDCES, FAND, president of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics. “The Academy supports the Healthy Meal Time Act because it would help schools establish evidence-based practices for lunch and recess schedules, ensuring students have the time they need to eat nutritious meals and support their health and well-being. We applaud Representatives Schrier and Bonamici for their leadership on this important issue.”

The Healthy Meal Time Act has been endorsed by the National Education Association, the Center for Science in the Public Interest, the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, and the School Nutrition Association.

title: Castor, Pelosi Introduce Bill to Help Aging Veterans & Veterans With Disabilities Stay in Their Homes
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Rep. Kathy Castor (FL-14) and Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi (CA-11) introduced the No Veteran Left Behind: Housing Retention Act of 2026 to help aging Veterans and Veterans with disabilities remain safely housed. The legislation would create a new grant program within the Department of Veterans Affairs’ Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) program, giving community providers resources to deliver tailored services that help veterans maintain their health, live independently and avoid homelessness.

“No veteran should lose their home because they cannot get the care and support they need. The patriotic Tampa Bay area expects veterans who served our country to be able to age with dignity and live safely,” said Rep. Castor. “This bill will give trusted community providers more tools to help Veterans manage their health, get to medical appointments and prevent an eviction before it happens. I’m proud to partner with Speaker Emerita Pelosi to help Veterans stay in their homes and ensure our commitment to them lasts long after their military service ends.”

“Veteran homelessness is a challenge to the conscience of our nation. No person who served our nation in uniform should be forced to sleep on our streets because the support they earned and deserve is out of reach,” said Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi. “This legislation helps codify the successful California pilot as a national model that helped fill the gap for San Francisco’s elderly and disabled Veterans—the fastest growing cohort. By meeting Veterans where they are, this transformative legislation would enhance access and stability for Veterans to their health care, transportation and daily supports that they need, earned and deserve. Just as our Veterans kept their promise to our nation, we must keep our promise to them when they come home.”

“Elderly and disabled veterans are the fastest growing group of veterans experiencing homelessness, and getting them into housing is only the first step. Keeping them there takes health care navigation, mental health support, and help with daily living, delivered where they live,” said House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Mark Takano (CA-39). “Speaker Emerita Pelosi and Rep. Castor’s bill does that. California’s pilot proved the model works, with fewer than 4 percent of veterans losing their housing and emergency room visits down 75 percent. Veterans’ Affairs Committee Democrats are proud to support this bill, and I thank them for their leadership.”

Veterans’ needs are changing as they age. In 2015, 55 percent of SSVF participants had a disabling condition; by 2023, that share had increased to 70 percent. Approximately half of SSVF participants in 2024 were aged 55 or older. The legislation would help community providers respond with more intensive, individualized support, including services delivered in veterans’ homes.

The No Veteran Left Behind: Housing Retention Act would support services including:

Mental and behavioral health care, including individual and group counseling, substance use disorder counseling, crisis intervention and peer support;

Food and meal assistance, help with grocery shopping, and transportation to medical appointments, grocery stores, job interviews and other community services;

Occupational therapy, functional assessments, coordination of assistive devices and home accessibility modifications;

Medication management support and help navigating health care options;

Eviction prevention, tenant support and in-home services that help veterans maintain safe, habitable housing;

Financial management assistance and therapeutic and social activities.

The bill would prioritize providers serving Veterans transitioning from homelessness to permanent housing and veterans who need ongoing services to remain housed and avoid unnecessary institutionalization. It would also require coordination among VA, health care providers, housing providers and community organizations to address Veterans’ needs and reduce duplication of services.

title: Castro Leads Texas Delegation In Demanding Turnaround Of Staggering SNAP Backlog Formed Under Abbott
text:
WASHINGTON, DC —Representative Joaquin Castro (TX-20) led the Texas Delegation, including Representatives Greg Casar (TX-35), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Lloyd Doggett (TX-37), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Christian Menefee (TX-18), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34), Al Green (TX-9), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Marc Veasey (TX-33), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-7), and Henry Cuellar (TX-28), in a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke L. Rollins demanding the turnaround of a massive backlog in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) applications that formed under Texas Governor Greg Abbott.

In the letter, the members admonished the state’s failure to process SNAP applications on time and keep families in need fed, writing, “Texans are facing increasing delays in accessing critical food and nutrition assistance because SNAP applications are not being processed in a timely manner. Texas’ SNAP application backlog rose from approximately 3,700 pending applications in January 2026 to an astonishing 175,000 by early September 2026. Federal law generally requires states to process SNAP applications and issue benefits within 30 days and to act on expedited applications within seven days—a standard Texas has not consistently met.…Each pending application represents a household that may be without the help it needs to keep food on the table.”

The members continued by underscoring the impact of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act on the staggering backlog, writing, “We are also concerned about the combined effect of the SNAP changes in Public Law 119-21, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), on Texas’ ability to deliver food assistance to eligible households on time. Expanded work requirements, narrowed exemptions, and newly imposed state cost sharing come at a time when SNAP caseloads remain high and families are already experiencing delays in benefit access…. [Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)] has acknowledged that the new SNAP mandates require a closer review of each case, which indicates that implementing OBBBA SNAP provisions is directly reducing processing capacity.”

The members also demanded an investigation, including an evaluation of contracted vendors, and federal intervention if the backlog was not adequately addressed.

The members requested a response by November 30, 2026. To download the letter, click here.

BACKGROUND:

The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) backlog rose from 3,700 in January 2026 to 175,000 in September 2026. The state’s on-time rate for SNAP renewals hit the lowest in four years, from 83% to 28% in July. Changes to SNAP under the so-called “One Big Beautiful Bill Act” (OBBBA) imposed expanded work requirements, new state cost sharing, and narrowed exemptions. These extra requirements have added to the volume and complexity to Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) cases in need of review. The OBBBA also made $187 billion in cuts to SNAP, eliminating benefits for 550,000 Texans. According to the Center for American Progress, the cuts could lead to 55,400 unnecessary deaths in Texas.

Prior to the OBBBA, the federal government paid 100% of SNAP benefit costs regardless of a state’s payment error rate. The OBBBA includes a provision that required states with a payment error rate of 6% or more to pay a share of the benefit cost. This provision goes into effect October 1, 2027. Texas’ FY 2025 payment error rate was 9.34, which means Texas would be responsible for 10% of the cost of SNAP benefits, approximately $709 million. Texas receives roughly $7 billion a year in federally funded SNAP benefits.

A separate provision in the OBBBA increased the state share of SNAP administrative costs. The previous federal/state administrative cost split was 50/50.?The OBBBA reduces the federal cost share from 50% to 25%. States are now required to cover 75% of program administration effective October 1, 2026.

title: RELEASE: Congressman Cloud Joins X-energy and Dow as NRC Issues Historic Construction Permit for Seadrift Nuclear Project
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Michael Cloud (TX-27) joined X-energy CEO Clay Sell, Dow executives, and Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) leadership at NRC headquarters as the Commission issued a construction permit for the Long Mott Energy project at Dow’s Seadrift Operations in Calhoun County, Texas.

Calhoun County is set to become home to the first commercial nuclear reactor in American history built to power an industrial plant. The permit clears the way for X-energy’s small modular reactors (Xe-100) to supply power and industrial heat to Dow’s Seadrift site. This is the first permit for a high-temperature gas-cooled reactor in over 50 years.

What this means for Texas:

Building a nuclear plant takes years of construction work, and running one requires a permanent, highly skilled workforce.

The project brings major new investments and grid power to the area.

Reliable, around-the-clock energy, in any weather, that isn’t tied to fuel prices.

Dow’s Seadrift Operations is a cornerstone of the local economy. Its dependable power and heat help keep the plant competitive.

“Texas’s 27th District is leading the nation into a new era of American energy,” said Congressman Cloud. “This permit will bring jobs, a stronger manufacturing base on the Gulf Coast, and energy built right here at home. Seadrift can power American industry for generations, and this is only the beginning for advanced nuclear energy in Texas,” concluded Congressman Cloud.

Congressman Cloud has been a consistent advocate for the Seadrift project. As a member of the House Appropriations Committee, he helped secure $2.675 billion for the Department of Energy’s Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program (ARDP), which supports advanced reactor projects including X-energy’s work at Seadrift. In March, he wrote to urge that nuclear funds be prioritized for the project. X-energy and Dow are now in the construction and long-lead procurement phase of the project. The NRC completed its Environmental Assessment for the site in May.

title: Costa, Bipartisan and Bicameral Coalition Press Administration to Expedite Delivery of Ukraine Aid
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Jim Costa (CA-21), a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, led a bipartisan, bicameral letter to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought. The lawmakers demanded an explanation for the Administration’s delay in executing the $400 million Congress provided for Ukraine security assistance in Fiscal Year 2026 and urged that delivery be accelerated. The effort builds on a similar letter led earlier this year by Senators Dick Durbin (D-IL) and Chuck Grassley (R-IA).

“Ukraine’s armed forces need and deserve continued American support, and Congress has provided the resources to deliver it,” the lawmakers wrote. “We remain committed to supporting Ukraine’s defense and will continue to hold the Administration accountable for delivering these funds as Congress intended.”

Background

Congress appropriated $400 million for the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative in the Fiscal Year 2026 government funding bill, supported by bipartisan majorities. The Trump Administration waited until the final days of the fiscal year to obligate the funds and have a slow delivery schedule that runs through FY2029, according to the Pentagon’s own spend plan.

In the letter, the lawmakers warned that slow delivery of support, as Ukraine enters another winter of Russian attacks on civilians and infrastructure, undermines the credibility of American commitments and the ability to deter Russian aggression. The lawmakers urged the Administration to:

Provide a written explanation of why the funds were not obligated until the final days of the fiscal year, including any conditions or holds the Office of Management and Budget placed on their apportionment.

Share a detailed delivery schedule, with the reasons delivery is projected to extend into FY2029 and the steps the Administration will take to accelerate it.

Explain why Patriot interceptors were reportedly excluded from the package and whether future Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative funding can address Ukraine’s air defense needs.

Ensure OMB apportions and executes any FY2027 Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative funding Congress provides promptly and without similar delay.

In addition to Congressman Jim Costa (CA-21), the letter was signed by Representatives Eugene Vindman (VA-07), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Don Bacon (NE-02), Wesley Bell (MO-1), Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Rick Larsen (WA-02), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Bradley Schneider (IL-10), Ed Case (HI-01), Johnny Olszewski, Jr (MD-02), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), William Keating (MA-09), and Mary Scanlon (PA-05); and Senators Thom Tillis (R-NC), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Chuck Grassley (R-IA), Joni Ernst (R-IA), and John Cornyn (R-TX).

title: Ahead of Veterans Day, Courtney Calls for Passage of the Major Richard Star Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, in a speech on the House floor, Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02) called on the U.S. House of Representatives to pass the Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102), a bipartisan bill that would fix an injustice in the law that currently diminishes earned retirement benefits for veteran retirees who also collect service-connected disability benefits. To watch Courtney's full speech, click here.

Courtney is one of 341 cosponsors of the Major Richard Star Act, and earlier this year, he signed a discharge petition to force a vote on the bill in the House. Having reached the signature threshold to force a vote, it is expected that the House will vote on the Major Richard Star Act on Veterans Day this Wednesday.

“On Wednesday, it will be time to finally pass a clean Richard Star Act, which veterans all over this country are going to be watching closely to make sure that their Members have listened to them and moved forward in terms of making sure those veterans get the full support and benefits, as Abraham Lincoln said, having “borne the battle,” Courtney said. “I implore all of my colleagues on Wednesday when this measure comes up to vote ‘yes,’ send it to the Senate, get it to the White House, and end, again, this unjust concurrent receipt offset.”

Currently, combat-injured veterans who were forced into medical retirement are only able to receive either U.S. Department of Defense retirement benefits or U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs disability compensation. The Major Richard Star Act would amend the law to allow these medically retired veterans to receive both their full retirement pay and disability compensation.

FULL TRANSCRIPT

Mr. Speaker, in a couple of days our country will pause in one of the 12 national public holidays, Veterans Day, to recognize the sacrifice and service of veterans, both living and deceased, which is the mandate of Veterans Day.

Veterans Day first appeared in this country on November 11th, 1919, when Woodrow Wilson issued an executive order decreeing that Veterans Day would be celebrated on that day, and in 1938, Congress moved and actually made it a national holiday.

There’s lots of ways people can participate in Veterans Day. They can attend veterans ceremonies. They can attend veterans parades. They can express vocally their support and appreciation for veterans in their communities. But all of us have a duty to do more, particularly here in Congress, to provide support for veterans. As Abraham Lincoln, in his second inaugural address, said, we have a duty to care for the veteran that has “borne the battle.” In other words, provide real, tangible support both in terms of health care and financial services.

In a couple of days. Congress is going to have an opportunity to follow through on that mission that Abraham Lincoln announced so many years ago when we take up the Richard Star Act, finally, for passage here in the House of Representatives.

This is a bill which will end one of the greatest injustices in the Veterans Administration system of benefits, where veterans who, again, have earned a pension and have earned a disability benefit because of a service-connected injury, are no longer going to be subject to an offset which reduces those benefits which they earn.

H.R. 2102 will be up for consideration because of a discharge petition to finally end this injustice, which veterans service organizations of every stripe have come to Washington year in and year out, pointing out the blatant unfairness of people who again worn the uniform of our country and actually suffered combat related injuries, being denied the full scope of retirement benefits that they've earned as well as the disability benefits.

This is an issue that should unite both sides of the aisle when we take it up pursuant to the discharge petition. Over 300 members have cosponsored this bill here in the House of Representatives. There was an attempt to sort of tweak it and mangle it, which failed earlier in this Congress, and on Wednesday, it will be time to finally pass a clean Richard Star Act, which veterans all over this country are going to be watching closely to make sure that their Members have listened to them and moved forward in terms of making sure those veterans get the full support and benefits, as Abraham Lincoln said, having “borne the battle.”

I implore all of my colleagues on Wednesday when this measure comes up to vote “yes,” send it to the Senate, get it to the White House, and end, again, this unjust concurrent receipt offset.

###

title: Courtney Statement on New Navy Contract Award for Applied Physical Sciences in Groton
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee, issued the following statement on the Navy’s new $19.9 million contract award to Applied Physical Sciences (APS) in Groton for conducting studies and developing new technologies for the advancement of undersea dominance and naval engineering.

“This new contract award for APS in Groton will support Navy programs authorized by the Seapower Subcommittee,” Courtney said. “APS does vital work for the U.S. Navy, strengthening maritime national security by addressing the threats and challenges of both today and tomorrow. On the heels of last month’s announcement that APS will establish its new headquarters in Pawcatuck, this contract award is a signal of the growth and collaboration that is on deck for the company as a continued part of southeastern Connecticut’s ever-growing defense industrial base.”

Last month, READCO announced that Applied Physical Sciences will establish its new headquarters at the planned Stonington Technology Park in Pawcatuck. Applied Physical Sciences’ current headquarters is in Groton, and the company also has a facility in Pawcatuck.

title: NBC News: Democratic lawmakers seek to restore deportation protections to Afghans in the U.S.
text:
A pair of House Democrats will try to bypass Republican leaders and force a vote to restore Temporary Protected Status to Afghan nationals in the United States by introducing a discharge petition when Congress returns Monday night.

Rep. Jason Crow, D-Colo., and Rep. Sam Liccardo, D-Calif., will file the petition, which would require signatures from 218 members to bring forth legislation to grant Afghans protection from deportation until mid-2029.

TPS, created by Congress in 1990, is a Department of Homeland Security program that allows migrants to live and work in the U.S. for up to 18 months if their home countries have been designated as unsafe. The time period can be extended.

President Donald Trump’s administration terminated the status for Afghanistan in May 2025, a designation that former President Joe Biden’s administration had granted in 2022.

“This administration is returning TPS to its original temporary intent,” then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said at the time. She added that “Afghanistan has had an improved security situation, and its stabilizing economy no longer prevent them from returning to their home country.”

While the Trump administration recently planned to deport dozens of Afghan immigrants and asylum-seekers to Pakistan, a federal judge last week temporarily blocked that move.

Crow and Liccardo would need all current House Democrats and a handful of Republicans to sign on to their discharge petition to reach the necessary 218 signatures. The pair already introduced a special rule on Oct. 1, allowing them to start collecting signatures as soon as they submit the petition on Monday.

“Our Afghan partners put their lives on the line to help protect American servicemembers like me,” Crow, who served as a paratrooper and an Army Ranger in Iraq and Afghanistan, said in a statement. “I’m working to force a vote that will protect Afghans already in the United States because I won’t let our nation leave these brave Afghans behind.”

If Crow and Liccardo are successful in reaching the 218-signature threshold, GOP leaders would be forced to bring forward the Afghanistan TPS Act for a floor vote. That bill, which the pair introduced in July, would grant TPS to Afghans until July 2029. The legislation would need a majority vote on the House floor to pass.

The bill already has four Republican co-sponsors: Reps. Don Bacon of Nebraska, Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida, Joe Wilson of South Carolina, and Morgan Luttrell of Texas. It also has the backing of Rep. Kevin Kiley, a Republican-turned-independent from California.

“Thousands of Afghans risked their lives alongside American troops because our country made them a promise: We would not abandon them,” Liccardo said. “Now, we risk sending them back into the hands of the very Taliban forces they helped us fight. This cannot wait until the Democratic majority takes over.”

The bill has the backing of more than 50 organizations, including Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America, Veterans of Foreign Wars and Amnesty International USA.

Once rare, discharge petitions have been successful several times in the 119th Congress as a small number of Republicans have bucked party leadership to join Democrats in getting measures to the floor.

In April, the House voted to reinstate temporary protection for Haitian immigrants after a few Republicans joined with Democrats on that discharge petition. The legislation passed 224-204, with 10 Republicans joining all Democrats in support. While the White House had vowed that Trump would veto the bill, Senate Republicans blocked the legislation from going to his desk.

Other successful discharge petitions have included votes on aid to Ukraine, extending Affordable Care Act subsidies and the Epstein Files Transparency Act put forth by Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif.

title: Crow Moves to Force Vote on  Granting Vulnerable Afghans Temporary Protected Status
text:
WASHINGTON—Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a former paratrooper and Army Ranger who serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and House Armed Services Committee, will file a discharge petition to force a vote on his Afghanistan TPS Act.

Crow’s Afghanistan TPS Act protects Afghans currently in the U.S. from deportation—and thereby provides them certainty and stability—by granting them Temporary Protected Status (TPS). The bill would designate Afghanistan under TPS until 2029. It comes as conditions in Afghanistan remain extremely dangerous, and follows a previous decision by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security to terminate TPS for Afghanistan.

Crow introduced his Afghanistan TPS Act alongside Representatives Sam Liccardo (D-CA), Don Bacon (R-NE), and Maria Elvira Salazar (R-FL) in July. The original legislation has been endorsed by more than 50 organizations including Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America (IAVA), Veterans of Foreign Wars, AfghanEvac, No One Left Behind, Global Refuge, Refugees International, Amnesty International USA, World Relief, International Refugee Assistance Project (IRAP), HIAS, Afghans For a Better Tomorrow, Center for Law and Social Policy (CLASP), American Friends Service Committee (AFSC), Human Rights First, Feminist Majority, and The Alliance for Diplomacy & Justice.

“Our Afghan partners put their lives on the line to help protect American servicemembers like me. After more than two decades of war, we made a promise that we’d look after them. It’s both a moral and national security imperative that we keep that promise,” said Congressman Crow. “I’m working to force a vote that will protect Afghans already in the United States because I won’t let our nation leave these brave Afghans behind.”

“This is about America keeping our word. Thousands of Afghans risked their lives alongside American troops because our country made them a promise: We would not abandon them. Now, we risk sending them back into the hands of the very Taliban forces they helped us fight. This cannot wait until the Democratic majority takes over—we need to reinstate Temporary Protected Status immediately and keep our friends safe,” said Congressman Liccardo.

As a combat veteran, Congressman Crow served three tours in Iraq and Afghanistan. He has been a long-standing champion of our Afghan allies as a Congressman. Crow has highlighted the importance of the SIV program in U.S. Congressional hearings and worked to ensure the authorization of 12,000 additional Afghan SIVs in the State Department's foreign operations funding bill. He has demanded the Trump Administration answer for reported plans to transfer Afghan refugees to unsafe third-country destinations. He introduced the Afghan Adjustment Act to provide a legal adjustment process for Afghan allies already in the United States, helped introduce the Afghan Allies Protection Act to expand and extend the SIV program, and started the Honoring Our Promises Working Group following the announcement of the withdrawal to help expedite SIVs and U.S. Refugee Admissions Programs.

title: ND delegation: North Dakota receives $206 million in second year of Rural Health Transformation Program
text:
Bismarck, ND – Congresswoman Julie Fedorchak and Senators John Hoeven and Kevin Cramer today announced that North Dakota will receive $206 million for the second year of the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). The announcement supports ongoing efforts to build a continuum of care across the entire state and follows a roundtable the delegation held with U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. in North Dakota last week, with the goal of ensuring an effective partnership between HHS, the North Dakota Department of Health and Human Services (NDHHS) and the state’s health care providers. Today’s award keeps the state on track to receive up to $1 billion over the five years of the RHTP.

“This additional $206 million in funding, on top of the $200 million we already received, represents an extraordinary opportunity to transform how we deliver health care in North Dakota, especially in our rural areas,” Fedorchak said. “I urge state leaders to think big and use these one time resources to fundamentally rethink and retool how we deliver healthcare in a way that maximizes access and quality at a cost that is sustainable.”

“This $206 million award builds on the progress North Dakota has made so far under the Rural Health Transformation Program and will unlock more opportunities to build a continuum of care across our state,” said Hoeven. “This award is timely, as we just had a productive conversation last week with HHS Secretary Kennedy, officials from the NDHHS and health care providers from across our state, part of our efforts to ensure this program works for our hospitals, clinics and other providers. We will continue working to support our state in implementing these funds, building effective partnerships and advancing solutions to truly transform rural health care services in North Dakota.”

“Rural hospitals are essential to our communities, and the Rural Health Transformation Program is an investment in their future,” said Cramer. “This second-year award provides an opportunity to build on the progress already being made. After a positive discussion with Secretary Kennedy last week, I look forward to working with our state leaders and CMS to deliver lasting improvements to transform healthcare delivery across our state.”

The delegation worked to establish the RHTP through the passage of the Working Families Tax Cut Act and supported Governor Armstrong and his team in putting forward a strong application. The state was awarded nearly $200 million for the program’s first year, which is twice the program’s baseline and comes as a result of the state:

Investing in statewide fiber optic infrastructure.

Building a network of new, state-of-the-art critical access hospitals (CAHs).

Leveraging both telehealth and CAHs to recruit and retain health care professionals and provide access to a comprehensive continuum of care.

NDHHS recently obligated the full year-one award, with the bulk of the funding going to the North Dakota Center for Rural Health, which will manage awards to sub-grantees. The state also advanced programs to make clinical equipment upgrades, improve health care workforce retention and support mobile mammography services.

title: Gonzalez Joins Texas Democratic Delegation in Demanding Turnaround of Staggering SNAP Backlog Formed Under Governor Abbott
text:
Contact: Alexis Torres

Washington, D.C. —Today, Congressman Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34) joined Congressmembers Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Greg Casar (TX-35), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Lloyd Doggett (TX-37), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Christian Menefee (TX-18), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Al Green (TX-09), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Marc Veasey (TX-33), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), and Henry Cuellar (TX-28), in a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Secretary Brooke L. Rollins demanding the turnaround of a massive backlog in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) applications that formed under Governor Greg Abbott.

In the letter, the Members admonished the state’s failure to process SNAP applications on time and keep families in need fed, writing, “Texans are facing increasing delays in accessing critical food and nutrition assistance because SNAP applications are not being processed in a timely manner. Texas’ SNAP application backlog rose from approximately 3,700 pending applications in January 2026 to an astonishing 175,000 by early September 2026. Federal law generally requires states to process SNAP applications and issue benefits within 30 days and to act on expedited applications within seven days—a standard Texas has not consistently met.…Each pending application represents a household that may be without the help it needs to keep food on the table.”

The Members continued by underscoring the impact of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act on the staggering backlog, writing, “We are also concerned about the combined effect of the SNAP changes in Public Law 119-21, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), on Texas’ ability to deliver food assistance to eligible households on time. Expanded work requirements, narrowed exemptions, and newly imposed state cost sharing come at a time when SNAP caseloads remain high and families are already experiencing delays in benefit access…. [Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)] has acknowledged that the new SNAP mandates require a closer review of each case, which indicates that implementing OBBBA SNAP provisions is directly reducing processing capacity.”

The Members also demanded an investigation, including an evaluation of contracted vendors, and federal intervention if the backlog was not adequately addressed.

The Members requested a response by November 30, 2026. To download the letter, click here.

BACKGROUND:

The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) backlog rose from 3,700 in January 2026 to 175,000 by September 2026. The state’s on-time rate for SNAP renewals hit the lowest in four years, from 83% to 28% in July. Changes to SNAP under the so-called “One Big Beautiful Bill Act” imposed expanded work requirements, new state cost sharing, and narrowed exemptions. These extra requirements have added to the volume and complexity to Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) cases in need of review. The OBBBA also made $187 billion in cuts to SNAP, eliminating benefits for 550,000 Texans. According to the Center for American Progress, the cuts could lead to 55,400 unnecessary deaths in Texas.

Prior to the OBBBA, the federal government paid 100% of SNAP benefit costs regardless of a state’s payment error rate. The OBBBA includes a provision that required states with a payment error rate of 6% or more to pay a share of the benefit cost. This provision goes into effect October 1, 2027. Texas’ FY 2025 payment error rate was 9.34, which means Texas would be responsible for 10% of the cost of SNAP benefits, approximately $709 million. Texas receives roughly $7 billion a year in federally funded SNAP benefits.

A separate provision in the OBBBA increases the state share of SNAP administrative costs. The previous federal/state administrative cost split was 50/50. The OBBBA reduces the federal cost share from 50% to 25%. States are now required to cover 75% of program administration effective October 1, 2026.

title: Rep. Grijalva Statement Following Senate Vote on Permitting Reform Bill
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva released the following statement after the U.S. Senate voted to advance the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) of 2026. Earlier in the day, she spoke at a rally outside of the U.S. Capitol in opposition to the bill. You can view her remarks here.

“Just one week after voters resoundingly rejected the Trump agenda, Congress should not be rushing to pass a bill that gives him even more unilateral authority to bypass our laws. This legislation was developed without hearings, meaningful tribal consultation and stakeholder engagement, or the rigorous review that a bill of this magnitude would normally go through. I remain deeply concerned about provisions that would gut protections for clean air and water, undermine tribal sovereignty, and potentially fast-track data center development.

“For Southern Arizona, this bill is not some abstract debate about federal permitting – it is about the water we drink, the air we breathe, the mountains and public lands we cherish, and the future we leave our children. I am especially concerned about a provision that would allow toxic mine tailings to be dumped on public lands in the Coronado National Forest.

“Alarmingly, this legislation could also make it easier for DHS to establish new immigrant detention centers by weakening environmental review requirements under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) — the very law Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes has invoked in challenging the proposed detention facility in Surprise, Arizona. We should not be stripping away critical safeguards to make it easier for this administration to expand its mass detention infrastructure.”

“For these reasons, I am a hard NO on BAAJA.”

title: Rep. Haridopolos Joins NASA and Space Florida to Announce CAPEWEEK
text:
November 9, 2026

Cape Canaveral, FL — Last week, U.S. Congressman Mike Haridopolos (FL-08) joined NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, CAPEWEEK Mission Commander Cyrus Sigari, and Space Florida President and CEO Rob Long to announce CAPEWEEK, a new annual aerospace and technology expo debuting in March 2028.

Held on the 15,001-foot former space shuttle landing runway at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center, CAPEWEEK will bring together leaders in aerospace, defense, artificial intelligence, energy, robotics, and advanced mobility for an industry exposition, leadership forum, live demonstrations, and public technology exhibits.

The event is projected to generate $5 billion in economic impact for Florida over its first decade and eventually attract more than 500,000 attendees annually. CAPEWEEK will showcase cutting-edge American innovation, foster industry partnerships, and give families and students firsthand exposure to emerging technologies.

“Here on Florida’s Space Coast, we don’t watch history, we make it,” said Congressman Haridopolos. “From Apollo to the Space Shuttle to today’s commercial space boom, our community has always led the way. CAPEWEEK will build on that legacy, bringing new investment, creating opportunities for local businesses, and inspiring the next generation of American innovators. There’s no better place to showcase the future of aerospace than right here on the Space Coast.”

“America should have a place where the people building the future can come together with the public that inspires and supports them,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “There are few more fitting places than Kennedy Space Center and the runway where the Space Shuttle returned from orbit. CAPEWEEK will put extraordinary aircraft, spacecraft, technologies, and the people behind them in one place and give hundreds of thousands of visitors a front-row seat to the next era of American innovation.”

“America is the techno-aerospace republic. The world's great air shows have long brought the industry together; CAPEWEEK gives America a stage of its own to join them,” said Cyrus Sigari, Founder and Mission Commander of CAPEWEEK. “Beyond just serving industry, we have designed CAPEWEEK to be where the next generation comes to see the future they were promised. A 10-year-old girl will be able to watch a flying car or a rocket cross the sky in the morning, meet the team that built it that afternoon, and go home that night believing she could build the next one.”

“For decades, we watched this runway bring orbiters home. Now it’s the front door for the companies building America’s future in space,” said Rob Long, President and CEO of Space Florida. “CAPEWEEK will bring the world’s customers, capital, and talent here for one week a year. Our job is to make sure the deals started here get done.”

“Florida launched the first space race, and Florida is going to win the next one,” said FL Gov.-elect Byron Donalds.“We want this state to be the world headquarters of space exploration, not only for astronauts and engineers, but for welders, electricians, machinists, technicians and pilots too. Pursuing the final frontier means good-paying jobs right here in Florida, and CAPEWEEK is how we launch that mission.”

“For decades, the partnership between NASA and the Department of the Air Force has inspired the world by leading America to the edge of the possible and beyond,”said Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink. “We continue carrying that spirit forward to protect and defend our nation. CAPEWEEK is poised to further unite our shared missions, celebrate our legacy of exploration, and showcase innovation - bringing together disruptors, decision-makers, and industry partners on one runway to supercharge the industrial base.”

###

title: Harshbarger’s Nuclear Advisory Committee Reform Act Passes U.S. House
text: “When it comes to nuclear energy, safety has to come first, and today's vote gets us one step closer to making sure America's top experts are focused on the issues that matter most,” said Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger. “This commonsense bill keeps independent safety review in place and concentrates it on new and significant issues instead of rehashing what's already been resolved. title: Wyden, Merkley, Hoyle, Bynum Announce over $5.3 Million to Enhance Railroad Safety
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, along with U.S. Representatives Val Hoyle and Janelle Bynum today announced over $5.3 million in federal investment to improve railroad infrastructure, increase safety, and boost economic growth.

“Farmers and manufacturers across Oregon rely on railroads to ship their products to markets across the world,” Wyden said. “This federal investment will improve the safety of railroad crossings, increase efficiency of Oregon’s railways, and help our local economies thrive. I will continue to fight for more resources for infrastructure projects that support small businesses across the state.”

“Critical investments like these play a vital role in preventing traffic disruptions and keeping trains, vehicles, and pedestrians safe,” said Merkley. “These common-sense projects in Douglas and Linn Counties will both keep the local economy moving and our community members safe.”

“Investments in rail infrastructure help connect our communities,” said Rep. Hoyle “This funding will strengthen rail safety across Douglas County, significantly improving emergency access concerns and the efficiency of intercity freight rail.”

“Nobody likes getting stuck at the train tracks, but I’ll take being a few minutes late over playing with our safety,” said Rep. Bynum. “This money is about making sure we can get around safely while giving our economy room to grow and bringing more business to Oregon.”

The $5.3 million in federal awards from the Federal Railroad Administration’s Railroad Crossing Elimination/Crossing Safety program will be distributed as follows:

$3,583,594 to the City of Harrisburg to close three at-grade rail crossings, improve track visibility and install several roadway improvements.

$1,763,336 to Douglas County to support the feasibility study and preliminary engineering of a future grade separation at the crossing intersection of Old Highway 99 and the Central Oregon and Pacific Railroad.

“We are truly grateful to receive $1,763,336 in federal funding to help move forward with planning and preliminary engineering for a future grade separation at the Wilbur Old Highway 99 and Central Oregon & Pacific Railroad crossing. This project is important to Douglas County because it addresses real concerns about emergency access, public safety, and the movement of freight through our community. We want to sincerely thank Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, along with all of Oregon’s federal delegation, for their support and for recognizing the importance of investing in transportation infrastructure in our communities. These projects take time and partnership to advance, and this funding gives us an opportunity to take a meaningful step toward finding a long-term solution. We appreciate everyone who has helped bring us to this point, and we look forward to continuing this work for the benefit of Douglas County residents and future generations,” said Douglas County Commissioner and Board Chair Tom Kress.
