title: Huffman Puts Trump Admin, Corporate Donors on Notice to Preserve Records
text:
Ahead of the 120th Congress, Ranking Member Huffman orders 36 federal agencies and private companies to preserve every record tied to Natural Resources Democrats’ investigations of the Trump administration

Washington, D.C. – Today, House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) sent letters to 36 federal agencies and private companies ordering them to preserve documents, communications, and other records tied to the Committee’s investigations of the Trump administration.

“For two years, this administration has stonewalled us and kept the American people in the dark while Democrats have fought tirelessly to daylight and stop their corruption. Those days of obstruction are over.” said Ranking Member Huffman. “I am sending a message to President Trump and his allies: our investigations will continue full steam ahead. And to every agency official and corporate executive receiving these letters: save everything. The American people deserve to know what you did with their government and their money, and we intend to get them answers.”

The letters seek to safeguard evidence gathered or sought during the Committee’s investigations in the 119th Congress so those inquiries can continue in the new Congress. Federal agencies are directed to preserve records covered by the Federal Records Act, along with documents, communications, and other materials relevant to congressional oversight. Private companies that have been subjects of Committee inquiries also received preservation requests.

In the letters, Huffman wrote, “For the past two years, the Trump administration has repeatedly failed to provide Congress with information necessary to conduct its oversight responsibilities and obstructed numerous congressional investigations.”

The preservation letters come amid reports that the Department of the Interior and other federal agencies may already be engaging in preemptive coverups by shredding official documents and using disappearing chat messages, raising concerns that evidence could be lost before investigators can obtain it. Those reports add urgency to securing the records Congress needs to investigate allegations of corruption and misconduct.

The American people deserve to know how decisions were made, whose interests they served, and how taxpayer resources were used. These letters are an early step toward ensuring that the incoming Congress can get those answers.

Federal agency recipients included the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA), Bureau of Land Management (BLM), National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), National Park Service (NPS), U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC), U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and U.S. Forest Service (USFS). Private sector and nonprofit recipients included Boeing, Chevron, Deloitte, Energy Fuels, Exiger, ExxonMobil, iHeartMedia, January AI, John Deere, Lithium Americas, Lockheed Martin, Mastercard, Mosaic, Northrop Grumman, Oracle, Palantir, Penske, Phorm Energy, RTX, SAP, SoftBank, TikTok Inc., TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC, Trust for the National Mall, UFC, United Airlines, and UnitedHealth Group.

title: JEFFRIES, SCHUMER STATEMENT FOLLOWING DEMOCRATIC LEADERSHIP MEETING
text:
UPDATE: Termination of Temporary Protected Status for Haitians and Syrians

On Tuesday, June 25, 2026, the Supreme Court ruled that the Trump administration could move forward with its plans to rip legal status away from nearly 350,000 current Haitian and Syrian Temporary Protected Status (TPS) holders. Following this decision, the Department of Homeland Security announced the termination of TPS for Haitians and Syrians, effective July 27, 2026.

Individuals who have lost TPS may be impacted in different ways, including loss of protection from deportation and loss of work authorization. However, there may be alternative legal pathways to remain and work in the United States. To learn more about what the end of TPS means for you and your family:

All TPS holders regardless of designation should visit the USCIS website for the latest updates on their TPS status.

Visit the NYC Mayor’s Office of Immigration Affairs website to learn more about what the expiration of TPS status means for impacted New Yorkers. Resource documents are available in English, Arabic, French and Haitian Creole.

Contact the Mayor’s Office of Immigrant Affairs (MOIA), whose Legal Support Centers offer free, confidential immigration legal help. Free, safe and confidential immigration legal services are available regardless of your immigration status and in your language by calling the MOIA legal support hotline at 800-354-0365 or visiting nyc.gov/knowyourrights.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON CBS: “WE’RE COMMITTED TO ACCOUNTABILITY AND TO HOLDING THE CROOKS ACCOUNTABLE”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on CBS Mornings, where he emphasized that Democrats are committed to holding the crooks accountable that are ripping off the American people and lowering the high cost of living.

NORAH O’DONNELL: Joining us now is the current House Democratic Leader, New York Congressman Hakeem Jeffries. He’s expected to become Speaker of the House in January. Leader Jeffries, good to see you. Welcome.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Good morning, great to be with you.

NORAH O’DONNELL: Well, you heard the President. He says he’s willing to work with Democrats on the issue of immigration. What do you think that looks like?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we clearly have a broken immigration system that needs to be fixed in a comprehensive way. ICE is way out of control. We need to put an end to Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine. And then we can find a path forward to make sure that immigration enforcement is fair, it’s just and humane. We can begin by moving in the House, and ultimately in the Senate, the Dream and Promise Act in order to restore protection for DACA recipients and TPS recipients, and that should be a foundation for more, broader work that can be done together.

NORAH O’DONNELL: And yet, while you say you’re willing to work with the President, you have said you’re not willing to work with his new Chief of Staff, Stephen Miller, who is behind some of these toughest immigration enforcement policies. You’ve called him a ‘dangerous xenophobe,’ ‘a reckless extremist who has American blood on his hands’ and it should be—’he should be eradicated like a malignant tumor. Fire him today.’ So, how are you going to work together?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We can work with the administration to the extent that they are willing to do things that make life more affordable for the American people and solve the problems that the American people have clearly demanded we address, as a result of the resounding results from Tuesday, without having to work with someone who is so clearly unqualified. And absolutely, in the context of being the architect of the violent mass deportation machine, it is fair to say that Stephen Miller has blood on his hands when we saw taxpayer dollars being used to brutalize and kill American citizens like Renee Nicole Good and Alex Pretti and violently target law-abiding immigrant communities.

GAYLE KING: Let’s move on to the news this morning, Hakeem Jeffries good to see you, Mr. Leader—about Jensen Huang and the breaking news there that he apparently had, that he may have had a relationship with a Chinese spy. What is your take on that? What do you think needs to be done there?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I haven’t been fully briefed on that issue. However, we are having a classified briefing later on today with some high-level members of the administration. I’m sure that this is an issue that will come up, and I’ll be prepared to address it more decisively subsequent to that classified briefing.

NORAH O’DONNELL: Well, let me ask you, though, Leader, President Trump was briefed a year ago that U.S. intelligence had electronic surveillance of this Chinese spy and that she was having a relationship with the CEO of NVIDIA. Then this spring, the Secretary of State Marco Rubio wrote a highly classified memo also about this relationship. Do you believe that damage was done to U.S. national security and that these high-end classified chips were provided to the Chinese government?

GAYLE KING: And did you see the memo?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I have not seen the memo. And, as I indicated, this is information that has not made its way to the Congress, certainly congressional leaders, in terms of any information that has ever been presented to us in either a classified or a non-classified setting. And I don’t believe that that information has been presented to the leaders of the Intel committees, whether they be Democrats and Republicans. It just so happens that we have a classified briefing later on today. This will certainly be an area that is discussed and a significant issue of concern.

GAYLE KING: Let’s move on to the issue of corruption. Jamie Raskin has made it clear that Democrats are going to go after corruption in the Trump administration. They talked about that on 60 Minutes last night. I’m curious about your feelings about that. Can we play a clip from the 60 Minutes interview about corruption?

RECORDING OF ROSS DOUTHAT: Your son manages or helps manage a cryptocurrency company called World Liberty Financial—

RECORDING OF DONALD TRUMP: Which son are we talking about?

RECORDING OF ROSS DOUTHAT: You are a co-owner of that company. Right?

RECORDING OF DONALD TRUMP: That’s correct.

RECORDING OF ROSS DOUTHAT: That’s correct, right? This company is also partially owned by investors connected to the government of the United Arab Emirates. I think if I told you that story, and it was about the Biden family, if I said Joe Biden is the part-owner of a company and it has all of these investments from the Middle East, you would say that sounds corrupt, right?

RECORDING OF DONALD TRUMP: Well, he did have a lot of different things—

RECORDING OF ROSS DOUTHAT: Sure, but you—

RECORDING OF DONALD TRUMP: But here’s the difference—

RECORDING OF ROSS DOUTHAT: But why is it different for you?

RECORDING OF DONALD TRUMP: Well, here’s, I’ll tell you why, because I know nothing about it.

GAYLE KING: Does that answer satisfy you?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Certainly, I think it leaves a lot to be desired. We have to do three things and are committed to doing three things as House Democrats. We’ve got to fight to make life more affordable for the American people. Far too many people all across this country—they’re working hard, they’re playing by the rules, but they’re struggling. They can’t thrive, and they can barely survive. We’ve got to turn that situation around—lower the high costs of gas and groceries and housing and make healthcare affordable for every single American. At the same period of time, we’ve seen unprecedented corruption unleashed on the American people. And we’ve got to get to the bottom of it so we can actually deliver a government that is committed to solving problems for hardworking American taxpayers as opposed to enriching folks, their family members, their friends or their donors. So I think that Jamie—

GAYLE KING: Do you think the House can do both things? Because there’s a lot of fatigue with corruption, investigations. The American people, as you said, have spoken. What they want—they want the country back on track. It really boils down to gas and groceries and how much everybody’s paying. Can the Congress do both things at the same time, do you think?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Yes, and we have to. So we’re going to focus aggressively and relentlessly on dealing with the affordability crisis. At the same period of time, we’re committed to accountability and to holding the crooks accountable if you’ve been stealing from the American people, screwing over the American people or shortchanging the American people, so we can actually focus on the things that matter in terms of solving problems for hardworking American taxpayers. We’re going to follow the facts, apply the law, be guided by the Constitution and then let the chips fall where they may, so we can deliver a government of the people, by the people and for the people.

NORAH O’DONNELL: And Leader Jeffries, one of the areas where the American people want progress is on healthcare, the high cost of healthcare, premiums going up double digits. You had a number of Democratic candidates, both in the House and the Senate, win by campaigning on something called Medicare for All. Will you support that? What kind of change will you lead on?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I think all across the ideological spectrum, House Democrats are definitively committed to making sure that every single American can get access to high-quality and affordable healthcare. Now, in terms of the initial steps that we’ve promised to take, we’ve got to reverse the Medicaid cuts that are devastating people all across this country, including in rural America, forcing hospitals to close at record levels. We’ve got to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits so that we can provide relief to tens of millions of Americans who’ve been experiencing skyrocketing premiums, in some cases over $1,000 a month in terms of increase. That’s unacceptable—

NORAH O’DONNELL: I hear you, but what about Medicare for All?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Right. And what I’m saying is that, and what we will do is then have a family conversation, Democrats in the House with Democrats in the Senate, led by our committee chairs in the House—that will be Richie Neal and Frank Pallone and in the Senate that’s Ron Wyden and Bernie Sanders—to see what kind of consensus we can come to with respect to our shared commitment around universal access to high-quality and affordable healthcare.

GAYLE KING: Sometimes family conversations, as you know, can be difficult. Right now, you are the lead candidate for the Speaker position. Are you ready? Something you want?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’re going to work hard to bring the country together. I put it in the hands of the American people. We also have to fight for a restoration of American values, and that’s something that I’m committed to accomplishing. That’s equal protection under the law. That’s liberty and justice for all. That’s a return to our great heritage as a nation of immigrants. And that certainly is making sure we protect the right to vote for everyone.

GAYLE KING: Alright, Leader Jeffries, right now we’ll just say congratulations because it was a huge night for the Democrats. Thank you so much for your time this morning.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Thank you.

Full interview can be watched here.

title: Congressman Jonathan L. Jackson Condemns Trump Administration’s Decision to Remove South Africa from AGOA, Warns of Damage to U.S.–Africa Relations
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Contact:

James Gomez, Senior Policy Advisor, James.Gomez@mail.house.gov

Sydney Broome, Communications Director, Sydney.Broome@mail.house.gov

November 6, 2026

Congressman Jonathan L. Jackson Condemns Trump Administration’s Decision to Remove South Africa from AGOA, Warns of Damage to U.S.–Africa Relations

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Jonathan L. Jackson today expressed strong opposition to the Trump administration’s decision to terminate South Africa’s participation in the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), effective January 1, 2027, warning that the action threatens decades of economic cooperation, undermines U.S. engagement with Africa, and places American strategic interests at risk.

“President Trump’s decision to remove South Africa from AGOA is a deeply troubling step backward in America’s relationship with the African continent. Rather than strengthening our economic partnerships and advancing shared prosperity, this administration is choosing a path that risks alienating one of Africa’s most important economic partners.

“AGOA was established to promote economic growth, expand trade, encourage investment, and create opportunities for both African and American businesses. It represents more than a trade preference program; it is an important instrument of American diplomacy and a tangible demonstration of our commitment to Africa’s economic development.

“South Africa is a major U.S. trading partner and an important regional economic power. Punishing the country through the withdrawal of trade benefits risks hurting workers, farmers, manufacturers, entrepreneurs, and businesses on both sides of the Atlantic. It also creates opportunities for other global powers, particularly China, to expand their economic influence across the continent at America's expense.

“As a member of Congress committed to strengthening U.S.–Africa relations, I believe our foreign policy must be guided by diplomacy, mutual respect, economic cooperation, and a recognition of Africa's growing importance in global affairs. Disagreements between governments should be addressed through constructive engagement and dialogue, not through measures that jeopardize longstanding economic relationships.

“I am particularly concerned that this decision could undermine the confidence of African nations in the United States as a reliable and consistent economic partner. At a time when the United States should be deepening its engagement with Africa, strengthening commercial ties, and competing for investment and strategic partnerships, we should not be closing doors.

“I call on the Trump administration to reconsider this decision, engage directly and constructively with the South African government, and work toward a diplomatic resolution that preserves South Africa’s participation in AGOA.

“Congress must also exercise its oversight responsibilities to ensure that decisions affecting our trade relationships and strategic partnerships with African nations are transparent, consistent with the law, and aligned with America's long-term interests.

“America's relationship with Africa must be built on partnership, not punishment; mutual respect, not confrontation; and shared economic opportunity, not exclusion. We cannot afford to turn our backs on South Africa or undermine the broader U.S.–Africa partnership.”

title: Kaptur Applauds $500,000 US DOJ Investment in Legal Aid of Western Ohio
text:
Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, announced that Legal Aid of Western Ohio will receive a $500,000 award through the US Department of Justice’s (DOJ) Office for Victims of Crime. The award will be used to increase the quality and quantity of victim support services for victims of domestic violence, elder abuse, stalking, financial exploitation, and other crimes.

“Strengthening our region’s access to quality, affordable legal services, and support for victims of crime is vital. We must empower our neighbors with the resources they need to have stability and success, and promote safety and security for those who have experienced terrible things” said Congresswoman Kaptur (OH-09). “I am honored to play a role in securing support and funding for organizations like Legal Aid of Western Ohio that are doing the hard work in Northwest Ohio to protect and advocate for those who need help most.”

Legal Aid of Western Ohio (LAWO) has long provided critical legal assistance to low-income residents across 32 counties in western and northern Ohio. Their support services focus on tangible legal aid including representing clients in civil matters, securing protection orders and custody agreements, and offering legal consultation.

As a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, Congresswoman Kaptur has advocated for increased Federal support for legal aid services throughout Northwest Ohio. In July 2026, she announced $1.3 Million in US DOJ funding for LAWO to increase services for victims of abuse and violence, particularly those that are over the age of 50 or living with disabilities. In 2025, she secured a $500,000 US Department of Veteran’s Affairs award for LAWO combat veteran homelessness.

If you or someone you know needs legal assistance, you can visit LAWO’s Legal Aid Line by clicking here.

title: AXIOS Boston: Massachusetts Democrats eye power in new Congress
text:
Massachusetts’ members of Congress will head back to a changed Washington next year, with Democrats in the majority and the Bay State’s delegation wielding considerable influence.

Why it matters: Massachusetts members could help steer the House floor, push legislation through committees and shape the Democratic agenda leading up to 2028.

The big picture: Leadership and committee picks are still to be made, but Massachusetts is fielding a very powerful team:

Katherine Clark is expected to become House majority leader, the first woman in the job.

Richard Neal is expected to return as Ways and Means chair, overseeing taxes and trade.

Jim McGovern is expected to reclaim the Rules chairmanship, which governs how bills reach floor votes.

Elizabeth Warren is positioned to chair Senate Banking and could angle for Democrats’ third top leadership spot.

Between the lines: How they use that clout, and whether they all agree, may signal where the Democratic Party heads before 2028.

Our delegation has factions.

Ed Markey and Ayanna Pressley carry national progressive followings energized by Democrats’ huge win.

Clark, Neal and McGovern are insiders tasked with moving legislation.

Jake Auchincloss will return to Washington as a leader of the party’s more moderate wing who just helped some new members get elected.

State of play: Newcomers, veterans and rising voices add to the mix.

Lori Trahan has worked with Republican Jay Obernolte on the FRONTIER Act, a bipartisan AI regulation framework. If Democrats set up a select committee on AI, Trahan could be on the shortlist to chair it.

Stephen Lynch and Bill Keating bring oversight and national security experience.

And there’s fresh blood in the form of Dan Koh, who won the 6th District to replace Seth Moulton.

Reality check: Donald Trump remains president. Democrats can set agendas, investigate the administration and negotiate spending, but can’t enact priorities over his veto.

What’s next: Sherrod Brown’s return to the Senate could complicate Warren’s Banking gavel.

We’ll be watching which subcommittee roles Lynch and Keating end up with, given Clark’s heightened authority.

The bottom line: The delegation will be punching above its weight, but D.C. clout doesn’t necessarily translate into tangible gains for Bay State residents.

title: Kelly applauds newly designated Opportunity Zones in Pennsylvania's 16th Congressional District
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Today, U.S. Representative Mike Kelly (R-PA), Chairman of the Ways & Means Subcommittee on Tax, applauded the U.S. Treasury Department's and IRS's designation of new Qualified Opportunity Zones (QOZs) beginning in 2027.

In all, 18 new Qualified Opportunity Zones have been designated across Pennsylvania's 16th Congressional District covering all six counties. More than 6,500 communities across the United States received QOZ designations this year.

"Opportunity Zones have been an incredible success in communities across the country since they were first created in the 2017 Tax Cuts & Jobs Act. Now, thanks to the passage of the Working Families Tax Cuts last year, rural communities across our region will be able to benefit, as well," said Rep. Kelly. "This policy puts private dollars, not taxpayer dollars, to work in our communities. I've been proud to support it, and I'm excited to partner with our local leaders to turn dreams into reality."

As Chairman of the Ways & Means Subcommittee on Tax, Rep. Kelly has led Opportunity Zones legislation in Congress. In 2025, The Working Families Tax Cuts (WFTC) made permanent and expanded Rep. Kelly's Opportunity Zones (OZ) legislation, which encourages private investment in low-income and rural communities. The WFTC expanded Opportunity Zones to cover rural communities, defined as any city or town with a population less than 50,000.

Locally, the City of Erie's Opportunity Zones, located in the downtown's 16501 ZIP code, remains a national model for the success of this program.

title: Latta, Peters Applaud House Passage of Nuclear REFUEL Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Congressman Bob Latta (R-OH-5) and Congressman Scott Peters (D-CA-50) released the following statements after the passage of their bipartisan Nuclear REFUEL Act on the floor of the House of Representatives by a vote of 397 to 2:

"The nuclear industry will continue to play a vital role in meeting the rising demand for power across our country," said Congressman Latta. "The Nuclear REFUEL Act will help streamline nuclear licensing for nuclear fuel recycling facilities and foster increased growth for this critical component of our power generation base. It is critical we work to promote safe nuclear technologies to advance American innovation, increase energy production, and lower costs. I'm proud to see my and Congressman Peters' legislation pass the House, and I'm thankful for Senators Husted and Whitehouse for their partnership on this bill in the Senate. I urge the Senate to take up this legislation and pass it expediently."

“Our bipartisan Nuclear REFUEL Act transforms what was once a liability into a resource. Reusing spent nuclear fuel for emission-free power is a win for clean energy, a win for the environment, and a win for public health. I’m glad to see this bill pass the House with support from both parties and bring us one step closer to a cleaner future,” said Congressman Peters.

Background:

Nuclear fuel recycling technology, known as pyroprocessing, creates a uranium-transuranic (U/TRU) mixed fuel that can be used by advanced fast reactors to make energy while reducing the amount of nuclear waste.

Currently, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission does not clearly state which regulatory pathway they will use to license recycling facilities that do not separate plutonium. They could be licensed under two categories: Part 50 or Part 70. Part 50 is typically targeted towards reactors (licensing utilization and production facilities), while Part 70 licensing focuses on fuel cycle (licensing uranium enrichment or fuel fabrication facilities).

The Nuclear REFUEL Act will clarify that a U/TRU facility would be licensed only under Part 70, which is a single-step licensing process and would significantly streamline the licensing requirements for fuel recycling facilities which will revitalize domestic investment in nuclear energy.

title: Liccardo & Crow Launch Discharge Petition to Force Vote on Protections for Afghan Allies
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressmen Sam Liccardo (CA-16) Jason Crow (CO-06) filed a discharge petition to force a House vote on the bipartisan Afghanistan TPS Act of 2026, legislation that would restore Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for more than 9,000 Afghans at risk of deportation after the Trump administration stripped their protections last year. Upon securing 218 signatures, the discharge petition will bypass House leadership and bring the bipartisan legislation to the House Floor for a vote.

Congressman Sam Liccardo released the following statement:

“This is about America keeping our word. Thousands of Afghans risked their lives alongside American troops because our country made them a promise: We would not abandon them. Now, we risk sending them back into the hands of the very Taliban forces they helped us fight. This cannot wait until the Democratic majority takes over—we need to reinstate Temporary Protected Status immediately and keep our friends safe.”

Congressman Jason Crow released the following statement:

“Our Afghan partners put their lives on the line to help protect American servicemembers like me. After more than two decades of war, we made a promise that we’d look after them. It’s both a moral and national security imperative that we keep that promise. I’m working to force a vote that will protect Afghans already in the United States because I won’t let our nation leave these brave Afghans behind.”

After the withdrawal from Afghanistan, the Department of Homeland Security granted more than 9,000 Afghans Temporary Protected Status (TPS) to seek refuge in the United States. Many of these individuals served alongside U.S. forces, making them particularly vulnerable to Taliban retaliation if deported.

On May 12, 2025, the Trump administration formally announced the termination of TPS for Afghanistan leaving thousands of Afghans at risk of deportation. The deadly impacts have already begun. Other Afghans facing deportation have expressed they’d rather take their own lives than return and face the Taliban’s wrath. Last week, the Trump administration began the process of deporting Afghan refugees. A federal judge in New York blocked the move which would have put Afghan refugees directly in the Taliban’s path. Liccardo and Crow’s discharge petition will be critical for the continued protection of our allies.

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces Bill to Make Sure No Veteran Navigates Maternal Care Alone
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (Nov. 9, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace (SC-01) introduced the Supporting Veteran Mothers Act of 2026, legislation requiring Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) medical facilities to maintain sufficient staffing levels of maternity care coordinators to ensure pregnant and postpartum veterans receive the care and support they deserve.

Our veterans answered the call to serve this country. When they become mothers, they should not have to fight their own government to receive maternity care.

The measure ensures the VA has the capabilities needed to support veteran mothers. Specifically, it sets minimum staffing requirements for maternity care coordinators, ensuring facilities have dedicated personnel to coordinate care from pregnancy confirmation through the postpartum period.

“Pregnancy and the postpartum period are some of the most physically and emotionally demanding times in a woman's life,” said Congresswoman Mace. “Women who served this country should never have to navigate those challenges without the support and care they deserve. We owe these women access to the care they need, when they need it. Our legislation puts real staffing requirements in place, demands accountability from the VA and makes sure veteran mothers are not left navigating the system alone.”

A Government Accountability Office (GAO) report earlier this year found the VA Maternity Care Coordinator program lacks clear standards and a performance management process. Without them, the program has no reliable way to measure results. The VA agreed with the finding in its comments. This bill closes the gap.

The Supporting Veteran Mothers Act would:

Establish minimum staffing requirements: Require covered VA medical facilities to maintain at least one full-time maternity care coordinator for every 75 to 100 patients annually, with dedicated maternity care responsibilities.

Require regular staffing reviews: Direct VA facilities to review maternity care coordinator staffing levels at least once every two years and document patient volume and staffing assignments.

Demand corrective action: Require facilities that fall short of staffing requirements to correct course, submitting and implementing plans outlining necessary staffing adjustments, timelines, and resources.

Increase congressional oversight: Require annual reports to the House and Senate Veterans' Affairs Committees detailing staffing levels, facility compliance, corrective action plans and coordinator capacity.

Make information public: Require the VA to publish public summaries of its annual reports.

The legislation specifically applies to VA medical facilities with more than 100 patients and requires the VA Secretary to issue initial implementation guidance within 180 days of enactment.

title: ICYMI: Harris Lays Out the Job Ahead for House Republicans in Washington Examiner Op-Ed
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — On Friday, Congressman Mark Harris (NC-08) penned an op-ed in the Washington Examiner outlining the work House Republicans must finish in the remaining days of their majority. Read the full op-ed here or below:

“On Tuesday night, the country watched as the American people made their choice for the makeup of the next Congress. It was not the outcome any of us in the Republican Party wanted, especially knowing that many of my colleagues will not be joining us in the 120th Congress. The next two years will be a completely different environment as we expect the Democrat Party to fight with President Donald Trump every step of the way, using every trick and investigation in the book to disrupt his agenda and the remainder of his term.

“But our work is not finished. In the remaining hours of our Republican majority, it is not the time to wave the white flag to the Left. It is time to finish the job.

“Starting on Nov. 9, we have 20 days left on the legislative calendar and a handful of unfinished business on the table, including a looming government funding deadline and a powerhouse reconciliation bill that will protect the conservative wins we have secured.

“The House Appropriations Committee has advanced all 12 fiscal 2027 funding bills, but only three have passed the House as the clock ticks toward the beginning of December. As we have seen with the two manufactured Democrat government shutdowns this year, the paychecks, benefits, and essential services Americans rely on are at stake when Washington fails to meet its due dates.

“At the same time, our nation is currently facing a staggering debt of nearly $41 trillion, and we now spend over $1 trillion a year just on interest. This Congress, House Republicans reversed the status quo — securing $1.1 trillion in spending cuts made possible by the Working Families Tax Cuts. From cracking down on taxpayer-funded health care for illegal aliens to rolling back Green New Deal subsidies, we proved that a disciplined, conservative approach to the budget can successfully push back against decades of Washington’s bad habits.

“As a member who came to Congress to do government differently and rein in reckless spending, I will not allow that to be thrown away because of an election outcome. We have an opportunity to finish the appropriations process in a fiscally responsible way and pass another reconciliation bill that further roots out the waste, fraud, and abuse that have drained taxpayer dollars and made it increasingly difficult to fund the programs Americans depend on.

“Our constituents did not send us to Washington to stop fighting just because the political landscape has shifted. They elected us to be good stewards of their hard-earned tax dollars, a responsibility that does not end until the very last moment we hold the gavel. Walking away now leaves the country vulnerable to more out-of-control spending. We owe the families we represent a secure financial future.”

title: Rep. Massie Forcing House of Representatives to Vote on Impeaching Secretary Hegseth
text:
Washington, D.C.- Representative Thomas Massie (R-KY), a member of the House Judiciary Committee, announces he is forcing a vote in the House of Representatives to impeach Secretary of Defense Peter Hegseth. Among his charges, Rep. Massie asserts that Secretary Hegseth is violating three specific provisions of the War Powers Resolution of 1973. Rep. Massie's actions today will force the House to vote on eight specific impeachment charges against the Secretary of Defense.

"By engaging in hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorization, Secretary Hegseth is breaking the law and must be held accountable," said Rep. Thomas Massie. "Secretary Hegseth's constitutional violations extend beyond the illegal war in Iran. He is abusing the power of his office to ignore congressional war powers resolutions, to kidnap foreign leaders, and to intimidate critics of the Trump administration by retaliating against them for exercising free speech. If we are to remain true to our oath to 'support and defend the Constitution of the United States,' the House of Representatives must act."

"My effort to impeach Secretary Hegseth is a much gentler version of what's coming when the Democrats assume control of the House and Senate next year," Rep. Massie continued. "They will hold hearings and trials. President Trump should replace Secretary Hegseth now while he can still get a replacement confirmed in the Senate."

The impeachment charges brought against Secretary Hegseth are summarized as follows:

Article I - Waging War in Contravention of the War Powers Resolution of 1973 Section 2(c): Charges Secretary Hegseth with waging the Iran war despite no declaration of war, statutory authorization, attack on the United States, or imminent threat. It establishes that the war was unlawful from its inception.

Article II - Waging War in Contravention of the War Powers Resolution of 1973 Section 5(c): Charges Secretary Hegseth with continuing the Iran war after both Houses of Congress directed the removal of U.S. forces through H. Con. Res. 86. It focuses on his refusal to obey Congress’s express direction to terminate unauthorized hostilities.

Article III - Waging War in Contravention of the War Powers Resolution of 1973 Section 5(b): Charges Secretary Hegseth with continuing hostilities in Iran after expiration of the War Powers Resolution’s 60-day termination period and any potential 30-day withdrawal period. It establishes that he treated mandatory statutory deadlines as discretionary.

Article IV - Ignoring Laws that Minimize Civilian Casualties: Charges Secretary Hegseth with ignoring laws that minimize civilian casualties.

Article V - Extrajudicial Killings: Charges Secretary Hegseth with replacing maritime law enforcement with unauthorized lethal military targeting of suspected drug traffickers, resulting in at least 243 deaths. It also addresses denial of quarter, secondary strikes on survivors, failure to rescue shipwrecked persons, and the creation of artificial legal authorities for the campaign.

Article VI - Suppressing Free Speech: Charges Secretary Hegseth with using DOD authority to retaliate against and intimidate Senator Mark Kelly for constitutionally protected speech questioning unlawful military orders.

Article VII - Kidnapping of a Sovereign Foreign Leader: Charges Secretary Hegseth with directing Operation ABSOLUTE RESOLVE to seize Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores in Venezuela without constitutional or legal authority.

Article VIII - Unlawful War in Yemen: Charges Secretary Hegseth with initiating Operation ROUGH RIDER without congressional authorization or an imminent threat to the United States, while also violating war powers reporting requirements.

title: McClellan, Warner, Kaine Press Social Security Administration on Abrupt Defunding of VCU Disability Benefits Support Program
text:
Washington D.C. – Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) and U.S. Senators Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) raised concerns about the Social Security Administration’s (SSA) abrupt decision to halt funding for the Work Incentives Planning and Assistance (WIPA) program’s National Training and Data Center (NTDC) at Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU), threatening critical services that help Americans with disabilities navigate Social Security benefits while seeking employment.

The NTDC provides training, certification, and technical assistance to more than 900 benefits counselors serving individuals with disabilities across the country. On October 2, 2026, SSA abruptly declined to fund VCU’s contract for another year and ordered the university to immediately halt work, disrupting essential training and support services for 74 WIPA projects nationwide.

In a letter to SSA Commissioner Frank Bisignano, the lawmakers demanded an explanation for the decision and pressed the agency to clarify how it intends to restore these critical services and fulfill its statutory obligations.

The lawmakers wrote, “We write to inquire about the Social Security Administration’s (SSA) decision to defund the Work Incentives Planning and Assistance program’s (WIPA) National Training and Data Center (NTDC). We are aware that on Friday, October 2, 2026, the SSA exercised its option not to extend its contract with Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU) to administer the NTDC and ordered VCU to immediately halt all work providing Community Work Incentives Coordinators (CWICs) nationwide with training, certification, technical assistance, and other resource support.”

The WIPA program helps individuals who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) due to severe, long-term medical conditions understand how employment may affect their benefits. Benefits counselors provide free, individualized guidance to help Americans with disabilities pursue employment opportunities without inadvertently jeopardizing the benefits they rely on.

The lawmakers continued, “CWICs at WIPA projects help bridge the information gap for beneficiaries by looking at their individual circumstances and advising them on how to maintain their benefits while working. To ensure the efficacy of the WIPA programs, the law also required SSA to establish a corps of work incentives specialists and provide training and technical assistance for those specialists. CWICs provide information and resources to help beneficiaries make informed decisions on returning to work.”

Despite Congress appropriating $23 million for the WIPA program in Fiscal Year 2026, SSA’s decision has left benefits counselors nationwide without access to necessary training resources, certification services, performance data, and institutional knowledge. These resources are critical to training new counselors and ensuring that both new and existing counselors provide accurate, reliable guidance to Americans with disabilities. The sudden loss of these services raises serious concerns about SSA’s ability to meet its statutory obligations and ensure that beneficiaries continue receiving the support they need.

The lawmakers pressed SSA to explain the rationale and timing of its decision, identify what training and certification resources remain available to benefits counselors, address disruptions to required performance reporting, and clarify whether the agency intends to restore these services through VCU, bring them in-house, or award a new contract.

Read the full letter here and below.

Dear Commissioner Bisignano,

We write to inquire about the Social Security Administration’s (SSA) decision to defund the Work Incentives Planning and Assistance program’s (WIPA) National Training and Data Center (NTDC). We are aware that on Friday, October 2, 2026, the SSA exercised its option not to extend its contract with Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU) to administer the NTDC and ordered VCU to immediately halt all work providing Community Work Incentives Coordinators (CWICs) nationwide with training, certification, technical assistance, and other resource support.

Disabled beneficiaries who qualify for SSDI or SSI benefits are among the most vulnerable populations who suffer from severe, long-term medical conditions. To maintain compliance, beneficiaries must navigate a series of strict and complex requirements set out by the Social Security Act, including on earned income. For beneficiaries who need to earn extra income to support themselves or their families, incorrectly interpreting the rules can lead to a termination of benefits.

The Ticket to Work and Work Incentives Improvement Act of 1999 directed the Commissioner of Social Security to establish a program to provide information about work and benefits to people who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) because of a disability. Using that authority, SSA established 74 WIPA projects in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and U.S. territories. WIPA projects and community organizations employ over 900 benefits counselors who provide free in-depth counseling to disabled beneficiaries on the effect of work on their SSDI or SSI benefits.

CWICs at WIPA projects help bridge the information gap for beneficiaries by looking at their individual circumstances and advising them on how to maintain their benefits while working. To ensure the efficacy of the WIPA programs, the law also required SSA to establish a corps of work incentives specialists and provide training and technical assistance for those specialists. CWICs provide information and resources to help beneficiaries make informed decisions on returning to work.

In Fiscal Year 2026 Congress appropriated $23 million to operate the WIPA program, 0.1 percent of SSA’s annual administrative budget. However, despite clear Congressional intent in support of the WIPA program, SSA has decided to unilaterally disband a vital component of the program. Without the NTDC, WIPA projects nationwide have lost access to valuable training resources and performance data to train new CWICs and ensure both new and existing Coordinators provide accurate and relevant information to beneficiaries. WIPA projects are also losing access to an invaluable source of institutional knowledge.

After this abrupt decision, it is unclear how SSA intends to comply with the statutory requirements of the Ticket to Work and Work Incentives Improvement Act of 1999 and Congressional intent set out in the Fiscal Year 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act.

title: RELEASE: Congressman Menefee Demands Trump’s EPA Release Long-Delayed Health Risk Report as Fifth Ward Families Continue to Die of Cancer
text:
HOUSTON, TX — Today, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) stood alongside Fifth Ward and Kashmere Gardens residents, community advocates, and local elected officials to demand that the Trump administration's Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) immediately release a long-delayed health risk evaluation of the contaminated Union Pacific rail yard and former Houston Wood Preserving Works site.

In conjunction with the press conference, Rep. Menefee sent a new letter to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin and Region 6 Administrator Scott Mason IV demanding the immediate release of the report, a 60-day public comment period, and a firm timeline for its completion. The Congressman gave EPA until December 1, 2026, to respond in writing, warning that he would use every tool available to him in the next Congress if the agency continues to withhold answers.

The press conference came 396 days after EPA received a draft of the health risk evaluation on October 9, 2025, with residents still waiting to learn what years of testing mean for their health, their homes, and their families.

“Trump’s Environmental Protection Agency has sat on a draft health risk assessment for 396 days. The families who live beside the rail yard have never seen it,” said Congressman Menefee. “So I'm here today as the congressman for this neighborhood to demand that EPA release the draft and start the public comment period.”

For decades, residents of Fifth Ward and Kashmere Gardens have raised concerns about contamination from the former wood treatment facility, which left behind toxic chemicals in the surrounding environment. In 2019, the Texas Department of State Health Services identified significantly higher than expected rates of certain cancers in census tracts surrounding the site, validating longstanding community concerns.

In 2023, EPA entered into an agreement requiring Union Pacific to investigate contamination at the site under federal Superfund law. The resulting health risk evaluation is intended to help determine what the contamination means for residents and what steps may be necessary to protect public health.

But despite receiving the draft evaluation more than a year ago, EPA has yet to release it for public review or provide a firm timeline for its completion.

“EPA has posted soil results, but numbers on a page don't tell a mother whether her backyard is safe,” Rep. Menefee said. “No family should have to pay to guess at an answer that the administration has right now.”

Rep. Menefee first pressed EPA for answers in a July 2 letter, requesting a briefing, access to draft materials, information about any extensions requested by Union Pacific, and a timeline for the final report. EPA did not respond until September 23, 83 days later, and failed to provide a release date or the requested briefing.

In his new letter, Rep. Menefee criticized EPA for repeatedly failing to deliver on its promises to residents, who were previously told to expect the report in late 2025 or early 2026.

“The community is done waiting. As am I,” Rep. Menefee wrote.

At today's press conference, Rep. Menefee was joined by members of EPA's Community Advisory Group (CAG), including Chair Joetta Stevenson and community advocate Sandra Edwards, who have spent years fighting for transparency and accountability.

Stevenson condemned the agency's continued delays and emphasized that residents need access to the draft so independent scientists and community experts can examine the findings.

“Give us that report so we can look at it, the public can look at it and do commentary about it,” said Ms. Joetta Stevenson, Chair of EPA's Community Advisory Group. “We're not playing with you.”

For Edwards, the delay is deeply personal. Just before the press conference began, she learned that another friend had died of cancer.

“We want that report. We want our report because you came out here to get the information. Give it to us. We need it to proceed. We need to know what our future looks like. We need to know where we stand,” said Ms. Sandra Edwards, community advocate and CAG member.

While the health risk evaluation will not establish the cause of individual cancer cases or fully account for decades of historical exposure, residents say its release is an essential step toward understanding current contamination, evaluating the investigation, and determining what cleanup measures are needed.

“People in these communities are suffering, and the Environmental Protection Agency needs to do its job and get this report to communities so that they can know what's what, provide public comment, and finally get the justice that they deserve,” Rep. Menefee finished.

title: House Passes Menendez Legislation to Strengthen Nuclear Regulatory Workforce
text:
Since President Trump took office, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission has lost over 400 expert staff, significantly impacting the teams that handle safety.

WASHINGTON, D.C. - Today, the U.S. House of Representatives passed the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) Staff Pay Alignment Act, legislation introduced by Congressman Rob Menendez (NJ-08) to help recruit and retain top safety experts at the nation’s nuclear watchdog agency.

Speaking on the House Floor during debate ahead of the vote, Congressman Menendez called on his colleagues to pass the measure, highlighting the critical role nuclear regulatory oversight plays in protecting communities across the country.

Watch Congressman Menendez’s full House Floor remarks here.

“Nuclear safety demands the most qualified experts on the job, which is why I am proud to see this legislation pass the House,” said Congressman Menendez. “With nuclear energy expanding across the country to meet our growing energy demands, this legislation gives our nation’s nuclear watchdog the competitive edge it needs to stay strong, independent, and fully staffed.”

Building on the bipartisan ADVANCE Act of 2024, the bill directly addresses severe workforce strains at a time when the nuclear energy sector is rapidly expanding.

The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) Staff Pay Alignment Act would:

Authorize a 10 percent pay increase to help the NRC retain top safety experts and compete with private sector compensation for specialized nuclear engineers and inspectors.

Rebuilds core agency capacity following recent losses of key expert personnel.

Ensures reactor deployments receive rigorous safety oversight.

Congressman Menendez, a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, has consistently advocated for stringent safety standards and community protections across domestic energy infrastructure.

The NRC Staff Pay Alignment Act now advances to the U.S. Senate for consideration.

title: MENG REINTRODUCES BILL TO MAKE DIWALI A FEDERAL HOLIDAY
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — As communities across the United States and around the world gathered to celebrate Diwali yesterday, U.S. Rep. Grace Meng (D-Queens), Chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus, reintroduced the Diwali Day Act to recognize Diwali as a federal holiday.

Diwali, also known as Deepavali or the Festival of Lights, is one of the most important holidays of the year for many religious groups including Hindus, Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists as well as billions in the South Asian, Southeast Asian and Indo-Caribbean communities. While the celebration holds a different significance for these diverse religious, ethnic and cultural groups, the Festival of Lights unites those who observe with reflection, prayer and gathering with loved ones.

“Diwali represents the triumph of good over evil and knowledge over ignorance,” said Meng. “At a time when anti-Hindu and anti-South Asian hate is on the rise, recognizing Diwali as a federal holiday sends a powerful message that Hindus, as well as Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists, are valued members of our society. Here in Queens, I see firsthand how meaningful Diwali is to so many families and communities. My Diwali Day Act will help educate Americans about the importance of this day, and I will continue working to create a more inclusive nation that honors the rich cultural traditions of its people.”

Hindu and South Asian communities across the country are facing an alarming rise in hate, intimidation, and targeted violence. This includes vandalism at Hindu places of worship, an attempted mass shooting during Navratri festivities at a Hindu temple in Illinois, and the recent racist disruption of a Diwali celebration in Washington State. CAPAC has been sounding the alarm that these acts of hate must be taken seriously and investigated by federal authorities.

Under Meng’s legislation, Diwali would become the 12th federally recognized holiday in the United States. Establishing a federal holiday for Diwali, and the day off it would provide, would allow communities to celebrate and demonstrate that the government values the rich cultures and traditions of its citizens. Meng is also the author of the Lunar New Year Day Act, which would establish Lunar New Year as a federally recognized holiday.

The Diwali Day Act is co-sponsored by 19 Members of Congress, including Reps. Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Wesley Bell (MO-01), Ami Bera (CA-06), André Carson (IN-07), Judy Chu (CA-28), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Timothy Kennedy (NY-26), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Deborah Ross (NC-02), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), Tom Suozzi (NY-03), Mark Takano (CA-39), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), and Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).

The measure is also endorsed by Asian Americans Advancing Justice (AAJC), Asian American Federation (AAF), Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA), Hindus for Human Rights, Hindu Temple Society of North America, Indian American Impact, Indian Diaspora Council, Indo-Caribbean Alliance, International Commission on Dalit Rights, National Asian Pacific American Bar Association (NAPABA), National Council of Asian Pacific Americans (NCAPA), OCA-Asian Pacific American Advocates, Sikh American Legal Defense and Education Fund (SALDEF), The Sikh Cultural Society, The Sikh Coalition, South Asian Impact Foundation, and Southeast Asia Resource Action Center (SEARAC).

title: WATCH: Pressley on MS NOW: “This Is Our Moment, And We Have A Mandate From The People To Match Their Energy”
text:

WASHINGTON – In an interview today on MS NOW, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), a member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, called on Democrats to meet the moment and use their new majority to govern boldly and aggressively pursue accountability for the corruption, cruelty, and economic harm inflicted by the Trump administration over the past two years.

Transcript: Pressley on MS NOW: “This Is Our Moment, And We Have A Mandate From The People To Match Their Energy”

MS NOW

November 8, 2026

REP. PRESSLEY: Good to be with you.

REP. PRESSLEY: Well, first, let me just say I’m so grateful to this decisive mandate from the American people for the Democrats to not only demonstrate that we’re the adults in the room and know how to govern, but to prove that we are the fighters in the room.

The unconstitutional, cruel, lawless, rogue actions of this administration across the board. So we have the receipts, Jacob. The receipts are what the American people are experiencing every day.

JACOB SOBOROFF: The job is not finished.” I remember, you know, I sat in that hearing room with you and Congresswoman Ocasio-Cortez and Congressman Raskin during the first Trump term as you conducted some of those oversight hearings, and I watched them myself as part of my reporting for this network, and the first Trump administration pushed back at almost every turn, tried to stonewall. REP. So their president is the one that was trying to bribe voters in order to keep a majority. So they are desperate. We’ve got them on the ropes, we have the receipts to prove it. title: Quigley's Bill Reauthorizing ALS Research Funding Signed into Law
text:
On November 3, 2026, Chicago Congressman Mike Quigley’s bill—the Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act (ACT for ALS Reauthorization Act) of 2026—was signed into law. Led by Representatives Quigley (IL-05) and Ken Calvert (CA-41) in the House and Senators Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) and Chris Coons (D-DE) in the Senate, the law renews programs from the 2021 ACT for ALS Law.

“For the past five years, the ACT for ALS has advanced scientific research and helped people with ALS access the promising treatments they need. This reauthorization of the bill continues that work and lends hope to a future where there is a cure for ALS,” said Congressman Quigley. “I'm glad this important bill was signed into law, and I’m thankful to my colleagues in both the House and the Senate for getting this done.”

“I'm thrilled that the ACT for ALS Reauthorization Act has been signed into law, renewing our commitment to finding cures and treatments for ALS,” said Rep. Calvert. “As a Co-Chair of the bipartisan ALS Caucus, I know just how hard those impacted by ALS have worked to get this bill enacted and I applaud their tireless advocacy. With the ACT for ALS Reauthorization Act officially signed into law, we celebrate this victory while remaining focused on the work ahead to end this terrible disease.”

The ACT for ALS Reauthorization Law will codify the Department of Health and Human Services’ (HHS) interpretation of Expanded Access Program eligibility guidelines and require the FDA to create a new 5-year Action Plan for rare neurodegenerative diseases. It will also continue to advance scientific understanding of neurodegenerative diseases and help Americans living with ALS access promising new treatments.

This legislation has been endorsed by I AM ALS, the Muscular Dystrophy Association, the ALS Association, and the ALS Network.

“Over the past 7+ years, this community has changed what's possible in ALS,” said I AM ALS co-founder Brian Wallach. “The I AM ALS community's leadership has brought us closer than ever to a cure by unlocking over $2 billion for federal ALS research, expanding and protecting access to life-changing therapies, and accelerating scientific breakthroughs. We thank our ALS congressional champions—including sponsors Senators Coons (D-DE) and Murkowski (R-AK) and Representatives Quigley (D-IL-05) and Calvert (R-CA-41)—and all the tireless advocates who helped renew this historic legislation for five more years.”

“These past months didn't just get a critical bill passed; they inspired a community that continually renews itself, welcomes new advocates, develops new leaders, and ensures that every generation is ready to fight for the next breakthrough,” said Troy Fields, volunteer co-chair of the I AM ALS legislative affairs team, and person living with ALS. “ALS is relentless, but we continue to prove so are we.”

“We must accelerate research and technology to help make ALS livable and cure it. To every advocate who walked into a congressional office and wouldn't leave without a commitment: you did this. To the families who shared their hardest moments, so other families might have more time: you did this,” said Calaneet Balas, president and CEO of the ALS Association. “We're grateful to our champions on both sides of the aisle who helped make this legislation possible. People living with ALS cannot wait, and neither will we.”

“Today's signing is a defining moment for the ALS community and for everyone working toward a future without this devastating disease,” said Sharon Hesterlee, Ph.D., President and CEO of the Muscular Dystrophy Association. “The Muscular Dystrophy Association was proud to help lead the effort to reauthorize the ACT for ALS because we know that every day matters for people living with ALS. This law preserves the momentum that is driving scientific breakthroughs, expands opportunities for people to participate in research and access promising therapies, and strengthens the partnerships that will lead to the next generation of treatments. Together, we are creating a future where ALS is no longer a fatal diagnosis but a disease that can be effectively treated and ultimately cured.”

“Final passage is a major win for people living with ALS and their families, and a testament to what sustained, collective advocacy can accomplish,” said Sheri Strahl, MPH, MBA, president and CEO of ALS Network. “ALS Network has been deeply engaged throughout this process, working directly with congressional leaders, shaping policy recommendations, bringing the lived experience of people with ALS to Capitol Hill, and mobilizing advocates across the country. We are proud of the role we played alongside partners throughout the ALS community, and are deeply grateful to Representatives Calvert and Quigley, Senators Murkowski and Coons, and every advocate whose persistence helped carry this legislation across the finish line.”

title: Amata Honors the Life of Congresswoman and Educator Pat Saiki
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Uifa’atali Amata is honoring the life of Congresswoman Pat Saiki, and her years of public service and lifelong dedication to educational opportunities. At the invitation of her family, Amata was humbled to speak Saturday at the Celebration of Life at Central Union Church in Honolulu.

Honoring the life of history-making Congresswoman Pat Saiki

Remarks in celebration of Pat Saiki’s life:

Talofa lava,

I join you in honoring the precious life of a beloved friend, Patricia Saiki. Most of us knew her as Pat. She lived a remarkable life of service, much of it right here in beautiful Hawaii, first as an educator, as state legislator, as Hawaii’s first Republican Member of the U.S. House since statehood, and just the second Congresswoman in Hawaii history, then as SBA Administrator under President George H.W. Bush. She was a history-maker, a difference-maker, and a champion for opportunities in education.

Pat was an example to me in both public life and private, since I knew the person and the public figure. For instance, she was bipartisan when possible, bridging divides, bringing people together. Washington could use more of that, but she exemplified that approach to putting people first and recognizing that politics, while important, had to be kept in perspective. She could balance being direct and a truth-teller with being diplomatic and tactful. In other words, she was skilled at her public roles. What counts more, is that she put that to use for people. Her energy and drive went for the public good, always a cause or project that would help people, often in the field of education.

I knew her for decades. Through her generous spirit, she had a key role in an eventful part of my life. She was the person behind my opportunity to serve as Secretary of a National Convention. You have to understand how unheard of that was at the time for someone from American Samoa, and this was years before I was elected to Congress. It simply would not have happened without her, but to her it was just being a friend and putting in a good word, and these attributes were a way of life for her. She was a friend to her friends, and she had a lot of friends. We will hold our memories of her friendship close to our hearts.

She was a wife and mother and grandmother. To her children and her grandchildren, I know you brought her joy, and that she was more proud of you than her titles and accolades, though she deserved every accolade.

Speaking at the Celebration of Life

She left us for a better place at the age of 96, and I think a long life can be something of Heaven’s reward on earth, before the true Heavenly rewards to come.

Today, may you all feel the strong support of others around you, and feel the many prayers and thoughts for you, her closest loved ones.

May those of us here resolve to live our lives well, as she did. Her presence was a joy and help to others, and a life to be celebrated. She was a blessing to us, and may we live like her, to bless others. May God’s comfort be near to each one today as we say goodbye to our friend and loved one, in joyful hope of the resurrection, enriched by having known her.

Thank you. Soifua ma ia manuia.

###

title: Amata Pushes to Save ASG Expiring ARPA Dollars in Final Funding Bill
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Uifa’atali Amata is pushing to use the last remaining legislative path to save ASG’s expiring ARPA funds, through possible inclusion in a year-end Continuing Resolution (C.R.), often called stopgap funding, that will be necessary to extend funding into 2027 for the U.S. government.

At the same time, Congresswoman Amata is sending a letter to U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent making the same case and once again highlighting the additional challenges of an island economy that relies heavily on shipping for necessary construction materials and equipment, and the need for additional leeway to complete projects.

“We’re fighting for more time for ASG while facing a firm deadline for ARPA use,” Amata said. “The fact that there are states that also are coming up against the deadline and facing loss of funds with unfinished projects means we’re not alone in urging this extension. In addition to calling for inclusion in the funding legislation, I’m making the same case again to Secretary Bessent, urgently asking for his support in providing more time for ASG.”

The current stopgap funding measure expires on December 11, 2026. With government funding set to expire, lawmakers must act to pass either full-year appropriations bills, another stopgap, or a hybrid package to avoid a partial government shutdown.

“I’m calling for Congress to avoid a shutdown, extend federal funding across the board, and include an ARPA extension in any funding legislation,” concluded Congresswoman Amata. “This would give time for the new Congress to work together on the funding priorities the American people want and expect.”

title: Amata Thanks and Honors Veterans for Veterans Day

Thank you Veterans

You mean so much to our islands, and we appreciate your leadership and wisdom,” said Congresswoman Amata. “I am humbled to serve our Veterans on the Committee, where we constantly hear from our Veterans and work for improved performance from the VA, based on that input from Veterans and Service Organizations.

This includes their healthcare, assisting transitions out of the Armed Forces, furthering their second careers or higher education, to hospice, burial services and dignified funeral honors, as well as survivor benefits and comfort. Our Veterans should know their families are secure.

“Like so many of us in American Samoa, my father and brothers served, and we love and honor our Veterans and our military families. May God protect our Service Members, and bless and uphold our Veterans.”

On Monday, the House was scheduled to vote on the bipartisan Veterans’ Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2026. title: RILEY ANNOUNCES TOOL TO HELP UPSTATE NEW YORKERS SAVE ON UTILITY BILLS
text:
In one minute or less, new site lets NY-19 residents check eligibility for federal and state programs to lower bills, weatherize homes

WASHINGTON D.C. — Today, Congressman Josh Riley (NY-19) announced a new online tool to help Upstate New Yorkers lower their utility bills. With utility costs squeezing family budgets, many residents may qualify for assistance they don’t even know is available. By answering a few short questions at riley.house.gov/save, residents can easily see which federal and state programs they may qualify for and exactly where to apply.

“Heating bills are too high, and winter is just getting started. There’s help out there, but like most things in government, it couldn’t be more confusing, and a lot of people who qualify never even apply,” said Riley. “So my office built a tool to cut through the red tape. In about a minute, you’ll know what you’re eligible for and how to get it, so you can keep more of your hard-earned money in your pocket where it belongs.”

The tool checks eligibility for a range of energy assistance and efficiency programs, including the Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP), Emergency HEAP, EAP, EEAP, EmPower+, HEAP Clean & Tune, and the Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP). Together, these programs can help with heating costs, emergency assistance when households face a shutoff or run out of fuel, furnace and heating equipment maintenance, and home energy upgrades that lower bills over the long term.

The tool is open to all residents of New York’s 19th Congressional District and comes as the 2026–2027 HEAP season begins. Residents can access the tool at riley.house.gov/save, and constituents who need additional help or have questions about an application can contact Congressman Riley’s office at (607) 242-0200.

The new tool is the latest step in Riley’s fight to take on the utility monopolies and lower costs for Upstate families. Since taking office, Riley has:

Joined the NYSEG and Central Hudson rate cases to fight their rate hikes directly, going head-to-head with the companies on behalf of Upstate ratepayers.

Introduced the Weatherization Enhancement and Readiness Act (H.R. 1355) to help families weatherize their homes, use less energy, and lower their monthly bills.

Introduced the Keep the Lights Local Act (H.R. 5487) to end foreign ownership of American utilities.

Introduced the No Bonuses for Utility Executives Act (H.R. 6590) to ban utility executives from cashing in on bonuses while they jack up rates faster than inflation.

Introduced the No Taxes on Utility Bills Act (H.R. 8350) so families can deduct the taxes and state surcharges tacked onto their gas and electric bills.

Introduced the Lowering Utility Bills Act (H.R. 8568) to stop utility companies from overcharging customers.

Introduced the FAIR Data Act (H.R. 9655) to make sure Big Tech’s data centers pay their own way instead of sticking Upstate families and small businesses with higher energy bills.

Introduced the Smart Meter Data Privacy Protection Act (H.R. 10284) to stop utility companies from selling your personal data collected through smart meters.

title: Rep. Scholten Introduces the Counsel for Kids Act to Ensure Pro Bono Legal Services for Unaccompanied Children
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – This week, U.S. Representative Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03) introduced the Counsel for Kids Act. The legislation would guarantee pro bono, in-person, independent legal counsel to unaccompanied children as they navigate immigration proceedings.

“Kids don’t belong in immigration court, period. Full stop. But when they are forced into that situation, they should not be alone. I know firsthand from working with migrants at a community legal aid organization the difference independent, quality legal support makes,” said Congresswoman Scholten. “The Counsel for Kids Act would guarantee free access to counsel for unaccompanied minors, which will help ensure children show up to their hearings, complete the required paperwork, and move through the process in a way that reduces backlogs and keeps the system functioning. For so many of these kids, having an attorney is the difference between finding protection and being deported, and we can do better than forcing them to face that alone.”

Under current law, the Office of Refugee Resettlement within the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) is responsible for providing pro bono legal counsel for unaccompanied children “to the greatest extent practicable.” This has historically been accomplished through contracting with third party providers who are trained in representing unaccompanied children in court. However, the Trump administration has recently announced that unaccompanied children will be represented by lawyers directly employed by HHS, rather than independent, third-party providers, threatening the right to independent legal representation and opening the door to violations of attorney-client privilege. The Counsel for Kids Act provides clear directives, stating that children are to receive in-person, independent counsel without charge – leaving no room for HHS to interpret the law in a way that infringes on their legal rights.

The Trump administration has also attempted to move legal consultations for children from in-person to online platforms, which would hinder attorneys’ ability to build a relationship with the child and prepare them properly for court proceedings. This bill strengthens current law to ensure the Trump administration cannot erode the quality of legal services to unaccompanied children under what they deem to be “the greatest extent practicable.”

The Counsel for Kids Act reflects Congresswoman Scholten's commitment to providing resources and legal representation to unaccompanied migrant children.

title: Congresswoman Schrier Introduces Bill to Protect Lunch and Recess Time for Kids
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08), introduced her Healthy Meal Time Act to ensure schools schedule enough time for children to eat a balanced, nutritious meal each day. Congresswoman Schrier is joined in introducing this legislation by Congresswoman Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01).

“Kids need to have enough time to eat and play at school," said Congresswoman Schrier, M.D. "As a pediatrician and a mom, I know that students will often skip lunch and rush to recess without eating enough. I am proud to introduce this bill to make sure our kids have the time they need to eat a nutritious meal at school. Creating schedules that ensure kids have enough time to eat and exercise will help them focus in school and stay healthy.”

The Healthy Meal Time Act would direct the U.S. Department of Agriculture, with input from the U.S. Department of Education, to create a study to share successful efforts and current best practices with schools surrounding meal and recess timing. Currently, no federal guidelines surrounding adequate school lunch times exist.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends that students have a minimum of 20 minutes of seated eating time at lunch. This legislation would require best practices to take into account this CDC recommendation, the time it takes for non-eating activities, and the time it takes to eat minimally processed and unprocessed foods.

“School meal times let students refuel and refresh their growing brains, and learning is limited when kids don't have enough food or time to eat. The Healthy Meal Time Act would establish best practices for lunch timing and length, giving schools key guidance and resources to make the best decisions for their students,” said Congresswoman Bonamici.

“Providing nutritious school meals is essential, but children also need adequate time to eat and benefit from them,” said Tamara Randall, MS, RDN, LD, CDCES, FAND, president of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics. “The Academy supports the Healthy Meal Time Act because it would help schools establish evidence-based practices for lunch and recess schedules, ensuring students have the time they need to eat nutritious meals and support their health and well-being. We applaud Representatives Schrier and Bonamici for their leadership on this important issue.”

The Healthy Meal Time Act has been endorsed by the National Education Association, the Center for Science in the Public Interest, the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, and the School Nutrition Association.

title: Rep. Watson Coleman, State Senator Zwicker Call On NJ DEP to Pause Sentinel Data Center in South Brunswick
text:
Ewing, NJ (November 9, 2026) - Today, Congresswoman Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12) and State Senator Andrew Zwicker (District 16 - Hillsborough) announced a letter to Commissioner Ed Potosnak of the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection demanding a pause on the permitting of the Sentinel Data Center in South Brunswick.

The letter highlights potential gaps in the environmental study of the project that could lead to adverse environmental and health impacts on the surrounding communities.

The letter reads, in part:

We respectfully request that DEP not issue the permit in its current form. Before any final decision, DEP must independently recalculate the Sentinel Data Center facility’s potential to emit and properly classify the facility to account for emergency operation and the full planned buildout; publish its health risk assessment inputs and its review of them; add enforceable limits on non-emergency use; and give the public an opportunity to review and comment on that information. We are not asking DEP to prejudge the application.

We are asking for a complete, transparent review that protects public health and gives residents confidence that the law will be enforced.

Congresswoman Watson Coleman introduced the Data Center Community Impact Act, legislation that would authorize a federal study on the environmental, economic, and public health impacts of data centers, with a focus on communities of color and low-income communities. Watson Coleman is also an original cosponsor of the AI Data Center Moratorium Act.

Senator Zwicker is a primary sponsor of NJ S4659, which would require the DEP to conduct a study and submit a report to the Governor and the Legislature concerning the environmental impacts of data center development in the State and prohibit the construction of new data centers until the study is complete.

Last month, State Senator Zwicker, along with Assemblymembers Frieman and Drulis, secured from the state an extension on the public comment period for the Sentinel Data Center project.
