title: Markey Demands Google Allow Schools to Disable AI Services Without Blocking Search Access
text:
Letter Text (PDF)

Washington (November 9, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), a member of the Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, today wrote to Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet Inc. and Google, demanding the company reverse its policy to block access to Google Search on K-12 student accounts at schools that want to disable artificial intelligence (AI) services, including Gemini, Google’s AI chatbot. AI chatbots are often designed to encourage compulsive use and emotional attachment exposing children to risks of manipulation and, in some more serious cases, have resulted in chatbots encouraging children to die by suicide. Google should not use its dominant position in the education technology market to force schools to adopt potentially dangerous AI technologies or risk losing a critical research tool like Google Search.

In the letter, Senator Markey wrote, “Just this month, a girl and her family sued Google after Gemini allegedly ‘helped coach her through a plan to commit suicide.’ The girl accessed Gemini through Google Search on a school-issued Chromebook, even though the school had blocked access to Gemini’s standalone app and website. At a time when schools, parents, and policymakers are working hard to implement safeguards on AI chatbots for our children, Google is recklessly forcing AI on schools and treating kids like collateral damage. Schools deserve the right to block student access to AI chatbots without also forfeiting access to an important educational tool.”

Senator Markey continued, “Google’s dominant position in education technology makes this ultimatum particularly concerning. Although Google has a right to create and offer new educational tools, it should not use its dominant market position to force schools to adopt them.”

Senator Markey requested the following information by November 30, 2026:

Will Google commit to allowing schools to disable generative AI features and chatbots on K-12 student accounts, including AI Overviews, Gemini, and Guided Learning, while retaining access to Google Search?

Is it technically feasible for Google to provide K-12 student accounts with Google Search results that exclude AI Overviews, Guided Learning, and other generative AI features or chatbots?

Please provide any research, testing, or risk assessments that Google has conducted on the safety, mental health, and learning effects of AI Overviews, Gemini, and Guided Learning on K-12 students, including for children under age 13.

How many K-12 schools and districts that use Google’s products currently restrict or prohibit students’ access to generative AI features or AI chatbots outside Google Search?

###

title: Senator Markey Statement on Permitting Reform Deal
text:
Washington (November 9, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), a member of the Environment and Public Works Committee, released the following statement on the Senate’s vote to invoke cloture on the motion to proceed to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) of 2026.

“We need to stop the Trump administration’s weaponization of our government against clean, affordable, and ready-to-go energy sources, and we need to build an energy grid that works for Americans now and into the future—that means cutting emissions and cutting costs. But as currently drafted, this bill attempts to address these goals by asking communities to trade the benefits of interstate transmission and the ability to make data centers pay more for grid power for the sacrifices of weakened clean water protections, intrusion on sovereign Tribal rights, and limits on the ability to be heard and considered during federal approval of projects ranging from hyperscale data centers to petrochemical plants. Legal experts have also raised serious concerns about the potential unintended effects of provisions that are meant to prevent Trump’s misuse of the permitting process but could impair environmental protections into the future at taxpayers’ expense. And without a committee process and sufficient time to work through and resolve these tradeoffs and questions, we do not have the answers we need.

“Voters sent a clear message last week that they want better deals than the ones they’ve gotten under unified Republican leadership. I believe we owe it to them to fight to win a better deal that delivers clean energy megawatts and jobs, near- and long-term savings on energy bills, and real climate benefits without leaving so many important members of our community on the losing side of the ledger.

“Because of these issues on timing, transparency, and threats to our clean air, water, and Tribes, I will vote against the motion to invoke cloture on this legislation. I will continue to discuss all these issues with my colleagues, both in the coming days and into the next Congress, and hope to work toward a better deal in the future.”

###

title: SENATOR MCCORMICK ANNOUNCES $191 MILLION IN ADDITIONAL FEDERAL FUNDING FOR RURAL HEALTHCARE IN PENNSYLVANIA
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Dave McCormick today announced that Pennsylvania will receive nearly $191 million in the next round of funding through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). This latest allocation continues the historic investment Senator McCormick strongly advocated for as part of the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, delivering additional resources to expand access to care, strengthen the rural health workforce, modernize facilities, and support innovative care models across the Commonwealth.

“The Working Families Tax Cuts Act is delivering once again for Pennsylvania,” said Senator McCormick. “I worked to include the rural health fund to protect rural Pennsylvania communities like the one I grew up in. This funding will make a real difference in expanding access.”

Building on last year’s award of more than $193 million, this new funding brings Pennsylvania even closer to securing nearly $1 billion over the five-year life of the program. The Rural Health Transformation Program represents the largest federal investment in rural healthcare in American history, and Senator McCormick’s work helped ensure Pennsylvania receives as much as possible.

These annual allocations are already helping bolster rural healthcare facilities, workforce pipelines, and technology upgrades statewide.

title: Sen. Merkley Statement on Senate Permitting Legislation
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Oregon’s Senator Jeff Merkley released the following statement on proposed legislation in the Senate to reform permitting:

“Transmission is much needed to move renewable energy from solar and wind farms to the places where there is a high demand for electricity.

“Data centers should pay their fair share for the resources they use.

“And having cleaner, cheaper renewable energy is important for reducing energy costs here at home, for our country’s competitive status in the world, and for our ability to tackle climate chaos.

“I strongly support the portions of this bill that seek these outcomes and praise the work of my colleagues – Senators Whitehouse and Heinrich – who have strived to accomplish these objectives.

“But at the demand of the fossil fuel titans, this bill also accelerates the extraction and burning of fossil fuels.

“Very simply: getting more renewable electrons where they are needed doesn’t tackle climate change if you simultaneously promote the burning of more fossil fuels. Unfortunately, this bill does exactly that.

“This bill could make it easier to build more data centers powered by ‘behind the meter’ natural gas plants.

“It makes it much easier to build natural gas pipelines that will transport incredible quantities of natural gas overseas as LNG.

“More pipelines and export terminals equal more American fracked gas burned at home and abroad.

“And while the models exclude American gas burned abroad from the climate impact of this bill, the Earth is affected the same no matter where the gas is burned.

“This bill has a number of other features that merit careful analysis. Yet, the bill has never had a public hearing. Not in the House. Not in the Senate.

“Robust consideration of the bill should be a priority in the new Congress.

“Here are some of the other issues that merit careful examination.

“The bill restricts states’ ability to raise and address clean water concerns on gas pipelines as well as transmission lines.

“It shortens timelines that make it hard-to-impossible for grassroots and community groups to raise concerns about projects.

“It eliminates tools that states and localities use to fight the development of new data centers and detention centers.

“And it impacts the sovereignty and rights of Tribes.

“Permitting reform for electrical transmission lines is essential.

“But the current bill raises too many serious issues that require more deliberation.

“I will vote against the bill before us today, but I look forward to working with my colleagues to get permitting reform right.”

###

title: Wyden, Merkley, Hoyle, Bynum Announce over $5.3 Million to Enhance Railroad Safety
text:
The City of Harrisburg and Douglas County to benefit

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, along with U.S. Representatives Val Hoyle and Janelle Bynum today announced over $5.3 million in federal investment to improve railroad infrastructure, increase safety, and boost economic growth.

“Farmers and manufacturers across Oregon rely on railroads to ship their products to markets across the world,” Wyden said. “This federal investment will improve the safety of railroad crossings, increase efficiency of Oregon’s railways, and help our local economies thrive. I will continue to fight for more resources for infrastructure projects that support small businesses across the state.”

“Critical investments like these play a vital role in preventing traffic disruptions and keeping trains, vehicles, and pedestrians safe,” said Merkley. “These common-sense projects in Douglas and Linn Counties will both keep the local economy moving and our community members safe.”

“Investments in rail infrastructure help connect our communities,” said Rep. Hoyle “This funding will strengthen rail safety across Douglas County, significantly improving emergency access concerns and the efficiency of intercity freight rail.”

“Nobody likes getting stuck at the train tracks, but I’ll take being a few minutes late over playing with our safety,” said Rep. Bynum. “This money is about making sure we can get around safely while giving our economy room to grow and bringing more business to Oregon.”

The $5.3 million in federal awards from the Federal Railroad Administration’s Railroad Crossing Elimination/Crossing Safety program will be distributed as follows:

$3,583,594 to the City of Harrisburg to close three at-grade rail crossings, improve track visibility and install several roadway improvements.

$1,763,336 to Douglas County to support the feasibility study and preliminary engineering of a future grade separation at the crossing intersection of Old Highway 99 and the Central Oregon and Pacific Railroad.

“We are truly grateful to receive $1,763,336 in federal funding to help move forward with planning and preliminary engineering for a future grade separation at the Wilbur Old Highway 99 and Central Oregon & Pacific Railroad crossing. This project is important to Douglas County because it addresses real concerns about emergency access, public safety, and the movement of freight through our community. We want to sincerely thank Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, along with all of Oregon’s federal delegation, for their support and for recognizing the importance of investing in transportation infrastructure in our communities. These projects take time and partnership to advance, and this funding gives us an opportunity to take a meaningful step toward finding a long-term solution. We appreciate everyone who has helped bring us to this point, and we look forward to continuing this work for the benefit of Douglas County residents and future generations,” said Douglas County Commissioner and Board Chair Tom Kress.

###

title: Senator Moody Secures More than $2.5 Billion in FEMA Funding for Florida Communities Affected by Disasters
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Senator Ashley Moody has now secured more than $2.5 billion in FEMA disaster assistance funds, as part of ongoing efforts to recover long-sought reimbursements for hard-hit Florida communities. Florida has been waiting on some of these recovery funds since 2017 but Senator Moody delivered them in less than 2 years in office.

“Excited to announce that we have hit yet another huge milestone for our state—securing more than $2.5 billion in long-sought FEMA disaster assistance for hard hit areas in our state. These are funds that communities have been waiting on for years, and something I began working on for Floridians as soon as I was appointed to the Senate. Our work is not done, and I will continue fighting to help Floridians get the federal support they need to recover from disasters,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

BACKGROUND:

Statewide, Senator Moody has secured more than $2.5 billion in FEMA public assistance funding. This includes funding for more than 500 projects. The money will be disbursed to the state and local communities for disaster recovery projects.

These projects include repairs to educational facilities, restoration of critical infrastructure, debris removal, and costs incurred during emergencies to protect life and property.

Senator Moody introduced the TRACK Act (Transparency in Recovery Assistance & Claims Knowledge Act) to bring more transparency to the FEMA disaster aid process, which has now been passed into law.

The TRACK Act mandates a status tracker on the FEMA website, so victims of a disaster have easily available knowledge and insight of their claim’s progress.

Following the strike of Hurricane Isaias earlier this month, Senator Moody has made multiple trips to the communities struck by the storm and is working with state and federal officials to facilitate the quick provision of aid. Senator Moody recently lednearly all of the Florida congressional delegation in an effort urging the President to accept Florida’s Major Emergency Disaster Declaration.

title: Sen. Moran Calls on Congress to Pass Aviation Safety Legislation
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Jerry Moran (R-Kan.) – chairman of the Senate Commerce Subcommittee on Aviation – today spoke on the Senate floor urging Congress to reach an agreement on aviation safety legislation that can pass both chambers and be signed into law by the President before the end of the year. Sen. Moran delivered his remarks ahead of the second anniversary of the deadly midair collision near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA) involving a regional passenger jet, Flight 5342, which originated in Wichita, Kansas, and a U.S. Army Black Hawk helicopter. The crash killed 67 people, including seven Kansans.

“Productive negotiations have taken place between the House and Senate, and I am encouraged by that progress, but we must finish the job, and we must get this right,” said Sen. Moran. “We cannot wait for another tragedy before addressing known safety concerns. Congress has a responsibility to finish aviation safety legislation. The Senate has acted. The House has acted. There is bipartisan support for improving aviation safety. Now we must resolve our differences and deliver a final bill.”

“I am grateful to the families of the victims for their continued commitment to aviation safety,” continued Sen. Moran. “To those families, I want to say: We have not forgotten your loved ones. We have not forgotten January 29th. The time for delay is over. We have the findings. We have the recommendations. We have a path forward. What we need now is the determination to finish the job.” Sen. Moran recently penned an op-ed in The Kansas City Star highlighting the need to pass aviation safety legislation to help prevent future tragedies and honor the lives lost in the Flight 5342 crash.

Click HERE to Watch Sen. Moran’s Full Remarks

Sen. Moran’s full remarks as delivered:

Madam President, sadly on January 29, 2025, our nation witnessed a tragedy. I witnessed it here at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport. Flight 5342, a regional jet originating in Wichita, Kansas, collided with a U.S. Army Black Hawk helicopter near that airport.

“Sixty-seven people lost their lives. Seven of them were from my state of Kansas. Nearly two years later, their families continue to live with an unimaginable loss. And Congress still has not completed the comprehensive aviation safety legislation necessary to address the failures that contributed to the tragedy. It’s unacceptable.

“Among those aboard Flight 5342 was Grace Maxwell. Grace should have graduated from Cedarville University with her bachelor’s degree. After graduation, she planned to pursue a master’s degree. Instead, her family is left to imagine that future, the future she would have had. The Maxwell family is not alone.

“The families of the victims have continued to urge Congress to act – not simply for their loved ones, but to make certain no other family has to experience this kind of tragedy. We owe them more than our condolences. We owe them action. In December, the Senate unanimously – December almost a year ago – the Senate unanimously passed the bipartisan ROTOR Act to strengthen aviation safety and help prevent future accidents.

“The ROTOR Act was carefully developed with the support and input of the crash victims' families, the National Transportation Safety Board, the Federal Aviation Administration, the Department of Transportation and the Department of Defense.

“Rather than pass the Senate's legislation, the House advanced its own proposal. The House bill contains important safety reforms, and I appreciate the work of my colleagues in both chambers. But the two bills take different approaches to some of the important safety requirements.

“Productive negotiations have taken place between the House and Senate, and I am encouraged by that progress. But we must finish the job, we’ve been talking about that progress and those negotiations for a long time. We must get the job done; we must get it done right.

“One of the most important provisions in the ROTOR Act is the requirement for Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast In, known as ADS-B In. This technology provides pilots with real-time information about nearby aircraft. This allows pilots to see surrounding air traffic from their cockpits and make better and quicker-informed decisions.

“It is particularly important in congested airspace, like the airspace surrounding Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.

“Investigators from both the Army and NTSB identified a series of failures that contributed to the January 29th tragedy, including faulty equipment, dangerous flight paths and inadequate tracking technology.

“The NTSB concluded that technology allowing pilots to see GPS-based information about nearby aircraft could have helped prevent this collision. With the appropriate technology, pilots could have had nearly a minute of warning to recognize the danger and potentially change course. Nearly a minute that could have made the difference between the life and the death of 67 people.

“The ROTOR Act incorporates those findings and puts critical safety improvements into law. It’s not an arbitrary mandate. It is a recommendation rooted in the independent investigation of a tragedy that should never have happened.

“The House and Senate have different approaches to ADS-B In. We need to find common ground and produce a bill that can pass both chambers. But compromise cannot mean abandoning the lessons of January 29.

“We must reach an agreement that addresses the recommendations of the NTSB and the Army's investigation. We cannot water down critical safety reforms. Our focus must remain on one mission: making our skies safer and preventing another tragedy.

“Every provision in the final bill should be measured against that standard. Does it address a demonstrated safety concern? Does it implement the recommendations of the experts who investigated this crash? Does it make our aviation system safer?

“Commonsense questions that need to be answered about the legislation.

“This work extends, however, beyond the ROTOR Act. As Chairman of the Commerce Subcommittee on Aviation, I have also worked to address the growing number of close calls involving aircraft on runways and airport surfaces.

“In June, I held a hearing to examine these incidents and identify ways to prevent them before they become tragedies as well. I worked with colleagues to advance the bipartisan Runway SAFE-T Act to improve training and technology and reduce runway and airport surface incidents. That legislation was approved by the Commerce Committee in September, and I will continue working with my colleagues to advance it.

“We cannot, should not, wait for another tragedy before addressing known safety concerns. Congress has a responsibility to finish aviation safety legislation. The Senate has acted. The House has acted. There is bipartisan support for improving aviation safety. Now we must resolve our differences and deliver a final bill.

“I am grateful to the families of the victims for their continued commitment to aviation safety. To those families, I want to again say: We have not forgotten your loved ones. We have not forgotten January 29th. We cannot. I cannot. The time for delay is over. We have the findings. We have the recommendations. We have a path forward. We just now need is the determination to finish the job.

“We cannot bring back the 67 people who lost their lives. But we can honor them by making certain that the failures that contributed to the tragedy are addressed and that the same mistakes are not repeated. The traveling public deserves to know that when they board an airplane, Congress has done everything within its power to protect their safety.

“We need to reach an agreement, pass comprehensive aviation safety legislation, and send a strong bill to the President's desk. The families of the 67 victims deserve nothing less. The American people deserve nothing less.”

title: Sen. Moran Announces Kansas Providers Will Receive $225 Million in Second Year of the Rural Health Transformation Program
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Jerry Moran (R-Kan.) today announced Kansas health care providers will receive $225,896,117 in federal resources through the second year of the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), an increase of $4 million from last year. For the second year in a row, Kansas will receive the sixth-highest amount in federal resources from the program, with the state receiving $222 million in the program’s first year.

“This is an important investment in rural health care across Kansas, and these resources will provide long-term upgrades for technology, staffing and equipment to better meet the needs of Kansans in small towns across our state,” said Sen. Moran. “I worked with my colleagues to establish this federal program, and Kansas will again receive the sixth-highest award in the nation. These resources are targeted to address the unique needs of rural communities in our state, and I look forward to working with Kansas health care providers and state leaders to strengthen access to quality, affordable care for rural patients in Kansas.”

Sen. Moran worked to establish the Rural Health Transformation Program last year to help identify the root challenges facing rural health providers and invest in solutions to improve outcomes for struggling providers. The program, administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), is implemented at the state level by the Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE).

title: Sen. Ossoff Working Across the Aisle to Support Georgia’s Rural Hospitals
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Jon Ossoff is working with Republicans and Democrats to support rural hospitals across Georgia.

Sen. Ossoff is cosponsoring the bipartisan Rural Development Hospital Technical Assistance Program Act to help prevent rural hospital closures and ensure access to health care in rural communities.

This bipartisan bill, first introduced by Sens. Mike Rounds (R-SD) and Peter Welch (D-VT), would make permanent the existing program at the U.S. Department of Agriculture that assists rural hospitals in improving efficiency and financial performance, bolstering quality of care, and supporting the community.

“Rural Georgians deserve great health care. This bipartisan bill will provide resources to struggling rural hospitals to ensure communities have access to the efficient and quality care they deserve,” Sen. Ossoff said.

Sen. Ossoff continues to work to protect Georgia’s rural hospitals.

In September, Sen. Ossoff delivered Federal funding to 18 rural hospitals across Georgia through the Rural Hospital Provider Assistance Program (RHPAP), a new program created earlier this year that offers Federal funding to rural hospitals to strengthen care and prevent hospital closures.

This year, Sens. Ossoff and Rev. Warnock brought Republicans and Democrats together to deliver health care upgrades for Southwest Georgia communities, including Federal funding to upgrade hospital infrastructure in Crisp County, deliver a new MRI machine to Irwin County, fund a new CT Scanner, mammogram machine, and ambulance in Clinch County, and purchase new medical equipment for maternal and neonatal care in Valdosta.

Sen. Ossoff also brought Republicans and Democrats together to expand health care services for families across North Georgia, including expanding health care transportation services in Rome, delivering a new Cardiac CT Scanner for a rural hospital in Union County, and delivering new equipment in Calhoun.

In July 2025, Sen. Ossoff cosponsored the bipartisan Rural Hospital Cybersecurity Enhancement Act to create new strategy and training resources to boost the number of cybersecurity and digital security professionals in rural hospitals across Georgia and nationwide.

title: Padilla Announces Nearly $70 Million to Strengthen California’s Electric Grid
text:
Padilla has now delivered more than $100 million for grid projects across California

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), a member of the Energy and Natural Resources Committee, announced $69,814,909 in federal funding to help strengthen California’s electric grid infrastructure against extreme weather. The funding through the U.S. Department of Energy will be distributed by the California Energy Commission to communities across the state.

“My POWER ON Act is helping communities upgrade their infrastructure to better withstand extreme weather, prevent outages, and protect families from power disruptions,” said Senator Padilla. “That is why I’m continuing to lead the effort to deliver these investments in grid resilience to California, making this nearly $70 million in funding possible. I’ll keep working to ensure California has the resources it needs to build a stronger, more reliable electric grid.”

The funding comes through the Grid Resilience Formula Grants to States and Tribes Program at the Department of Energy, which was created by Senator Padilla’s Preventing Outages with Enhanced Resilience and Operations Nationwide (POWER ON) Act. The POWER ON Act was signed into law by President Biden in 2021 as part of the historic Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, authorizing $5 billion over five years to help prevent blackouts, shutoffs, and utility-caused wildfires and to help states weatherize their electric grids. California has now received nearly $107 million thanks to Padilla’s legislation – resulting in a stronger, more reliable grid and more jobs and workforce opportunities.

Padilla has been a consistent and vocal advocate for the need to strengthen our electrical grid. Earlier this year, Padilla introduced legislation that would reauthorize the Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnerships (GRIP) Program through 2031. Last year, Padilla led California lawmakers in denouncing the DOE’s cuts of $7.6 billion in critical grants for energy projects across California and the country. DOE’s list of cuts includes 79 projects and over $3.3 billion in investment across California, with over $2 billion in projects eliminated from Republican-represented districts in California. In 2024, Padilla announced $600 million in federal funding for California to upgrade 100 miles of transmission lines to improve the state’s grid reliability and deliver clean, affordable electricity faster.

title: Padilla, Schiff Introduce Bill to Transfer Land to the Barona Band of Mission Indians
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff (both D-Calif.) introduced legislation to transfer 847 acres of federal land from the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) into trust for the Barona Band of Mission Indians. Representative Darrell Issa (R-Calif.-48) introduced companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

The Barona Band of Mission Indians is a federally recognized Tribe in San Diego County, which was forced out of their first federally established reservation when the City of San Diego bought a portion of the Capitan Grande Reservation from the federal government to build a reservoir. After the reservation was flooded, the Tribe purchased the Barona property to create their current reservation. The Barona Tribe and the Viejas Band of Kumeyaay Indians also share a joint-trust patent to jointly manage the remaining 15,000 acres of the Capitan Grande Reservation surrounding the reservoir.

The proposed parcels in the bill are adjacent to the existing 7,500-acre Barona Indian Reservation near Ramona in San Diego County and have deep cultural and historical significance to the Tribe. Adding this land into trust would connect land between the Barona Indian Reservation and the Capitan Grande Reservation. The bill would preserve existing rights-of-way, public recreational access and public trails, emergency access for federal personnel, and existing water rights and service agreements.

“The Barona Band of Mission Indians have consistently fought to unify their ancestral home — and it’s past time we restore and reunify their lands to protect and preserve their sacred sites,” said Senator Padilla. “My bill would transfer over 840 acres of federal land to connect the Barona Indian Reservation and the Capitan Grande Reservation and better protect sacred sites, traditional use areas, and cultural resources on ancestral land.”

“I am proud to join Senator Padilla in introducing legislation that will restore historical and ancestral land to the Barona Band of Mission Indians who have fought to regain their land after being pushed out,” said Senator Schiff. “This commonsense legislation is a pivotal step in supporting tribal conservation and cultural preservation.”

“For generations, our people have been separated from the lands that hold our history, our ceremonies, and our sacred places. Today, that separation begins to end. This legislation is the bridge to Capitan Grande, a land bridge that reconnects Barona with our ancestral home,” said Barona Chairman Raymond Welch. “We are grateful to Senator Alex Padilla, Senator Adam Schiff, and Congressman Darrell Issa for listening to our people and working together across the aisle to make this possible. By placing this land in trust, they have honored our past and strengthened our future.”

Padilla is a strong advocate for restoring Tribal ownership of ancestral lands. Last month, the Senate unanimously passed Padilla’s Pit River Land Transfer Act, a bicameral and bipartisan bill to promote Tribal management of over 500 acres of land in California by transferring federal land to the Pit River Tribe. In July, Padilla testified at a Senate Committee on Indian Affairs hearing to advocate for critical water investments for California Tribes. In March, Padilla and Schiff introduced legislation to transfer 860 acres of land from the BLM into trust for the Pechanga Band of Indians.

Last year, Padilla and Schiff announced a trio of bipartisan, bicameral bills to promote Tribal management of over 2,000 acres of land in California by transferring federal land to the Yuhaaviatam of San Manuel Nation, the Pit River Tribe, and the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians. In 2024, the Senate passed of a pair of Padilla’s bills to support the restoration of Tribal lands for the Jamul Indian Village and the Lytton Rancheria of California, the first of which became law.

title: ON THE JOB FOR MICHIGAN: Upper Peninsula Veterans Service Officer Highlights Peters’ Work to Expand Access to Burial Benefits for Veterans
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – In a new “On the Job” video from U.S. Senator Gary Peters’ (MI) office, Denise Formolo, a Veterans Service Officer for Dickinson County, highlights Peters’ work to expand veterans’ access to the burial benefits they earned in service. Prior to the passage of Gerald’s Law in 2024, only veterans who passed away in a VA facility were able to qualify for burial benefits. Peters’ legislation ensured that veterans who choose to pass away in their homes are not denied burial assistance. The legislation is named after Army veteran Gerald “Jerry” Elliot of Kingsford, whose family was denied the benefit after he passed away in a non-VA facility. The video is part of the On the Job for Michigan series, which highlights Peters’ leadership and advocacy on behalf of Michigan constituents and communities.

“No veteran should have to make a decision to stay in a hospital to die versus going home surrounded by their family,” said Denise Formolo, Veteran Service Officer at Dickinson County Veterans Affairs. “Senator Peters really stepped up to the plate when it came to Gerald’s Law.”

Formolo continued, “I think it's our responsibility as citizens of the United States to make sure that we take care of these veterans and that we take care of their families after.”

Watch the “On the Job” video here.

“Our brave men and women in uniform have sacrificed so much in the defense of our nation,” said Senator Peters, former Lieutenant Commander in the U.S. Navy Reserve and member of the Armed Services Committee. “We owe it to them to ensure that they receive the benefits that they have earned through their service, including a dignified burial.”

As the son of a World War II veteran and a former Lieutenant Commander in the U.S. Navy Reserve, Peters is committed to advocating for Michigan’s servicemembers, veterans, and military families, and fighting to ensure they receive the resources and benefits they have earned. Earlier this year, Peters introduced the Gerald’s Law Reauthorization Act of 2026, which would extend the expanded benefits established by Gerald’s Law through 2030.

In 2021, Peters was inducted into the Michigan Military and Veterans Hall of Honor for his efforts to support our nation’s veterans and military. In 2017, Peters was recognized as Legislator of the Year by the Vietnam Veterans of America for authoring the bipartisan Fairness for Veterans Act, which was signed into law as part of the national defense bill. The legislation requires veteran discharge review boards to give liberal consideration to petitions for honorable discharge status if the servicemember has been diagnosed with PTSD, TBI, or other related conditions connected to their military service. In 2022, Peters helped enact the Sergeant First Class Heath Robinson Honoring our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics (PACT) Act – which delivered VA health care and benefits to all generations of toxic-exposed veterans and their survivors for the first time in our nation’s history.

title: Sens. Johnson, Baldwin Introduce Bipartisan Resolution Congratulating Milwaukee Brewers on Historic World Series Championship
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Ron Johnson (R-Wis.) and Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.) introduced a bipartisan resolution congratulating the Milwaukee Brewers on winning the 2026 Major League Baseball World Series. This victory marks the first World Series championship in Brewers franchise history and the first Major League Baseball championship for the city of Milwaukee since the Milwaukee Braves won the World Series in 1957.

The Brewers completed a historic regular season with a franchise-record 103 wins and their fourth consecutive National League Central Division title. In the postseason, the Brewers defeated the San Diego Padres in the National League Division Series and went on to sweep the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series. The Brewers finished the postseason with an 11-2 record after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in five games to bring the World Series title home to Milwaukee.

“Congratulations to the Milwaukee Brewers’ players, coaches, and staff on their historic World Series victory. I am thrilled for this team and its loyal fans, who have waited more than 40 years for this moment,” said Sen. Johnson. “Wisconsinites are proud to call the Brewers our own and to celebrate this historic achievement together. Go Brewers!”

“In a season for the history books, the Milwaukee Brewers brought so much pride to Milwaukee and the entire state of Wisconsin. Generations of Wisconsin families cheered on the Crew, kids stayed up well past their bedtimes, and game after game, this team showed what it means to win the Wisconsin way – with resilience, teamwork, and grit. This was a season to remember, and it is a privilege to recognize and honor the team that made history and the fans who cheered them on every step of the way,” said Sen. Baldwin.

The resolution celebrates the players, coaches, stadium staff, and loyal Brewers fans who helped make this victorious season possible.

title: Rosen Votes to Advance Bipartisan Bill to Reform Permitting Processes, Increase Clean Energy Projects, Lower Energy Costs
text:
Landmark Bipartisan Permitting Reform Bill Will Make It Easier To Build More Solar, Wind, Geothermal Projects In Nevada, Lowering Energy Costs & Creating Good-Paying Jobs

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) released the following statement after voting to advance the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), landmark legislation that will make it easier to build more clean energy projects while keeping strong environmental regulations in place. This will help create more good-paying jobs, lower energy costs, and strengthen American energy independence.

“Hardworking families are being squeezed by ongoing inflation and sky-high cost of living, particularly due to rising energy prices. I’ve always been clear that lowering costs for Nevada families and creating good-paying jobs are priorities for me, and this historic bipartisan bill will allow us to achieve both,” said Senator Rosen. “As the state with the most solar jobs per capita and an abundance of geothermal and other clean energy sources, Nevada stands to greatly benefit from increased investments in renewable energy projects that create good-paying jobs and lower energy costs, all while reducing carbon emissions. Unfortunately, current government red tape has made it nearly impossible to bring these clean energy projects online, which is why sensible reform like this bipartisan bill is needed. While further improvements can and should be made to strengthen this bill, we cannot squander the opportunity to deliver results and lower costs for families.”

title: Schatz Statement On Bipartisan American Affordability And Jobs Act
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Brian Schatz (D-Hawai‘i) released the following statement on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026.

“The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is a historic bill that reflects years of bipartisan work to reform our outdated permitting processes while protecting the environment.

“Permitting delays drive up costs and stall projects, making electricity, housing, and public transportation more expensive. This legislation will help lower costs, build clean energy, modernize America’s grid, cut emissions, and hold data center developers accountable.

“This bill is a bipartisan compromise, and deals like this are tough. We heard from Native leaders and advocates and secured some key changes to improve the historic preservation title and ensure that federal agencies consult with Native Hawaiian organizations, Tribes, and others about historic and cultural resources. I understand these changes won’t be enough for everyone to support the bill, but we’ll continue working to ensure Native Hawaiian organizations and Tribes have a meaningful voice in decisions affecting their communities.

“While BAAJA is not perfect, it represents a rare opportunity to pass strong, bipartisan legislation that will help lower costs and make it easier for American workers to build the things our country needs. I will vote to pass it and will continue working with my colleagues to deliver results for people in Hawai?i and across the country.”

title: STATEMENT: Sen. Schiff Statement on Permitting Reform Legislation
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), member of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works and Ranking Member of the Fisheries, Water, and Wildlife Subcommittee, issued the following statement after voting against the motion to proceed to the permitting reform legislation on the Senate floor:

“The need for a permitting reform package has only grown in the past decade, as bureaucracy has stymied the development of vital projects from clean energy to housing that could lower costs. And I appreciate the work done by Senators Whitehouse and Heinrich to negotiate a bipartisan agreement, as a lasting solution can only be reached by reaching across the aisle. In particular, the transmission and grid reform provisions are very positive. And the changes that they secured in the manager’s amendment make this a better bill. Nevertheless, the bill needs further improvement before I can support it.

“My top priorities in such an agreement are to bring down energy bills through new clean energy development, to lower emission rates, to support tribal sovereignty, and to stop the administration from attacking American clean energy projects. This includes restoring the billions of dollars in terminated energy projects in California, as well as the offshore wind projects the administration baselessly and illegally canceled. The president’s comments today, that notwithstanding any compromise in this bill, he intends to continue blocking wind projects, demonstrate a singular but telling lack of good faith. I have said from the start that we need to have confidence that any permitting reform legislation is not going to be weaponized by this or any future administration to single out states and provide giveaways to the oil and gas industries. In its current form, this bill does not satisfy those priorities and raises other serious concerns.

“This legislation would jeopardize tribal sovereignty through major changes to the National Historic Preservation Act, impact the State of California’s authorities under the Clean Water Act, and constrict federal agencies’ ability to protect vulnerable wildlife under the Endangered Species Act. While I support the provisions in this bill that require data center companies to cover the costs of grid infrastructure and protect American taxpayers from footing the bill — which mirror my legislation — the legislation overall contains too many giveaways to oil and gas with insufficient constraints on an energy policy that has prioritized corporate profit over the pocketbooks of hard-working Americans and public health. I believe Congress should work on stronger guardrail provisions to ensure that such provisions will not be used to improperly tilt the playing field in favor of fossil fuels by the Trump administration, which has failed to provide any assurance to Congress that it will follow the law if this bill is enacted.”

###

title: Schmitt Joins AG Blanche to Tout $68 Million Award for St. Louis Law Enforcement to Tackle Violent Crime
text:
Schmitt Advocated for St. Louis to Receive Award Through DOJ’s Model Cities Initiative

ST. LOUIS, MO — Today, U.S. Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) joined Attorney General Blanche in St. Louis to celebrate the $68 million award for local law enforcement through the Department of Justice’s Model Cities Initiative. The grant will help local law enforcement implement comprehensive, innovative crime-fighting solutions that will start in St. Louis and can be adapted and applied in cities across the nation. Schmitt advocated for St. Louis to be chosen for this program, and the grant will build on Schmitt’s successful work to crack down on crime in St. Louis and his ongoing efforts to keep Missouri communities safe.

Download Schmitt’s remarks HERE.

“I’m a proud St. Louisan, but for too long violent crime has tormented our communities and left families feeling unsafe. As Missouri’s Attorney General and now as a U.S. Senator, I have spent my career fighting for a safer Missouri, and I am so proud that St. Louis was one of the four cities chosen as part of the Model Cities Initiative to support our law enforcement officers and serve as an example for the rest of the nation. We’ve gotten far too used to seeing violence in our city’s headlines, but that doesn’t have to be our reality. I am grateful that President Trump, Attorney General Blanche, and the entire Trump Administration are focused on fighting crime, and I look forward to our continued efforts to make life better—and safer—in the Show-Me State,” said Senator Schmitt.

“The Model Cities Initiative reflects the Trump Administration’s commitment to reducing crime across the country and ensuring the safety of every American,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “These cities are setting an example of proactive law enforcement that will strengthen the rule of law and improve public safety in their jurisdictions. As violent crime rates continue to fall to historic lows, the Department of Justice is redoubling our efforts to invest in local communities and keep American families safe.”

Background:

Senator Schmitt worked closely with local stakeholders throughout the application process and held multiple calls and in-person meetings with Department of Justice leadership, including Attorney General Todd Blanche, to emphasize the importance of this funding to St. Louis and its public safety efforts.

The investment aims to help St. Louis reduce violent crime, improve public safety, and build partnerships to help address the drivers of crime—and builds on Schmitt’s efforts to surge additional federal law enforcement resources to St. Louis, including a permanent increase in FBI personnel and other federal law enforcement surges like Operation Show Me Justice and Operation Viper, which resulted in the arrest of over 500 criminals.

The funding will support investments in police recruitment, officer compensation and wellness, and police academy improvements, as well as upgrades to the Real-Time Crime Center, radio communications, and emergency response drones. It will also help replace police vehicles, provide ballistic shields for patrol cars, and establish a new citizen reporting portal. Additionally, the grant will expand community services through a law enforcement-led homeless outreach program, additional social workers and victim advocates, and partnerships supporting crisis intervention, treatment, and housing assistance.

Alongside St. Louis, three other cities were selected to participate in the Model Cities Initiative: Jackson, MS; Jacksonville, FL; and Baton Rouge, LA.

title: Sen. Tim Scott celebrates Treasury and IRS announcement of more than 6,500 new Opportunity Zone designations
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Tim Scott (R-S.C.) issued the following statement after the U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) announced Qualified Opportunity Zones (QOZs) designations for more than 6,500 communities across all 50 states, territories, and the District of Columbia. South Carolina received 112 new designations.

“The American Dream should not be limited by your ZIP code, and Opportunity Zones are bringing new possibilities to communities that have been overlooked for far too long. The proof is in the pudding with more than $110 billion in private-sector investments nationwide, and we are just getting started,” said Sen. title: Thune Discusses the Work Ahead for Congress
text:
Click here to watch the video.

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) today delivered the following remarks on the Senate floor:

Thune’s remarks below (as delivered):

“Madam President, there is no doubt about it, Tuesday night was a tough election night.

“It was certainly not the outcome that we had hoped for.

“But it was the outcome the American people chose.

“And we have to listen to them.

“I’m proud of what Republicans have been able to accomplish for the American people in the 119th Congress – most especially the Working Families Tax Cuts, which allows hardworking Americans to keep more of their hard-earned money.

“But the American people let us know that they need more.

“Inflation is still too high, and just going to the grocery store can take a huge chunk out of a family’s budget.

“And steep gas prices have only increased that burden.

“And so I think the election gave us two things, Madam President:

“One, an opportunity to reflect on what we as a party need to do better.

“And two, a clear message that this coming Congress needs to double down on the work that we’ve been doing on affordability.

“As I said, I’m proud that this Republican Congress has put more money in Americans’ pockets with the Working Families Tax Cuts.

“And I’m proud too of other measures we passed like the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which will help address the cost of housing by increasing supply.

“But as the American people have emphasized, there is more work to be done.

“A very good start would be the bipartisan permitting reform legislation that we will vote on this evening – legislation that Republicans wanted to bring up earlier this fall.

“Energy prices affect pretty much everything when it comes to affordability, Madam President.

“High energy costs don’t just mean higher gas and electric bills, they mean higher costs for a wide variety of goods and services – from hot dogs to home repairs.

“And so one of the biggest things we can do to address affordability for the long term is to ensure a reliable and affordable energy supply.

“And that starts with ensuring that energy projects don’t face unnecessary permitting barriers.

“Madam President, regrettably my Democrat colleagues delayed consideration of permitting reform legislation before the election.

“But I’m hopeful that later today they will allow us to proceed to the bill, and hopefully finish it this week.

“Republicans are paying attention. The American people are paying attention.

“Tonight is the first opportunity for Democrats to show whether they are serious about addressing costs, or whether their rhetoric on affordability was just that.

“Madam President, I want to offer my congratulations to all those who won on Tuesday.

“And I want to especially welcome our new Republican senators – and our new Democrat senators as well.

“And I want to say to my Democrat colleagues – new and old – that Republicans are ready to work with you to address the American people’s concerns.

“As I suggested, we can notch our first bipartisan win for the American people before the new Congress even starts by passing permitting reform in the coming days.

“But I do want to say one thing, Madam President.

“Republicans are ready and willing to work with our Democrat colleagues.

“But that does not mean rubberstamping a leftist agenda.

“It does not mean standing by while Democrats attempt to dismantle the tax relief that we passed for the American people.

“It does not mean standing by while Democrats attempt to reinstate the chaos that existed at the border under the Biden administration.

“I hope my Democrat colleagues realize … what this election was … and what it was not.

“This election was a sign of Americans’ frustration with the high cost of living that they’ve been dealing with, literally, since the opening days of the Biden administration.

“It was not – it was not – a mandate for radical policy and socialist fantasies.

“And so while Republicans are prepared to work in a bipartisan way, we will also emphatically oppose Democrats when required to protect hardworking Americans and our system of government.

“We will oppose any attempt to balloon the size of government or tear down American institutions, as the Democratic Socialists would like to do.

“In fact, growing the size of the government is the last thing we should be doing if we want to make life more affordable for hardworking Americans.

“And I hope my Democrat colleagues realize this.

“The American people are not looking for socialist government and leftist fantasies.

“They’re looking for lower gas prices. They want their grocery bills to stop growing. They want to be able to afford to buy a house for their growing family.

“And if Democrats are committed to real work on those issues, then Republicans are ready to work with them.

“My Democrat colleagues have spent a lot of time talking about affordability this election cycle.

“But they don’t exactly have a stellar record on delivering.

“Their signature bill in the 117th Congress – the so-called American Rescue Plan Act – helped plunge the country into an inflation crisis from which we’re still trying to fully emerge.

“And Democrats unanimously voted against tax relief for hardworking Americans in the 119th Congress.

“So Madam President, we will see what the 120th Congress brings.

“I hope it will bring a lot of bipartisan work to address the challenges facing the American people.”

title: Van Hollen Statement on Current Opposition to Moving Forward with Permitting Reform Legislation
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) released the following statement regarding his vote against moving forward with the permitting reform legislation under consideration in the Senate:

“When I look at legislation before the Senate, I evaluate how it will benefit Maryland and how it will benefit our nation. And while permitting reform is an important priority, this bill is unfortunately lacking key provisions that are central to communities across Maryland. For starters, this bill does not fully address the Trump Administration’s current efforts to block Maryland’s pending offshore wind project, which would lower energy costs for households across our state and create thousands of good-paying jobs. What’s more, this bill undermines critical provisions that protect the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries – an economic and environmental lifeline for folks across our state. I’m putting forward changes to the bill to address these concerns; however, while I support the goal behind tackling our burdensome and outdated permitting system, given this bill’s impact on Maryland, I cannot support it in its current form.”

title: Warner, Kaine, McClellan Press Social Security Administration on Abrupt Defunding of VCU Disability Benefits Support Program
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) and U.S. Rep. Jennifer McClellan (D-VA-04) raised concerns about the Social Security Administration’s (SSA) abrupt decision to halt funding for the Work Incentives Planning and Assistance (WIPA) program’s National Training and Data Center (NTDC) at Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU), threatening critical services that help Americans with disabilities navigate Social Security benefits while seeking employment.

The NTDC provides training, certification, and technical assistance to more than 900 benefits counselors serving individuals with disabilities across the country. On October 2, 2026, SSA abruptly declined to fund VCU’s contract for another year and ordered the university to immediately halt work, disrupting essential training and support services for 74 WIPA projects nationwide.

In a letter to SSA Commissioner Frank Bisignano, the lawmakers demanded an explanation for the decision and pressed the agency to clarify how it intends to restore these critical services and fulfill its statutory obligations.

The lawmakers wrote, “We write to inquire about the Social Security Administration’s (SSA) decision to defund the Work Incentives Planning and Assistance program’s (WIPA) National Training and Data Center (NTDC). We are aware that on Friday, October 2, 2026, the SSA exercised its option not to extend its contract with Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU) to administer the NTDC and ordered VCU to immediately halt all work providing Community Work Incentives Coordinators (CWICs) nationwide with training, certification, technical assistance, and other resource support.”

The WIPA program helps individuals who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) due to severe, long-term medical conditions understand how employment may affect their benefits. Benefits counselors provide free, individualized guidance to help Americans with disabilities pursue employment opportunities without inadvertently jeopardizing the benefits they rely on.

The lawmakers continued, “CWICs at WIPA projects help bridge the information gap for beneficiaries by looking at their individual circumstances and advising them on how to maintain their benefits while working. To ensure the efficacy of the WIPA programs, the law also required SSA to establish a corps of work incentives specialists and provide training and technical assistance for those specialists. CWICs provide information and resources to help beneficiaries make informed decisions on returning to work.”

Despite Congress appropriating $23 million for the WIPA program in Fiscal Year 2026, SSA’s decision has left benefits counselors nationwide without access to necessary training resources, certification services, performance data, and institutional knowledge. These resources are critical to training new counselors and ensuring that both new and existing counselors provide accurate, reliable guidance to Americans with disabilities. The sudden loss of these services raises serious concerns about SSA’s ability to meet its statutory obligations and ensure that beneficiaries continue receiving the support they need.

The lawmakers pressed SSA to explain the rationale and timing of its decision, identify what training and certification resources remain available to benefits counselors, address disruptions to required performance reporting, and clarify whether the agency intends to restore these services through VCU, bring them in-house, or award a new contract.

Read the full letter here and below.

Dear Commissioner Bisignano,

We write to inquire about the Social Security Administration’s (SSA) decision to defund the Work Incentives Planning and Assistance program’s (WIPA) National Training and Data Center (NTDC). We are aware that on Friday, October 2, 2026, the SSA exercised its option not to extend its contract with Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU) to administer the NTDC and ordered VCU to immediately halt all work providing Community Work Incentives Coordinators (CWICs) nationwide with training, certification, technical assistance, and other resource support.

Disabled beneficiaries who qualify for SSDI or SSI benefits are among the most vulnerable populations who suffer from severe, long-term medical conditions. To maintain compliance, beneficiaries must navigate a series of strict and complex requirements set out by the Social Security Act, including on earned income. For beneficiaries who need to earn extra income to support themselves or their families, incorrectly interpreting the rules can lead to a termination of benefits.

The Ticket to Work and Work Incentives Improvement Act of 1999 directed the Commissioner of Social Security to establish a program to provide information about work and benefits to people who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) because of a disability. Using that authority, SSA established 74 WIPA projects in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and U.S. territories. WIPA projects and community organizations employ over 900 benefits counselors who provide free in-depth counseling to disabled beneficiaries on the effect of work on their SSDI or SSI benefits.

CWICs at WIPA projects help bridge the information gap for beneficiaries by looking at their individual circumstances and advising them on how to maintain their benefits while working. To ensure the efficacy of the WIPA programs, the law also required SSA to establish a corps of work incentives specialists and provide training and technical assistance for those specialists. CWICs provide information and resources to help beneficiaries make informed decisions on returning to work.

In Fiscal Year 2026 Congress appropriated $23 million to operate the WIPA program, 0.1 percent of SSA’s annual administrative budget. However, despite clear Congressional intent in support of the WIPA program, SSA has decided to unilaterally disband a vital component of the program. Without the NTDC, WIPA projects nationwide have lost access to valuable training resources and performance data to train new CWICs and ensure both new and existing Coordinators provide accurate and relevant information to beneficiaries. WIPA projects are also losing access to an invaluable source of institutional knowledge.

After this abrupt decision, it is unclear how SSA intends to comply with the statutory requirements of the Ticket to Work and Work Incentives Improvement Act of 1999 and Congressional intent set out in the Fiscal Year 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act.

We request answers to the following questions by November 16, 2026:

Why was the decision made to defund NTDC? Please provide a full account of the facts that informed the decision to defund NTDC.

When was the final decision made to defund NTDC? When were NTDC staff and VCU staff informed of the decision?

What training resources, if any, do WIPA projects have access to following the closure of the NTDC?

WIPA projects are required to submit its quarterly performance data at the end of this month. The performance data WIPA projects submit to maintain grantee status was collected and tracked through the WIPA STAR system. Given the sudden cancellation of the WIPA STAR system, will the reporting deadline be extended?

To obtain/maintain certification, CWICs were required to receive training through VCU. How will CWICs now receive certification training? Will SSA waive certification requirements if CWICs are unable to access the training?

Will SSA bring the training and technical assistance previously performed by VCU in-house? If not, does SSA plan on issuing a recompete of the contract?

title: Warnock Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Restore “I Have a Dream” Plaque at Lincoln Memorial
text:
Senator Reverend Warnock introduced legislation to restore the plaque commemorating Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s “I Have a Dream” speech at the Lincoln Memorial

Despite years of damage, the historic plaque cannot be replaced without an act of Congress

Senator Reverend Warnock: “The spot where Georgia’s greatest son spoke those historic words deserves to be properly restored to honor his legacy, vision, and fight for justice”

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA) introduced the bipartisan Renewing the Dream Act to restore the plaque commemorating Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s “I Have a Dream” speech at the Lincoln Memorial. The plaque marks the exact spot where Dr. King delivered his iconic speech during the 1963 March on Washington, but years of wear and tear have left the historic marker faded and increasingly difficult to read. Private funds have been raised to replace the plaque but the King family was informed by the U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) that its replacement would require an act of Congress.

“Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s words from his ‘I Have a Dream’ speech resonate as powerfully today as they did then,” said Senator Reverend Warnock. “The spot where Georgia’s greatest son spoke those historic words deserves to be properly restored to honor his legacy, vision, and fight for justice.”

“America was founded on the ideals of life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. To become a more perfect union, leaders like Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. had to speak the truth and challenge our nation to live up to our founding ideals,” said Senator Tim Scott (R-SC).“His ‘I Have a Dream’ speech brought the promise of America closer to reality, and by continuing to honor his legacy on this plaque, we can remind future generations of the power of speaking the truth and standing up for justice for all.”

“I’m grateful to Senator Raphael Warnock for introducing the Renewing the Dream Act to replace the plaque commemorating my father’s ‘I Have a Dream’ speech at the Lincoln Memorial,” said Dr. Bernice King. “His call for freedom, justice, and equality still demands action. I urge bipartisan support for this legislation and a renewed commitment to confronting injustice, practicing nonviolence, and creating the Beloved Community.”

Senator Warnock has long worked to honor and carry forward the legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and the Civil Rights Movement. For more than 20 years, he has served as Senior Pastor of Atlanta’s historic Ebenezer Baptist Church, the former pulpit and spiritual home of Dr. King.

The legislation was introduced alongside Senator Tim Scott (R-SC).

Full text of the Renewing the Dream Act is available HERE.

title: Wyden, Merkley, Hoyle, Bynum Announce over $5.3 Million to Enhance Railroad Safety
text:
The City of Harrisburg and Douglas County to benefit

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, along with U.S. Representatives Val Hoyle and Janelle Bynum today announced over $5.3 million in federal investment to improve railroad infrastructure, increase safety, and boost economic growth.

“Farmers and manufacturers across Oregon rely on railroads to ship their products to markets across the world,” Wyden said. “This federal investment will improve the safety of railroad crossings, increase efficiency of Oregon’s railways, and help our local economies thrive. I will continue to fight for more resources for infrastructure projects that support small businesses across the state.”

“Critical investments like these play a vital role in preventing traffic disruptions and keeping trains, vehicles, and pedestrians safe,” said Merkley. “These common-sense projects in Douglas and Linn Counties will both keep the local economy moving and our community members safe.”

“Investments in rail infrastructure help connect our communities,” said Rep. Hoyle “This funding will strengthen rail safety across Douglas County, significantly improving emergency access concerns and the efficiency of intercity freight rail.”

“Nobody likes getting stuck at the train tracks, but I’ll take being a few minutes late over playing with our safety,” said Rep. Bynum. “This money is about making sure we can get around safely while giving our economy room to grow and bringing more business to Oregon.”

$3,583,594 to the City of Harrisburg to close three at-grade rail crossings, improve track visibility and install several roadway improvements.

$1,763,336 to Douglas County to support the feasibility study and preliminary engineering of a future grade separation at the crossing intersection of Old Highway 99 and the Central Oregon and Pacific Railroad.

title: Young Column: Thank You to 250 Years of Hoosier Veterans
text:
WASHINGTON – The following column by Senator Todd Young (R-Ind.) on Veterans Day is available for publication:

Thank You to 250 Years of Hoosier Veterans

Senator Todd Young

Every year on Veterans Day, we thank America’s veterans and their families for their dedication to protecting our freedoms.

This year, as we celebrate America’s 250th birthday, it is an opportunity to give thanks for our earliest Hoosier heroes—not only for the hardships they bore and the heroics they displayed to free our nation, but for their part in establishing our state. Many of the men who cleared Indiana’s wilderness were also the soldiers who won America’s independence.

One of the most significant victories of the Revolutionary War was fought here in the winter of 1779, when George Rogers Clark and a band of Virginia militiamen marched across flooded and frozen plains to siege Fort Sackville in Vincennes.

By raising the American flag over this lonely frontier outpost, Clark was claiming the Northwest Territory for the new nation, dramatically altering its map and future, and ensuring the eventual formation of Indiana.

Endorsing the construction of the grand monument to Clark’s victory in Vincennes, a New York newspaper wrote in 1929: “It was as necessary as Yorktown. It was more significant than Bunker Hill. It was as inspiring as Valley Forge.”

After the American Revolution was won, cash-strapped states rewarded their veterans not with money, but with land. Virginia awarded 150,000 acres north of the Ohio River—Clark’s Grant—spanning present-day Clark, Floyd, and Scott Counties. Hundreds of veterans then settled in the Indiana Territory, as America’s first soldiers became Indiana’s earliest settlers.

Veterans like Captain Robert George, an artillery officer who settled in Clark County and helped establish the first settlement on the Ohio River. His land tract helped found and develop the town of Utica. Upon his death in 1804, his property passed to his family and fellow veterans who were instrumental in founding the communities of Clark County.

Other Revolutionary veterans followed. Thomas Carr, Sr., a captain in the Continental Army, settled in Clark County near Fourteen Mile Creek. Carr served as a delegate to the Indiana Constitutional Convention, helping draft our state’s founding charter and contributing to the design of Indiana’s judicial and election systems.

As the nineteenth century began, thousands joined a migration into the newly created Indiana Territory, leading families over the Cumberland Gap, down the Ohio River, or through the wilderness of the Old Northwest.

Nearly 2,000 veterans of the American Revolution spent the remainder of their lives in Indiana. They rest in small churchyards, on family farms, deep in forests, even in densely populated urban areas, across from schools—often under crumbling headstones whose inscriptions have weathered beyond legibility, save for the faint, enduring words: “A Soldier of the Revolution.”

The wilderness they encountered upon arriving in Indiana has been replaced by communities built upon the ideals these veterans fought for in their time.

Today’s American service members serve across the world, but a chain of devotion connects these worn and crumbling graves to the men and women who wear the uniform today and keep us safe.

On this Veterans Day, let us give thanks to these first Hoosier veterans, the spirit of service and sacrifice they established, and the heroes who carry it forward today. May our nation never forget the selfless sacrifices of our men and women in uniform.

title: Congressman Mark Alford Elected Secretary of the House Republican Conference for the 120th Congress
text:
Today, Congressman Mark Alford (MO-04) was elected by his Republican colleagues to serve as the Secretary of the House Republican Conference for the 120th Congress.

Rep. Alford, a career communicator with more than 35 years of broadcast communications experience, sought the leadership post to serve as a liaison for members, expand messaging capabilities, and ensure every Republican voice is amplified within leadership.

Congressman Alford issued the following statement:

"I am deeply honored by the trust my colleagues have placed in me to serve as Secretary of the Republican Conference. From my first day in Washington, my mission has been simple: I am here to help. As Conference Secretary, I look forward to being a servant leader and a catalyst to provide key resources for our members, while ensuring that leadership ALWAYS hears your voices as we navigate the 120th Congress."

Prior to his election as Conference Secretary, Rep. Alford served as Deputy Vice Chair for Communications at the National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC) and as Chairman of the Republican Study Committee’s (RSC) Strategic Messaging Task Force. In those roles, he delivered key support initiatives for members:

Held personalized media training sessions to help members refine interview abilities.

Helped launch the RSC’s “Right to the Point” podcast to highlight member stories.

Hosted “Member Masterclass” workshops on media interaction best practices.

Provided in-office and at-home studio consultations on camera setup, framing, and technology needs.

As Conference Secretary, Rep. Alford will build upon these efforts by implementing several key priorities:

Mentorship Programs: Expanding the Freshmen Mentorship Program and the Chief of Staff Mentorship Program to best prepare incoming members and their key staff to serve their constituents.

Conference Camaraderie: Organizing regular member and staff events to increase unity, expertise, and collaboration.

Job Bank & Member Priorities: Continuing the success of the House GOP Job Bank and working across the leadership team to elevate the legislative priorities of all Republican Conference members.

"Our conference is strongest when every member has the tools, training, and platform to share their story and represent their constituents effectively," said Rep. Alford. "I am ready to get to work for our members and our conference."

title: Congressman Al Green to Join Removal Coalition for Press Conference on Impeachment, Accountability, and Congressional Action
text:
(Washington, D.C.) — On Wednesday, November 11, 2026, Congressman Al Green will join Jessica Denson, founder of the Removal Coalition, for a press conference at the House Triangle in Washington, D.C., to discuss the continued pursuit of presidential accountability through impeachment and congressional action. title: Bacon Honors Nebraska Secretary of State Bob Evnen on House Floor
text:
Bacon Honors Nebraska Secretary of State Bob Evnen on House Floor

Remarks Recognize Evnen's Leadership and Service to Nebraska

Washington, D.C. – Rep. Don Bacon (NE-02) today delivered remarks on the House floor recognizing Nebraska Secretary of State Bob Evnen for his years of public service and leadership. Bacon highlighted Evnen's work to strengthen election security and transparency, modernize state business services and promote Nebraska agriculture in international markets.

Full video of Rep. Bacon's remarks is available for viewing and download here.

Below are Rep. Bacon's remarks as delivered:

I rise today to recognize and honor a dedicated public servant who has led our state with integrity, vision, and effectiveness: Nebraska’s 27th Secretary of State, Bob Evnen.

Since taking office in January 2019, Secretary Evnen has worked to strengthen our elections, support our economy and represent Nebraska around the world.

On elections, Bob authored a bill instituting Nebraska’s Voter ID law, expanded hand-counted post-election audits after every statewide election, and opened testing processes to public observers to increase transparency. He also worked to secure ballot drop boxes, all with the goal of giving Nebraskans confidence in their elections.

Secretary Evnen also served as a leader in Nebraska’s business community. By modernizing state filing systems, cutting red tape, and eliminating unnecessary fees, his office made it easier and less expensive for entrepreneurs to start, operate, and grow their business in Nebraska.

As Nebraska’s Ambassador abroad, Bob showcased our state’s world-class agricultural products, especially our premium corn and beef. His trade missions to Taiwan, Israel, Bulgaria, Egypt, and beyond opened international markets for our farmers and ranchers.

Whether securing our elections, promoting our agriculture, modernizing state services, or serving on the Board of Pardons, Bob brought the same diligence to the office that marked his 40-year legal career and his service on the State Board of Education.

Along with his wife Debra, his children, and his grandchildren, Secretary Evnen embodies Nebraska values. On behalf of our state, I thank Secretary Evnen for his outstanding service and commitment to Nebraska.
