title: Congressman Baird Rides Aboard Legendary Vietnam Gun Truck in DC Veterans Parade
text:
Congressman Baird rode aboard a replica of the Vietnam-era gun truck “Brutus,” traveling down Constitution Avenue, Sunday, as part of the National Veterans Parade. The parade honored all those who have defended America throughout our nation’s 250-year history.

Joining Congressman Baird aboard Brutus was Roger Blink, replica builder of Brutus and driver of the original gun truck, Indiana State Representative Beau Baird, as well as other veteran members of the Army Transportation Corps.

“One of my main goals this year was to provide Vietnam veterans a meaningful tribute during America’s 250th anniversary,” said Congressman Baird. “Many Vietnam veterans did not receive the gratitude and recognition they deserved upon returning home. Many came home without the parades and celebrations given to past generations of veterans. Seeing Brutus travel along the same parade route presidents walk after being inaugurated, I hope this tribute offers Vietnam veterans, and all who served, a small measure of the honor they have earned.”

Background: The service of Congressman Baird and the Vietnam Gun Trucks

The tribute has personal significance for U.S. Congressman Jim Baird (IN-04). The Congressman served as a convoy commander for the 523rd Transportation Company. The company is known for multiple renowned gun trucks including Ace of Spades, Proud American, King Kong, and Satan’s Lil Angel. As a first lieutenant, Jim Baird led convoys of up to 200 vehicles and often rode aboard the gun trucks that protected them.

“One of the greatest privileges of my time in Congress has been creating opportunities to honor Vietnam veterans,” said Congressman Baird. “Those I served alongside and all who sacrificed for the cause of freedom in that war deserve the recognition too many were denied when they returned home. As we celebrate America’s 250th anniversary, seeing Brutus travel through our nation’s capital will honor their courage and remind Americans of the immense service and sacrifice of Vietnam veterans.”

The original Brutus served with the 359th Transportation Company, defending supply convoys against enemy ambushes. To protect trucks carrying supplies from coastal ports to inland bases, soldiers transformed ordinary Army cargo trucks into “gun trucks,” first adding sandbags, then reinforcing the vehicles with steel armor and mounted machine guns. These improvised defenders helped protect fellow soldiers and keep vital supplies moving.

The National Veterans Parade is a nonpartisan celebration of every veteran, regardless of branch, generation, background, political affiliation, or religious belief.

This year the National Veterans Parade featured numerous marching bands, active-duty military ceremonial and performing units, historic military vehicles, floats, pageant titleholders, and special tributes to veterans of the past.

Images courtesy of the office of Congressman Jim Baird

title: Rep. Balint Announces Departure of Chief of Staff Megan Garcia
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Becca Balint (VT-AL) today announced that Chief of Staff Megan Garcia will be departing her office at the end of this week to take on a new role in the private sector. Garcia has served as Balint’s Chief of Staff since she was sworn into Congress in January 2023, helping establish and lead the office through its first four years. Kate Gorud, currently Deputy Chief of Staff and Legislative Director, has also served on Rep. Balint’s team since 2023 and will succeed Garcia as Chief of Staff. Kaleigh Calvao, currently Senior Legislative Assistant, will serve as Legislative Director.

“Megan has been by my side since the very beginning of my time in Congress, and it’s hard to imagine the team or the work we've done without her,” said Rep. Balint. “She came to this role with a decade of experience on the Hill, expertise on technology policy, and experience as a foundation and non-profit leader, and she brought that knowledge and leadership to the work of building our office from the ground up. She has helped shape how we work, how we serve Vermonters, and the kind of team we are. She's been an exceptional leader, a trusted confidante, and a steady partner through it all. I will miss working alongside her tremendously, but I'm so grateful for everything she's helped us build. I'm also incredibly proud of Kate and Kaleigh as they step into their new roles, and I have every confidence in the team as we keep fighting for Vermont.”

“I’ll forever be grateful to Rep. Balint for trusting me to be her first Chief of Staff and giving me the opportunity to help build this office from the ground up,” said Garcia. “These four years have been some of the most meaningful of my career. I’ve had a front row seat to the way Rep. Balint leads: with so much heart, conviction, humor, and an unwavering commitment to the people she represents. Even in the hardest moments, she never loses sight of why we’re here or who we’re here to fight for. It’s been a privilege to work alongside her and to help build a team that cares so deeply about serving Vermonters. I’ll miss this work, and, most of all, the people I’ve had the chance to do it with in Vermont and in DC. I’m so proud of what we’ve built together, and I know Kate and Kaleigh will carry it forward with the same dedication and care.”

Kate Gorud, incoming Chief of Staff

Kate Gorud (she/her) is Rep. Balint’s incoming Chief of Staff. She has worked in the U.S. House of Representatives since 2014 and brings more than a decade of Capitol Hill experience to her new role. Gorud has served as a key member of Rep. Balint’s staff since her first term in Congress, most recently as Deputy Chief of Staff and Legislative Director. In this role, she built the Congresswoman’s Community Project Funding program, helped secure federal disaster relief funding for Vermont farmers, and led legislative efforts to advance policies that address the needs of Vermont communities and working families.

Before joining Rep. Balint’s team, Gorud worked for Rep. Mark Pocan (WI-02) and former Rep. Matt Cartwright (PA-08), where she honed her expertise in the federal appropriations process, worked with family dairy farms on dairy policy and helped small businesses navigate federal COVID response programs. Gorud is deeply honored to continue working alongside Rep. Balint on behalf of Vermonters.

Kaleigh Calvao, incoming Legislative Director

title: Buchanan Backs Bipartisan Bill to Improve Hurricane Warnings for Vulnerable Floridians
text:
Legislation Would Close Gaps in Emergency Alerts, Strengthen Storm Preparedness and Protect the Floridians Most at Risk

WASHINGTON – Congressman Vern Buchanan recently cosponsored the Fixing Gaps in Hurricane Preparedness Act (H.R. 4563), bipartisan legislation led by Rep. Maxwell Frost (D-Fla.). The bill ensures hurricane warnings and preparedness tools reach the seniors, people with disabilities and other Floridians most at risk when a storm hits.

“Every hurricane season, lives are lost when emergency warnings either never reach people or are not clear enough to act on,” said Buchanan. “After Helene and Milton, Southwest Florida saw how quickly a storm can turn deadly. Every Floridian deserves a warning they can understand and a plan they can follow. When a storm is coming, no one in our community should be left behind.”

The Fixing Gaps in Hurricane Preparedness Act directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to study how seniors, people with disabilities, non-English speakers and rural and urban communities receive and respond to emergency alerts. NOAA would also evaluate how these groups prepare for hurricanes and tropical storms and, then use those findings to build forecasts, warnings and planning tools that work for the people who rely on them most.

Roughly two-thirds or more of the deaths from Hurricanes Katrina, Florence and Ian were people over the age of 60, and every Central Florida death from Hurricane Dorian was someone between the ages of 56 and 86. In Southwest Florida, where so many retirees call home, closing these gaps can save lives.

The bill’s provisions are included in the bipartisan Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2025 (H.R. 5089), which advanced out of the House Space, Science and Technology Committee in September 2025. Buchanan is urging Congress to bring the package to the House floor and get it across the finish line.

As Co-Chair of the Florida Delegation and Chairman of the Health Subcommittee, Buchanan has made disaster readiness a priority. This includes the Protecting Hospitals from Disaster Act, bipartisan legislation he introduced with Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA) in February to help hospitals and clinics prepare for, respond to and recover from natural disasters so they can stay open and keep caring for patients when storms hit.

title: For Immediate Release: Rep. Burchett Introduces Bill to Give Municipalities Control Over Data Centers
text:
Washington, D.C. (11/10/2026): Today, Rep. Burchett introduced the Community Control of Data Centers Act. This legislation prevents federal funds from going towards the construction or operation of data centers before obtaining state and local approval. The recent boom in AI has made data centers a central component of infrastructure that may have major economic implications. Despite potential benefits, it is important that the decision to build them should be made by the Americans who live in those towns, not Washington bureaucrats and Big Tech CEOs.

“As the former Mayor of Knox County, I know how important local control is over projects that could have adverse effects on the municipality where they’re located,” said Rep. Tim Burchett. “This bill allows local governments to retake control over new data center construction, putting the power back in the hands of the folks who are most affected. People are sick and tired of federal overreach that harms their communities, businesses, and the places they call home.”

title: Bynum Holds Moment of Silence for Silver Rail Elementary School Victims on House Floor
text:
Tonight, Congresswoman Janelle Bynum called for a moment of silence to remember those lost in the tragic Silver Rail Elementary School Shooting in Bend last month. She was joined on the House floor by members of the Oregon Delegation and the Gun Prevention Violence Task Force.

“Thanksgiving is just around the corner, and our families are staring down the holiday outfits that won’t be worn, the pieces of pie that’ll go untouched, and the place cards beside chairs that won’t be filled,” said Congresswoman Bynum. “My heart is with our families, our students, our educators, and all of Oregon. I am with you, and I know we can’t keep saying goodbye to our children like this. Our babies deserve to feel safe. They deserve better. And I promise to continue fighting to protect all of America’s children.”

Watch the full remarks and moment of silence HERE and read them below.

Mr. Speaker, Mr. Speaker, Mr. Speaker, it’s been almost a month since we lost our babies in the Silver Rail Elementary School Shooting in Bend.

And while the news outlets have since packed up and gone home, our community is still grieving and holding on tightly to the babies we have lost.

Thanksgiving is just around the corner, and our families are staring down the holiday outfits that won’t be worn, the pieces of pie that’ll go untouched, and the place cards beside chairs that won’t be filled.

My heart is with our families, our students, our educators, and all of Oregon. I am with you, and I know we can’t keep saying goodbye to our children like this.

Our babies deserve to feel safe. They deserve better. And I promise to continue fighting to protect all of America’s children.

Now, I ask that you join me in a moment of silence to remember everyone who was lost.

title: Bynum, Hoyle, Wyden, Merkley, Announce over $5.3 Million to Enhance Railroad Safety
text:
Representatives Janelle Bynum (OR-05) and Val Hoyle (OR-04), along with U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, announced over $5.3 million in federal investment to improve railroad infrastructure, increase safety, and boost economic growth.

“Nobody likes getting stuck at the train tracks, but I’ll take being a few minutes late over playing with our safety,” said Rep. Bynum. “This money is about making sure we can get around safely while giving our economy room to grow and bringing more business to Oregon.”

“Farmers and manufacturers across Oregon rely on railroads to ship their products to markets across the world,” Wyden said. “This federal investment will improve the safety of railroad crossings, increase efficiency of Oregon’s railways, and help our local economies thrive. I will continue to fight for more resources for infrastructure projects that support small businesses across the state.”

“Critical investments like these play a vital role in preventing traffic disruptions and keeping trains, vehicles, and pedestrians safe,” said Merkley. “These common-sense projects in Douglas and Linn Counties will both keep the local economy moving and our community members safe.”

“Investments in rail infrastructure help connect our communities,” said Rep. Hoyle. “This funding will strengthen rail safety across Douglas County, significantly improving emergency access concerns and the efficiency of intercity freight rail.”

“We are truly grateful to receive $1,763,336 in federal funding to help move forward with planning and preliminary engineering for a future grade separation at the Wilbur Old Highway 99 and Central Oregon & Pacific Railroad crossing. This project is important to Douglas County because it addresses real concerns about emergency access, public safety, and the movement of freight through our community. We want to sincerely thank Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, along with all of Oregon’s federal delegation, for their support and for recognizing the importance of investing in transportation infrastructure in our communities. These projects take time and partnership to advance, and this funding gives us an opportunity to take a meaningful step toward finding a long-term solution. We appreciate everyone who has helped bring us to this point, and we look forward to continuing this work for the benefit of Douglas County residents and future generations,” said Douglas County Commissioner and Board Chair Tom Kress.

title: Carbajal Statement on New Trump Administration Food Assistance Cuts
text:
U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), a member of the House Agriculture Committee, released the statement below following a new Trump administration proposal to cut an additional 6 million Americans from the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), also known as CalFresh in California. This new proposal would add to the SNAP cuts enacted under Trump’s so-called 'One Big Beautiful Bill,' which have resulted in more than 5 million Americans losing food assistance since July 2025.

“I'm outraged that the Trump administration is proposing an additional round of deep SNAP cuts that could hurt millions of families nationwide. This new round is on top of the cuts they already enacted through the ‘Big Ugly Bill’, which led to over 5 million Americans losing access to food assistance since July 2025, including over 300,000 people in California,” said Rep. Carbajal, a member of the House Agriculture Committee. “Over the past year, I visited food banks across the Central Coast and saw firsthand how the initial round of SNAP cuts put a big strain on seniors, veterans, children, and more. It is just heartless to do this again to families who are already struggling under the Trump administration’s failed economic policies. I will continue to fight for Central Coast families and work to rollback these terrible cuts.”

Background:

According to the Trump administration’s regulatory impact analysis of the proposed rule:

6.3 million individuals in 3.2 million households will lose their SNAP benefits entirely.

The 3.2 million families impacted make up 17 percent of SNAP households.

SNAP benefits will be cut by $50.82 billion.

Federal spending on benefits will be cut by $44.65 billion over 5 years (FY2027-FY2031), and state spending on benefits will be cut by $6.17 billion.

SNAP administrative expenses will increase by $1.24 billion.

Federal spending on administrative expenses will increase by $309.5 million over five years.

State spending on administrative costs will increase by $928.5 million.

Increased burden on participants is estimated to be approximately $71.7 million over five years.

Because SNAP participation is often used to streamline eligibility for basic needs programs, the proposed rule's effects reach beyond the program.

1.78 million children would no longer be categorically eligible for school meals. Of those children:

97 percent would likely remain eligible but need to go through an onerous paperwork process to maintain eligibility.

93,000 children would be shifted from free to reduced-price school meals.

28,000 children would lose free school meals entirely and have to pay full price.

42,000 children will no longer receive Summer EBT (“Sun Bucks”) beginning in the summer of 2029.

An estimated 13,000 of these children would lose benefits they qualify for due to administrative burden (i.e., not applying for SEBT, even though they remain eligible).

5,500 women, infants and children would be kicked off the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC).

title: Castro, Casar, Crockett, Doggett, Garcia, Menefee, Escobar, Green, Johnson, Veasey, Fletcher Demand Turnaround Of Massive Medicaid Backlog Formed Under Abbott
text:
Red Tape From So-Called “One Big Beautiful Bill” Contributed To Massive Backlog

Law Slashed $1 Trillion From Medicaid

WASHINGTON, DC — Representative Joaquin Castro (TX-20), alongside Representatives Greg Casar (TX-35), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Lloyd Doggett (TX-37), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Christian Menefee (TX-18), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Al Green (TX-9), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Marc Veasey (TX-33), and Lizzie Fletcher (TX-7) sent a letter to Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. and Texas Health and Human Services Commissioner (HHSC) Stephanie Muth demanding a turnaround to the massive Medicaid backlog in Texas that formed under Governor Greg Abbott that ballooned since January 2026. The members demanded an investigation, including an evaluation of contracted vendors, and federal intervention if the backlog was not adequately addressed. The members also urged the HHSC Commissioner Stephanie Muth to request funding from the Texas Economic Stabilization Fund to reduce the backlog.

In the letter to HHSC Commissioner Stephanie Muth, the members underscored the One Big Beautiful Bill Act’s (OBBBA) impact on Texas’ ballooning Medicaid and SNAP backlog, writing, “Since the passage of [(OBBBA)], over 635,000 Texans have lost SNAP food benefits, over 280,000 Texans have lost Medicaid, and over 850,000 Texans did not activate the Marketplace health insurance plans that became too expensive after Congressional Republicans failed to pass an extension of Marketplace enhanced premium tax credits….Yet despite this critical need, Texas is now facing an unprecedented surge in unprocessed benefits applications. According to recent reports, Texas’ Medicaid application backlog rose from 1,671 pending applications in January 2026 to a staggering 237,505 in early September 2026. At the same time, the SNAP application backlog rose from approximately 3,700 pending applications in January 2026 to more than 175,000 in early September 2026.”

In the letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., the members shared examples of real-life harm caused by delays stemming from the massive uptick in the state’s Medicaid backlog, writing, “Nearly four million Texans are currently enrolled in Medicaid. These families rely on Medicaid to access primary care, prenatal services, medications, and lifesaving treatments. Long delays disproportionately harm children, pregnant women, seniors, and Texans with disabilities. For four months, one Texan woman received no update from HHSC on her Medicaid for Pregnant Women application—a program that would have helped her afford essential prenatal care like ultrasounds and checkups earlier in her pregnancy.”

In the letter to Secretary Kennedy, the members continued by attributing OBBBA red tape to the delays and errors that prevent eligible people from accessing benefits, writing, “Recent federal provisions enacted in Public Law 119-21, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), have exacerbated Texas’ administrative bottlenecks and placed strain on HHSC’s already overwhelmed and mismanaged system….Since Texas HHSC uses an integrated application across human services programs like Medicaid, SNAP, and Medicare Savings Programs, infrastructural changes to one program can lead to technical errors across programs. Those technical errors can wrongly end a recipient’s coverage across programs, stripping people of the benefits they rely on.”

The members requested a response by November 30, 2026. To read the letters to Secretary Kennedy and Commissioner Muth, click here and here.

“We are in a cost-of-living crisis and Republicans in Washington and Texas don’t seem to care,” said Congressman Castro. “Texas’ staggering backlog in Medicaid and SNAP applications threatens to push more families into poverty. We must work to reverse the backlog, restore funding and help families in need see their doctor and put food on the table.”

“Nearly two years after Donald Trump promised to lower costs on day one, working families are draining their savings and taking on debt just to see a doctor or put food on the table,” said Congressman Greg Casar. “Now Texans are stuck in a dangerous backlog of SNAP and Medicaid applications. Donald Trump and Greg Abbott must clear it now, before more families go without care or go hungry.”

“Too many families wait months for food assistance and access to a family physician as Greg Abbott continues failing to meet federal requirements and violates a SNAP corrective action plan I secured. Republican indifference is harming our most vulnerable—children, pregnant women, seniors, and disabled individuals,” said Congressman Doggett. “Greater transparency into this crisis is urgently needed as Governor-elect Hinojosa and a new Democratic state house majority works to clean up Abbott’s mess.”

“Trump and Abbott have turned their backs on Texas families,” said Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia. “First, they slashed Medicaid and food assistance. Now, hundreds of thousands of Texans are stuck waiting for the health care and food assistance they desperately need. No parent should have to worry about getting their child to the doctor or putting food on the table because their government cannot do its job. This is not just incompetence. It is cruelty. Abbott must commit the resources to clear these backlogs, and the Trump Administration must make sure Texans get the benefits they are entitled to. Our families cannot afford to wait.”

“Texas's 18th Congressional District has one of the highest concentrations of SNAP recipients in the state, yet families are going hungry and suffering without access to proper healthcare because of massive backlogs in Medicaid and SNAP applications brought on by Abbott and Trump,” said Congressman Menefee. “Folks are legally entitled to these benefits, yet Republicans remain hell-bent on withholding them from our most vulnerable communities.”

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

The Medicaid backlog rose from 1,671 applications in January 2026 to 237,505 by early September 2026. In July, Texas processed 65% of Medicaid applications on time, down from 81% last year. The OBBBA cuts $1 trillion in Medicaid funding over ten years. The number of people participating in Medicaid and the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) in Texas dropped by about 247,317 between September 2025 and July 2026.

The members, in addition to Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34) and Henry Cuellar (TX-28), sent a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke L. Rollins demanding the turnaround of a massive backlog in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) applications.

To learn more, click here.

title: Reps. Cisneros, Mejia, Morrison Propose Tariff Hotline for Small Business Owners
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Gil Cisneros (CA-31), Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), and Congresswoman Kelly Morrison (MN-03) introduced the Small Business Tariff Relief Hotline Act to give business owners a dedicated place to voice their tariff‑related issues so they can’t be ignored. If passed, this legislation would create a Tariffs and Refunds Hotline within the Small Business Administration (SBA) Office of Advocacy for small businesses to report tariff related issues, and require the Chief Counsel to submit annual reports to Congress summarizing these issues and recommending fixes. The Small Business Majority is a supporting organization of the legislation.

“Tariffs are crushing our small businesses by driving economic uncertainty, job loss, and rising costs across the country,” said Congressman Gil Cisneros. “In 2025, small businesses with fewer than 10 employees lost more jobs than any other year in recent history. For the small businesses that tried to voice their concerns on the effects of Donald Trump’s economic chaos, they were dismissed with the Office of Advocacy telling Congress it is ‘out-of-scope’. I introduced the Small Business Tariff Relief Hotline Act to give our small businesses a voice on tariffs and the refund process, and require the SBA Office of Advocacy to actually listen to small businesses across the country and work with Congress to provide relief.”

“Small businesses are the backbone of our communities and our economy, and right now, too many of them are navigating Donald Trump's chaotic tariff disruptions on their own,” said Congresswoman Analilia Mejia “When costs rise and supply chains get tangled, small business owners shouldn’t have to wonder who to call or whether anyone will pick up. By creating a dedicated Tariffs and Refunds Hotline and requiring annual Congressional oversight, we make sure these concerns are tracked, taken seriously, and acted on. I am proud to co-lead this effort because our small business owners deserve a government that listens when they ask for help. It is time to stand up for the entrepreneurs who power our economy.”

“President Trump’s tariffs are driving up prices, making life more unaffordable, and posing an existential threat to our small businesses. Small businesses aren’t able to absorb the costs of tariffs in the same way that larger businesses are – and they certainly don’t have the time or people power to tackle all the administrative burden of seeking tariff refunds,” said Congresswoman Kelly Morrison. “We need the Small Business Administration to create a direct line to help small business owners get the refunds they need and are owed from these illegal tariffs. This legislation is an important step to both help us save our small businesses – the engine of our economy – and also to lower costs for all Americans. I’m going to continue to do everything I can to make life more affordable for Minnesotans, to fight for our small business owners, and help grow a thriving economy.”

According to research conducted by the Small Business Majority, in 2025, 60% of small businesses reported higher costs due to tariffs and over 80% of small businesses classified tariffs as a major worry for their business.

Full text of the bill can be found here.

Rep. Cisneros is a member of the House Committee on Small Business, the Ranking Member on the Subcommittee on Contracting and Infrastructure, and on the Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations. He is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and serves on its leadership team as the Freshman Representative.

###

title: Costa Statement Following House Vote on Impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
text:
WASHINGTON - Today, Congressman Jim Costa (CA-21), a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, released the following statement after the House voted 211-204 to refer articles of impeachment against Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth to the House Judiciary Committee, effectively blocking the impeachment effort:

“After consultation with retired senior military officers and former Secretaries of Defense, I voted against the effort to block impeachment proceedings. I am deeply disappointed that House Republicans chose to shield Secretary Hegseth from accountability rather than allow Congress to consider these serious allegations. Our Constitution is not optional, and those entrusted with our national security must be held accountable when they abuse that trust.

No Secretary of Defense, nor any cabinet member, is above the law, and no President has the authority to drag our nation into an endless war without accountability to the American people.

For months, Secretary Pete Hegseth has helped carry out a war in Iran without congressional authorization, disregarding the constitutional authority of Congress and the limits established by the War Powers Resolution. The articles of impeachment also raise serious allegations of unlawful military strikes, extrajudicial killings, disregard for civilian lives, suppressing free speech of veterans, and abuse of power.

Our service members have been put in harm’s way, American families are paying the price of this war, and the Secretary continues to evade accountability for his decisions.

As a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, I take seriously our responsibility to defend the Constitution and ensure that decisions of war and peace are subject to the rule of law. Supporting our troops does not mean giving this Administration a blank check to wage war.”

title: Davids Introduces Bipartisan Legislation to Protect American Manufacturing Jobs After Threatened Program Elimination
text:
Today, Representatives Sharice Davids (D-KS-03), David Joyce (R-OH-14), Zoe Lofgren (D-CA-18), Sarah McBride (D-DE-AL), and Mike Turner (R-OH-10) introduced a bipartisan bill to protect small and medium-sized local factories from sudden, politically motivated cuts by presidential administrations. The successful 40-year-old Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) helps small factories update equipment, train workers, and keep jobs in local communities.

“Shutting down one of the best job-creating programs in the country makes zero sense,” said Davids. “Our local machine shops and small factory owners don't care about political games in D.C. They just want reliable support so they can hire workers, lower costs, and compete. This bill fixes the loopholes used to cut funding, so groups like Kansas Manufacturing Solutions can keep helping local workers and businesses succeed.”

“Last year, when the Trump Administration tried to quietly cut funding for Manufacturing Extension Partnership centers across the country, including the Delaware Manufacturing Extension Partnership, we fought back to protect this program that helps small and mid-sized manufacturers grow, innovate, and compete,” said Representative Sarah McBride (D-DE-AL). “This bipartisan bill builds on that work by helping to keep MEP centers open and establishing clear, consistent standards for how they are evaluated and funded. When small and mid-sized manufacturers have the support they need to compete, they create jobs, strengthen supply chains, and drive innovation. I’m proud to support this effort because American manufacturers deserve certainty, and taxpayers deserve accountability.”

“Small and mid-sized manufacturers are a driving force behind Ohio’s economy, supporting local jobs, businesses, and communities,” said Representative David Joyce (R-OH-14), Co-Chair of the House Manufacturing Caucus. “These businesses need reliable support and resources. I’m proud to help lead this effort to strengthen the MEP program and ensure Ohio manufacturers have what they need to grow and remain competitive for years to come.”

“The MEP program is essential to supporting our small- and medium-sized manufacturers that make up the backbone of the U.S. manufacturing base,” said Representative Member Zoe Lofgren (D-CA-18), Ranking Member of the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee. “This important bill will help protect the MEP program against arbitrary disruptions by the Trump Administration while ensuring its stability over time.”

Even though Congress sets aside $175 million each year for local factory support, the Trump Administration recently proposed completely removing funding for the program in its 2027 budget, claiming private companies should pay for these services themselves. Because of sudden funding freezes and delays from Washington over the past year, nearly 90 percent of state manufacturing centers across the country have been forced to freeze hiring or lay off workers.

The Defend American Manufacturing Act 2.0 protects local factory support centers by fixing laws that allow funding to be frozen. Specifically, it:

Guarantees Support: Changes the law from saying the government "may" fund these centers to saying it "shall" fund them, stopping agencies from skipping payments approved by Congress.

Keeps Funds Flowing: Ensures centers fixing small paperwork issues can keep running while being checked, giving agencies a strict 180-day deadline to finish re-evaluations.

Stops Unfair Closures: Prevents government officials from shutting down or cutting off funding for a center unless it receives a poor performance grade.

Speeds Up Replacement: Requires the government to find a new center operator within 30 days if a contract is canceled, ensuring tax dollars go directly to helping factories.

Protects Tax Dollars: Adds strict checks to watch for fraud or misuse of funds.

Created in 1988, MEP operates centers in all 50 states and Puerto Rico. These centers give small local factories hands-on advice on upgrading tech, protecting against cyber threats, training workers, and managing supply chains. In 2024 alone, the program helped small manufacturers make $15 billion in new sales, save $2.6 billion in costs, and create or save over 108,000 jobs across the country.

In Kansas, where 86 percent of exports are factory goods, the local MEP — Kansas Manufacturing Solutions (KMS) — helps hundreds of small businesses. In 2024, KMS helped create or save 2,339 jobs, saved local businesses $14.3 million, and brought in $328 million in sales. In Kansas’ Third District alone, the group directly helped 552 small factories that employ more than 30,000 workers.

This is not the first time the current administration has attempted to dismantle MEPs. In April 2025, the administration abruptly tried to cut funding to MEPs in ten states — including Kansas — just hours before publicly promising to support American manufacturing. Davids immediately fought back, introducing the original Defend American Manufacturing Act to mandate program operations. Her quick action helped force a reversal that protected MEPs like KMS. However, the administration’s threats continue, prompting Davids to introduce today’s bill to ensure politicians cannot quietly pull the rug out from under American workers.

Davids’ bipartisan bill matches a Senate version led by Senators Jon Husted (R-OH) and Adam Schiff (D-CA). The bill is supported by the American Small Manufacturers Coalition.

title: DelBene Leads Call to Protect Service Members’ Private Medical Records
text:
Today, Representatives Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Mark Takano (CA-39), and Sara Jacobs (CA-51) sent a letter to Department of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth demanding answers on reports that the Department inappropriately accessed private medical records to target transgender service members for separation, potentially violating the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

On January 27, 2025, the Trump administration issued an Executive Order banning transgender people from military service. In September 2026, the Federal News Network reported that service members believed the Department inappropriately accessed, searched, and used private medical records, including clinical therapy notes, to identify and target transgender service members for separation. The letter seeks clarification and transparency on the use of these records, which appear to violate HIPAA.

The letter also asks what the Department is doing to ensure any HIPAA-compliant disclosure of service members’ health information is limited and warns that weaponizing medical information may cause service members to avoid treatment or withhold information from their providers, harming their health and undermining military readiness.

“Service members deserve to be able to trust that their private medical information is protected and will not be used against them,” said DelBene. “This report is deeply concerning and sets a dangerous precedent that will not only compromise military preparedness but also threaten the health of our service members. The Department must provide answers on this potential misuse of sensitive information and violation of medical privacy laws.”

“Amidst an illegal, multi-billion dollar war, the Department of Defense has wasted vital staff power and limited resources scouring through troops’ medical records so that Secretary Hegseth can weaponize that information to identify and kick out transgender servicemembers. That should alarm every American,” said Takano, Chair of the Congressional Equality Caucus. “The transgender military ban and the Pentagon’s actions implementing it are a stain on our military. I’m thankful to Rep. DelBene and CEC Vice Chair Jacobs’ work to conduct this important oversight on Hegseth’s extremist witch hunt and demand better for our servicemembers.”

The letter is supported by the Human Rights Campaign, SPARTA Pride, and the National Institute of Military Justice.

The letter was also signed by Representatives Pete Aguilar (CA-33), Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Becca Balint (VT-AL), Wesley Bell (MO-01), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), André Carson (IN-07), Troy Carter (LA-02), Sean Casten (IL-06), Judy Chu (CA-28), Gilbert Cisneros (CA-31), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Herbert Conaway Jr. (NJ-03), Angie Craig (MN-02), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Sharice Davids (KS-03), Danny Davis (IL-07), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Diana DeGette (CO-01), Christopher Deluzio (PA-17), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Lois Frankel (FL-22), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Al Green (TX-09), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Timothy Kennedy (NY-26), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Rick Larsen (WA-02), Teresa Leger Fernandez (NM-03), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Sarah McBride (DE-AL), James McGovern (MA-02), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Jerrold Nadler (NY-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Emily Randall (WA-06), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Janice Schakowsky (IL-09), Bradley Schneider (IL-10), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Eric Sorensen (IL-17), Greg Stanton (AZ-04), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Paul Tonko (NY-20), Norma Torres (CA-35), Ritchie Torres (NY-15), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25), and Frederica Wilson (FL-24).

title: NEW: Deluzio Report on PA-17 ICE Arrests Sheds Light on Trump’s Deportations in Western PA: “ICE is not Targeting the Worst of the Worst”
text:
CARNEGIE, PA – Today, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) released a new report analyzing recent ICE detentions and the impact of 287(g) agreements in Pennsylvania’s 17th Congressional District. A 287(g) agreement is part of the Immigration and Nationality Act that authorizes local police officers to perform and execute federal immigration enforcement alongside Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

The data analyzed in this report was collected and published earlier this year (January 1, 2026 - August 6, 2026) by the Deportation Data Project and initial analysis was shared with the Congressman’s office by Western Pennsylvania organization, Frontline DIGNITY.

Between January 1 - August 6, 2026, there were 209 ICE detentions in Pennsylvania’s 17th Congressional District, which includes all of Beaver County and half of Allegheny County. 112 (around 54%) detentions were attributed to a 287(g) agreement. 134 of the 209 detentions occurred in Beaver County, PA. 92 (68.7%) of these detentions came through the 287(g) program. 75 detentions occurred in the PA-17 portion of Allegheny County, PA. 20 (27%) of these detentions came through the 287(g) program.

Congressman Deluzio’s report highlights three major findings after analyzing the data:

ICE detentions are more frequent in communities with 287(g) agreements, especially in Beaver County, PA, which has a countywide 287(g) agreement.

Most people detained have no threat level and do not have a conviction or any pending charges.

ICE’s data collection raises a major question of why people are being detained under a 287(g) agreement in locations where there was no active 287(g) agreement.

Congressman Deluzio released the following statement with the release of his new report:

“ICE is now the most funded law enforcement agency in the country, all while endangering American lives and liberties. The findings in this report show that 287(g) agreements are increasing ICE detention rates in our communities—all while redirecting local law enforcement time and resources into federal immigration enforcement that is overwhelmingly targeting people who pose no risk to our communities. I think local law enforcement should be focused on local public safety.

“Additionally, this report highlights the real failures in ICE’s reporting of detentions. The public has a right to clear and complete information about what is happening in our neighborhoods and the departments or agencies—funded with public money—that are responsible for carrying them out.

“This report also backs up what I learned after conducting oversight at ICE’s largest detention center in Pennsylvania: ICE is not targeting the so-called “worst of the worst” in their immigration enforcement efforts. In fact, the evidence is clear: the Trump Administration mass deportation regime is primarily targeting people who have committed no crimes, face no allegations of violence, and are lawfully pursuing their shot at the American Dream. I think that’s wrong, and I am going to keep pushing back against ICE’s reckless abuses.”

Frontline DIGNITY’s Executive Director Jaime Martinez shared the following statement:

"The numbers tell a story we've been witnessing on the ground for months: this is not about public safety. It's about mass deportation. Every detention leads to a person, a family, and a community forced to live with the consequences of an immigration enforcement system that increasingly prioritizes arrests and profit over human dignity.

“At Frontline DIGNITY, we believe public safety should build trust, not fear. We brought this data to Congressman Deluzio's office because our communities deserve more than rhetoric. They deserve answers, transparency, and accountability. We commend the Congressman for taking these findings seriously and exercising his oversight authority. No community should have to wonder whether the institutions entrusted with protecting them are instead being used to tear families apart."

Congressman Deluzio’s Actions on Immigration and ICE Oversight:

In May 2026, Congressman Deluzio and Congresswoman Summer Lee (PA-12) conducted an unannounced oversight visit of Moshannon Valley Processing Center, ICE’s largest detention center in Pennsylvania.

Congressman Deluzio has made statements and sent letters to ICE demanding answers about multiple ICE detentions across Pennsylvania’s 17th District.

Congressman Deluzio sent letters to ICE in collaboration with other members of the Pennsylvania delegation on issues ranging from detention standards, earnings reports by the for-profit prison corporation running Moshannon and other ICE facilities, and most recently demanding more transparency in detention data—specifically on how 287(g) arrests are recorded.

A video recording of Congressman Deluzio’s virtual press availability on November 10, 2026 is available upon request.

title: Congressman DeSaulnier Announces Veterans Town Hall and Resource Fair
text:
Walnut Creek, CA – Today, Congressman Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10) announced he will host a Veterans Town Hall and Resource Fair on Monday, November 23rd from 1:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. at the Center for Community Arts in Walnut Creek. The event will include an update from Congressman DeSaulnier on his work in Congress to support the veteran community as well as a resource fair with representatives from federal agencies and Veteran Service Organizations to share information on resources and benefits available to veterans.

Veterans Town Hall and Resource Fair

Monday, November 23rd

Resource Fair: 1:00 – 3:00 p.m. PT

title: Rep. Estes Applauds $225.9 Million for Kansas Rural Health Care
text:
Kansas health care providers will receive $225,896,117 in the second year of the Rural Health Transformation Program, the sixth-highest award in the nation and about $4 million more than the state received last year.

Congress created the program in the Working Families Tax Cuts, signed into law by President Trump in 2025, and funded it at $50 billion over five years. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services administers it, and the Kansas Department of Health and Environment decides where the money goes in Kansas. The state’s first-year award of nearly $222 million paid for provider grants, equipment and facility upgrades.

“Kansas ranking sixth in the country two years running shows our state made a strong case for what rural providers here actually need,” said Rep. Ron Estes (R-Kansas). “This funding pays for the staffing, equipment and technology that hospitals and clinics in our small towns rely on every day. It comes from the Working Families Tax Cuts, and I was proud to help craft those provisions and vote for them so we can keep quality care accessible across rural Kansas.”

Rep. Ron Estes represents Kansas’ 4th Congressional District. He serves on the House Ways and Means Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Social Security, and on the House Budget Committee and the Joint Economic Committee. He is also a co-chair of the House Aerospace Caucus.

title: PRESS RELEASE: Congressman Michael Guest Introduces Resolution to Honor Veterans on Veterans Day 2026
text:
Congressman Michael Guest Introduces Resolution to Honor Veterans on Veterans Day 2026

Washington, D.C. - Congressman Michael Guest (R-MS) introduced a resolution in the United States House of Representatives to honor “the service and sacrifice of America’s veterans” and to call “on the people of the United States to observe Veterans Day in recognition of the heroic actions of America’s veterans to protect the United States and allow freedom to endure.”

This is Congressman Guest’s fifth year to introduce his annual resolution. He is proud to be joined by Congresswoman Susie Lee of Nevada introducing this year’s bipartisan resolution.

Veterans Day was originally called Armistice Day to celebrate the end of the “war to end all wars.” The war ended at the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month in 1918. In 1947, after World War II came to an end, Raymond Weeks organized Veterans Day in Birmingham, Alabama, honoring all veterans; and the idea caught on, prompting Congress to turn Armistice Day into what we now know as Veterans Day in order to recognize and honor all American veterans who have served our country throughout history.

For over 250 years, our Veterans have served America with distinction and honor. Looking back on our history, World War II stands as a testament to our nation's sacrifice. Over 80 years later, the United States is still blessed to have a number of those heroes still with us today. From the frozen hills of Korea and the jungles of Vietnam to the sands of the Gulf War and the battlefields of the Global War on Terrorism, generation after generation of Americans have answered the call to serve.

That unbroken line of courage extends to this very moment. Today, Americans hold a special place in their hearts for the brave men and women currently deployed in the Middle East—including Mississippi’s own National Guardsmen. They are standing on the front lines, risking everything to keep us safe at home.

Congressman Guest stated, “To ensure their legacy is permanently recognized, I have proudly introduced a bipartisan resolution to honor the service of all our veterans—past, present, and those currently in harm's way. Today, we remember those who went before us, and we pray for our Mississippi guardsmen standing watch today.”

The resolution was supported by more than 80 bipartisan Members of the U.S. House of Representatives who joined as original cosponsors of the legislation:

A copy of the resolution can be found here. Congressman Guest encourages veterans who are having trouble accessing their benefits through the Veterans Administration to contact his office at (769) 241-6120.

Congressman Michael Guest represents Mississippi's Third Congressional District. Currently serving his fourth term, Congressman Guest is the Chairman of the Border Security and Enforcement Subcommittee of the Committee on Homeland Security and is also a member of the House Appropriations Committee.

title: Congressman Abe Hamadeh Introduces Legislation to Prevent Federal Funding for Euthanasia
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. – Congressman Abe Hamadeh (AZ08) has introduced legislation aimed at preventing the adoption of all forms of human euthanasia in the U.S.

Congressman Hamadeh’s Protecting Vulnerable Patients, Seniors, and Families Act prohibits the distribution of federal funds to hospitals and medical entities who facilitate active euthanasia administration; clinical or self-administered, of lethal drugs intended to end a patient’s life.

“When I read about the heartbreaking case of Brigitte “GG” Stegemann, who was murdered through Canada’s assisted suicide program, I knew we had to take action,” stated Congressman Hamadeh referring to the 83-year-old Ontario, Canada grandmother who did not provide verbal confirmation of consent to being killed on the day of her death. “Despite expressing regret about entering Canadas euthanasia program just prior to her death, Ms. Stegemann was ruthlessly slain by bureaucrats, whose only concern was cutting costs. As American healthcare costs continue to rise, death should never be an easy go-to alternative for care, treatment, or support.”

The legislation comes amid growing concerns over the expansion of physician assisted suicide in countries across the globe. Notably expanded in the Netherlands and recently used to kill a child. Critics warn that these expanding programs raise serious questions about informed consent, patient safeguards, and the potential for vulnerable individuals to face pressure when making life-or-death decisions.

Congressman Hamadeh's legislation seeks to establish clear federal funding restrictions while preserving the rights of patients to make informed decisions about their medical care, including the right to refuse unwanted treatment.

Key provisions of the Protecting Vulnerable Patients, Seniors, and Families Act include:

· Prohibiting federal funding for medical entities that facilitate active euthanasia or physician assisted suicide.

· Preventing taxpayer dollars from supporting the administration of lethal drugs intended solely to cause a patient's death.

· Protecting patients' rights to decline medical treatment, including during end-of-life care.

· Preserving patient autonomy and informed consent in medical decision-making.

· Establishing a narrow exception for lawful death sentences imposed for capital crimes.

The legislation reflects Congressman Hamadeh's commitment to protecting vulnerable Americans and ensuring that rising healthcare costs never become a justification for replacing compassionate medical treatment and support with extermination.

title: ICE: Harder Demands Release of Local Nurse, Educator Detained in Louisiana on Threat of Deportation
text:
New York Times highlights Dr. Ann Lawani’s life in the Valley threatened by aggressive ICE policies

Image

Harder wrote to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin demanding Dr. Lawani be returned to California for legal proceedings after being abruptly transferred across the country

WASHINGTON – Today, Rep. Josh Harder (CA-09) sounded the alarm on outrageous new deportation tactics by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) that caused a local constituent to be detained, arrested, and abruptly transported across the country. Dr. Ann Lawani – a nurse, caregiver, and 13-year resident of Lodi in the U.S. legally under judicial protection – was sent thousands of miles away to Louisiana in violation of a federal court order. In response, Harder wrote to U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin to demand Dr. Lawani’s immediate return to California for any further legal proceedings.

Dr. Lawani lives in Lodi, where she is a caregiver for her 83-year-old father. She also oversees the education of 230 nursing students at the University of San Francisco, and she practices as a nurse at John Muir Health. Her abrupt absence has already caused significant disruptions on campus and pulled yet another healthcare worker away from a community facing severe shortages. Dr. Lawani’s story was featured this morning in the New York Times.

“Given her longstanding compliance, lack of criminal history, and substantial community ties, there is no apparent public safety justification for keeping Dr. Lawani detained thousands of miles from home while her case proceeds,” wrote Rep. Harder. “Our immigration enforcement system should focus on protecting communities from danger, not removing the individuals who dedicate their lives to serving them. Dr. Lawani's continued detention undermines that mission while imposing unnecessary harm on her family and the countless people who depend on her.”

In his letter, Harder demanded that ICE release Dr. Lawani under an order of supervision and facilitate her immediate return to California, and that DHS provide her and her attorney with the proposed country of removal, supporting travel documentation, and an explanation of the basis for her continued detention.

“My sister is an amazing caregiver, healthcare leader, and educator in our community, and I was devastated not just at her unacceptable arrest, but the decision to send her across the country and detain her unnecessarily. Not only is Dr. Ann a scholar in her profession, but an extremely skilled nurse with unmatched dedication to her patients and students alike. She gives everything she has, daily, to save lives and train the nurses of the future to be as trained, ready and dedicated as she is. As a recognized expert in palliative care as well, I can assure anyone, countless lives have been lost due to her absence, since her wrongful detainment. For someone that vital to the community to be tracked, abruptly vacuumed into an abyss and moved across the country, is simply EVIL and consequential. My family and I want to see my sister returned home safely and as soon as possible, and like so many families in our community, we want an end to the chaos caused by these agencies. I want to thank Congressman Harder for his work to bring Ann home as well as the USF family for their relentless support,” said Samuel Lawani, brother of Dr. Lawani.

“I speak with confidence to what I know firsthand: Dr. Ann Lawani is a person of exceptional professional accomplishment and moral character, deeply embedded in our university community, with responsibilities that hundreds of nursing students and, in turn, the patients they will someday care for, depend upon her fulfilling. Her continued absence causes real and mounting harm to the students and faculty who rely on her mentorship, to our accreditation-mandated curriculum work, and to the safety-net partnerships she has built,” said Eileen K. Fry-Bowers, Dean of the School of Nursing and Health Professions.

Read Harder’s full letter to DHS Secretary Mullin here.

Harder has been pushing for reforms at ICE and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for months, including successfully calling for former Secretary Kristi Noem’s firing. Following her departure, Harder demanded the new Secretary Markwayne Mullin prioritize clear standards for enforcement, bans on face coverings, mandatory identification, new use-of-force policies, and bans on racial profiling. Harder has also continued to oppose any new federal funding for ICE until these reforms are enacted, and he has repeatedly conducted oversight investigations at the Stockton ICE facility.

title: Hayes Responds to Proposed Rule to Remove an Additional 6.3 Million Americans from SNAP
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture, Jahana Hayes (CT-05) issued the following statement in response to the U.S. Department of Agriculture proposed rule to eliminate broad-based categorical eligibility (BBCE), which allows individuals who qualify for Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) or similar state benefits to qualify for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).

“The cruelty of the Trump Administration has no limits. The newly released proposed rule once again targets the most vulnerable among us by narrowing eligibility and blocking families from vital food assistance,” said Ranking Member Hayes. “Eliminating $187 billion in funding in H.R. 1 was not enough; Republicans are now advancing a rule that will push an additional 6.3 million people off SNAP. This change does not aim to mitigate fraud or abuse – it is to inflict harm on families struggling to get by.”

According to the Trump administration regulatory impact analysis of the proposed rule:

6.3 million individuals in 3.2 million households will lose their SNAP benefits entirely.

The 3.2 million families impacted make up 17 percent of SNAP households.

SNAP benefits will be cut by $50.82 billion.

Federal spending on benefits will be cut by $44.65 billion over 5 years (FY2027-FY2031), and state spending on benefits will be cut by $6.17 billion.

SNAP administrative expenses will increase by $1.24 billion.

Federal spending on administrative expenses will increase by $309.5 million over five years.

State spending on administrative costs will increase by $928.5 million.

Increased burden on participants is estimated to be approximately $71.7 million over five years.

Because SNAP participation is often used to streamline eligibility for basic needs programs, the effects of the proposed rule reach beyond the program.

1.78 million children would no longer be categorically eligible for school meals. Of those children:

97 percent would likely remain eligible but need to go through an onerous paperwork process to maintain eligibility.

93,000 children would be shifted from free to reduced-price school meals.

28,000 children would lose free school meals entirely and have to pay full price.

42,000 children will no longer receive Summer EBT (“Sun Bucks”) beginning in the summer of 2029.

An estimated 13,000 of these children would lose benefits they qualify for due to administrative burden (i.e., not applying for SEBT, even though they remain eligible).

5,500 women, infants and children would be kicked off the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC).

The number of states opting in to broad-based categorical eligibility has increased steadily each year because of its positive impact on participants and program administration. Currently, 46 states, Republican and Democratic alike, opt to use BBCE.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON PBS: “WE WILL VISIT ACCOUNTABILITY ON THE WRONGDOERS”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on PBS News Hour, where he emphasized that House Democrats will continue fighting to hold corrupt crooks ripping off the American people accountable and working to lower the high cost of living.

AMNA NAWAZ: Leader Jeffries, welcome back to the show. Thanks for joining us.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Great to be with you.

AMNA NAWAZ: So we’re speaking a week after sweeping midterm Democratic wins. You’re on track to win the largest House majority since 2008. The news, of course, is that you’re also slated to vote later on whether or not to move forward with impeachment of Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. You’ve said you’re a hard yes on that move to impeach him. Will this new Democratic majority mean more impeachment efforts of more Trump administration officials?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’ll cross that bridge when we get to it. We’re focused right now on making sure we’re doing everything possible to hold people accountable for what has happened up until this point, which is why I’m a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution. He’s abused his power. He’s undermined our national security. And Pete Hegseth is the architect of this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has made our country less safe and made life more expensive for the American people.

AMNA NAWAZ: Could that accountability mean more impeachment efforts along the way, though? You haven’t ruled that out?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We haven’t ruled anything in, and we haven’t ruled anything out.

AMNA NAWAZ: I want to ask you about—just yesterday, you received a classified briefing about the NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and his affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. What did you learn in that briefing that told you if US national security had or had not been compromised?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, because it was a classified briefing, I’m limited in what I can reveal, but it certainly is the case that the NVIDIA issue came up. There was a discussion about it, and clearly there’s a need for Members of Congress to be briefed moving forward so we can fully understand exactly the implications for America’s national security. I think the President himself yesterday indicated that the FBI has launched an investigation into the NVIDIA situation. That’s another indication of the serious nature of what may have gone on in terms of involvement by the Chinese Communist Party. And so, Members of Congress, both the Gang of Eight as well as the broader House and Senate, are going to need additional briefings and additional information, certainly in a classified setting, so we can unpack the nature of the damage that may have been done to our country.

AMNA NAWAZ: It was also reported that the President had been briefed on this affair a year ago. Did you see anything that says to you the administration should have acted on this earlier, before these revelations became public?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We haven’t gotten any information that’s been disclosed to us yet to be able to draw any conclusions with respect to the timeline, but that certainly will be exactly the type of questions that we’re going to need to ask. Secretary Rubio wasn’t present at that briefing. He’s overseas, as I understand it. We were briefed by the Director of National Intelligence, as well as the CIA Director. The FBI Director was not present. Certainly, if in fact it is the case that there has been an FBI investigation, which would certainly be appropriate, that has been launched, we’re going to need to hear from the FBI as well.

AMNA NAWAZ: I’m sure you have heard President Trump also say, after those sweeping Democratic wins, that he would love to work with you and the incoming majority, particularly on something for immigration. He then promoted Stephen Miller, the man behind his hard-line immigration approach, to Chief of Staff. Yesterday, you called Mr. Miller a stone-cold racist. You said you have zero interest in working with that kind of individual. So what is one thing that you think you can prioritize getting done with this White House?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, in this Congress, we were able to pass a meaningful housing affordability bill that was bipartisan in nature. That effort was led, of course, by Maxine Waters in the House, working alongside French Hill, a conservative Republican from Arkansas. And in the Senate, that effort was led by Senator Elizabeth Warren, working in partnership with Tim Scott. We were able to get that bill to the President’s desk. He didn’t sign it, but it has become law, and it was a meaningful step forward in terms of trying to create a supply of housing that the American people can afford. And that’s the type of foundational work that hopefully can be done in the next Congress. We’re committed to driving down the high cost of living in every area—that’s housing, that’s healthcare, that’s groceries, that’s gas, that’s caregiving—and to making this country affordable again for everyone.

AMNA NAWAZ: Leader Jeffries, what about on the immigration front? Is there something you can do with this White House?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, certainly on the immigration front, we have a broken immigration system. It needs to be fixed. It should be fixed in a comprehensive way. Immigration enforcement should be fair, just and humane. We’re not going to provide a dime to the administration’s violent mass deportation machine. Let’s work together, perhaps beginning with moving the Dream and Promise Act this Congress as a foundation for the type of work that can be done in the next Congress.

AMNA NAWAZ: That Dream and Promise Act, of course, impacting the DACA recipients. I should point out, it’s been reported some dozens of DACA participants are among those already deported under this administration’s immigration crackdown. Would you support efforts to bring them back into the US?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Certainly. Anyone, whether they are a citizen, whether they were here lawfully, whether they’re a DACA recipient who’s been treated unfairly and unjustly by the administration, we need to provide remedial assistance to them and undo the damage that’s been done to the country, to law-abiding immigrant families and to the American people over these last 20 months or so.

AMNA NAWAZ: What about working across the aisle? As we just reported, Jim Jordan has been elected the Leader of the House Republicans. You, a few years ago, called him the poster child for MAGA extremism and a clear and present danger to our democracy. Do you still believe that’s true? Can you work with him?

LEADER JEFFRIES: That remains to be seen. What I do believe is that the American people gave Democrats in the House and the Senate a decisive majority and want us to get things done on their behalf. They want us to fight for an affordable America, and at the same period of time, they want a Congress that’s going to be a check and balance on an out-of-control executive branch. And that’s going to mean that we visit accountability on the wrongdoers, the individuals who have unleashed this unprecedented corruption on the country over the last two years or so.

AMNA NAWAZ: But what does Jim Jordan’s election say to you about what to expect from House Republicans for the next two years?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I haven’t had an opportunity to talk to Jim today subsequent to his election or see anything that he said about the course that he’s going to chart. We’re going to have a historic majority, the largest majority that any party has had this century, 258 Democrats and counting. We, of course, will always be willing to try to find common ground on the other side of the aisle if there’s interest in doing something meaningful to make life more affordable for the American people. And we’ll see the posture that Jim, as well as the House Republicans, take in the new Congress.

AMNA NAWAZ: You will indeed have a historic majority. And we know House Democrats will hold their Speaker nomination vote next week. It is widely expected that you are poised to make history as the first Black Speaker of the US House of Representatives. You know you face a number of detractors, though, particularly among the incoming newly-elected Members. LaKesha Womack from North Carolina, for example, has said, ‘I don’t think this is a time for us to be moderate,’ when asked if she would back you as Speaker. What is your message to those joining your Caucus now who think that you are too moderate or too establishment to lead Democrats right now?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’re going to work as hard as we can to make the case, of course, to every single Member of the House Democratic Caucus, both current Members and incoming Members, as it relates to the agenda that we’ve set forth. We know that the American people are demanding change that’s bold, that’s dramatic and that’s transformative. And that’s absolutely what we’re going to work hard to deliver.

AMNA NAWAZ: Have you had any conversations with those incoming Members who’ve expressed doubt about your speakership yet?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I’ve had conversations with a lot of different Members, but there are over 81 new Members of the House Democratic Caucus, and so that’s ongoing.

AMNA NAWAZ: Alright, that is House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries joining us tonight. Leader Jeffries, always good to speak with you. Thank you so much for your time.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Thank you.

Full interview can be watched here.

title: Joyce Introduces Bipartisan Legislation to Protect American Manufacturers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representatives Dave Joyce (OH-14), Sharice Davids (KS-03), Mike Turner (OH-10), Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), and Sarah McBride (DE-AL) introduced the Defend American Manufacturing Act 2.0. This bipartisan legislation would strengthen the federal Hollings Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) and protect the resources that help small and medium-sized manufacturers remain competitive.

The proposed changes would require the Department of Commerce to allocate congressionally appropriated funds for Manufacturing Extension Partnership centers, establish clear deadlines for addressing underperforming centers, and prevent funding suspensions or cancellations without a negative performance evaluation. These changes would provide manufacturers with an impartial review process, protect access to critical services, and create greater transparency in how decisions are made.

“Small and mid-sized manufacturers are a driving force behind Ohio’s economy, supporting local jobs, businesses, and communities,” said Congressman Joyce, Co-Chair of the House Manufacturing Caucus. “These businesses need reliable support and resources. I’m proud to help lead this effort to strengthen the MEP program and ensure Ohio manufacturers have what they need to grow and remain competitive for years to come.”

“Shutting down one of the best job-creating programs in the country makes zero sense,” said Congresswoman Davids. “Our local machine shops and small factory owners don’t care about political games in D.C. They just want reliable support so they can hire workers, lower costs, and compete. This bill fixes the loopholes used to cut funding, so groups like Kansas Manufacturing Solutions can keep helping local workers and businesses succeed.”

Background

The Hollings Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) is a national network of centers established in 1988 under the Omnibus Trade and Competitiveness Act (P.L. 100-418). The program provides customized services to small and medium-sized manufacturers to improve production processes, upgrade technological capabilities, and support product innovation. Operating under the Department of Commerce’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), the MEP network includes centers in all 50 states and Puerto Rico.

MEP centers provide manufacturers with technical assistance and resources in areas including production modernization, technology adoption, supply chain strengthening, workforce development, business operations, capital access, and improved management practices.
