title: McCormick: Protecting America’s digital infrastructure starts with common sense
text:
Washington, D.C. — In case you missed it, Congressman Rich McCormick (GA-07) recently wrote an op-ed in The Hill highlighting his newly introduced Common-Sense Cloud Security Act and the urgent need to modernize America's cybersecurity standards as threats to our critical infrastructure continue to evolve.

The legislation directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to update cloud security guidance, strengthen cyber risk assessments, and establish a voluntary certification program to help organizations better prevent, detect, and contain cyberattacks. In the op-ed, McCormick emphasized that protecting America's digital infrastructure requires more than keeping hackers out. It means limiting the damage they can cause once inside, ensuring a single breach cannot compromise an entire network.

“The key challenge is not simply keeping attackers out. It’s limiting what they can do when they get in,” McCormick wrote.

McCormick underscored the importance of practical, risk-based security standards that protect the hospitals, businesses, financial institutions, and government agencies Americans rely on every day without slowing American innovation.

You can read the full op-ed in The Hill or below.

Image

America has embraced cloud computing at a remarkable pace with nearly every aspect of life now running through the cloud. Businesses, hospitals, banks, and government agencies rely on cloud services to store data, run operations, and deliver critical services. As our reliance grows, so does our exposure to cyber threats. The very innovation that has transformed our economy has also created new vulnerabilities that demand our attention.

That’s why I introduced the Common-Sense Cloud Security Act. This bill directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop updated guidance for securing cloud environments and assessing cyber risk in ways that reflect how modern systems actually operate.

The key challenge is not simply keeping attackers out. It’s limiting what they can do when they get in.

Think of a cloud network like a building. Strong locks, passwords, and identity checks keep intruders out. But security also depends on what happens inside. An intruder should not be able to walk into every room, access every file, or reach every critical system. The same principle applies in the cloud.

For far too long, cybersecurity has focused on preventing a breach without giving enough attention to containing one. In today’s increasingly interconnected environments, one compromised account or application should not put an entire network at risk.

Resilience matters just as much as prevention.

As a Marine Corps veteran and member of the House Armed Services Committee, I know firsthand that military and national security depend on the strength of the systems behind them. My work on the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee and the House AI Task Force have reinforced a critical lesson: American innovation and digital security must advance together. As technology evolves, so must our ability to protect it.

Security experts often use the term “blast radius” to describe how far an attack can spread and how much damage it can cause. A single compromised account, application or service should not become a gateway to an entire organization. Effective cybersecurity is not just about detecting threats. It is about containing them. Measuring and reducing that risk provides a more meaningful assessment of security than simply determining whether suspicious activity can be detected.

The rise of super intelligence (formerly, “artificial intelligence”) makes this challenge even more urgent. Modern SI systems increasingly interact with multiple applications, databases and services across an organization. While these capabilities can create tremendous productivity and efficiency gains, they can also expand the potential consequences of a compromise. The more authority a system has, the more important it becomes to establish clear limits on what it can access.

This is not about slowing innovation with another unnecessary layer of bureaucracy. It is about developing practical, risk-based security standards that reflect how modern cloud systems actually work and giving organizations meaningful ways to demonstrate that they are in compliance.

If effective cybersecurity means limiting the damage caused by a breach, then our standards must reflect that reality. That is why my Common-Sense Cloud Security Act directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop updated guidance for modern cloud environments, including identity management, oversight of third-party connections, detection of suspicious activity, and ways to assess the potential impact of a compromise. The bill would also establish a voluntary certification program and help ensure federal cloud security requirements keep pace with evolving technology and threats.

No law or standard can eliminate every cyber threat. What we can do is make attacks harder, limit their impact, and improve our ability to recover when they occur.

I will continue working with cybersecurity experts and industry leaders to strengthen the security of the cloud infrastructure Americans rely on every day. In today's interconnected world, security is not measured by whether a breach occurs. It is measured by how well we contain it. Cyber threats will continue to evolve, but a single breach should never be allowed to become a systemic failure. That is the standard we should strive for as we secure America’s digital future.

title: McGovern and Raskin Condemn Trump Administration’s Withdrawal from Human Rights Accountability Mechanism
text:
WASHINGTON—Today, Congressman Jim McGovern, Co-Chair of the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission and Ranking Member of the House Rules Committee, and Congressman Jamie Raskin, Executive Committee Member of the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission and Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, released the following statement condemning the United States’ absence from its Universal Periodic Review.

Today, the Trump Administration refused to participate in the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) of the UN Human Rights Council in a shameful attempt to shield itself from accountability for its failure to uphold the rights of the American public. This mechanism provides a standard peer-review-type evaluation of the human rights commitments of every UN member. In 2025, the Trump Administration broke with precedent and announced that the United States would not participate in the UPR, as it had done without objection in 2020, 2015, and 2010. This gave the U.S. the ignominious distinction of becoming the first Member State to refuse to engage in the UPR, undermining the mechanism’s legitimacy and making our nation a pariah.

The UPR has been a vital venue in which Administrations of both parties have sought to hold accountable the world’s worst abusers of human rights. Secretary of State Marco Rubio encouraged U.S. engagement as recently as 2024, when as Senator he wrote to then-Secretary of State Blinken urging him to raise human rights issues during China’s fourth UPR, including the unjust imprisonment of Dr. Gulshan Abbas, Joshua Wong, and Jimmy Lai. “The United States must stand up for the principle of the universality of human rights and help hold the PRC accountable for its ignoring its obligations to respect human rights under international law,” Rubio said. We agree. But the United States cannot credibly demand that China’s government—or any other—honor their human rights commitments while refusing to subject its own record to scrutiny.

The Administration’s refusal is also out of step with the American public. A recent study found that 92 percent of Americans believe that leading by example on human rights is important to the United States' global reputation. Withdrawal from the UPR undermines American credibility, suggesting the Administration lacks confidence in its ability to defend its human rights record. It also risks encouraging rights-abusing governments, such as China and Russia, to follow the U.S. precedent to evade accountability themselves.

The Trump Administration should reverse its decision. The American people demand scrutiny. As we prepare for a new Congress, we recommit ourselves to fostering respect for human dignity and the systems that help to uphold it—for the sake of the American people and our neighbors around the world.

title: Reps. Mejia, Cisneros, Morrison Propose Tariff Hotline for Small Business Owners
text:
For Immediate Release: November 10, 2026

Contact: Beth Wiesinger | NJ11AMPress@Mail.House.Gov

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Congressman Gil Cisneros (CA-31), and Congresswoman Kelly Morrison (MN-03) introduced the Small Business Tariff Relief Hotline Act to give business owners a dedicated place to voice their tariff-related issues so they can’t be ignored. If passed, this legislation would create a Tariffs and Refunds Hotline within the Small Business Administration (SBA) Office of Advocacy for small businesses to report tariff-related issues, and require the Chief Counsel to submit annual reports to Congress summarizing these issues and recommending fixes. The Small Business Majority is a supporting organization of the legislation.

“Small businesses are the backbone of our communities and our economy, and right now, too many of them are navigating Donald Trump's chaotic tariff disruptions on their own,” said Congresswoman Analilia Mejia. “When costs rise and supply chains get tangled, small business owners shouldn’t have to wonder who to call or whether anyone will pick up. By creating a dedicated Tariffs and Refunds Hotline and requiring annual congressional oversight, we make sure these concerns are tracked, taken seriously, and acted on. I am proud to co-lead this effort because our small business owners deserve a government that listens when they ask for help. It is time to stand up for the entrepreneurs who power our economy.”

“Tariffs are crushing our small businesses by driving economic uncertainty, job loss, and rising costs across the country,” said Congressman Gil Cisneros. “In 2025, small businesses with fewer than 10 employees lost more jobs than in any other year in recent history. For the small businesses that tried to voice their concerns on the effects of Donald Trump’s economic chaos, they were dismissed with the Office of Advocacy telling Congress it is ‘out-of-scope.' I introduced the Small Business Tariff Relief Hotline Act to give our small businesses a voice on tariffs and the refund process, and require the SBA Office of Advocacy to actually listen to small businesses across the country and work with Congress to provide relief.”

“President Trump’s tariffs are driving up prices, making life more unaffordable, and posing an existential threat to our small businesses. Small businesses aren’t able to absorb the costs of tariffs in the same way that larger businesses are – and they certainly don’t have the time or people power to tackle all the administrative burden of seeking tariff refunds,” said Congresswoman Kelly Morrison. “We need the Small Business Administration to create a direct line to help small business owners get the refunds they need and are owed from these illegal tariffs. This legislation is an important step to both help us save our small businesses – the engine of our economy – and also to lower costs for all Americans. I’m going to continue to do everything I can to make life more affordable for Minnesotans, to fight for our small business owners, and help grow a thriving economy.”

According to research conducted by the Small Business Majority, in 2025, 60% of small businesses reported higher costs due to tariffs, and over 80% of small businesses classified tariffs as a major worry for their business.

title: RELEASE: Congressman Menefee Joins Colleagues in Demanding Action on Growing Medicaid Backlog
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Representative Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) joined members of the Texas Democratic Delegation calling on the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and Texas Health and Human Services Commission to address the state's growing Medicaid backlog.

Texas' Medicaid application backlog has grown from 1,671 pending applications in January 2026 to more than 237,000 by early September. The delays come as federal changes under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act place additional strain on an already overwhelmed state benefits system.

In letters to U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Texas Health and Human Services Commissioner Stephanie Muth, the members called for an investigation into the backlog, including an evaluation of contracted vendors, and federal intervention if the state fails to adequately address the delays.

“Our district has one of the highest concentrations of SNAP recipients in the state, yet families are going hungry and suffering without access to proper healthcare because of massive backlogs in Medicaid and SNAP applications brought on by Abbott and Trump,” said Congressman Menefee. “Folks are legally entitled to these benefits, yet Republicans remain hell-bent on withholding them from our most vulnerable communities.”

The members also raised concerns about the impact of administrative changes under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which cuts approximately $1 trillion in federal Medicaid funding over 10 years. Because Texas uses an integrated application system for programs like Medicaid and SNAP, technical errors and processing delays in one program can affect a person's access to other benefits.

The letters also highlighted the consequences for vulnerable Texans, including children, pregnant women, seniors, and people with disabilities. In one reported case, a pregnant Texas woman waited four months without an update on her Medicaid application, delaying access to coverage for prenatal care.

The Medicaid backlog rose from 1,671 applications in January 2026 to 237,505 by early September 2026. In July, Texas processed 65% of Medicaid applications on time, down from 81% last year. The OBBBA cuts $1 trillion in Medicaid funding over ten years. The number of people participating in Medicaid and the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) in Texas dropped by about 247,317 between September 2025 and July 2026.

The letter was signed by Reps. Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Greg Casar (TX-35), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Lloyd Doggett (TX-37), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Al Green (TX-9), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Marc Veasey (TX-33), and Lizzie Fletcher (TX-7).

title: Speaker Johnson Addresses Press as Congress Reconvenes
text:
WASHINGTON — Yesterday, Speaker Johnson delivered remarks to press ahead of the House’s first votes following the midterm elections. Speaker Johnson highlighted House GOP wins in the 119th Congress as well as the extraordinary class of incoming House GOP Members.

Watch the Speaker’s full remarks here.

Below are Speaker Johnson’s remarks as delivered:

It's good to be back here in the Capitol with all our colleagues after a long and demanding campaign cycle to be certain. The results were not what we hoped for, and we worked for, as you all know, but this is our system. I know without any shadow of a doubt that we left it all on the field. I personally raised well over half a billion dollars for this campaign cycle, and I logged enough miles campaigning for my colleagues to circle the globe over nine times. There's not much more that many of us could have done, and the people have spoken. Are we disappointed with the results? Of course we are. But we're never discouraged. That's not in our worldview. And I just want to say we made our case in plain and simple terms. The American people voted, and we're going to have a new crop of Members take their seats at the start of the new year. This is our system.

I was delighted to welcome all the new Members on the House floor last night. Hakeem Jeffries and I met them, and we'll be doing a reception, a dinner, for the new Republican freshman class. And we're very excited about this group. It's an extraordinary, talented group of people, patriots, who are willing to step forward and serve their country. And I cannot be more proud of who they are. You're going to get to know them well and you'll be duly impressed.

The question facing Republicans right now is how do we respond after getting knocked down? And the answer is to get right back up. We stand for enduring. We stand for and defend, every day, the founding principles of the greatest nation in the history of the world. And you all have said, we say over and over, it's objectively true that we are the freest, most successful, most powerful, most benevolent nation that has ever been on the earth. But it is not guaranteed to us. Ronald Reagan used to remind us that freedom is never more than one generation away from extinction. We do not pass it in the bloodstream. It's got to be fought for and protected, and then it has to be taught and preserved and passed along to the next generation so that they too will have the same liberty and opportunity and security that we have known and, sadly too many Americans have taken for granted.

And so, what we fight for is, you all have heard me refer to, what I call seven core principles of American conservatism: individual freedom, limited government, the rule of law, peace through strength, fiscal responsibility, free markets, and human dignity. We believe in the principles that have endured, that have made us the longest lasting constitution, the envy of all governments and countries. Everyone wants to be like America and there's a reason for that. And those principles are under assault. They're under great challenge. And I fear that in the days ahead, in the next two years of this Congress, they will be openly challenged here, perhaps even in the halls of Congress. And so, we're entrusting that our team, even though we will be in the minority in the next Congress, will stand strong and defend those principles. And we look forward to doing it. And we will. This is a moment of sober reflection for us as in part, in terms of how we handle that.

We were so proud to run on our extraordinary record because as you all know, and you catalog here every day, in spite of having one of the smallest margins in the history of this institution and an unprecedented obstruction by Democrats who brought shutdowns and the longest shutdowns in US history – 120 days to be complete, even then we delivered for the people. We brought famously the largest tax cut for working families and middle-class earners in American history. We had the biggest spending cut in US history, $1.6 trillion focusing on rooting out fraud and waste in government, making it work more efficiently and effectively for the people. We secured the border tight. That was the number one issue in 2024, and we took care of that problem. And we restored common sense. We did things like cutting burdensome crushing regulations to allow job creators and entrepreneurs to do more of what they do and add more jobs and more opportunity for more Americans. And because of that, we're experiencing the lowest poverty rate in the history of those data points since they began in 1959 with the lowest poverty rate in America right now. We also have the safest as streets. We have the lowest violent crime rate in 126 years. Because of our policies and what we did, we had the biggest decline in prescription drug costs in over 60 years. We had a million jobs out in the private sector, just in the last 19 months or so. And it goes on and on and on. Trump Accounts for every newborn. You have the first ever nationwide school choice program codified in the law. Nearly 130 Executive Orders codified and signed into law and so much more. And so, we're going to double down on the things that worked when we do this reflection after an election, which both parties do. We're going to fix what doesn't, and we're going to spend the next two years fighting tooth and nail to put ourselves in the best possible position to win back Congress and preserve this grand experiment in self-governance.

title: THIRTY ARMED SERVICES DEMOCRATS, VETERANS, RAISE ALARM OVER MARCH ATTACK ON NSA BAHRAIN, PENTAGON’S POOR TREATMENT OF EVACUATED MILITARY FAMILIES
text:
Congressmembers Ryan, Deluzio, and Senator Blumenthal led the letter to Secretary Hegseth, letter covered by MSNOW

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, 30 members of Congress signed on to a letter demanding action and answers from the Pentagon about the poor treatment of military servicemembers and their families who were evacuated from Naval Support Activity Bahrain (NSA Bahrain) in March 2026.

This letter comes after MS NOW reported on the details of a hasty and traumatic evacuation from NSA Bahrain in March, noting that many military family members have been living out of hotels and short-term rentals and are being required to pay out of pocket to cover these expenses. The letter demands that the Department of Defense right this wrong and support these evacuated military families.

The members of Congress also asked the Secretary how much it would cost to repair the severe damage to NSA Bahrain and how the incapacitation of the base has impacted U.S. operations in the Iran War and the wider Middle East.

The letter is co-led by Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Congressman Pat Ryan (NY-18), and Senator Richard Blumenthal (CT). The letter signatories are members of the House Armed Services Committee, the Senate Armed Services Committee, or are members of the Democratic Veterans Caucus.

“The American people – military families especially – are rightly furious about the war in Iran and Hegseth’s continued betrayals, cover-ups, and broken promises,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “The families evacuated from NSA Bahrain have been put through hell. Parents shielding their kids from bomb blasts, homes abandoned in a panic, cherished memories lost forever, and now facing huge personal financial burdens. It is unbelievable the DoD leadership denied the Navy’s request to extend safe haven entitlements. The Pentagon has a TRILLION dollar budget, and it’s unconscionable that Pete Hegseth is choosing to leave these families in the lurch. We’re demanding answers and accountability.

The letter reads, “President Trump launched the Iran War on February 28th before evacuating the roughly 8,300 military personnel, DoD civilians, and their families stationed at NSA Bahrain. Families were authorized to evacuate only after the war started, subjecting them to the Iranian retaliatory strikes that heavily damaged the base. Since March, these evacuees have been under constant emotional, financial, and psychological stress... While the Department of Defense has provided safe haven entitlements to offset the cost of living for evacuees, this funding is scheduled to be terminated in November or after the 180th day of receiving the entitlement, before many have found permanent housing and transportation.”

The members continue, “Because NSA Bahrain was a critical logistics hub for U.S. Central Command, we require a better understanding of how the severe damage to the base has impacted U.S. operations… We have significant concerns about the morale and welfare of the troops deployed to the region, especially in light of the reporting on the conditions onboard the USS Gerald R. Ford and USS Abraham Lincoln, which both served record breaking deployments.”

Specifically, the members requested answers by November 13, 2026 to the following questions:

Why was the Navy’s request to extend the safe haven entitlements for evacuees denied?

Who made this decision?

Why are safe haven entitlements for evacuees being terminated before the arrival of household goods?

What will the Department of Defense do to ensure that evacuees from NSA Bahrain are not paying out of pocket for living expenses incurred by the evacuation?

What processes, if any, are in place for evacuees to receive reimbursement for expenses incurred, and how many reimbursement cases are pending?

Given the damage to NSA Bahrain, which logistic hub (or hubs) has the Department of Defense been using amidst the Iran War?

What has been the operational impact of the loss of NSA Bahrain?

Does the Department of Defense intend to repair and rebuild NSA Bahrain?

If so, how much is the expected cost for such work?

What is the financial cost of the damage to NSA Bahrain?

The House signatories of the letter are: Reps. Chris Deluzio (PA-17, co-lead), Pat Ryan (NY-18, co-lead), Wesley Bell (MO-01), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), Herb Conaway (NJ-03), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Jason Crow (CO-06), Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), John Garamendi (CA-08), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), Bill Keating (MA-09), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Adam Smith (WA-09), Eric Sorensen (IL-17), Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), Mike Thompson (CA-04), Derek Tran (CA-45), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), and George Whitesides (CA-27).

The Senate signatories of the letter are: Sens. Richard Blumenthal (CT, co-lead), Tammy Duckworth (IL), Kirstin Gillibrand (NY), Mazie Hirono (HI), Jacky Rosen (NV), Elizabeth Warren (MA).

The full text of the letter is below and is linked here.

Dear Secretary Hegseth:

We write to raise concern over reporting that servicemembers and their families are continuing to face significant hardship following their evacuation from Naval Support Activity Bahrain (NSA Bahrain) in March this year. Additionally, we seek to better understand how the incapacitation of NSA Bahrain has impacted U.S. operations in the Iran War and the broader Middle East. In an August town hall, Chief of Naval Operations, Adm. Daryl Caudle, said that the Navy would not be using NSA Bahrain for the foreseeable future. This is significant not only for the thousands of servicemembers and their families personally involved, but also because NSA Bahrain is a critical logistics hub that has served as the headquarters for U.S. Naval Forces Central Command and U.S. Navy Fifth Fleet since 1995.

Servicemembers and Their Families are Not Receiving Adequate Support

As you know, President Trump launched the Iran War on February 28th before evacuating the roughly 8,300 military personnel, DoD civilians, and their families stationed at NSA Bahrain. Families were authorized to evacuate only after the war started, subjecting them to the Iranian retaliatory strikes that heavily damaged the base. Since March, these evacuees have been under constant emotional, financial, and psychological stress. Some have had to move across continents, stay in temporary lodging for months, enroll their children in a new school mid-year, pay out of pocket for significant costs associated with a move and more, all often without access to belongings they were forced to leave behind. While the Department of Defense has provided safe haven entitlements to offset the cost of living for evacuees, this funding is scheduled to be terminated in November or after the 180th day of receiving the entitlement, before many have found permanent housing and transportation.

In a recent town hall, Navy officials relayed that your Department of Defense leadership had denied a request to extend the safe haven entitlements, and that each evacuee had to seek individual approval from the Acting Secretary of the Navy. This is unacceptable. To make matters worse, the signing of a lease is being used as a triggering event for termination of the safe haven entitlement. This is bad policy. Although a family may have signed a lease for a permanent residence, they may still have to use a rental vehicle or stay in temporary lodging while they wait for their household goods to arrive from overseas. Requiring servicemembers to pay out of pocket for expenses that were forced upon them by your mismanagement of the Iran War is wrong. You must fix this.

Loss of NSA Bahrain and U.S. Presence in the Middle East

As the Iran War reaches the ninth month, our constituents have expressed increasing concern about the cost of the conflict and the lack of transparency surrounding U.S. operations and strategic goals in the region. Because NSA Bahrain was a critical logistics hub for U.S. Central Command, we require a better understanding of how the severe damage to the base has impacted U.S. operations. In August, the New York Times reported that the U.S Navy is now resupplying from Diego Garcia, an island in the Indian Ocean 2,200 miles away from the Persian Gulf. We have significant concerns about the morale and welfare of the troops deployed to the region, especially in light of the reporting on the conditions onboard the USS Gerald R. Ford and USS Abraham Lincoln, which both served record breaking deployments.

In executing the Congress’s oversight authority under Article I of the Constitution, we request answers to the following questions by November 13, 2026.

Why was the Navy’s request to extend the safe haven entitlements for evacuees denied?

Who made this decision?

Why are safe haven entitlements for evacuees being terminated before the arrival of household goods?

What will the Department of Defense do to ensure that evacuees from NSA Bahrain are not paying out of pocket for living expenses incurred by the evacuation?

What processes, if any, are in place for evacuees to receive reimbursement for expenses incurred, and how many reimbursement cases are pending?

Given the damage to NSA Bahrain, which logistic hub (or hubs) has the Department of Defense been using amidst the Iran War?

What has been the operational impact of the loss of NSA Bahrain?

Does the Department of Defense intend to repair and rebuild NSA Bahrain?

If so, how much is the expected cost for such work?

What is the financial cost of the damage to NSA Bahrain?

title: Pelosi, Castor Introduce Bill to Help Aging Veterans & Veterans With Disabilities Stay in Their Homes
text:
Washington, D.C. — Yesterday, Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi and Rep. Kathy Castor introduced the No Veteran Left Behind: Housing Retention Act of 2026 to help aging Veterans and Veterans with disabilities remain safely housed. The legislation would create a new grant program within the Department of Veterans Affairs’ Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) program, giving community providers resources to deliver tailored services that help veterans maintain their health, live independently and avoid homelessness.

“Veteran homelessness is a challenge to the conscience of our nation. No person who served our nation in uniform should be forced to sleep on our streets because the support they earned and deserve is out of reach,” said Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi. “This legislation helps codify the successful California pilot as a national model that helped fill the gap for San Francisco’s elderly and disabled Veterans—the fastest growing cohort. By meeting Veterans where they are, this transformative legislation would enhance access and stability for Veterans to their health care, transportation and daily supports that they need, earned and deserve. Just as our Veterans kept their promise to our nation, we must keep our promise to them when they come home.”

“No veteran should lose their home because they cannot get the care and support they need. The patriotic Tampa Bay area expects veterans who served our country to be able to age with dignity and live safely,” said Rep. Castor. “This bill will give trusted community providers more tools to help Veterans manage their health, get to medical appointments and prevent an eviction before it happens. I’m proud to partner with Speaker Emerita Pelosi to help Veterans stay in their homes and ensure our commitment to them lasts long after their military service ends.”

“Elderly and disabled veterans are the fastest growing group of veterans experiencing homelessness, and getting them into housing is only the first step. Keeping them there takes health care navigation, mental health support, and help with daily living, delivered where they live,” said House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Mark Takano. “Speaker Emerita Pelosi and Rep. Castor’s bill does that. California’s pilot proved the model works, with fewer than 4 percent of veterans losing their housing and emergency room visits down 75 percent. Veterans’ Affairs Committee Democrats are proud to support this bill, and I thank them for their leadership.”

Veterans’ needs are changing as they age. In 2015, 55 percent of SSVF participants had a disabling condition; by 2023, that share had increased to 70 percent. Approximately half of SSVF participants in 2024 were aged 55 or older. The legislation would help community providers respond with more intensive, individualized support, including services delivered in veterans’ homes.

The No Veteran Left Behind: Housing Retention Act would support services including:

Mental and behavioral health care, including individual and group counseling, substance use disorder counseling, crisis intervention and peer support;

Food and meal assistance, help with grocery shopping, and transportation to medical appointments, grocery stores, job interviews and other community services;

Occupational therapy, functional assessments, coordination of assistive devices and home accessibility modifications;

Medication management support and help navigating health care options;

Eviction prevention, tenant support and in-home services that help veterans maintain safe, habitable housing;

Financial management assistance and therapeutic and social activities.

The bill would prioritize providers serving Veterans transitioning from homelessness to permanent housing and veterans who need ongoing services to remain housed and avoid unnecessary institutionalization. It would also require coordination among VA, health care providers, housing providers and community organizations to address Veterans’ needs and reduce duplication of services.

National Alliance to End Homelessness

New Visions

Village for Vets

USVETS

The American Legion

Veterans of Foreign Wars

National Coalition for Homeless Veterans

Disabled American Veterans

title: Pou Brings Nearly $1 Million To Aid  New Jersey Victims of Human Trafficking
text:
PATERSON, NJ – Today Congresswoman Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) announced $934,758 in federal funding from the U.S. Department of Justice to enhance the identification, response, and existing systems for victims of human trafficking in Paterson and Passaic County.

“Human trafficking is a horrific issue that touches far more families and individuals than we sometimes realize,” said Rep. Nellie Pou. “Behind every statistic is a human being who deserves to feel safe and who should be able to live without fear. Bringing this funding to St. Joseph’s Health and Covenant House New Jersey, is crucial to achieving the goal of making our communities safer.”

The recipient of this grant is St. Joseph’s Health who, in partnership with Covenant House New Jersey, will provide immediate, on-site victim engagement, conduct comprehensive needs assessments, and facilitate direct connection to the state’s Human Trafficking Victim Services program.

“As healthcare providers, we have a unique opportunity and responsibility to recognize when someone may be experiencing human trafficking and to respond not only with compassion and dignity, but also to connect them to the appropriate resources and support. This grant will allow St. Joseph’s Health to strengthen education across our organization, create more consistent pathways for identification and referral, and deepen our partnership with Covenant House New Jersey. Most importantly, it will help ensure that vulnerable individuals in our community know that St. Joseph’s is a safe place where they can receive care, support and a connection to the services they need,” said Debbie Smith, Chief Nursing and Patient Care Officer at St. Joseph’s Health.

This federal funding will integrate healthcare and proven community-based systems that will improve victim identification, access to care, and advance safety, recovery, and long-term stability for victims of human trafficking.

As a member of the House Homeland Security Committee, Congresswoman Pou has championed public safety initiatives. This includes introducing the Combating International Drug Trafficking and Human Smuggling Partnership Act, fighting to protect vital legislation like the Violence Against Women Act, and promoting federal resources that help survivors rebuild their lives.

title: Congresswoman Luz Rivas Votes to Proceed with Impeachment Proceedings Against Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth

title: Ruiz Leads Call to Pass the Major Richard Star Act by Veterans Day
text:
Washington, D.C. - November 9, 2026 - Today, Congressman Dr. Raul Ruiz (CA-25), Lead Democratic on the Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102), held a press conference with House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs Ranking Member Mark Takano (CA-39) to demand passage of the bill by Veterans Day. The bill ends the “wounded veteran tax,” the offset that takes a dollar of retirement pay from combat-wounded, medically retired veterans for every dollar of VA disability compensation they receive.

“Combat-wounded veterans who were forced to medically retire are being shortchanged by the VA,” said Congressman Dr. Raul Ruiz (CA-25). “For every dollar in VA disability compensation these veterans receive, a dollar is taken out of their retirement pay. Our veterans deserve respect, they do NOT deserve to be treated like a burdensome, expendable line item in a budget. That is why I am proud to co-author the Major Richard Star Act, which ends this unfair offset. Our veterans stood up for us. Now we must stand up for them. I urge Speaker Johnson to bring it up for a vote and my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to vote yes.”

Ruiz thanked Ranking Member Takano for his Herculean effort to secure the final signatures on the discharge petition and force a vote. He thanked the veterans service organizations for standing with combat-wounded veterans every step of the way.

“Veterans, we have heard your call for action, and we are ready to help deliver relief. For 59,000 combat-injured veterans, relief has been long overdue, but House Democrats have worked tirelessly to change that. In just five months, we secured the necessary support to discharge the rules and bring the Major Richard Star Act to the House floor for a final vote. We are closer than ever; now is the moment to finish the job. I urge my colleagues in the Senate to act swiftly so we can deliver this critical support before Veterans Day,” said Ranking Member Takano.

Tens of thousands of veterans lose about $14,400 a year, according to the Military Officers Association of America.

At the press conference, Ruiz shared the story of Daniel Hinojosa Jr., who served nine years in the U.S. Army and deployed to Iraq three times. He came home with injuries to his brain, back, neck, and knees. Medically retired in 2011, he was told he had to choose between his VA disability compensation and the Army retirement he earned. Today, Daniel is earning his master’s in social work and interning in Ruiz’s Beaumont office, helping other veterans.

Ruiz and Takano introduced the resolution to begin the discharge petition process on April 30. The petition reached the required 218 signatures on September 15. Separately, the bill has 340 bipartisan cosponsors in the House and 80 in the Senate.

title: Scanlon, Garcia Lead 22 House Democrats in Opposing HHS Secretary Kennedy’s Plan to Subject Vulnerable Immigrant Children to a Captive and Compromised Legal Unit
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05) and Rep. Sylvia Garcia (TX-29) last week led 22 House Democratic colleagues in opposing Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.’s plan to create a captive legal unit named the “Unaccompanied Alien Children Legal Representation Division” (UACLRD). The proposed unit would disregard congressional intent to protect vulnerable immigrant children by creating insurmountable conflicts of interest and precluding effective representation.

A recent notice outlining a revised Statement of Organization of the HHS Office of General Counsel (OGC) includes the creation of an entirely new division within the office called the “Unaccompanied Alien Children Legal Representation Division” (UACLRD) that would operate “as a legal service provider” and provide “direct legal services” to unaccompanied children. Congress has recognized on a bipartisan basis that unaccompanied children require assistance navigating our immigration system due to their unique vulnerability and developmental level. In 2008, Congress passed the Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act (TVPRA), which requires that HHS ensure counsel for these children. For nearly two decades, HHS has sought to fulfill the TVPRA’s mandate by funding outside independent legal services providers.

“By contrast, legal representation provided by attorneys who work for HHS would create fundamental and unavoidable conflicts of interest. These attorneys would be subject to supervision by agency leadership and undoubtedly be influenced by the priorities of the administration in office, including implicit or explicit pressure to advance the Trump administration’s aim of swiftly removing unaccompanied children without meaningful consideration of due process,” the members wrote. “Effective legal representation often requires diligent identification and pursuit of avenues of legal protection for which a child client may be eligible, including asylum, Special Immigrant Juvenile Status (SIJS), trafficking visas, or other forms of relief—actions at odds with federal agencies’ current emphasis on rapid case completion and removal.”

Establishment of UACLRD raises troubling questions on conflicts of interest, attorney independence, disregard for congressional intent, and ensuring the confidentiality of clients is one of the most notable concerns. Attorney independence is essential for ensuring compliance with client confidentiality requirements. If information about child clients gathered by HHS attorneys are recorded in government systems, it raises the possibility that DHS—the agency responsibility for prosecuting immigration cases against these children—would have access to information that should be confidential under attorney-client privilege.

“Moreover, HHS is the agency responsible for unaccompanied children’s care and custody, but attorneys for unaccompanied children regularly need to advocate to HHS’s Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) for release of children to safe, vetted sponsors—work that is especially urgent given ORR’s unnecessarily prolonged detention of children in their custody under the Trump administration,” the members continued. “Attorneys cannot serve as independent advocates when they are employed by the very agency whose decisions they may need to contest.”

“UACLRD is irreparably compromised. We urge you to eliminate this division immediately,” the members concluded.

In the letter, the members requested answers to a number of questions by Wednesday, November 18, 2026.

title: Reps. Vargas, Jacobs, Levin, Peters and Senators Padilla and Schiff Demand Answers After 8-Year-Old is Detained at Immigration Check-In
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representatives Juan Vargas (CA-52), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), Mike Levin (CA-49), and Scott Peters (CA-50) and U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA) demanded answers from the Trump Administration after an eight-year-old Haitian child who lost Temporary Protected Status was taken into federal custody after an immigration check-in in San Diego.

“An ICE officer reportedly invoked the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 while taking him into custody, apparently placing the child in restraints and separating him from the person who brought him for his hearing. Video footage appears to show the use of restraints on a child who seemed to pose no threat to those around him, raising serious questions about the handling of this incident,” wrote the lawmakers. “We express concerns about the basis for this action and the harm it may cause a young child who appeared for his required hearing.”

“With this letter, we emphasize that the safety and well-being of children and families in San Diego County must remain the highest priority,” the lawmakers continued. “We also request confirmation on the child’s whereabouts, whether his family is aware of his location, and what steps your agencies are taking to ensure he can be reunited with them.”

Read the full letter HERE and below.

Dear Secretary Mullin and Secretary Kennedy,

We write to express deep concerns regarding reports that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detained an eight-year-old Haitian child at a scheduled immigration hearing in San Diego, California, on November 5, 2026. An ICE officer reportedly invoked the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 while taking him into custody, apparently placing the child in restraints and separating him from the person who brought him for his hearing. Video footage appears to show the use of restraints on a child who seemed to pose no threat to those around him, raising serious questions about the handling of this incident. We express concerns about the basis for this action and the harm it may cause a young child who appeared for his required hearing before the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR).

Our September 22, 2026, letter concerning ICE enforcement activity around school and educational institutions addressed the fear and disruption these actions cause in our communities. House Members of the San Diego congressional delegation also wrote to both the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Department of Education on October 14, 2025, highlighting concerns from twenty-five San Diego County school district superintendents. The superintendents requested DHS to adopt clear consistent enforcement policies and coordination between the departments to keep schools safe places to learn. This reported detention underscores those concerns. Following this third-grade student’s detention, San Diego Unified School District reportedly sent crisis counselors to Fay Elementary School to support his classmates, who expressed fear and distress. The effects of this action extend far beyond one child and his family.

With this letter, we emphasize that the safety and well-being of children and families in San Diego County must remain the highest priority. We will continue to monitor this situation closely and expect timely updates on the child’s well-being and your agencies’ response to these concerns. We also request confirmation on the child’s whereabouts, whether his family is aware of his location, and what steps your agencies are taking to ensure he can be reunited with them. We ask that you promptly review this child’s case and give it your full and fair consideration based on its merits, consistent with all applicable laws, rules, and regulations. Please provide our offices with an update regarding your findings from this review by December 1, 2026.

title: Vindman Introduces Legislation to Expand Access to Cardiovascular Screening and Early Detection
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) today introduced legislation to expand access to important cardiovascular screening tests by requiring coverage without cost sharing under group health plans, individual health insurance coverage, Medicare, and Medicaid.

The Cardiovascular Disease Early Detection and Prevention Act would require coverage of Lp(a) and ApoB testing without cost sharing for individuals with certain cardiovascular risk factors, including a family history of premature cardiovascular disease, a personal history of heart attack or stroke, elevated LDL cholesterol, diabetes, obesity, or other recognized risk factors. By removing out-of-pocket costs for these tests, this legislation would help eligible patientsidentify cardiovascular risks earlier and work with their health care providers to make informed decisions about prevention and treatment.

“Too many Americans face serious health consequences because cardiovascular risks go undetected until it’s too late,”said Vindman. “By expanding access to critical screening tests and eliminating out-of-pocket costs for eligible patients, we can help more Americans identify potential risks early and take steps to protect their health. I’m grateful to the Boatman family for sharing their story and helping bring attention to this important issue, and I’m proud to work alongside them to introduce legislation that could save lives.”

Vindman introduced this legislation after hearing from veteran and constituent Johnny Boatman, who lives with cardiovascular disease. Mr. Boatman is an advocate with the Partnership to Advance Cardiovascular Health (PACH), where he raises awareness of cardiovascular disease and the importance of early detection and prevention.

“I served 25 years in the Army, and I learned that the threats you see coming are the ones you can defeat,” said Johnny Boatman, PACH Patient Advocate. “My heart condition was hereditary, and by the time it was found, prevention was no longer an option for me. It doesn’t have to be that way for others. H.R. 8260 gives families the chance to know their risk early, with no cost standing in the way. I’m fighting for this bill so other families get the head start mine never had.”

The Cardiovascular Disease Early Detection and Prevention Act was co-drafted with Roseline Moise, Vice President of Heart Sistas, Inc., based on the lived experience of Hyvelle Ferguson-Davis, Founder and President of Heart Sistas, Inc.

“Nothing for us without us. I survived a stroke, two heart attacks, a bypass, and 10 stents keeping me alive,” said Hyvelle Ferguson-Davis, Founder/President of Heart Sistas, Inc. “I think families shattered by heart disease and strokes. Today, is a remarkable day in drafting the Cardiovascular Early Detection and Prevention Act of 2025 (CEDPA) advancing early detection, prevention, and health equity. Change starts with me, and it stops with Us, together we are going to save lives.”

“For far too many families, heart disease is discovered too late,” said Roseline Moise, Vice President of Heart Sistas, Inc. “This legislation represents a powerful step toward health equity. By expanding access to advanced testing like Lp(a) and ApoB, we can identify risk earlier, prevent avoidable tragedies, and save lives.”

This bill is also endorsed by the Partnership to Advance Cardiovascular Health (PACH) and the Family Heart Foundation.

“You can exercise, eat well and keep your LDL in check and still have dangerously high Lp(a),” said Ryan Gough, Executive Director of PACH. “This inherited risk factor goes undetected by routine cholesterol tests, and too many patients learn they have it only after a heart attack or stroke. A simple, one-time test can change that. Expanding access to Lp(a) screening means identifying risk before tragedy strikes. It’s meaningful progress in the fight against America’s #1 killer—heart disease.”

“According to recently published data from the Family Heart Foundation, fewer than 2% of adult Americans have been screened for Lp(a), a powerful, independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease,” said Hilly Paige, Jr, the Chief Innovation Officer for the Family Heart Foundation. “Lp(a) screening has been shown to be cost saving for the US healthcare system, is endorsed by the most recent 2026 US Dyslipidemia Guidelines, and yet coverage by insurance companies remains suboptimal, with many people facing high out of pocket costs. H.R. 8260 represents an important step forward to improve access for Lp(a) and ApoB testing.”

title: Barrasso Secures Commitments From Trump Admin Nominees on Wyoming Soda Ash, Uranium, and Community Banks
text:
“Last week, one of the largest [soda ash] producers announced that it’s going to cut hundreds of jobs, which is a devastating blow to the workers and the families across the region, a number of whom I talked with this past weekend. And the cause is clear: It’s Communist China. They’re rigging the market against our producers. They’re flooding global markets with their subsidized soda ash.”

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator John Barrasso (R-Wyo.) secured commitments from Trump administration nominees to defend Wyoming soda ash producers and hold China accountable for dumping soda ash into global markets, support Wyoming uranium producers, and help Wyoming’s community banks by cutting burdensome regulations.

Christopher Abbott, nominee for Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Enforcement and Compliance, and Francis Browne, nominee for Under Secretary of the Treasury for Domestic Finance, testified during today’s Senate Finance Committee hearing.

On Wyoming Soda Ash Exports:

“Thank you, Mr. Chairman. Mr. Abbott, Wyoming’s Green River Basin is home of the world’s largest deposits of natural trona. It’s the mineral that is refined into soda ash.

“It’s our state’s top international export. I was with many of the folks who worked there, I was with them this past weekend.

“For generations, the industry has supported families and built strong communities across Southwest Wyoming.

“Last week, one of the largest producers announced that it’s going to cut hundreds of jobs, which is a devastating blow to the workers and the families across the region, a number of whom I talked with this past weekend.

“And the cause is clear: It’s Communist China. They’re rigging the market against our producers. They’re flooding global markets with their subsidized soda ash.

“And our miners can beat anyone on a level playing field. But Communist China has no interest in fair competition.

“Will you commit to working with our trade partners to hold China accountable for dumping soda ash into global markets?”

Follow-up:

“I’m very grateful to hear that. At the same time, some countries are moving to restrict U.S. soda ash.

“The office that you’ve been nominated to lead helps American producers fight back when other countries take unfair trade actions against us.

“So, will you help continue to defend soda ash and other American exports against unfair restrictions in the international market?”

On Russian Uranium:

“Could I also ask about uranium? Russian uranium, specifically. Because Wyoming has the largest uranium reserves in our nation.

“Our miners are ready to power America’s nuclear renaissance.

“To get there, we must end our dependence on hostile nations for nuclear fuel.

“And in 2024, this Congress banned imports of Russian uranium.

“Since then, Russia has been expanding its influence over the global uranium market, opening new paths around the ban that we have in place.

“The 2024 law gave Commerce the authority to stop that circumvention that they’ve been engaged in.

“The office that you’ve been nominated to lead is responsible for that enforcement.

“So, what steps is Commerce taking to stop uranium from Russia’s global network from entering the United States through various routes?”

Follow-up:

“Are there better things that we could be doing in Congress in terms of giving you some additional tools that can strengthen your enforcement of the ban?”

On Community Banks:

“Mr. Browne, a question for you about community banks. Because in Wyoming, we have a lot of local banks. They are the lifeblood of our rural communities.

“Twenty-six community banks are currently headquartered in the state of Wyoming. And they serve farmers, ranchers, and small businesses in places that often are really too small for a Wall Street bank to even notice.

“They know their customers. They understand the people in their communities. They understand the needs of the people that live there and work there.

“And for years, regulations written for the biggest banks have buried these small banks under mountains of paperwork.

“When one of these local banks closes, rural Wyoming loses access to credit. And it’s a real problem in our small communities.

“How will you make sure that financial regulations are better scaled to the size and the risk of community banks?”

title: Bennet Statement on Permitting Reform Vote
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet released the following statement after voting against advancing the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026:

“Our electric grid is under significant strain and faces growing demand. We need to build new transmission, bring more energy, especially clean energy, onto the grid, and keep electricity affordable. We should make it easier to build new infrastructure, and I strongly support efforts to make this a reality.

“However, permitting reform is complex, and the details matter. I am concerned that not all perspectives were sufficiently heard during the drafting of this far-reaching piece of legislation.

“As drafted, the bill does not do enough to ensure sovereign Tribal governments can protect their cultural resources and ancestral homelands, which they have stewarded since time immemorial. The bill also fundamentally overhauls how the federal government engages with the public and local communities as projects move through the permitting process. These changes must be vetted more thoroughly before passing into law. Given these concerns, I cannot support advancing this bill at this time.

“There is no doubt that we must act on these issues. That means working toward meaningful, bipartisan permitting reforms that provide certainty and reduce unnecessary delays – while also protecting our environment, respecting Tribal sovereignty and self-determination, and preserving meaningful public input. I stand ready to work with my colleagues on a path forward that achieves these goals and supports Colorado’s communities, workers, and energy priorities.”

title: Ahead of Veterans Day, Blackburn, Rosen Announce Introduction of Bipartisan Bills to Support Veteran Education Programs
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Ahead of Veterans Day, U.S. Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) and Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.) announced the introduction of two bipartisan bills to support and improve veterans' education and career programs. The first bill, the Veteran Education Empowerment Act, would reauthorize and improve a grant program that helps establish and fund student veteran centers at colleges and universities. These centers serve as a critical resource for nearly one million veterans attending college each year, ensuring they have the support they need as they transition to the classroom and workforce.

The Senators also introduced the Veteran Technology Employment Success Act, a bill to improve the VET TEC High Technology program, which funds short-term, high-tech training for veterans and servicemembers to start careers in the tech industry. Specifically, this bill would require the VA to collect data on the success of the program and update implementation to ensure the training veterans receive is in line with industry demands.

Daines Commemorates Native American Heritage Month on Senate Floor, Celebrates Rich Legacy of Montana’s Tribes
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Steve Daines today spoke on the floor of the U.S. Senate to commemorate Native American Heritage Month and his memories from working with Montana’s tribes.

Watch the full speech HERE.

Daines’ remarks as prepared for delivery:

This month is Native American Heritage Month.

It’s been a meaningful tradition of mine for the last 14 years to celebrate the rich legacy of Montana’s tribes, and this month is particularly meaningful as I close out my time in the U.S. Senate.

My interest in Montana’s tribes began at a young age. I grew up in the Gallatin Valley- I’m a graduate of Longfellow Elementary & a proud Bozeman Hawk.

And as a child, I lived two doors down from a member of the Crow Tribe, who was a Code Talker during World War 2.

His name was Barney Old Coyote, and he was an American hero. Barney served our country during World War 2 by speaking the Crow language in a national “code talk” program. The beautiful complexity of the Crow language allowed it to be used to transmit and receive military intelligence without fear of being intercepted.

Because of Barney and his fellow “Code Talkers,” countless communications were securely sent overseas, and many American lives saved.

In 2015, Barney Old Coyote was awarded Congress’ most prestigious honor, the Congressional Gold Medal, along with fellow Crow Code Talkers Samson Birdinground, Cyril Not Afraid, and Henry Old Coyote.

And fun fact, I attended grade school with Rachel Old Coyote, the cousin of Darrin Old Coyote, who was Chairman of the Crow Tribe.

So you see, my roots here run deep.

Today, I’d like to reflect on memories from working with Montana’s tribes, from the wins we’ve had over the years to priorities I hope my successors will continue after my departure.

Montana is home to many tribes, including Crow, Cheyenne, Blackfeet, Assiniboine, Gros Ventres, Salish, Kootenai, Pend d’Oreille, Little Shell, Sioux, Chippewa, and Cree.

When I was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives, there were only 11 federally recognized tribes. I made it a priority to introduce the “Little Shell of the Chippewa Indians Restoration Act,” which granted federal recognition to the Little Shell Tribe.

In 2019, after years of work, my bill passed and the Little Shell were finally granted the recognition they deserved.

Today we are the home of 12 federally recognized tribes, spread across seven reservations, from Fort Peck in the East to the Flathead in the west.

It’s been my honor to visit each reservation and my priority to meet regularly with tribal leaders and members, both in Montana and D.C., and work closely together to improve the quality of life in Indian Country- from health care and education to resource development and increasing law and order.

Each one of these communities has helped weave together a rich tapestry of culture that shaped Montana into the place it is today.

The Battle of Little Bighorn, one of the most significant battles in Montana history, is one such example. This year we commemorated its 150th anniversary.

The battle marked a pivotal moment in the Great Sioux War and the American Indian Wars. It was my honor to pass a resolution commemorating and honoring all those who fought, so that future generations understand and appreciate the enduring spirit of our tribes.

Another example is the legacy of Blackie Wetzel, who was a fierce champion of his people, a former President of the National Congress of American Indians, who advocated for tribes, including in the oval office with JFK.

In 1971, Blackie worked with Coach George Allen to create the iconic logo that became a powerful symbol of leadership and excellence during Washington’s three Super Bowl victories.

Reflecting back in 2002, Blackie Wetzel proclaimed, “It made us all so proud to have an Indian on a big-time team.”

After the franchise lost its popular brand in 2020, Blackie’s son, Don Wetzel, met with me to share how important the logo remained to him, his family, and many in Indian Country. He wanted to use the logo for the good of Native Americans, especially to raise awareness of Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women.

But instead the logo was censored by even the NFL and on official merchandise.

Since then, I’m proud to say that the League and Team have taken steps to restore the logo to a place of honor and prominence.

This same Warrior-like spirit is demonstrated through a compelling fact that many don’t know: Native Americans serve in the military at the highest rate of any group. They are patriotic, courageous Americans who serve our country in uniform with distinction and pride.

As an example of that heritage, in 2020 I was honored to join a special ceremony renaming the Billings VA Outpatient Clinic in memory of Dr. Joseph Medicine Crow, a proud War World 2 veteran and Crow Nation Tribal Chief who earned a Bronze Star and was awarded the President Medal of Freedom.

During my tenure, I also fought to restore tribal rights and promote our tribal nations.

I’ve been a member of the Senate Committee on Indian Affairs since the beginning of my time as a Senator. And so from the very start, I made communication and consultation with our tribes one of my top priorities.

The “Northern Cheyenne Lands Act” was one of our earliest victories and the second bill I ever got signed into law while serving in the U.S. House.

This bill corrected a 114-year-old survey error by the federal government, when they expanded the Northern Cheyenne reservation but failed to give them control over natural resources on the land.

Tribal sovereignty has always been a core issue. And while there’s still work to be done, lots of progress has been made.

Our team has worked with tribal leaders from every corner of the state to address priorities, from water rights and infrastructure to investing in education and rural health care.

I prioritized settling longstanding water rights issues and bringing clean water to tribes. We were able to resolve all claims to water rights on the Blackfeet reservation and permanently settle the CSKT water dispute.

And most recently, my bills to reauthorize funding for water infrastructure in Fort Peck and modernize the Crow Tribe water settlement were signed into law by President Trump.

I also championed and signed into law the “Protecting Indian Tribes from Scams Act” to give tribes and the FTC tools to fight against scams targeting tribes.

We worked on countless bills to address the Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women crisis and scourge of drug trafficking and crime on our reservations.

From the “Savanna’s Act” and the “Not Invisible Act” to my Mitigating METH Act, we made significant progress in tribal public safety.

I was also honored to lead the annual resolution bringing awareness for Montana’s Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women.

There is still work to be done.

Before I leave office, I urge my colleagues to support Montana’s final Indian Water Rights Settlement and pass my bill, the “Northern Montana Water Security Act”. Closing the chapter on Montana water settlements remains a top priority for my remaining weeks.

I also urge my colleagues to pass my bill, the “Crow Revenue Act,” which would fix long-standing inholdings on the Crow reservation while providing certainty for the Bull Mountains Mine.

I’d like to thank all those who played a role in protecting and preserving our tribal legacy. It’s been an honor to collaborate so closely with leaders of Indian nation throughout the years. I am incredibly grateful to have been able to experience the traditions and cultures of our tribes, and I’ll leave office with a deep appreciation for the enduring Indian spirit.

Thank you.

###

title: Daines, Merkley Announce Sweeping Bipartisan Proposal to “Save the Senate”
text:
End the Senate’s Dysfunction and Deliver Results for the American People

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Steve Daines (R-Mont.) and Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) announced the rollout of a sweeping bipartisan proposal that would enact major changes to the Senate’s governing rules. These changes would help restore the Senate’s purpose of robust debate and bipartisan policymaking so that the Senate can legislate effectively and tackle pressing challenges facing the country.

These major reforms will “Save the Senate.”

“For much of our history the American people could rely on the Senate to tackle our hardest challenges. But over the past 50 years, deliberation in the U.S. Senate has all but ground to a halt due to toxic, partisan political culture. As a result, the Senate has become unnecessarily— and unacceptably— diminished as the world’s greatest deliberative body.

“Both parties had a role in creating the Senate’s dysfunction, and both parties have a responsibility to fix it. That’s why we’re working together— a Democrat and a Republican— to put forward this proposal to Save the Senate.

“Our proposal will incentivize bipartisan cooperation, strengthen committees, empower members of both parties to bring and amend bills on the Senate floor, help prevent government shutdowns, and reduce needless procedural delays. These reforms will help the Senate solve our nation’s problems and deliver results for the American people,” said Daines and Merkley.

Specifically, the proposal would:

Increase time for debate on more legislation by eliminating cloture votes on nominations, motions to proceed, and amendments. Retains cloture vote prior to final passage under regular order.

Create a Senate version of the House “suspension” calendar. Bipartisan bills that have cleared committee would be eligible for swift Senate passage at a two-thirds threshold.

Create a fast-track tool that would allow bipartisan bills that have cleared committee to be processed, amended and passed at a simple majority threshold.

Create another fast-track tool that would allow bipartisan spending bills to be brought to the Senate floor, amended, and passed in two days.

Read the full details of Daines’ and Merkley’s proposals HERE.

Fetterman Celebrates $15 Million in Funding for Pennsylvania School Districts
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) announced $15 million in funding to two Allegheny County school districts through the Department of Energy’s (DOE) Renew America’s Schools program. This federal funding, which has been frozen by the administration since last year, will now go to Pittsburgh Public Schools (PPS) and Wilkinsburg School District (WSD) over the next five years.

“Bringing money back to our public schools ensures every child not only receives the education they deserve but in a place that’s safe and comfortable,” said Senator Fetterman. “I applaud DOE for taking necessary action to provide funding for crucial upgrades to ensure students in Pittsburgh and Wilkinsburg are able to learn in proper conditions.”

The Renew America’s Schools program will provide technical assistance to support critically needed infrastructure and HVAC upgrades to 20 outdated school buildings along with the necessary trained workforce to perform the upgrades, and education for regional school districts to create efficient and cost-effective schools. PPS, the second largest school system in Pennsylvania, provides educational services to 18,380 kindergarten through 12th grade students. WSD serves 535 kindergarten through 6th grade students.

Lummis Celebrates One Year Since President Trump Pardoned Wyoming Mechanic Troy Lake
text:
Cheyenne, WY — Last week, U.S. Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) marked the one-year anniversary of President Trump pardoning Wyoming diesel mechanic Troy Lake after the Biden administration sent Mr. Lake to prison for keeping emergency vehicles and school buses on the road.

“One year ago, President Trump gave Troy Lake his life back,” said Lummis. “Troy spent his career keeping rural Wyoming running, and the Biden administration repaid him for helping first responders and school buses stay on the road by sending him to federal prison. Thankfully, Troy is now exonerated and home with his family, and Washington no longer treats mechanics like criminals. A pardon fixes one injustice, but only Congress can ensure no mechanic faces jail time for serving their communities.”

In the last year, the Trump administration has stopped criminally charging mechanics in diesel tampering cases.

On September 30, 2025, Senator Lummis sent President Trump a letter requesting a pardon for Troy Lake.

title: Merkley, Wyden Announce $1.8 Million in Federal Funding to Support Public Safety Services in Tribal Communities
text:
Portland, OR – Oregon’s U.S. Senators Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden today announced that four Oregon Tribes have secured a combined $1,804,643 from the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) to develop, expand, and enhance culturally appropriate services for crime victims in Tribal communities.

“We should do all we can to keep our communities safe and support victims of crime,” said Merkley. “This investment from the federal government will allow Tribal communities across Oregon to provide critical services for survivors and their families to begin the process of recovery and healing.”

“Tribal members in Oregon should feel safe in their communities and have appropriate services available if they become victims of crime,” Wyden said. “I’m glad these federal resources are available to achieve those goals, and I’ll keep battling to secure similar funds for tribal communities throughout our state.”

Four of the awards, which come from the DOJ’s Tribal Victim Set-Aside Services and the Services for the Victims of Crime programs, support Tribes implementing trauma-informed, victim-centered services, including direct services like counseling and crisis intervention, culturally specific traditional healing, and infrastructure projects like building shelters or modular homes. Funding also supports Missing or Murdered Indigenous Persons (MMIP) search efforts and family support, alongside strategic planning, community outreach, and provider training.

The four recipients for this latest Tribal Victim Services Set-Aside program funding are as follows:

$494,092 for the Columbia River Inter-Tribal Fish Commission

$284,130 for the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde

$264,918 for the Cow Creek Band of Umpqua Tribe of Indians

$284,130 for the Klamath Tribes

Additionally, the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde received $477,343 from the Services for the Victims of Crime program. With this funding, the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde will expand its Domestic Violence Department by funding one full-time peer support specialist to provide peer support, case management, safety planning, court accompaniment, and victim support group facilitation. The project will also offer contracted civil legal services and support transportation needs of victims. The project addresses critical victim services gaps in this rural area, which is more than 20 miles from courts and social services.

“We thank Senator Merkley and Senator Wyden for standing with the tribal communities of the Columbia River and fighting to secure this funding. Our people have always cared for one another, and this investment strengthens that care. With these resources, we can expand crisis response, legal advocacy, and culturally grounded healing, so that no Native survivor of violence or abuse along the river has to face it alone,” said Aja DeCoteau, Executive Director, Columbia River Inter-Tribal Fish Commission.

“As a tribal people, we carry with us the historical traumas of violence and racism. These fuel the domestic violence cycles that too many of our people experience in their lifetime,” said Grand Ronde Tribal Chairwoman Cheryle A. Kennedy. “Those who suffer at the hands of a loved one are looking for safety. A safe place to live, to rest, and a path to physical and emotional freedom. With these grant dollars the Tribe can further our resources to give them that. Grants like these save lives and we’re grateful that the Department of Justice recognizes that.”

“I extend our appreciation and offer our many thanks to the Oregon Congressional Delegation, Senators Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden and Congressman Cliff Bentz, for much needed U.S. Department of Justice Tribal Victim Services Grant Award,” said Klamath Tribes Tribal Council Chairman William Ray, Jr.

“The Cow Creek Band of Umpqua Tribe of Indians is grateful for this funding and the opportunity it provides to strengthen services for victims of crime in our community,” said Cow Creek Band of Umpqua Tribe of Indians Chair Carla Keene. “Supporting individuals and families who have experienced trauma is an important responsibility, and we are committed to ensuring they have access to the resources, advocacy, and culturally responsive care they need to heal and move forward. This investment will help us continue this important work, not only for our Tribal citizens, but for the broader community we serve. We appreciate the Senators’ support and their recognition of the importance of these services.”

###

title: Warren, Merkley Press White House for Answers on Insider Trading Scandal Involving Trump Teleprompter Aide
text:
Senators seek answers on alleged misuse of nonpublic information, the seemingly lack of effective White House ethics safeguards, and potential conflicts of interest involving the President’s family

“Since President Trump took office, the White House appears to have become consumed by a culture of corruption and greed that has placed personal financial interests ahead of the public interest.”

Text of Letter (PDF)

Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senators Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) pressed the White House Counsel for answers following the allegations that a former Trump aide and teleprompter operator used advance knowledge of President Donald Trump’s speeches to profit from bets on prediction markets. The senators criticized the administration’s seeming failure to take meaningful action to address ethics concerns. The letter demands information on steps the White House is taking to prevent White House employees from abusing their positions for personal financial gain.

“Since President Trump took office, the White House appears to have become consumed by a culture of corruption and greed that has placed personal financial interests ahead of the public interest,” wrote the senators.

The senators highlighted the White House’s failure to take any publicly known, meaningful steps to strengthen its practices and policies in response to the allegations against the Trump aide, despite the potential for abuse of nonpublic government information by others. In July 2026, reports revealed that Trump’s longtime teleprompter operator and a former deputy assistant to the president allegedly used advance knowledge of Trump’s speeches to place bets on Kalshi. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission reached a settlement with Perez requiring him to pay $173,539 in monetary penalties and barring him from trading for three years.

“More action is required—from the President, from you, and from other White House officials—to provide the public with confidence in the integrity of the federal government under President Trump,” continued the senators.

The senators also raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest between the President’s family and prediction-market companies. Donald Trump Jr. has held advisory roles and financial interests connected to prediction-market platforms, raising questions about the need for strong ethics safeguards and confidence in impartial federal oversight.

The senators requested answers by November 23, 2026, to determine what additional safeguards are needed to prevent abuses of power, strengthen ethics enforcement, and protect the public’s trust in government.
