title: VIDEO: Sen. Moran Speaks on the Senate Floor to Honor Kansan & Aviation Leader Ed Bolen
text:
Sen. Moran’s full remarks as delivered:

“Over the weekend, there was an announcement, Madame President, and I rise as a result of that announcement. I rise tonight, this evening, to recognize Ed Bolen, a native of Salina, Kansas, who has been a leading voice for the aviation industry for decades.

“After 22 years as president and CEO of the National Business Aviation Association (NBAA), Ed announced his retirement.

“Ed’s passion for flying began early when he was introduced to aviation by his father, who served on the board of the Salina Regional Airport Authority.

“Ed went on to earn his pilot’s license, and he turned a love of flying into a career as a champion of general aviation and the men and women who support that industry.

“Early in his career, Ed served as a legislative aid for U.S. Senator Nancy Kassebaum of Kansas, where he played a key role in the passage of the historic General Aviation Revitalization Act of 1994. This legislation helped revitalize aircraft manufacturing, preserve thousands of jobs and strengthen the general aviation industry, which remains a critical component of the Kansas economy.

“Throughout his career, Ed has worked across the aisle to achieve results for aviation. His career included time as a member and chair of the Management Advisory Council at the Federal Aviation Administration, and he also served on the Commission on the Future of U.S. Aerospace Industry. In each of these roles, he helped shape our national aviation policies to further national security, economic growth and technological advances.

“Since joining NBAA in 2004, Ed has continued to be a champion for the aviation industry that he loves so much. He’s been a trusted advisor to Members of Congress, policy makers and aviation stakeholder, building consensus around issues that matter most to the future of aviation.

“Whether advocating for safer and more efficient aviation system, protecting access to our nation’s airports and airspace, supporting workforce development or championing air traffic control modernization, Ed has met every challenge with determination, thoughtful leadership and unwavering commitment to the community he represents.

“In true Kansas fashion, Ed has always focused on people, on relationships, on bringing others together to accomplish positive outcomes. The mindset has made him not only an effective advocate, but also a valued friend, advisor and respected voice throughout the aviation community. It is fitting that Ed first discovered his love for flying at a regional airport in Kansas, the Air Capital of the World.

“On behalf of the United States Senate, I want to thank Ed for his years of service and his steadfast commitment to the men and women who make up the aviation community. I express my appreciation to him and his family for his commitment, and I wish them the very best now and in the future. His leadership will clearly be missed.”

# # #

title: Murray Presses Secretary Mullin on GEO Group’s Contract Extension at the ICE Processing Center in Tacoma, Warns Obstruction Won’t Stand
text:
Senator Murray demands answers and calls out GEO Group’s neglectful, inhumane management of the facility

Murray: “One way or another, the truth will come out and there will be accountability. History will remember who stood in the way of reasonable oversight to cover up egregious violations of human rights.”

Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, sent a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin demanding answers on the GEO Group’s 10-year contract extension issued for the Northwest ICE Processing Center (NWIPC) in Tacoma, Washington.

“I write with grave concern regarding U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) efforts to further entrench immigration detention in Washington state for at least the next 10 years,” Senator Murray wrote. “I, along with other members of the Washington and Oregon delegations, have repeatedly raised concerns regarding GEO Group’s operation of the detention center and detainees’ insufficient access to medical care, inadequate nutrition, and barriers inhibiting attorneys from providing legal counsel to detained clients. Yet, ICE is continuing to arrest and detain hundreds of immigrants in Washington, including those with no criminal conviction, exacerbating conditions in detention and creating additional burdens on the federal and immigration court system.”

Senator Murray detailed repeated complaints and reports about unsafe and unsanitary conditions in the facility, including a lack of protections against sexual abuse and assault, and noted: “In 2023, the Washington State Legislature granted public health officials the authority to conduct health inspections of private detention facilities. GEO Group has repeatedly denied state health inspectors access to the facility as the state sought to enforce the law, prompting the state to sue the detention center operator. While that litigation continues, ICE and GEO Group reportedly entered into a temporary contract that contains language purporting to override state and local law and provides significant additional protections to GEO Group, including a provision requiring the federal government to cover the company’s legal fees. This language continues a dangerous trend in weakening basic protections for detainees and workers, while shielding private prison companies from accountability for abuse. It also puts taxpayers on the hook for GEO Group’s potential legal violations and inhumane treatment of detainees.”

“Instead of working in tandem with state and local governments, ICE appears to be pursuing a course that would diminish lawful local oversight of the detention facility, evade oversight, and weaken basic protections for detainees and workers,” Senator Murray wrote. “ICE’s effort to rapidly cement the detention center operator contract for another 10 years appears to be an attempt to avoid the necessary public scrutiny that would otherwise accompany the establishment of new detention facilities and operation of these facilities.”

“Nobody in the custody of the United States government should be denied basic medical care, served food that makes them sick, held in isolation for weeks, or worse. The detention conditions under this administration have been nothing short of despicable. And even as this administration has tried to obstruct oversight and conceal its wrongdoing, the American people are already horrified by what little they have been allowed to see,” Senator Murray concluded and requested information on how the contract was enacted and how ICE will uphold detention standards.

Senator Murray has spoken out forcefully and consistently against the Trump administration’s cruel and counterproductive mass deportation campaign and the egregious treatment by ICE and DHS of American citizens, legal immigrants, and undocumented immigrants. As Vice Chair of the Appropriations Committee, she led Democrats’ efforts fighting tooth and nail to secure meaningful reforms in law to rein in ICE and Border Patrol—which Republicans ultimately refused altogether and chose to skirt Democrats by delivering another massive blank check for the agencies with no accountability. Earlier this year, at a Senate Appropriations Homeland Security Subcommittee hearing on the FY27 budget request for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS)—Murray pressed Secretary Markwayne Mullin on the conduct of ICE and Border Patrol and Republicans’ refusal to enact reforms into law. Senator Murray also joined dozens of her Senate colleagues in calling for stronger accountability measures for ICE officers, and urging DHS to fulfill its previous commitments to deploy and expand the usage of body-worn cameras, strengthen officer identification requirements, and review enforcement protocols.

In June, Senator Murray released a video calling for an independent investigation in response to the fatal shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo by ICE, and demanding ICE release all of the footage of the tragedy. In March, Senator Murray released a video about the numerous violent shootings we are seeing from Trump’s reckless ICE and CBP agents across the country—and the urgent need to rein in these rogue agencies. Senator Murray highlighted the stories of Marimar Martinez, Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, Carlos Jimenez, Francisco Longoria, and Carlitos Ricardo Parias—all of whom were shot by ICE or CBP agents. Throughout the video, Senator Murray calls out the egregious use of force from federal agents, their lies that don’t hold up in court, and the extreme danger they are putting families and communities in by recklessly using firearms. Senator Murray also called out Republicans for refusing to negotiate serious and common sense measures to rein in ICE and CBP.

In July 2026, Senator Murray called on ICE to stop the deportation of a small business owner, Eduardo Aguirre Esparza, who has lived in Seattle for 23 years and is the husband of an American citizen. Eduardo was forcefully detained and in the process of being deported before courts could consider emergency relief. In December 2025, Murray called attention to the violent assault of Wilmer Toledo-Martinez in Vancouver, Washington and she successfully advocated for his release from the Northwest ICE Processing Center (NWIPC). Wilmer was lured out of his home under false pretenses, violently detained by federal agents, and mauled by an attack dog despite not resisting arrest or attempting to flee. Not long after, Murray also called attention to the case of Jose Paniagua Calderón, whose foot was run over by agents in Vancouver.

In February 2025, Senator Murray signed onto a letter demanding that DHS end wrongful searches and interrogations of Tribal members, and continued to push for answers from DHS on the matter last December. In March 2025, Murray also reintroduced her Stop Shackling and Detaining Pregnant Women Act. In September 2025, Senator Murray and Senator Richard Blumenthal led 27 of their Senate colleagues in a letter expressing concern with prevalence and the treatment of pregnant, postpartum, and nursing women in ICE detention. In November 2025, Senator Murray joined 48 of her colleagues in the Senate and House of Representatives in introducing the Restoring Access to Detainees Act, which would mandate that DHS allow people who have been detained to contact their legal counsel and families.

Senator Murray also met with farmworkers, advocates, and community members in Burlington last year to listen to their concerns amid a recent spike in ICE activity—including large-scale raids and the detention of local activists and leaders—in Northwest Washington, particularly in Whatcom and Skagit counties.

In Washington state, Senator Murray has been conducting oversight of the Northwest ICE Processing Center (NWIPC), despite the Trump administration’s efforts to block Congressional oversight of federal immigration detention facilities. After a protracted legal battle over Washington state’s ability to enforce health and safety standards at NWIPC, a federal appeals court ruled in August 2025 that the state should be allowed to enforce such standards at the detention center, and that failure to comply could result in fines of up to $10,000 per violation. In December 2025, Senator Murray led Members of the Washington state Congressional delegation in a letter to ICE, expressing grave concerns with conditions at NWIPC in Tacoma, Washington and demanding answers to a long list of questions regarding overcrowding and lack of access to medical services, food, and legal counsel for individuals detained at the facility.

Murray has been outspoken against the Trump administration’s inhumane immigration agenda from the start, strongly opposing passage of the Laken Riley Act. Murray was one of the few Senate Democrats to take to the floor to speak out forcefully against its passage.

The full letter is available HERE and below:

Dear Secretary Mullin:

I write with grave concern regarding U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) efforts to further entrench immigration detention in Washington state for at least the next 10 years. An August 2026 Request for Proposals (RFP) identified the Northwest ICE Processing Center (NWIPC) in Tacoma, WA as one of four “turn-key facility” targets for 10-year-long contracts, and ICE recently awarded a 10-year contract to continue operating NWIPC to the facility’s current owner and operator, the GEO Group.

I, along with other members of the Washington and Oregon delegations, have repeatedly raised concerns regarding GEO Group’s operation of the detention center and detainees’ insufficient access to medical care, inadequate nutrition, and barriers inhibiting attorneys from providing legal counsel to detained clients. Yet, ICE is continuing to arrest and detain hundreds of immigrants in Washington, including those with no criminal conviction, exacerbating conditions in detention and creating additional burdens on the federal and immigration court system.

Washington state and local communities have adopted laws and regulations to ensure the safety of those in detention, protect the rights of employees, and protect public health. The need for these state and local protections has been demonstrated time and time again at NWIPC. The Washington State Department of Health has received thousands of complaints about unsafe and unsanitary conditions in the facility that raise concerns about neglect and cruelty. Notably, GEO Group has been found liable for exploiting detainee workers and unjustly enriching itself through unlawful labor practices at the facility. That decision has since been affirmed by a federal appeals court. Additionally, in a May 2026 report, the University of Washington Center for Human Rights raised serious concerns about the lack of protections against sexual abuse and assault in the detention center.

In 2023, the Washington State Legislature granted public health officials the authority to conduct health inspections of private detention facilities. GEO Group has repeatedly denied state health inspectors access to the facility as the state sought to enforce the law, prompting the state to sue the detention center operator. While that litigation continues, ICE and GEO Group reportedly entered into a temporary contract that contains language purporting to override state and local law and provides significant additional protections to GEO Group, including a provision requiring the federal government to cover the company’s legal fees. This language continues a dangerous trend in weakening basic protections for detainees and workers, while shielding private prison companies from accountability for abuse. It also puts taxpayers on the hook for GEO Group’s potential legal violations and inhumane treatment of detainees.

Instead of working in tandem with state and local governments, ICE appears to be pursuing a course that would diminish lawful local oversight of the detention facility, evade oversight, and weaken basic protections for detainees and workers. In August, ICE issued the solicitation seeking proposals from contractors, with draft contract language stating that “If any conflicts between federal, state, or local laws or rules arise, the federal rules shall be followed.” This language falsely conveys that detainees in ICE custody, employees at the facility, and the local communities affected by the detention operations tied to NWIPC are no longer protected by applicable state and local laws. ICE’s effort to rapidly cement the detention center operator contract for another 10 years appears to be an attempt to avoid the necessary public scrutiny that would otherwise accompany the establishment of new detention facilities and operation of these facilities.

Please provide responses to the following questions no later than November 20, 2026:

What funds is ICE using or planning to use to fund the contracts resulting from this RFP? Please provide the originating public law with section number(s), appropriation account in which the funding resides, and period of availability for each source of funding.

What alternative periods of performance were considered for the Northwest ICE Processing Center? What is the justification for pursuing a 10-year contract?

Is ICE considering purchasing any existing facilities under the contractor-owned, contractor-operated-and-maintained pricing model required by the solicitation? If so, which facilities or categories of facilities are under consideration?

Please describe how existing Department of Homeland Security (DHS) oversight entities, including the Office of Inspector General, Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties, and the Office of the Immigration Detention Ombudsman, will be resourced to ensure that NWIPC is meeting all detention standards.

Please describe how existing medical services will be resourced, including staffing for mental health and behavioral health providers, to ensure that NWIPC is meeting the medical needs of noncitizens in custody. Additionally, please detail how ICE will mitigate the adverse impact of expanded detention operations on the public health of individuals in its custody, employees at NWIPC and the communities located in the areas surrounding NWIPC.

Attachment 11 of the RFP permits virtual attorney visitation booths to be used for asylum interviews, credible fear interviews, and immigration judge hearings, and suspends the attorney access performance measures during those uses. How is attorney access measured in those periods? How will ICE ensure compliance with applicable law and national detention standards regarding access to counsel?

The performance work statements state that more stringent state or local laws “shall not apply” to contract performance, while Attachment 16 of the RFP requires bidders to write that the facility will be operated consistent with state and federal law. Please explain this inconsistent guidance, as well as expectations for ICE contractors to observe federal, state, and local laws.

Among the wrongly detained at NWIPC are the spouses of American citizens, the parents of American citizens, and immigrants with no criminal record who have contributed to our communities for decades. America should be known for its dignity and humanity, and those values should not disappear at the doors of this detention center.

You and I both know we can enforce our immigration laws in a way that is humane, even-handed, and fair—it is abundantly clear that many in the administration, like Stephen Miller, are intent on weaponizing our immigration system to inflict suffering and cruelty on good people and innocent families. That is not remotely acceptable to me, nor should it be to you.

Nobody in the custody of the United States government should be denied basic medical care, served food that makes them sick, held in isolation for weeks, or worse. The detention conditions under this administration have been nothing short of despicable. And even as this administration has tried to obstruct oversight and conceal its wrongdoing, the American people are already horrified by what little they have been allowed to see. One way or another, the truth will come out and there will be accountability. History will remember who stood in the way of reasonable oversight to cover up egregious violations of human rights.

Sincerely,

###

title: Senator Murray: “Congress is Not Donald Trump’s Customer Service Line,” Outlines How Democratic Majority Will Fight to Lower Costs, Stop Corruption, and End War with Iran
text:
Murray: “Congress is a co-equal branch of government—not Donald Trump’s customer service line. Republicans may have forgotten that, but the American people just sent them a reminder that will echo for years to come.”

Murray: “We are fighting a deeply entrenched and lawless Administration. So, it is not going to be easy or quick. The only way to accomplish our goals is the hard way. We are going to have to roll up our sleeves, and grind it out. It’s going to take hard work, sustained pressure, and sharp political strategy. Building something is always going to be harder, slower work than burning it down.”

***WATCH: Senator Murray’s full speech***

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, spoke on the Senate floor on how the incoming Democratic Congress will fight to lower costs, help families get by, put an end to Trump’s reckless war of choice with Iran, and fight the rampant corruption coming out of every corner of this administration.

Senator Murray’s remarks, as delivered, are below:

“Last week the American people used their voices. They used their votes. They did their job. Now, it is time for Congress to finally get back to its job. We are here to be a voice for the American people, not a rubber stamp for the President.

“Look, Congress is a co-equal branch of government—not Donald Trump’s customer service line. Republicans may have forgotten that, but the American people just sent them a reminder that will echo for years to come.

“And now, Democrats are going to try something Republicans seem to have forgotten about: keeping our promises. We are going to hit the ground running by fighting to lower costs, to stop corruption, and to end Trump’s war with Iran. That’s what America voted for. And that’s what we will work to deliver.

[TRUMP’S TARIFFS AND TRADE WAR]

“A Democratic Congress means pressing to put an end to Trump’s stupid tariffs and trade wars. Nobody in America wants to pay more for groceries just so Trump can pick a fight with Canada.

[ACCOUNTABILITY FOR ICE]

“A Democratic Congress means real accountability for ICE. Republicans wrote ICE a blank check. We are going to be writing them subpoenas.

[CRACKING DOWN ON CORRUPTION]

“A Democratic Congress means cracking down on corruption: insider trading, selling pardons and access, crypto scams, no-bid contracts, war profiteering—all of it.

“If you thought Trump was your ticket to get rich quick by breaking laws, abusing power, and defrauding the American people, you thought wrong. When the gavels change hands, the days of rampant, consequence-free grifting will come to an end. Bet on that.

[ACCESSIBLE AND AFFORDABLE HEALTH CARE]

“And of course, when it comes to health care, a Democratic Congress means reversing health care cuts—just for a start. Every time Republicans take power, they make a mess out of health care.

“We have got to reverse the Medicaid cuts that are shutting down our hospitals. We have got to restore the ACA tax credits that make health care far more affordable for families. And we need to stop Trump’s plan to use AI to cut seniors off from their Medicare benefits.

“But we can’t stop there—because if Republicans’ health care strategy is ‘death by a thousand cuts,’ Democrats have to be more than the party of a thousand band-aids.

“We need a robust public option, and universal coverage. And we are going to have that conversation in the next Congress.

[PUBLIC HEALTH]

“We are also going to have a conversation about undoing all the damage RFK Jr. has done to our health in this country.

“A Democratic Congress means putting science back in public health.

“Right now, measles cases are at record levels. Instead of solving the problem, our nation’s highest health official is covering it up. Instead of championing vaccines, RFK Jr. has been championing conspiracies. He should be fighting viruses, not vaccines.

“Americans don’t want viruses that we eliminated roaring back and killing babies. Americans don’t want lettuce to give them diarrhea. They don’t want promising clinical trials cut off, or respected researchers sacked. They don’t want FDA’s gold standard overruled by Secretary Kennedy’s wildest conspiracies or Trump’s biggest donors.

“Chaos and corruption may have spread like a plague under Trump and RFK Jr, but you know what they say: sunlight is the best disinfectant. Accountability is coming. And RFK Jr. is far from the only person we will be holding accountable.

[HOLDING VOUGHT ACCOUNTABLE]

“A Democratic Congress means Russ Vought’s days of breaking our laws and extorting our communities without consequence are coming to an end. As incoming Chair of the Appropriations Committee, you better believe I am going to be demanding answers and accountability for the brazen robbery and illegality we have seen from Trump’s OMB director.

“I’m going to have hearings, and I’m going to use our funding bills to rein in the abuses and corruption of this administration while we invest in our American families. I will expose this administration’s corruption and the games Russ Vought and OMB have been playing with our American tax dollars.

“I am going to drag this Administrations’ crooked schemes into the light of day for every American to see—and you better believe I am going to stamp this president’s very ugly and very un-American brand of politics and corruption into the dust.

[MAKING CHILD CARE AFFORDABLE]

“Now let me just say: I am going to make certain a Democratic Congress means getting serious about the child care crisis. Child care is too hard for parents to find. It’s too expensive for families to afford. It is too tough for providers to keep their daycare facilities open. And this all is crushing our families and our economy.

“I have been fighting for child care since my first day in politics—and you can bet that next Congress I am going to be loud about beating the drum, pounding the pavement, and charting a course towards a future where every family in this country can get quality, affordable child care. And with so many new colleagues now coming who have young kids joining us, I know we are going to make progress.

[DEFENDING PUBLIC EDUCATION]

“That doesn’t just go for child care though—it also goes for defending public education.

“A Democratic Congress means Trump’s plan to demolish the Department of Education is dead in the water. We’ve been fighting these efforts since Trump’s first day in office—but with gavels in hand, we are going to have even more power to put an end to this nonsense once and for all.

“There is no world where this former Pre-K teacher will let Trump bulldoze the programs that support our kids, because every student deserves to be able to get a great education—and afford college—no matter their zip code, or the size of their parent’s bank account.

[INVESTING IN INFRASTRUCTURE]

“And a Democratic Congress means building infrastructure for all Americans—instead of letting Trump build monuments to himself. Republicans have voted to cut off vital investments to create great jobs and rebuild America’s infrastructure. Well guess what? Democrats are going to fight to keep investing in the roads, and bridges, and ports, and airports that people use every day.

[FIGHTING FOR REPRODUCTIVE FREEDOM]

“We are also going to be pushing hard to fight back on abortion. A Democratic Congress means countering Republican attacks on abortion and clawing back the rights they have chipped away.

“Make no mistake, Republicans spent decades on their crusade to overturn Roe and rip away women’s rights. So I will spend every day of this majority fighting to win them back. Democrats will be relentless and tenacious.

“And that means putting abortion rights to a vote on the floor and making every senator say where they stand. It means protecting Title X, Planned Parenthood, and contraception access from this administration’s attacks. It means elevating the voices of women across the country about being investigated for miscarriages, or forced to death’s door before a doctor could treat them.

“I do not expect quick, easy victories—but I am in this fight for as long as it takes. We will claw back every inch we can at every opportunity we can. I will keep pushing until we have the trifecta we need to restore abortion rights in all 50 states.

[KILLING TRUMP’S BLANK CHECK FOR WAR]

“Now, when it comes to Trump’s wars, let’s be clear: a Democratic Congress means Donald Trump is absolutely not getting his $1.5 trillion war budget, or the nearly $70 billion he wants to bankroll the Iran war.

“There is no way on God’s green earth that I am going to let Republicans jam through a funding bill that blows war spending through the roof and at the same time cutting family priorities like child care, housing, and health care.

“This war with Iran should never have started. It is putting our service members in harms’ way. It is blowing gas prices through the roof. It is undermining our credibility on the world stage—not to mention weakening our position on other fronts. This administration is responsible for the deaths of nearly 200 Iranian school children, for God’s sake.

“Trump’s war has been a disaster from top to bottom. We are going to push to end this war as responsibly as we can, and we are going to hold Trump and Hegseth accountable for starting it in the first place.

[LOOKING FORWARD]

“Now, there’s going to be a lot more to say on these issues—and many other challenges where Republicans are going to have to accept reality and come to the table to work with us. Like: how do we develop a responsible framework for AI regulation that makes sure regular people are the ones reaping the benefits of this technology, not the ones bearing the burdens of it?

“The clock is ticking to get our arms around this. We cannot let this powerful technology—and the companies developing it—run amok.

“Or, how do we preserve Social Security in a way that keeps our promise to seniors, and prevents painful cuts to benefits? Social Security is projected to run dry in 2032—meaning every Senator just elected is going to have a say in how we solve this. Those conversations need to start now.

“Or, for anyone wondering if I can find common ground with Trump: Let’s pass the Sunshine Protection Act. Let’s give people a bit more sunshine. Let’s finally end the tyranny of changing the clock back and forth just to see the sun set before you leave work.

“There is no question we have got our work cut out for us in the Congress ahead. I think we all know this is not going to be easy. I’d like to say the overwhelming results sent an undeniable message to the White House, but we all know this President has no problem denying election results, or spitting in the face of Congress, or flouting our laws.

“Republicans forgot Congress is not a rubber stamp. Our challenge is to remember it is not a magic wand. We are a co-equal branch of government. We can check this President, but we still have to contend with his veto power, and we still have to face a conservative Supreme Court.

“We can bring down prices, but not with a wave of our hands. We can fight corruption, but not with a strong press statement. And we can end Trump’s war with Iran, but not with a snap of our fingers.

“We are fighting a deeply entrenched and lawless Administration. So, it is not going to be easy or quick. The only way to accomplish our goals is the hard way. We are going to have to roll up our sleeves, and grind it out. It’s going to take hard work, sustained pressure, and sharp political strategy. Building something is always going to be harder, slower work than burning it down.

“But I want to end with the good news. The American people turned out in a very big way last week. They sent a message as loud and clear as I have ever heard in politics. And as a result, next year Democrats will have more hands to take on that work than at any time in the Trump era.

“And we are—every single one of us—ready to meet this moment.”

###

title: Sen. Ossoff Cosponsoring Bipartisan Legislation to Protect Georgia Veterans from Addiction
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Jon Ossoff is supporting bipartisan legislation to protect Georgia veterans from opioid addiction.

Sen. Ossoff cosponsored the NOPAIN for Veterans Act to expand access to non-opioid pain treatments that veterans previously could not obtain through the VA National Formulary.

The bipartisan bill, first introduced by Sens. Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV) and Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), would help address gaps in care by providing veterans with access to non-opioid alternatives and help prevent addiction among Georgia veterans.

“Veterans have made huge sacrifices on behalf of our Nation, and too often struggle with substance abuse and addiction upon returning home,” Sen. Ossoff said. “This bipartisan legislation would help ensure the VA can quickly provide safe pain management treatments for veterans and protect veterans from addiction.”

Sen. Ossoff continues his work to support veterans and Georgia communities in combatting addiction.

In February, Sens. Ossoff and Rev. Warnock brought Republicans and Democrats together to help Hire Heroes USA expand their efforts to provide in-person employment support to transitioning servicemembers, veterans, and military spouses throughout the State of Georgia.

In January, Sen. Ossoff announced the passage of a key provision in last year’s National Defense Authorization Act that will help protect health care by increasing oversight over the Department of Defense’s ability to modify or downsize military hospitals and clinics.

Last December, Sen. Ossoff cosponsored the bipartisan Overcoming Prevalent Inadequacies in Overdose Information Data Sets (OPIODS) Act of 2025 to help prevent opioid deaths.

Last August, Sens. Ossoff and Rev. Raphael Warnock announced $900,000 in Federal funding through the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) to support efforts across Georgia to fight the opioid crisis.

In 2022, Sen. Ossoff’s bipartisan Rural Opioid Abuse Prevention Act was signed into law, which helped rural communities experiencing a high level of opioid overdoses respond to the crisis.

Rosen, Curtis Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Provide Transportation Allowance for Servicemembers Stationed at Remote Bases
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and John Curtis (R-UT) introduced a bipartisan bill to provide a transportation allowance for servicemembers stationed at remote and isolated installations who have long commutes because of a lack of housing or essential services near their assigned duty stations. The Transportation Relief for Servicemembers at Remote and Isolated Locations Act would reimburse fuel costs, vehicle maintenance, and public transportation costs for those servicemembers assigned to remote or isolated bases, like Naval Air Station Fallon and Creech Air Force Base in Nevada.

“Due to a lack of essential services and housing around our more isolated bases, too many servicemembers are forced to spend more of their hard-earned money just to get to and from work every day. As gas prices and car costs continue to rise, so does the strain on the budget of our servicemembers,” said Senator Rosen. “I am proud to introduce this bipartisan bill to support our servicemembers while they do everything they can to defend our freedoms and national security.”

“Installations like Dugway Proving Ground and Tooele Army Depot are doing vitally important work for our national security,” said Senator Curtis. “But serving at these remote locations comes with unique sacrifices for servicemembers and their families, who may be forced to choose between long and increasingly expensive commutes or living with limited access to essential services. This bipartisan legislation recognizes the unique challenges of serving in remote locations and will help ease the cost of living for military families while strengthening our ability to recruit and retain those who wish to serve.”

Senator Rosen has fought to ensure that servicemembers and veterans in Nevada and across the country have access to all the benefits and resources they need, particularly those in more rural areas. The Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act included Senator Rosen’s provision to designate Creech Air Force Base as a remote and isolated installation. She recently introduced two bills to fund and improve important veterans education programs. Senator Rosen also introduced bipartisan legislation to cut bureaucratic hurdles and improve health care access for servicemembers and veterans. Earlier this year, Senator Rosen helped secure a 3.9 percent pay raise for U.S. servicemembers and billions of dollars in federal funding for job and housing assistance programs for Nevada’s servicemembers in the bipartisan funding package.

Sen. Tim Scott applauds CMS’ second year of rural health transformation awards
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Tim Scott (R-S.C.) issued the following statement regarding the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services’ (CMS) announcement of $10 billion in second-year funding through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP).

“Access to high-quality healthcare should not depend on where a family lives,” said Sen. Scott. “I applaud CMS for its continued commitment to supporting rural hospitals, medical professionals, and patients. This investment will help make sure South Carolinians can get the care they need and that no community is left behind.”

South Carolina will receive nearly $196 million to advance its state-developed plan to strengthen rural healthcare, with priorities ranging from chronic disease management and workforce development to expanded telehealth access and investments in modern technology and data. The RHTP was authorized through the Working Families Tax Cut Act in July 2025. The program provides $50 billion in funding over five years to all 50 states to improve rural health across the country.

Background:

Year one of RHTP provided more than $167 million for 228 projects across South Carolina.

In 2025, Sen. Scott introduced the Improving Care in Rural America Reauthorization Act to continue rural health outreach services programs that were signed into law under President Trump in 2020.

Three key programs would be reauthorized through fiscal year 2030: Rural Healthcare Services Grants, Rural Health Network Grants, and Small Healthcare Provider Quality Improvement Grants.

title: Shaheen Statement on Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
Slotkin Statement on Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act Procedural Vote
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) released the following statement after voting yes on a procedural vote to advance the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) on the Senate floor.

“Today, I voted yes to advance the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. The Senate has just returned to DC and there are significant priorities to address. Voting yes for this legislation to advance today allows for those discussions to continue.

“This bill is not perfect, like no piece of legislation is. It has real strengths and weaknesses. Most importantly, this bill will bring down costs for Michiganders by making it cheaper and easier to build energy infrastructure — something I have heard loud and clear from Michiganders for years. It is also the first federal legislation that places guardrails on data centers and prevents them from passing increases in electricity bills for Michiganders.

“However, I have real issues with the provisions in this bill that weaken the Clean Water Act and the impacts this bill has on the sovereignty of our tribal nations. In particular, I am concerned about tribal nations’ ability to meaningfully engage on projects that may harm their sacred places.

“I support making meaningful improvements to address these concerns during the amendment process, and I look forward to working with my colleagues to get this right before final passage.”

Welch, Crapo, Ruiz, Bilirakis, Tenney Lead Bipartisan, Bicameral Bill to Better Protect Servicemembers from Burn Pits, Improve Care for Veterans
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Ahead of Veterans Day, U.S. Senators Peter Welch (D-Vt.) and Mike Crapo (R-Idaho), along with U.S. Representatives Raul Ruiz (D-CA-35), Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12), and Claudia Tenney (R-NY-24), introduced the Waste Incineration Protection, Exposure Oversight, and Updated Tracking of (WIPE OUT) Burn Pits Act. This bipartisan, bicameral legislation would build on the Sergeant First Class Heath Robinson Honoring our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics (PACT) Act by ensuring all instances of toxic exposure from burn pits are accounted for. The legislation would also establish a clear framework for identifying, tracking, and mitigating risks of open‑air burn pits located near U.S. forces and push for replacement with safer alternatives.

The PACT Act, which Senator Welch championed as a member of the House of Representatives, was signed into law by President Biden in 2022, To date, more than 7 million veterans have been screened for toxic exposures because of the PACT Act.

“When we passed the PACT Act four years ago, we took a major step toward ensuring that the cost of war always includes the cost of caring for the warrior. But there’s always more we can do to improve servicemember safety, including finding better ways to track and mitigate the risks of burn pits,” said Senator Welch. “I’m proud to partner with Senator Crapo on this bill which builds on our bipartisan work to expand benefits and open doors to care for veterans exposed to toxic chemicals.”

“While the Pentagon has largely phased out the use of burn pits, many foreign partners and entities continue to operate them near installations where U.S. personnel live and work,” said Senator Crapo. “We must take proactive steps to reduce the risk of toxic exposure by providing safer waste disposal alternatives, working with foreign partners to eliminate hazardous burn pits and ensuring servicemembers’ health records accurately document potential exposure so veterans can access appropriate benefits and care in the future.”

“I’m proud to lead the bipartisan, bicameral WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act to protect servicemembers from the harmful effects of toxic burn pits.” said Rep. Dr. Raul Ruiz. “This bill requires the Department of Defense (DoD) to find, record, and test the air at every burn pit site used by other countries or contractors that are endangering the lives of our troops. The PACT Act gave presumptive benefits and health care to veterans harmed by burn pit exposure. The WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act aims to end the use of toxic burn pits once and for all.”

“Our servicemembers put their lives on the line to defend our nation, and they should never have to face lifelong health consequences because of the toxic exposure they endured while serving. The WIPE Out Burn Pits Act is an important step toward protecting our military personnel, addressing the dangers of burn pit exposure, and ensuring those who serve our country have the support and protections they deserve. We have a responsibility to safeguard the health of our heroes, and I will continue fighting to make that a priority,” said Rep. Bilirakis.

“Our servicemembers should not have to worry that the air they breathe while defending our country could jeopardize their health for years to come,” said Rep. Tenney. “We have seen the devastating consequences of toxic exposure on our veterans and their families, and we must do everything possible to prevent future generations from facing the same challenges. The bipartisan WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act will help identify dangerous exposure risks, improve accountability, and ensure our troops have accurate health records if they need care in the future. Protecting those who serve our nation must remain a top priority, both during their service and long after they return home.”

For decades, the Department of Defense (DoD) relied on open-air burn pits to dispose of waste during overseas contingency operations, exposing U.S. servicemembers to toxins linked to long-term health conditions, including respiratory disease, cancer, and heart issues. The PACT Act took historic steps to expand care and benefits for veterans suffering from toxic exposure.

The WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act builds on that progress by ensuring all instances of toxic exposure from burn pits are recorded in a servicemember’s health records. While DoD has reduced its own use of burn pits, servicemembers are still exposed to active burn pits not controlled by DoD, and safer alternatives exist for instances when DoD does operate burn pits. Specifically, the WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act:

Establishes a clear framework for identifying, tracking, and mitigating the risks of non‑DoD open‑air burn pits located near U.S. forces, and ensure that exposure to toxic substances is incorporated into servicemembers’ health records;

Directs the Secretary of Defense to submit a report to Congress detailing the location and use of all nearby burn pits, including those operated by allies, partners, or local entities;

Requires the deployment of alternative solid waste disposal systems in locations where the DoD operates burn pits; and

Mandates diplomatic engagement, jointly by the Secretaries of Defense and State, with host nations to create a wind down plan the use of burn pits in areas where U.S. personnel could be exposed.

Provisions of the lawmakers’ legislation were included in the Senate’s Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27) National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), including provisions to:

Prioritize the deployment of alternative solid waste disposal systems to contingency locations where DoD identifies that open-air burn pits remain in use;

Update DoD policy to ensure that non-DoD controlled burn pits are recorded in impacted servicemembers’ health records.

The House’s FY27 NDAA report also included provisions from the WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act that would:

Require DoD to brief Members of Congress on servicemember exposure to non-DoD controlled burn pits; and

Study DoD’s current use of alternative waste disposal methods and what is further needed to finally eliminate the DoD’s reliance on burn pits.

This legislation also builds on Senator Welch and Rep. Ruiz’s bipartisan, bicameral Waste and Illegal Property Eradication (WIPE) Act, which supports servicemember health and strengthen national security by improving how the U.S. military eliminates certain materials both at home and overseas. The WIPE Act’s provisions prohibiting the use of open-air burn pits to dispose of contraband or classified materials and authorizing the use of alternative solid waste disposal systems were included in the final National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26).

The WIPE OUT Burns Pit Act is endorsed by Burn Pits 360, the Disabled American Veterans (DAV), FealGood Foundation, Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America (IAVA), Military Officers Association of America (MOAA), and the Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors (TAPS).

Learn more about the WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act.

Read and download the full text of the legislation.

Senator Welch has championed efforts to limit toxic substance exposure among veterans in the Senate, including the bicameral Airborne Hazards and Open Burn Pit Registry 2.0 Act, which passed as part of the FY25 NDAA, and the bipartisan Burn Pit Elimination Act, both bills that would improve protections for veterans under the PACT Act and prevent future toxic exposure cases. A bipartisan amendment led by Sens. Welch, Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), and Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) requiring the VA to conduct a review on mortality and toxic exposure data for veterans who served in Kosovo also passed with bipartisan support in the Senate.

Senator Welch also cosponsored the Burn Pit Registry Enhancement Act, Reducing Exposure to Burn Pits Act, and Toxic Exposure Education for Servicemembers Act, bills that build on the PACT Act to provide increased support for veterans exposed to burn pits, improve data collection on burn pit and toxic substance exposure, and help mitigate future toxic substance exposure for servicemembers.

Senator Welch’s talented team of caseworkers can help Veterans, families, and survivors with casework related to the VA, as well as other federal agencies. Vermont veterans and servicemembers seeking assistance are encouraged to visit welch.senate.gov or call his Burlington office: 802-863-2525.
